No manager has a PIN on this device yet (it has never been synced): the confirmation is enough.
“… plan limit reached” when generating a new code
Another device still occupies the place: unpair it as above, or revoke it in the back office. The same message appears
on the device when you pair it with a code while the plan is already full (1).
To switch roles between kitchen display and floor phone, there is no need to unpair: change the role from the
device details in the back office, then restart the app.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Pair the register, phone, kitchen display or kiosk
- Manage your devices (rename, change role, replace, revoke)
- Close the register
- Previous pairings: find and export the data of a former store

pages.title: Hardware diagnostics (scanner, drawer, beep, server)

sections.heading: Hardware diagnostics (scanner, drawer, beep, server)
sections.text: Register menu › Hardware diagnostics tests each part of the station, one by one.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Test each part
- Barcode scanner (1): “Scan a code with the barcode scanner” — scan any product, and the code read is shown.
- Camera: Scan with camera.
- Printer: the printer that is set up and its width; Print a test ticket (2).
- Cash drawer: Open the drawer (drawer connected to the printer).
- Beep: Test the beep.
- Network: the server address; Test the server connection.
Read the results
Each test shows its result under the button: “Ticket printed in … ms” (1), “Beep played”, “Server reachable in … ms”
(2), “Last successful sync: …”. Copy the report copies everything so you can send it to support.

sections.heading: On other devices
sections.text:
The same screen exists on all devices; it only shows what makes sense for the device:
Device · Where to find it · Tests available
Register · Register menu › Hardware › Hardware diagnostics · barcode scanner, camera, printer, drawer, beep, network
Floor phone · More actions (“⋯”) on the floor plan › Hardware diagnostics · camera, printer (if set up on the phone), beep, network
Kitchen display · Screen settings menu › Hardware diagnostics · beep, network
Kiosk · technical screen (after the manager PIN) › Hardware diagnostics · printer, beep, network
At the bottom of the screen, Online help opens the help center section for the device.
Step by step on the phone: Phone menu.
No printer configured
Set up the printer first (see Printer).
Drawer not opened: printer unreachable
The drawer opens through the printer: if the printer does not respond, neither does the drawer. Set up the printer.
Server unreachable: …
No Internet or server unavailable (cause in parentheses: “connection refused”, “timed out”, “host not found”, “no
network connection”). The register keeps selling offline; see
Sync.
Nothing appears when I scan with the barcode scanner
The scanner is not connected (USB cable, Bluetooth pairing) or is not in “keyboard” mode. Check its manual.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Connect and set up the printer
- Floor phone menu
- Scan with the camera
- The printer does not print
- A register no longer syncs

pages.title: Charge: cash, card, several methods

sections.heading: Charge: cash, card, several methods
sections.text:
Tap Charge … under the ticket: the Checkout sheet replaces the ticket. At the top, Remaining; below, the
methods: Cash, Card, Meal voucher (if the store accepts them) and Other (check, gift voucher…
depending on the store settings).

sections.heading: In cash
sections.text:
Enter the amount received
With Cash (2) selected, tap a quick cash button (Exact, 20,00, 50,00…) (3) or type the amount on the keypad.
The bottom button (4) shows what is missing as long as the amount does not cover the total.
Read the change and charge
Cash received (1) and Change (2) are shown in large type: give back the change shown, then tap Charge ….
Expected result: Sale recorded, the Ticket no. … (1), the change to give (2) and “Sale sealed — fiscal
no. …”. New sale (3) prepares the next ticket; the ticket prints if a printer is set up.

sections.heading: By card
sections.text:
Type the amount on the card terminal then confirm
Tap Card. The register shows the Amount to enter on the card terminal (1). Type it on your payment terminal,
have the customer pay, then tap Accepted (2) if the terminal accepted, Declined otherwise.
If a payment terminal is connected to the register (payment connector), the amount is sent to it directly and the
register waits for its response.

sections.heading: Several payment methods
sections.text:
Add the payments one by one
Choose a method, enter part of the amount, tap Add …: the payment joins Payments added (1) and Remaining
goes down. Finish with another method (here Exact in cash) (2), then Charge … (3). The trash icon removes a
payment added by mistake.

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
Same sheet; the Android tablet also shows the Tab tile (payment on a customer's account).
Card payment declined — choose another method.
The terminal declined the card (or you tapped Declined). Offer another method; nothing is recorded until the sale is
paid in full.
The card exceeds the total by … — no change on card.
No change is given on a card: the card amount must be at most equal to the remaining amount.
No open cash session — open a session before charging.
Open the session (yellow Open session banner); the ticket is kept.
The “Other” method is not offered in this store
The “Other” labels (check, gift voucher…) are set in the back office. Without a label, the method is not offered.
Card payment is blocked or waiting for the terminal
See Card payment is declined or blocked and
Connect a payment connector.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Meal vouchers and tips
- Reprint a ticket
- Returns and voids

pages.title: Apply a discount (on a line or on the ticket)

sections.heading: Apply a discount (on a line or on the ticket)
sections.text:
Two kinds of discount: on one line (one product) or on the whole ticket. Up to the store threshold (by default
10 % or 20,00 €, adjustable in the back office), the register applies it directly; above it, the register asks for
a reason and a manager's PIN.

sections.heading: Line discount
sections.text:
Tap the line
Tap the ticket line: the Line discount window opens, with the heading Discount on “Expresso”. Choose Percentage
or Amount (€) (1), then type the value (2). The preview (3) shows the discount and the new amount. Tap Apply (4).
Expected result: under the line, “Discount −10 %”; the line price is struck through and recalculated.

sections.heading: Ticket discount
sections.text:
Tap Discount under the ticket
Tap Discount under the lines, then proceed as for a line: Percentage or Amount (€), value. If the discount
exceeds the threshold, the preview says so (1): choose a Reason (2) (the store's reasons; the default ones are shown in the
register's language: Goodwill gesture, Damaged product, Employee, Competition, Other), then tap
Manager PIN… (3).
The manager approves
The manager types their PIN and taps Approve (see Approve with the manager PIN).
The discount appears in the totals (1), with the name of the manager who approved it.
To remove a discount, reopen the window (line or Discount) and tap Remove the discount.
Ticket discount beyond the threshold without manager approval
The discount exceeds the store threshold: choose a reason and have a manager enter their PIN. Thresholds are set in the
back office (Checkout and payments section).
The discount exceeds the discounted amount (RG-SALE-11)
You cannot discount more than the price: lower the amount or the percentage.
No manager with a PIN on this register
No manager has a PIN known to this register: set a PIN in the back office (PIN & approvals), then sync the register.
Approval expired — ask for the manager PIN again
The approval is only valid for a few minutes: have the PIN entered again.
The approved discount disappeared after resuming a held ticket
This is intentional: a PIN-approved discount is not kept in a held ticket (“PIN-approved discounts to re-enter”). Apply
the discount again after resuming the ticket.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Approve with the manager PIN
- Charge
- Control discounts given at the register
- Manager PIN and approvals

pages.title: Make a sale (products, search, cart)

sections.heading: Make a sale (products, search, cart)
sections.text:
The sales screen shows the product grid on the left and the Receipt on the right (on a phone, the cart opens at the
bottom of the screen). In a restaurant, choose Direct sale to sell at the counter without a table.
A complete sale on iPad: three products (including a burger with its options), Charge, card payment accepted.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Add the products
- Tap a tile (3): the product is added to the ticket; a badge shows the quantity already in the cart. A product
with a photo in the back office shows it on its tile (wide tile, or any tile on a tablet): it is kept on the device
and stays visible offline.
- Search in Search or scan (2): type a few letters of the name or a barcode.
- Scan with the barcode scanner (the code goes into the search) or with the camera (icon to the right of the field,
see Scan a code).
An open window (discount, payment…) refuses the scan: "Close this window to scan" (see
Scanning while a window is open).
In a restaurant, check that Direct sale (1) is selected. Customer (phone, card) (4) attaches a customer to the
sale (loyalty, tab).
A product with options (cooking, side…) or a combo opens a choice window: see Variants, weight, options and
combos.
Adjust the ticket
Tap a line (1) to apply a discount to it; + and − (2) change the quantity (at 0, the line disappears). Under the
lines: Discount (discount on the whole ticket), Hold (3) (set the ticket aside) and Clear. The Total and
the VAT update live.
Charge
Tap Charge (4): the checkout sheet opens. The next steps are described in
Charge: cash, card, several methods.
Expected result: after payment, Sale recorded and the ticket number; New sale clears the ticket for the next
customer.

sections.heading: Reading a tile
sections.text:
On iPhone, iPad and Android, every tile of the grid reads the same way.
- The price: on a one-column tile, the amount is shown without the currency symbol (“3.90”) so that it fits in
full; on a two-column tile, it carries the symbol. A product sold by weight adds “/kg” after the amount
(“3.90 /kg”); read aloud (VoiceOver, TalkBack), it is “3.90 € per kilo”.
- The initials: a product with no image shows its initials on its colour, in place of the thumbnail.
- The stock badge: for a product whose stock is tracked, a badge appears as soon as 2 or fewer are left: the
remaining number with an alert icon (“2”), then in the error tone at 0 (out of stock) and below (“−1”). Read aloud:
“low stock: 2” or “out of stock”. A product whose stock is not tracked has no badge.
- The cart counter: the number of units already in the cart is shown on the tile. For a product with variants, it
is the sum of all its variants in the cart.
- The “Variants” or “Meal deal” mention: a tile of a product with variants carries “Variants”, a meal-deal tile
“Meal deal”. As soon as the product is in the cart, the mention disappears (the counter takes its place); the stock
badge then stays visible as an icon only, next to the counter. If a product is both a meal deal and has variants,
only “Meal deal” is shown.
- In Arabic, the grid is mirrored: column 1 is on the right, the tile's text is right-aligned, and the suffix
becomes “/كغ” (the amount stays readable left to right).

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
Same layout; lines carry the MV badge when the product can be paid with a meal voucher.
The same sale on an Android tablet, paid in cash.
No product matches “…”.
Nothing matches the search. Try another word (without accents, start of the name), or check that the product is active
in the back office.
Unknown code … — search prefilled
The scanned barcode is not linked to any product. Search for the product by name; ask your manager to add the barcode
to the product record.
…: product not sold in this store
The product exists but it is disabled for your store (store override in the back office).
No local products — sync the catalog.
The register has not received the catalog yet (recent pairing, or no Internet). Tap the sync badge then Sync now.
Not enough stock: … — manager PIN to sell anyway
The store does not allow negative stock and there is not enough of this product left. A manager can authorize the sale
with their PIN; otherwise remove the line.
A product does not appear on the register
See A product does not appear on the register: inactive product, hidden
category, store override, or register not synced.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Charge
- Apply a discount
- Put a ticket on hold
- Get the cart back after the app stops
- Create and edit a product
- Set up the sales screen

pages.title: The print queue (retry, redirect, abandon)

sections.heading: The print queue (retry, redirect, abandon)
sections.text:
Every print job (receipt, kitchen ticket, report) goes through a queue. If the printer runs out of paper or does not
respond, the sale continues and the print job waits. A job is never deleted: you reprint it, redirect it or abandon
it with a reason (traced).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Register menu › Printer settings › Print queue
Filter by type (1): All, Kitchen tickets, Receipts, Reports. Each job (2) shows its printer, its time
and its status (Pending, Printed, failed).
Retry, redirect or abandon
On a failed job: Reprint (“Reprint started”), Redirect to another configured printer, or Abandon (“… will
not be printed. The abandon is traced in the audit log.”).
Expected result: the queue empties; the footer of the sales screen no longer shows “Printing pending: …”.
No other printer configured
To redirect, you need a second printer set up (for example the kitchen one).
Receipts stay “Pending”
The printer is offline, out of paper or its cover is open: fix the problem, and the queue restarts by itself, in order.
Test with Hardware diagnostics.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Connect and set up the printer
- The printer does not print

pages.title: Connect and set up the receipt printer

sections.heading: Connect and set up the receipt printer
sections.text:
Vendora prints on ESC/POS receipt printers: network (TCP, port 9100 by default), Bluetooth or USB
(Android). The setting is specific to each device and printing does not need the Internet. A failed print never
blocks a sale: the receipt waits in the print queue.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Register menu › Printer settings
Enter the printer's Address (1) (its IP address, for example 192.168.1.50) and the Port (9100 by default), then
the Paper width (2): 80 mm (48 columns) or 58 mm. Don't know the address? Tap Search the network (3) (or
Search via Bluetooth): the printers found are listed, tap yours.
With no printer at hand (training, demo), Use the simulated printer simulates printing without any hardware.
Save and print a test ticket
Further down: Store name (ticket header), and This device prints kitchen tickets (1) — check it on **only
one** device in the store, the one that prints the floor phones' tickets (otherwise each ticket prints twice). Tap
Save then Test ticket (2). Remove the printer (3) deletes the setting.
Expected result: “Printer saved” then “Test ticket printed”; the ticket comes out.
No printer answers on port 9100
The printer is off, on another network, or is not a network printer. Check the cable / Wi-Fi, print its configuration
page (printer button) to read its IP address, then enter it.
No local network: connect the register to the store Wi-Fi
The register is not on the store Wi-Fi (mobile data only): network search is not possible.
Invalid address or port (port 1–65535)
The address or the port was entered incorrectly (e.g. “192.168.1.50”, port “9100”).
Printer unreachable — retrying automatically
The printer no longer responds; receipts wait in the queue and go out again as soon as it is back. See
The print queue.
No paired printer.
Android, Bluetooth: first pair the printer in Android's Bluetooth settings, then come back here (Allow Bluetooth if
asked).
The ticket prints twice in the kitchen
Several devices have This device prints kitchen tickets checked: leave it on only one.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- The print queue
- Hardware diagnostics
- Store network
- The printer does not print

pages.title: Register

sections.heading: Register
sections.text: Use the register every day (tablet or phone, iOS or Android): open the register, sell, take payments, refund, close.

pages.title: Count stock and report breakage

sections.heading: Count stock and report breakage
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
The register's Stock count screen is part of advanced stock, included in the Commerce plan: on the Free plan, it shows Included in Commerce. Breakage / loss stays available on every plan.

sections.heading: Count stock
sections.text:
Register menu › Stock count
As long as no stock count has been started, the register says so (1). A manager starts a Full count or a
Partial count in the back office.
Count
When a stock count is in progress, tap Count, scan each product or search for it, and type the counted quantity.
“…: … counted” confirms each entry; My counts: … product(s) sums them up. Several people can count at the same
time on several devices.

sections.heading: Report breakage or a loss
sections.text:
Register menu › Breakage / loss
Search for or scan the product, then enter the Lost quantity (1), the reason (2) — Breakage, Expiry,
Damaged or Other — and details if needed. Have a manager enter their PIN (3), then tap Remove (4).
Expected result: Loss recorded; the product's stock goes down and the loss shows up in the stock reports.
The register shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module. The register says “Subscribe from the back office to turn it on. Your data is kept.” The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription; the screen opens again after the next sync. See The register on the Free plan.
No stock count in progress: the manager starts it from the back office.
Ask a manager to start the stock count in the back office, then sync the register.
… is not part of this count
The stock count is partial and this product is not included.
Count closed: counting refused
A manager has closed the stock count: counts are no longer accepted.
Unreadable counted quantity
Type a number (use a comma for products sold by weight).
Loss refused
The manager PIN is missing or was refused.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Start and validate a stock count
- Track lots and expiry dates
- Approve with the manager PIN
- The Free plan

pages.title: The register menu (session, stock, hardware, account)

sections.heading: The register menu (session, stock, hardware, account)
sections.text:
The Register menu opens with the three-line icon at the top right of the sales screen. It is organized in four
parts.
Part · Entry · Tutorial
Session · Session sales · Reprint, Returns
Cash in / Cash out / X report · Cash movements
Settle tab · Tab
Close session no. … / Z reports · Close the register
Enter training mode · Training mode
Open drawer (with a drawer connected, manager PIN) · Hardware diagnostics
Stock · Supplier receipts, Transfers to receive, Alerts (managers) · Receiving, Transfers, Alerts
Stock count, Breakage / loss · Stock count and breakage
Hardware · Printer settings (with the print queue and the store network) · Printer
Hardware diagnostics · Diagnostics
Account · Tables (restaurant) · Tables or direct sale
Kiosk orders to pay · Kiosk orders
Switch user · PIN sign-in
Unpair this device · Unpair
The status badge at the top of the screen (Up to date, Sending…, Offline) opens the
Sync window.

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
Same menu, shown as a sliding sheet; scroll down to see Hardware and Account.
A menu entry is missing
Some entries depend on the role (Supplier receipts, Transfers and Alerts: managers), on the hardware (Open drawer) or
on the business type (Tables: restaurant with a floor plan). The “Developer” part only exists in test versions.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Make a sale
- Register

pages.title: Training mode (dummy tickets)

sections.heading: Training mode (dummy tickets)
sections.text:
In training mode, the register works normally but every sale is a training sale: no fiscal value, nothing in
revenue or in the Z reports.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Close the real session
Training mode can only be turned on with no open session: close the register first (see
Close the register).
Register menu › Enter training mode
A manager approves with their PIN (1).
Expected result: the TRAINING — dummy tickets banner (1) stays at the top of the screen. Tickets read
“Training sale no. … — no fiscal value”.
Know what training mode refuses
A training sale can never touch a real order or a real payment:
- Real order: a dining-room bill, a kiosk order “to pay at the register” or an order from any other channel cannot be
charged in training. When you tap Charge (1) on the bill, a red banner explains the refusal — “Training mode: this
order is real — exit training to take payment for it” — and no payment sheet opens. The order stays open, untouched.
To charge it, leave training mode first.
- External payment: no provider, QR or driven-terminal payment is offered. Still available: cash, keyed card,
meal voucher, tab and Other.
Leave training mode
Register menu › Leave training mode, manager PIN. You can then open a real session.
Close the register session before entering training mode
A real session is open: close it, then try again. The message appears as soon as you tap Enter training mode,
before any manager PIN is requested.
Leave training mode to open a real session
Training mode is still on: leave it before opening the register for real.
Training mode: this order is real — exit training to take payment for it
You tapped Charge on a real order (dining room, kiosk, other channel) while the register is in training mode. Nothing
was charged and the order stays open: leave training mode (Register menu › Leave training mode, manager PIN), then
charge it normally.
Training mode: no real payment — provider, QR or terminal payment unavailable
In training, only cash, keyed card, meal voucher, tab and “Other” are offered. For a provider, QR or terminal payment,
leave training mode.
Training mode refused: manager approval required.
Only a manager can turn training mode on or off.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Handle rejected sync events (if an older register sends a training charge on a real order, the server rejects it)
- Approve with the manager PIN
- The register menu

pages.title: Cash in / cash out and the X report

sections.heading: Cash in / cash out and the X report
sections.text:
Every cash movement outside a sale (bank deposit, purchase paid in cash, extra change brought in) must be recorded,
otherwise the register will look wrong at closing. The X report is an interim reading: it closes nothing.

sections.heading: Record a cash out (or a cash in)
sections.text:
Open the movement
Register menu › Cash out (or Cash in). Enter the Amount (€) (1), choose a Reason (required) (2) (Bank
deposit, Cash supplier purchase, Other cash out…), add a comment if needed (3), then Save (4).
Get the cash out approved
A cash out requires a manager's PIN (“Cash out — manager approval required”), unless the owner has set a
threshold for the store (manager PIN thresholds): with a €50 threshold, a
€20 cash out is recorded right away, without a PIN (1), and stays in the approvals log, marked “No PIN”:
A €200 cash out is above the threshold: the Manager PIN window opens (1), the manager types their PIN (2) then
Approve.
Expected result: “Cash out of … recorded — expected: …” (followed by “· no PIN (under the store threshold)” when
the PIN was not asked).

sections.heading: Read the X report
sections.text:
Register menu › X report
The X report no. … (1) covers the session: number of sales, revenue incl. VAT, discounts, **revenue by payment
method** (2), VAT by rate.
Check the cash
At the bottom: Opening float, each movement (1) with its reason and the manager who approved it, then the
Expected amount (3) — what the drawer should contain. Correct (2) cancels a mistake with an opposite movement
(the original movement stays visible). Print prints the X report on the register printer.
Choose a reason to record the movement.
The reason is required: tap one in the list.
Manager approval required for a cash out.
Have a manager enter their PIN.
Cash session closed — open a session before recording a movement.
Open the session first (see Open the register).
No open session — X report unavailable
The X report only covers the current session. Closed sessions can be viewed in Z reports.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Close the register and read the Z report
- Approve with the manager PIN
- Check register sessions and discrepancies
- Cash discrepancy at closing: what to do?

pages.title: Variants, products sold by weight, options and meal deals at the register

sections.heading: Variants, products sold by weight, options and meal deals at the register
sections.text:
Some products need a choice before they go into the cart. The register then opens a window; as long as a required
choice is missing, the add button stays grayed out.

sections.heading: Product options (doneness, side, extras)
sections.text:
Choose the options
Tap the product (here Burger du bistrot). Each group shows its rule (2): 1 required choice, **up to 3
choices**… Tap one option in each required group (1).
Add the extras and confirm
Paid extras show their price (“+1,00 €”) (1). The Add · … button (2) shows the total price of the line, extras
included: tap it.
Expected result: the ticket line lists the chosen options (“À point · Frites maison · Cheddar”), which are also sent
on the kitchen ticket.

sections.heading: Meal deal (starter, main, dessert)
sections.text:
Build the meal deal step by step
Tap the tile marked Meal deal (e.g. Formule midi). The screen shows the current step (1 / 3) (1) and
Choose your starter (2): tap a product (3). The meal deal moves on to the next step by itself; Back and
Next let you go back or skip an optional step.
Options and extras in the meal deal
A dish with options (e.g. Entrecôte grillée, “+ 4,00 €” extra) opens its choices inside the meal deal:
Saignant (1), Salade verte (2), then Confirm (3).
Add the meal deal
The Your meal deal box (1) sums up the choices. For several identical meal deals (two identical kids' menus), set
Quantity (2) with + / − before adding: the button price is multiplied accordingly. The Add meal deal · …
button (3) shows the price, extra included (here 19,90 € + 4,00 €). Same flow on a table's bill and on the kiosk.

sections.heading: Variants and products sold by weight (retail)
sections.text:
- Variant (size, flavor, format): the product carries the Variants badge; tap it, the Choose a variant
window opens, tap the right one. A variant that is out of stock or disabled does not appear.
- Product sold by weight: the Weight of … window opens; enter the weight in grams; the price is calculated
per kilo (“…/kg”). With a scale that prints labels, just scan the label: the weight and price are read from the code.

sections.heading: Fresh products: choose the lot
sections.text:
For a product with expiry tracking (yogurts, milk, meat…), the register knows its
lots and their use-by date, even offline.
Choose the lot
Tap the product: if it has at least two lots in stock, the Choose the lot window opens. The lot closest to its
use-by date comes first and is already ticked (1), marked Recommended; each lot shows its use-by date, the
quantity in stock and, when relevant, Expires in 3 days or Expired (2). Keep the suggested lot or tap another
one, then Add this lot (3). With a single lot, it is taken automatically, without a window.
Check or change the lot on the line
The cart line shows Lot … · Use by … (1). Tap it to change lot: the same window opens on the line's lot. Two
different lots of the same product make two lines.
Expected result: the chosen lot is saved with the sale. If you took a different lot from the suggested one, the
choice is written to the audit log (user, register, lot set aside). A return
puts the item back on the sale's lot.
Meal deal incomplete: choose your …
A required step of the meal deal has no choice. Go back to the step shown and tap a product.
This meal deal is no longer available
The meal deal was disabled or changed in the back office while you were building it. Close the window, sync the
register and start again.
This line belongs to a meal deal: act on the whole meal deal
You cannot discount, comp or remove a single dish from a meal deal: act on the meal deal line.
No variant available
All of the product's variants are inactive for this store. See your manager (back office, product page).
Scale product not listed (PLU …)
The scale label carries a PLU code that doesn't exist on any product page. The manager adds this PLU in the back
office.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Make a sale
- The kiosk: product page, options and meal deal
- Offer options: modifiers and extras
- Create a multi-step meal deal (menu)
- Products with variants

pages.title: Open the register with its opening float

sections.heading: Open the register with its opening float
sections.text:
As long as no session is open, the register shows No session — checkout locked: you can build a cart, but you
can't take payment. The session starts with the opening float (the cash in the drawer); it ends with closing and
the Z report.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Enter the opening float
At the first sign-in of the day, the Open the session window appears by itself. Otherwise, tap Open session in
the yellow banner at the top of the screen.
Enter the counted amount in Opening float (€) (1). Later (2) closes the window without opening the session.
Open the session
The register confirms the amount in full (“That is 150,00 €”) (1): check it, then tap Open session (2).
Expected result: the yellow banner disappears and the header shows “your name · Session #…”. You can take
payments.
No session — checkout locked
No session is open: tap Open session in the banner. If the session was closed, you need to open a new one (the
previous Z report stays in Z reports).
A session is already open on this register.
Nothing to do: yesterday's session wasn't closed, or a coworker has already opened it. If it dates from yesterday,
close it first (see Close the register), then open a new one.
No open cash session — open a session before charging.
You tapped Charge without a session: open one, the cart is kept.
The opening float is shown in a currency other than the store's
The register receives the store's currency as soon as it is paired: the opening float is shown in that currency, even
before the first catalog sync. If another currency appears (app or server not yet up to date, or a device paired
before this update with an empty catalog), tap Later, wait for the badge to show Up to date, then open the
session. If the currency is still wrong, check the store's currency (see
Manage your stores).

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Make a sale
- Cash in / cash out and the X report
- Close the register and read the Z report
- Check register sessions and discrepancies
- Read and download Z reports

pages.title: Get the cart back after the app stops

sections.heading: Get the cart back after the app stops
sections.text:
The register saves the cart in progress at every change (product added, quantity, discount, customer). If the app
stops in the middle of a sale — crash, force stop, tablet switched off — there is nothing to enter again: the cart
comes back when you reopen the app.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Reopen the app
Start the app again. If you were signed in when it stopped, the register goes straight back to the sale screen. If it
asks who you are, enter your PIN: the cart is only given back to the person who entered it.
Expected result: the ticket (2) gets its lines, discounts and customer back, and the **Session restored after
restart** banner (1) says what was recovered (“Cart in progress recovered: 4 items”). The cash session is still open:
no opening float to enter again.
Check the ticket, then take payment
Read the banner: it reports what changed while the app was stopped (“1 price updated”, “1 item removed from the
catalog”, “PIN-approved discounts to re-enter”). Fix what needs fixing, then take payment as usual.
Expected result: the banner goes away when you close it, or as soon as the cart is paid, put on hold or cleared.
The cart is empty after restart
The cart waits for its author: if a colleague signs in instead of you, they start from an empty cart and yours
comes back when you enter your PIN. A cart that was already paid, put on hold or cleared before the app stopped is
not restored. Carts that are never picked up are deleted when the session is closed.
A price changed or a line is missing
Intended: the cart is given back at the current prices, and a product removed from the catalog while the app was
stopped is not put back on the ticket. The banner says how many lines are affected.
The discount approved by a manager is gone
Intended: as with a ticket on hold, discounts that require the manager PIN are not kept. Apply the discount again.
Nothing is restored on the kiosk or on the waiter phone
Intended: on the kiosk, one customer's cart must never be shown to the next customer; it always starts again from the
welcome screen. On the waiter phone, the order is already saved on its table: reopen the table.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Make a sale
- Put a ticket on hold and recall it
- Sign in with your PIN

pages.title: Approve with the manager PIN

sections.heading: Approve with the manager PIN
sections.text:
Some actions need a supervisor's approval: discount above the threshold, return, void, cash out, training mode,
leaving kiosk mode, line comped or voided after being sent to the kitchen… The register then opens the Manager PIN
window. The cashier stays signed in; the approval is recorded in the manager's name (audit log).
The owner can waive the PIN for small cash outs, small returns, voiding a sent line and loss / breakage (manager PIN
thresholds): under the threshold, the register does not show this window (or
only asks for the Reason: “Under the threshold set by the store: no manager PIN, the action is still recorded in
the log.”) and the final message says so (“… · no PIN (under the store threshold)”).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Read what is being requested
The first line (1) shows the action to approve (“Discount above the threshold — manager approval required”). The
Reason is prefilled with the one chosen by the cashier.
The manager types their PIN
The manager types their PIN (4 to 6 digits) (2) and taps Approve (3). Cancel refuses: the action is not
carried out.
Expected result: the action is applied with the note “approved by …”.
Wrong PIN — 4 attempts left
The PIN typed is not that of a manager of the store. After several mistakes, the manager PIN is locked for a while.
Too many attempts: manager PIN locked until …
Wait until the time shown, or have another manager approve.
No manager with a PIN on this register — set a PIN in the back office (PIN & approvals) then sync
No manager has a PIN known to this register. Set one in the back office, then tap Sync now.
Last sync more than 72 h ago — manager PIN in degraded mode
The register has been offline for a long time: the PIN is checked against the local copy. Restore the Internet
connection as soon as possible.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Apply a discount
- Returns and voids
- Manager PIN and approvals
- View the audit log
- PIN refused or locked, manager degraded mode

pages.title: Approve an assistant proposal on the register

sections.heading: Approve an assistant proposal on the register
sections.text:
Your AI assistant reads your figures and can propose actions: a draft purchase order, a price change, the
handling of an anti-fraud alert a product's availability, the correction of a product's record its withdrawal from sale the creation of a product or its extension to all stores. Nothing is applied without a manager's approval. On the register and the **floor
phone, you read it and decide from Alerts**. Other devices (kitchen display, kiosk) do not have this screen.
It is the same screen for every kind and it is identical on iPhone, iPad, Android phone and tablet. The full tutorial
(states, limits, allowing the assistant) is the back office one:
Approve the assistant's proposals.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Assistant proposals
Open Alerts (see Read manager alerts), then tap the **Assistant
proposals** row, which shows the number of pending proposals. An “Assistant proposal to review” alert opens the
proposal concerned directly.
Each row gives the title built by Vendora, the key figure (“€5.90 → €9.05 (+53.4%)”), the originating assistant (“for”
the user it acts for), the state (Pending, Applied, Declined, Expired, Out of date, Replaced) and
the deadline. The list is sorted as in the back office: pending first, then what expires in under 6 hours, then high
risk, then the deadline.
- A high-risk proposal carries the High risk badge.
- When the list contains more than one family, a Family: All families filter appears (on iOS and Android alike);
pick a family to show only that one.
- A Back office badge marks a proposal that is decided in the back office only (see below).
Read the details
The details always follow the same order as in the back office: the header (title, state, deadline, family and scope,
risk, origin “Prepared by the assistant · for …”), the warnings (for example “Change of +53.4%: more than 30%.
Check the price before approving.”), what will be applied (or created), the Vendora figures, the text “Written by
the assistant · not checked by Vendora” (with Read all to expand it), the History, then the decision. Only the
“what will be applied” and “Vendora figures” zones say what will really be done.
On a phone, the lines of a purchase order appear as cards; on a tablet, as a table when every column fits in full, otherwise as cards (tablet in portrait, large text size, import of many products). The approve button and the
confirmation box are at the bottom of the details: scroll if needed.
Fill in the input and tick the confirmation
- Reason for an alert: the Reason (pre-filled by the assistant, editable) field is filled in by the assistant; read
it or edit it, your reason is the one recorded. It is required.
- Price change above 30%: tick “I confirm a change of +53.4%”. **The register asks for this box in addition to the
PIN**: the PIN does not prove you read the change. The button stays inactive until it is ticked.
- “This action cannot be undone.” appears before the button when the decision is final (handling an alert).
Approve with your PIN
Tap the approve button (“Approve and create the draft”, “Approve and apply the price”, “Approve: acknowledge the alert”;
on a phone, the short version with a padlock: “Create the draft”, “Apply the price”, “Acknowledge”). The register
always asks for the signed-in manager's PIN, owner and administrator included: “Approve the proposal · …'s PIN”.
Above the keypad, a summary written by Vendora, in the register's language, recalls what you are approving (for
example “Confiture de fraise: €5.90 → €9.05”). Enter your PIN (4 to 6 digits); the server checks it.
Expected result: the details switch to Applied with the success message: “Draft created: send it from the back
office”, “Price applied: registers will receive it at their next sync.”, “Alert acknowledged”. A draft is never sent
automatically: reviewing and sending it is done in the back office.
A wrong PIN shows “Incorrect PIN, 2 attempts left”; after too many attempts, “Too many attempts: PIN locked for one
minute.” (the same lock as the manager's other PINs).
Or decline, without a PIN
Tap Decline (Decline the proposal on a tablet). The Reason for declining sheet offers Not useful, **Wrong
figures, I'll do it myself and Other; details are optional, required for Other. Tap Confirm declining**.
Declining does not ask for a PIN (it has no effect), but remains reserved for the signed-in manager and is recorded in
their name.
Offline
Reading and approving need the network. Without a connection, the screen shows “Connection needed to view and approve”
and “Proposals received stay listed in Alerts.”; tap Try again once the network is back. If the network drops on an
already open detail, the text stays readable but the buttons are disabled (“No connection: read-only, approval will
resume with the network.”). Nothing is approved until the server has answered.

sections.heading: Purchase order
sections.text:
The lines (product, unit cost, quantity, total excl. tax, “partial total” if a cost is missing), the Vendora figures per
product and the note “Draft not sent: you will send it yourself, from the back office.”

sections.heading: Price change
sections.text:
“Selling price incl. tax” before → after in large type, the gap, “VAT unchanged (5.5%)” and “Sales already made keep
their price.” Only the price changes: never the VAT or the availability. For the price of one store, approve as
above.

sections.heading: The price for all stores: “Back office only”
sections.text:
The company price (“All stores (company price)”) is listed on the register of the store, with the Back office
badge, and you can read it in full (change, Vendora figures, assistant text). But it is not decided here: a
“Decided in the back office” card says “Open the back office to decide.” and no button is offered, not even
Decline. A manager (Manager, owner or administrator) decides it from
Approve the assistant's proposals.

sections.heading: An anti-fraud alert
sections.text:
The assistant can only propose handling an anti-fraud alert, never a fiscal integrity alert. The details show “Alert
to handle” (rule, summary, person concerned, “Raised on …”, Proposed decision), then the reason to approve and the
Acknowledge or Dismiss button. Result: “Alert acknowledged” or “Alert dismissed”.

sections.heading: A product's availability
sections.text:
The assistant proposes making one or more products unavailable (“no more apple tart tonight”), or putting them **back on
sale**. In the list, the title reads “Product availability · Tarte Tatin” and the strong value “Unavailable”; for a group,
“Make 3 products unavailable” and “On sale → Unavailable”. The details show On sale → Unavailable (a phone shows **one
card per product** with “Today” and “After”; a tablet, a table), then “This store's price and VAT are unchanged.”,
“Orders already taken are not changed.” and “Stays unavailable until a manager puts it back on sale.”
Approve with the manager's PIN. Tap Remove (or Put back for a return to sale; on a tablet, “Make 3 products
unavailable”). The register always asks for the signed-in manager's PIN; above the pad, the summary reads “Tarte Tatin:
unavailable at Le Petit Bistrot (demo)” (or “back on sale at …”). No extra box or input is required. **Nothing is removed
from sale before your approval.**
Expected result: the state becomes Applied with “Unavailable: registers receive it at their next sync” (plural,
“Unavailable: registers receive them…”; for a return to sale, “Back on sale: …”).
What this changes:
- Price and VAT do not change. The product stays unavailable until it is put back on sale: nothing puts it back on
sale by itself.
- The online menu follows right away; registers, floor phones and kiosks receive it at their next sync, then the
product leaves the sales list and the search.
- A line already in the cart is not removed: it stays sellable until the app is restarted. On restart it is removed
with the message “Session restored after restart · 1 item removed from the catalog”. Orders already taken are not changed.
Out of date. If a product changed since the proposal (already unavailable, archived, now a product with variants, price,
VAT or availability changed by hand), the state is Out of date and nothing is applied; for a group, the whole group
is out of date. A single box says what changed and concludes “Nothing was applied. Ask your assistant for a new
proposal.”; the block is titled What was proposed.
What the assistant declines (no proposal then reaches the register): a product already in the requested state, the
opposite request of a proposal already waiting for a manager, a product with variants or a variant (set in the back
office), an archived product, any price or VAT request through this action. Details:
Approve the assistant's proposals.

sections.heading: Correcting a record, withdrawing a product from sale
sections.text:
The assistant can also propose correcting a product's record (name, category, barcode, purchase cost, stock tracking, meal
vouchers) or withdrawing it from sale in all stores, or putting it back (actions subject to activation). These proposals
are decided in the back office: on the register they are listed and readable in full with the Back office badge,
with no button. What they cover, how they differ from a store's out-of-stock and what they refuse:
Approve the assistant's proposals.
The assistant can also propose creating a product (action subject to activation). This proposal is decided in the back office: on the register it is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge, with no button; the VAT rate, which you choose if the assistant names none, is set there. Details: Creating a product.
The assistant can also propose extending a product to all stores (action subject to activation). This proposal is decided in the back office, and only by an owner or an administrator: on the register it is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge, with no button. Details: Extending a product to all stores.
The assistant can also propose changing the price of several products at once (action subject to activation). A group for your store is decided here: read the table (“See the N lines”), tick the confirmation box (from two products), then enter the manager PIN. A group for the whole company is decided in the back office only: it is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge, with no button. Details: Changing several prices at once.
The assistant can also propose creating a category or editing it (renaming it, moving it, changing its order: action subject to activation). This proposal is decided in the back office: on the register it is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge, with no button. A category's order applies to the kiosk, the online menu and the back office, not to the buttons on the register. Details: Creating or editing a category.
The assistant can also propose creating a modifier group or editing one (extra price, options added, renamed or removed, number of choices, deactivation: action subject to activation). This proposal is decided in the back office: on the register it is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge, with no button. Sales and orders already entered keep their options and extra prices; a basket put on hold keeps its extra prices. Details: Creating or editing a modifier group.
The assistant can also propose attaching a modifier group to products or categories, or detaching it (action subject to activation). This proposal is decided in the back office: on the register it is listed and readable (targets, VAT rates) with the Back office badge and the sentence “Open the back office to decide.”, with no button. The confirmation box and its reasons exist in the back office only: the register never shows them. Sales and orders already entered keep their options; the change only applies to lines added afterwards. Details: Attaching or detaching a modifier group.

sections.heading: Correcting stock, recording a loss
sections.text:
The assistant can also propose correcting stock after a count or recording a loss (actions subject to activation).
These proposals are decided on a register of the store, as in the back office, always with your PIN:
- A loss: the Reason for the loss field already shows the reason suggested by the assistant (“pre-filled by the
assistant, editable”). Keep it or pick another. It is never “Theft”: if it is a theft, choose it yourself. With no
suggested reason, nothing is preselected and the button stays inactive.
- A large difference (at least 2 units and over 20% of theoretical stock): tick the “I confirm the large differences…”
box first, then enter the PIN. The order is the same as in the back office: reason, box, PIN.
- The waiter phone shows the proposal read-only, with no button, with the sentence “Approve it on a register or
in the back office, not on a floor phone.”
The stock movement is written in your name (the one the PIN belongs to). The table, the out-of-date cases and what the
assistant refuses are described in
Correcting stock after a count, recording a loss.

sections.heading: Receiving an order, transferring, initial stock, threshold
sections.text:
The assistant can also propose to receive a purchase order, transfer products to another store, **set a product's
initial stock or set its low-stock threshold (actions subject to activation). These proposals are decided on a
register of the store concerned, as in the back office, always with your PIN**:
- A receipt shows on the registers of the order's store. Costs are those of the order, as in the back office. First
tick the "goods actually received" box, then enter the PIN.
- An initial stock: first tick the "in stock" box, then enter the PIN.
- A transfer only shows on the registers of the source store; the PIN is enough. The transfer is created approved,
but shipping and receiving are still done by hand.
- A store threshold is approved with the PIN. A company-wide threshold can be read, with the sentence "Open the
back office to decide.", without any button.
- Starting a stock count is approved with the PIN; writing off an expired lot first needs the "lots removed
from sale" box, then the PIN.
- The floor phone shows these proposals read-only, without buttons.
Details and refusals: Assistant proposals.

sections.heading: Editing the sales screen
sections.text:
The assistant can also propose editing the sales screen of a store (action subject to activation). On the register and
the floor phone this proposal is read-only: it is listed and fully readable with the Back office badge and the
sentence “Open the back office to decide.”, with no button at all. A manager decides it in the back office (the
Apply to the sales screen button); a register of another store does not list it.
- Warnings (hidden button, screen shown nowhere) are at the top of the proposal.
- Operations read in order, as they will apply, one line per operation, with the verb first: Add a button,
Move a button, Remove a button, Set the size of a button. Each line takes the previous ones into account. All
64 operations at most are shown, with no “View the N lines”.
- After validation, the register receives the new screen at its next sync. It **stays on the page that is
open (if it still exists) and the cart is kept**: a sale in progress is not touched.
- If the screen's pages changed since the proposal, it is Out of date: nothing is applied (see below).
Details, operations and limits: Editing the sales screen.

sections.heading: States and special cases
sections.text:
- Expired: “Approval window has passed: nothing was applied.” Out of date: “The data changed since the proposal:
nothing was applied.” (Vendora says what changed when it knows). Replaced: “Replaced by a newer proposal”, with
View the new proposal. In all these cases, nothing is created.
- Already handled: “Already handled by … at …” (with the register concerned in parentheses): another manager decided
before you.
- “(access removed)” after the assistant's name: its access was removed since; the proposal can still be decided.
- “The assistant can no longer propose “Catalog” actions; this proposal can still be decided.”: the family was
removed since; you can still decide.
- “This proposal is shown in full in the back office.”: this version of the app cannot show this kind of proposal in
full. The title, summary and scope stay visible, with “Open the back office to decide.” and no button. Update the app,
or decide in the back office.
The data changed since the proposal: nothing was applied.
A product, a supplier or an alert changed since the proposal. Nothing was created. Ask your assistant for a new proposal.
Approval window has passed: nothing was applied.
The proposal was more than 72 hours old. Nothing was created; ask your assistant for a new one.
Replaced by a newer proposal
The assistant prepared a newer proposal for the same thing: tap View the new proposal.
Already handled by … at …
Another manager decided before you. Nothing more is done.
You don't have the role to approve this proposal.
Only a manager of the store can decide. Sign in with a Manager, administrator or owner account.
No connection: nothing was approved. Try again.
Check the store network (see Store network: local hub and main register), then approve again.
The approve button stays inactive
The reason of an alert is empty, or the “I confirm a change of …” box (price above 30%) is not ticked. Scroll to the box:
it is above the button.
No button, only “Decided in the back office”
It is a proposal decided in the back office only (price for all stores), or a kind that this version cannot show. Decide
from the back office.
The Assistant proposals entry does not appear in Alerts
You are signed in with a Cashier account, or the device is a kitchen display or a kiosk: only managers, on the register
and the floor phone, have access to it.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Approve the assistant's proposals (back office)
- Read manager alerts
- Approve with the manager PIN

pages.title: Receive a supplier delivery on the register

sections.heading: Receive a supplier delivery on the register
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Supplier receipts require the Suppliers and purchasing module, and entering batches and expiry dates requires advanced stock, both included in the Commerce plan. On the Free plan, the register shows Included in Commerce instead.
The delivery driver is here: instead of going to the office, check the delivery right on the register by scanning the
products.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Register menu › Supplier receipts
The entry appears in the Stock part of the menu for managers. The list shows orders that are Sent or **Partly
received**, with the number of expected lines. Tap the order for this delivery.
Scan or count
For each line: “Ordered … · already received … · expected …”. Scan each product (the quantity goes up) or enter the
Received quantity. All received fills every line with the expected quantity. A product over-delivered by more
than 20 % asks for confirmation (Overage above 20 %).
Fresh products: enter the lot and the use-by date
For a product tracked for expiry (yoghurts, milk, meat… — see Expiry), as
soon as a quantity is received the line shows “Expiry-tracked product: lot number and use-by date are required”.
Enter the Lot No. printed on the packaging (1), then tap Choose the use-by date and pick the date in the
calendar (2): the button then shows the date. The calendar uses the language of the app (French, English or Arabic),
whatever the language of the device.
Does the delivery mix several lots of the same product? Tap Add a lot (4): each lot has its number, its use-by
date and its Lot quantity (3). The total “Lots: … of … received” (5) must reach the received quantity; it stays
red otherwise. The bin removes a lot. With a single lot there is nothing else to enter: it takes the whole received
quantity.
A line that was not delivered (received quantity 0) asks for no lot.
Validate the reception
Tap Validate the reception. Expected result: “Reception of … recorded: stock updated”, with the number of gaps
reported and “remainder expected” or “order complete”.
The lots you entered can be used right away on this register, even offline: at the sale, the
Choose the lot window offers them, the closest use-by
date first. The other registers and the Expiry page of the back office receive them at the next synchronisation.
The register shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module. The register says “Subscribe from the back office to turn it on. Your data is kept.” The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription; the screen opens again after the next sync. See The register on the Free plan.
No delivery expected: orders sent to the supplier appear here.
No order has the “Sent” status: first send the purchase order from the back office.
Product not in this order: set it aside or do a direct reception in the back office
The scanned product is not on this order. Set it aside; receiving without an order is done in the back office.
Nothing to receive: scan or enter the received quantities
No quantity has been entered: scan the products or use All received.
Lot number and use-by date are required for “…” (product tracked for expiry)
This product has a received quantity but one of its lots has no number or no use-by date. Fill in Lot No. and
Choose the use-by date for each lot, or remove the extra lot with the bin. If the product was not delivered, set
its Received quantity back to 0.
The lot quantities of “…” do not add up to the received quantity
With several lots, the sum of the Lot quantity fields must equal the Received quantity of the line (total
“Lots: … of … received” in red). Correct the quantity of a lot, or the received quantity.
This order no longer expects a reception
The order has already been completed (on another register or in the back office).

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Receive a stock transfer
- Manage your suppliers and their prices
- Place a purchase order and receive it
- The Free plan

pages.title: Receive a stock transfer

sections.heading: Receive a stock transfer
sections.text: When another store sends you goods, the transfer waits to be received on your register.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Register menu › Transfers to receive
The entry appears in the Stock part of the menu for managers. Tap the transfer (number, origin store).
Count the items
“From … · scan each item or count with +/−; any discrepancy needs a reason and the manager PIN”. Scan or adjust with
+ / −. For a difference from the shipped quantity, choose the Reason for the discrepancy (required) (Damaged
on delivery…).
Confirm
If there are discrepancies, have a manager enter their PIN in Manager PIN (… discrepancies), then tap Confirm receipt. Expected result: the transfer
moves to “Received” and the store's stock goes up by the counted quantities.
Reason for the discrepancy (required)
The counted quantity differs from the shipped quantity: choose a reason.
The transfer doesn't appear
It hasn't been shipped by the origin store yet, or the register isn't synced (Sync now).

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Receive a supplier delivery
- Transfer stock between stores

pages.title: Sell on a tab and collect a tab payment

sections.heading: Sell on a tab and collect a tab payment
sections.text: The tab is a trusted customer's account: they pay later, up to a limit set in the back office.

sections.heading: Put a sale on the tab
sections.text:
1. Attach the customer to the sale (Customer (phone, card), see Attach a customer).
2. Tap Charge, then choose the Tab method (“Put on tab …”). The customer banner shows “Tab of … / limit …”.

sections.heading: Collect a payment
sections.text:
Attach the customer first
The payment is made for the customer in the cart: attach them, then open Register menu › Settle tab. Without a
customer, the register shows the message (1).
Enter the amount and the method
The Tab payment — … window shows the amount still owed. Enter the amount paid and the method (cash, card), then
confirm.
Expected result: “Tab payment of … collected — still owed …”. The payment is not revenue (the sale was counted
on the day it happened); it appears separately in the X and Z reports (“Tab settlements”).
Attach the customer first (Customer banner of the cart)
Attach the customer to the cart, then reopen Settle tab.
… has nothing to settle on the tab
The customer owes nothing: check that it's the right customer.
Limit exceeded: tab after sale … / …
The sale would push the tab over the limit. A manager can unlock it with their PIN, or the customer pays part of it
another way.
No tab allowed for this customer (limit 0)
The customer has no tab limit: this is set in the back office (customer profile).
Tab not available on a table bill
A table bill can't be put on a tab from the floor phone: charge it at the register.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Attach a customer to the sale
- Manage tabs (customer credit)

pages.title: Store network: local hub and main register

sections.heading: Store network: local hub and main register
sections.text:
Devices in the same store find each other on the Wi-Fi by themselves and form the store network: one of them
becomes the hub, the others connect to it. This is what shows “Live in store” in the status badges and lets
tickets reach the kitchen instantly, even if the Internet is down.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Register menu › Printer settings › Store network
The status (1) shows the device's role: “This device is the hub (port …) · … connected”, “Live in store · hub …” or
“Looking for other devices…”.
Choose the main register
Turn on Main register (2) on one register only: it takes priority for relaying sends and kitchen statuses. Tap
Apply.
If automatic discovery fails
Some Wi-Fi networks (guest, corporate) block discovery. In that case, enter the Hub address (3) in the format
“192.168.1.20:4242” (the address and port shown on the hub device), then Apply.
Expected result: “Live in store · hub …” on all devices.
Expected format: 192.168.1.20:4242
The hub address must contain the IP address and the port, separated by a colon.
Store network off
The device isn't on any local Wi-Fi, or the network blocks traffic between devices. Check the Wi-Fi; otherwise enter
the hub address. Without the store network, everything goes through the Internet (a little slower).

sections.text:
- Sync: status, sync now
- Kitchen display settings
- Set up floor phones (zones, checkout)
