pages.title: Void a ticket, process a return with or without a receipt

sections.heading: Void a ticket, process a return with or without a receipt
sections.text:
A charged sale is never erased: you void it (the whole ticket, during the session) or you process a return
(some of the items). In both cases, a “RETURN” or “VOIDED” ticket is issued and a manager approves with their PIN.

sections.heading: Find the ticket
sections.text:
Open the session sales
Register menu › Session sales. For each ticket: Void ticket … (1), Refund on ticket … (2). At the top,
Return without receipt (3) when the customer no longer has their receipt.

sections.heading: Process a return
sections.text:
Choose the items and the refund
In Return, increase the returned quantity of the items concerned with + (1) (“1 returnable”), choose the
Reason (2), then the Refund (3): Original methods (the way the customer paid), Cash or Card. **To
refund** shows the total. For a broken product, the “Broken product — not put back in stock” switch keeps it out of
stock. A fresh product tracked by lot goes back to the sale's lot (see choose the lot).
Tap Refund (4).
Return a whole meal deal in one gesture
A meal deal that was sold shows as a single line (1), with the Meal deal badge, the number of meal deals still
returnable and the price paid for one; its items are listed below (2). The + stepper (3) returns a whole meal
deal: all of its items, at the price actually paid (extras included), with a single reason. To refund (4) shows
that exact amount. If only one item is damaged, its “Broken product” switch writes off that item alone. The return
receipt prints the meal deal and its items, like the sales receipt. A meal deal is never partly returned: for a single
dish, refund the whole meal deal or offer a goodwill gesture.
The manager approves
Return / refund — manager approval required (1): the manager types their PIN (2), then Approve.
Expected result: “Return … recorded — give back … in cash (approved by …)” (1). Hand back the amount shown. For a
card refund, do it on the card terminal (“refund … on the card terminal”).

sections.heading: Void a whole ticket
sections.text:
Void ticket … in the session sales, reason, manager PIN: “Ticket … voided — … (approved by …)”. The ticket stays
visible, marked VOIDED; it counts in “Voids” on the Z report.
The void is itself sealed and signed by the register: it takes the next fiscal number, without changing the X or Z
totals. The printed void ticket carries one more line under the original fiscal number: “No fiscal annulation : N”
(the void ticket is printed in French, whatever the register's language). It is the fiscal number of the void; the original sale's
number is unchanged.
A sale that has already been refunded, even in part, can no longer be voided: the register shows “Ticket already
partly refunded: return the rest instead”. Process a return on the remaining items instead.

sections.heading: Return without receipt
sections.text:
Return without receipt: search for the products, quantities, reason. Without the original receipt, the refund is
made in cash, or as store credit if a customer is identified, at the catalog price at most.
Refund refused: manager approval required.
The manager PIN wasn't entered or was refused. Try again with a manager present.
Ticket already partly refunded: return the rest instead
You tapped Void ticket … on a sale of which part has already been refunded: voiding it would refund twice. Use
Return on ticket … for the remaining items.
Ticket …: everything has already been returned
All the items on this ticket have already been refunded.
Ticket details unavailable — return not possible from this register
The ticket comes from another register or from an old session whose details this register doesn't have. Process a
Return without receipt, or do the return from the original register.
Returns without a receipt are disabled for this store (sales policy)
The store has disabled them in the back office (Checkout and payments section).
A meal deal is returned as a whole: all of its items, in the same number
The return only took part of a meal deal. Use the stepper on the meal deal line: it returns all of its items together.
Choose at least one line to return
Increase the returned quantity of at least one item before tapping Refund.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Approve with the manager PIN
- Close the register and read the Z report
- Manager PIN and approvals (returns, voids)
- Check register sessions and discrepancies

pages.title: Scan with the camera (burst, manual entry, torch)

sections.heading: Scan with the camera (burst, manual entry, torch)
sections.text:
A handheld scanner (USB or Bluetooth reader) scans straight into Search or scan: nothing to tap. Without a
scanner, the device's camera does the same job.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open the scanner
On the sales screen, tap the Scan with camera icon to the right of the search field. The Scan a code window
opens. The first time, the device asks for camera access: tap Allow the camera, then accept the system prompt. The
camera is only used to read barcodes: no photo is saved.
Aim at the barcode
Hold the barcode inside the frame: a beep sounds and the product is added to the cart. In a dark place, tap
Torch.
- Burst mode (chained scans) (1): the window stays open, scan items one after another. When it is off, the window
closes after each code.
- Manual code entry (2): if the code is damaged, type the digits printed under the bars, then Add (3).
Expected result: the product appears in the ticket with its quantity.

sections.heading: Scanning while a window is open
sections.text:
On the sales screen, the handheld scanner does not work everywhere while a window is open: the top window decides
whether it expects a code.
- These windows accept the code: Declare a loss (the scanned product is picked), the choice of the **sale's
customer** (loyalty card or QR, except when creating a customer record), attaching a customer to a past sale, the
return without a receipt (the code goes into the "name or barcode" search: nothing is added until you tap the
product), the camera scanner, and also inventory, transfers to receive and supplier receiving. On
these last three screens, pick an item in the list first; otherwise the screen answers "Select an item in the list
first to scan".
- Every other window refuses the scan, as does the payment in progress (payment sheet on a phone, payment
column on a tablet) and the Sale recorded screen. The device plays an error beep and shows "Close this window
to scan" for 4 seconds. The cart does not change and no digit of the code lands in a field of the window.
With no window open, nothing changes: the code is added to the cart as usual. On the floor plan, a scanned code is
ignored.
Unknown code …
No product carries this barcode. Search for the product by name; the manager adds the barcode to the product page in
the back office.
Close this window to scan
A window that does not expect a code is open (discount, payment, cash movement…). The scan is refused on purpose, with
an error beep: nothing is added to the cart. Finish or close the window, then scan again. You can still type in the
window with the keyboard: only scanning is refused.
Camera unavailable
Camera access was denied or the device has no usable camera. On iPad / iPhone: Settings › POS › Camera. On Android:
tap Try again or allow the camera in the Android settings. Manual code entry remains available.
Camera denied
You denied camera access. Without this permission, camera scanning is unavailable; the handheld scanner and search
still work.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Make a sale
- Hardware diagnostics (scanner, drawer, beep)
- Barcodes: enter, scan, generate internal codes
- Print price labels

pages.title: Sync: status, sync now, rejected events

sections.heading: Sync: status, sync now, rejected events
sections.text:
Vendora works offline: the device sells, takes payments and sends to the kitchen even without Internet, then
sends everything to the server as soon as the connection comes back. The badge at the top right of the screen
sums up the status:
Badge · Meaning
Up to date · Everything has been sent, catalog up to date.
Sending… · Sending in progress.
… pending · Sales or operations are waiting to be sent.
Offline / Offline · … · No connection; whatever is pending will go out when the network is back.
… rejected · The server refused an operation: have your manager check it.
Attention · Wrong device time or sync behind: a banner says what to do (see A register no longer syncs). Sales continue.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Tap the badge
The Sync window shows the last sync (1) (“Synced at … · Live in store”) and the number of events to send.
Sync now
Tap Sync now (2) after a change in the back office (new product, price, PIN, floor plan) to receive it right away,
without waiting for the automatic sync.
Expected result: the badge goes back to Up to date.

sections.heading: Rejected events
sections.text:
When the badge shows “… rejected”, tap View rejected events: each line shows the operation and the reason it was
refused (session already closed, product deleted…). Nothing is lost: the manager handles them in the back office
(Handle rejected sync events; see also
A register no longer syncs).
Offline — last sync …
The device has no connection. Keep selling; check the Wi-Fi. If it lasts, test the connection in
Hardware diagnostics.
Last sync more than 72 h ago — only managers can sign in
After three days without a sync, only managers can sign in (degraded mode). Restore the connection, then tap **Sync
now**.
Never synced
The device has just been paired and hasn't received the catalog yet: wait a few seconds or tap Sync now.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Account and connection banners
- Store network
- A register no longer syncs
- “Update required” on the device

pages.title: Restaurant on the register: tables or direct sale

sections.heading: Restaurant on the register: tables or direct sale
sections.text:
In a restaurant, the register has two home screens, brought together by the Tables | Direct sale switch at the top
of the screen (1).
- Tables: the floor plan, zone by zone (Salle, Terrasse… with the number of tables) (2). Tap a table (3) to
open it or see its bill. The rest works the same as on the floor phone: see
Take the order.
- Direct sale: the classic sales screen, for the counter and takeout.
The legend at the bottom of the plan shows the statuses: Free, Occupied, Bill requested.

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
On an Android tablet, the plan and the table's bill are shown side by side.
No tables: the floor plan is set up in the back office (Floor plan).
No floor plan has been published for this store: create it in the back office (Draw your floor plan),
publish it, then sync the register.
The Tables switch doesn't appear
The store's Tables module is inactive, or the floor plan has no table. The module is active by default for a
restaurant; for another profile (a grocery store with a terrace…), the owner ticks it in the back office under
Stores › Modules, then the register receives it at its next sync.
The Tables switch disappeared during service
The Tables module has just been turned off in the back office: the register goes back to direct sale. As long as a
table bill is still open, the switch stays visible so you can settle it; it disappears once every bill is paid.
Nothing is lost: the floor plan and the bills come back if the module is turned on again.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Read the floor plan
- Plan and bill side by side on a tablet
- Draw your floor plan (zones, tables)

pages.title: Send the receipt by email, WhatsApp or SMS; reprint a ticket

sections.heading: Digital receipt
sections.text:
When a customer is attached to the sale (see Attach a customer) and has
agreed to receive their receipts, the Sale recorded screen offers one button per allowed channel. These buttons are:
- Envoyer le reçu à … (“Send the receipt to …”, by email);
- Reçu par WhatsApp au … (“Receipt by WhatsApp to …”);
- Reçu par SMS au … (“Receipt by SMS to …”; the number is masked on screen).
Tap the right button: the register confirms “Receipt requested: …”. Without a customer, or without consent, no button
appears: this is normal. The customer's consents are set in their profile in the back office (Create and find your customers).

sections.heading: Reprint a ticket from the session
sections.text:
Open the session sales
Register menu › Session sales lists the tickets of the current session, from newest to oldest, with their lines
and payments.
Tap the ticket's printer icon
Tap the printer icon (1): a duplicate is sent to print (“Duplicate of ticket … sent to print.”). From the same
list, Attach a customer to ticket (2) adds a forgotten customer afterwards (manager PIN). **Return without
receipt** (3) is explained in Returns and voids.
Printing failed (…) — reprint from the history
The printer didn't respond; the ticket stays in the Print queue. Fix the printer, then send it again (see
The print queue).
Reprint refused: manager approval required.
The store requires a manager PIN for duplicates: have a manager approve it.
No button to send the receipt after the sale
No customer is attached, or their profile has no email / phone number or no consent. Attach the customer before
charging, or complete their profile in the back office.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Attach a customer to the sale
- Connect and set up the printer
- Create and find your customers
- The printer doesn't print

pages.title: Put a ticket on hold and recall it

sections.heading: Put a ticket on hold and recall it
sections.text:
Customer went back for an item? Put their cart on hold: the register is free for the next customer, and the
ticket comes back in one tap.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Put the cart on hold
Tap Hold below the ticket. The Put on hold window suggests a label (“Customer 1”): replace it with a name that
means something to you (1), then tap Confirm (2).
Expected result: ““Table terrasse” put on hold”, the ticket is empty and the Held tickets (1) button (1)
appears at the top of the ticket.
Recall the ticket
Tap Held tickets (…), then the ticket you want (1) (time it was put on hold and number of items). If a cart is in
progress, it is put on hold in turn.
Expected result: the lines come back into the ticket; you can charge.
… held tickets at most: recall one first
The number of held tickets is limited: recall and charge (or clear) a ticket before setting another one aside.
The discount approved by a manager disappeared when the ticket was recalled
By design: discounts that require a manager PIN are not kept in a held ticket. Apply the discount again.
A held ticket has disappeared
Tickets that are not recalled are deleted when the session is closed, and they are only visible on the register
where they were set aside.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Make a sale
- Apply a discount

pages.title: Take a meal voucher, a tip, a provider payment

sections.heading: Meal voucher
sections.text:
Only eligible products can be paid with a meal voucher (MV badge on the ticket line), up to the daily cap
set by the store. No change is ever given on a meal voucher.
On a bill split into Equal shares, each share can be paid with a meal voucher up to its portion of the eligible
items (e.g. a 30,00 € bill, of which 30,00 € is eligible, in 4 shares: Eligible 7,50 € per share).
In the dining room, the same MV badge marks the dishes payable by meal voucher on the lines of a table's bill
(1) — waiter phone, tablet, register in Tables mode — as soon as they are added: you know in advance what the
guest can pay by voucher. It only appears when the store accepts meal vouchers, never on a meal deal nor on a voided,
comped or already paid line. VoiceOver and TalkBack read it as “Meal voucher eligible”.
Tap Meal voucher
In the payment sheet, tap Meal voucher (1). The help line (2) sums up: Eligible (total of the items payable by
voucher), cap, allowed (the smaller of the two). Enter the voucher's value, then tap Add … (3).
Pay the rest with another method
The voucher appears in Payments added (1); the trash icon (2) removes it. Pay the rest in cash or by card, then tap
Charge … (3).
Find the vouchers in the Z report
When the session is closed, the Z report (like the X report) breaks revenue down by method: the Meal voucher
line (1) totals the vouchers taken during the session, register sales and table bills included. It is not part of
the drawer's expected cash. The amount to send to the redemption centre is tracked in the back office
(Meal vouchers: tracking and remittance slips).

sections.heading: Tip
sections.text:
Below the payment methods, Tip (optional, not revenue) opens the tip entry (cash or card). It is **outside revenue
and VAT**: the amount due and the change don't change.
Choose the Beneficiary (1): For Camille (caisse) (you) — the signed-in seller, selected by default at the counter —,
For Lucas (salle) (table server) — the server who opened the bill, selected by default on a bill —, another store
member (For Inès (salle)…), or the service's Shared pool. The list shows the active members with a register PIN:
it is available offline. A deactivated member leaves the list at the next sync.
After checkout, Session sales shows the line “Tip €2.00 · Lucas (salle)” (or “· Shared pool”) under the sale.
Tips appear separately in the X and Z reports, broken down by beneficiary.

sections.heading: Provider payment (QR, connected terminal)
sections.text:
If the store has set up a payment provider, the sheet offers its methods: the customer scans a Payment QR code
shown by the register (“The customer scans the QR code with …”), or the amount goes straight to the connected terminal.
Cancel provider payment drops the current request. Connectors are set up in the back office:
Connect a payment connector.
Meal vouchers are not accepted in this store
The option isn't turned on in the back office (the store's sales policy). Without it, the Meal voucher tile doesn't
appear.
No item on this ticket is eligible for meal vouchers
No product on the ticket is marked “meal voucher” on its product page (alcoholic drinks, for example). The manager
checks the option on the product page.
Maximum … in meal vouchers
The amount exceeds what is allowed (eligible items or cap). Pay the difference with another method.
No change is given on meal vouchers
The voucher is worth more than what remains to be paid in eligible items: the register doesn't give change on it.
Unreadable tip — digits and comma only
Type the tip using digits and a comma (e.g. 2,50).

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Take payment: cash, card, several methods
- Close the register and read the Z report
- Meal vouchers: tracking and deposit slips
- Track and distribute tips
- Track provider payments and reconcile them

pages.title: Accept an invitation

sections.heading: Accept an invitation
sections.text:
Your manager has invited you to Vendora. The email “Invitation à rejoindre le back-office” (invitation to join the
back office; the subject is in French) says who is inviting you and with which role, and contains a link
valid for 72 hours that can be used only once.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open the link in the email
Click the link in the email (or copy it into your browser). The Welcome page opens. You can
change the language (Français, English, العربية) at the top right.
No email? Look in your spam folder, then ask your manager to
Resend invitation (Settings › Team).
Choose your password and your PIN
- Password (at least 8 characters) (1) and Confirmation (2): both must be identical.
- Register PIN (optional, 4 to 6 digits) (3): to sign in on the store's registers, even
offline. Leave it empty if you do not use the registers; you can set it later in
Control › PIN & approvals.
The Activate my account button (4) stays grayed out as long as the password is too short, the two entries
differ or the PIN does not have 4 to 6 digits:
Activate your account
Everything is in order: the Activate my account button (1) turns green. Click it.
Expected result: you land directly on the back office Dashboard, already signed in. Next
time, sign in with your email and this password (Sign in).
You see the pages your role allows (a manager does not see Subscription or API keys, for example).
Your PIN reaches the registers at their next sync (less than a minute).
This link has expired (72 h). Ask your manager to resend the invitation.
More than 72 hours have passed. Your manager clicks Resend invitation in Settings › Team:
you receive a new link.
Unknown link: it may have been replaced by a newer resend.
You opened an old email: the invitation has been resent since. Use the link from the latest email received.
Also check that the link was not cut off when you copied it.
Invitation already accepted
Your account is already activated: sign in with your email. Forgotten
password: use Forgot password?.
Password: 8 characters minimum
Choose a password with at least 8 characters.
PIN must be 4 to 6 digits
The PIN contains only digits, 4 to 6 of them. Or leave the field empty.
PIN already used in this store, choose another one
A colleague already has this PIN. Choose another one, or leave it empty and set it later.
Unable to activate.
The server did not respond (connection lost). Check your connection and try again; the link remains valid.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Sign in to the back office, forgotten password
- Find your way around the back office
- Build your team: roles, invitations, PIN

pages.title: Pair a register or a phone (code, QR)

sections.heading: Pair a register or a phone (code, QR)
sections.text:
Pairing means linking a device to your store, once and for all. In the back office, you choose what the
device will be (register, floor phone, kitchen display, kiosk) and its name; the back office shows a
QR code valid for 15 minutes; on the device, the Vendora app scans it, and the device is named and set up automatically.
Add a register in 20 seconds: type, name, QR code, device paired.
Email address to confirm
Until the owner's email address is confirmed, adding a device (code or kit) is refused: see Confirm your email address. A register that is already paired is not affected.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Settings › Devices › Add a device
In the menu, open Settings › Devices, choose the store if you have several, then click
Add a device (1). Installing several devices at once? Use
Prepare an installation kit (2) instead, see below.
Shortcut: the Add a device button on the dashboard (Live card).
Choose the device type
The wizard has three steps (1): Type, Settings, Pairing. Choose the type (2), then Continue (3):
Type · What it is for
Main register · The counter register: also takes payment for bills settled at the table. Reserved for the owner; replaces the current main register.
Register · An additional register: sales, tickets, drawer and Z.
Floor phone · Order taking at the table by waiters.
Kitchen display · The tickets of one or more prep stations.
Kiosk · Self-service ordering by customers.
The type sets what the device will show: the app has nothing to choose. Only a kitchen display and a floor phone
can change role later; a register or a kiosk is replaced (Manage your devices).
Set the name and the server address
- Device name (1): shown in the back office and on the device, which will not need to enter it. Empty: a name is
suggested (“Register 2”…).
- Depending on the type: Main register and Prints the tickets of the other devices for a register;
Stations displayed for a kitchen display; Zones served for a floor phone; Kiosk preset for a kiosk.
- Server address (in the QR code) (2): the address at which the device will reach Vendora. It is
deduced from the page; if you see “Local address: a real device will not reach it”, replace it with
the address given by Vendora or your installer (e.g. http://192.168.1.20:8080 on the store network).
Click Generate the code (3).
Scan the QR code with the device
The back office shows the QR code (1), the same code in plain text (2) — 6 characters, e.g. LDY-8QR — and
“Waiting for the device…” (3). The code expires after 15 minutes and can only be used once.
On the device, open the Vendora app. The Pair this device screen appears:
1. Tap Scan the QR code and aim at the QR in the back office (allow the camera if the app asks).
The app fills in the address and the code and pairs on its own.
2. Without a camera: tap Custom server, enter the
Server URL, then the Pairing code (6 characters) (with or without the hyphen) and tap Pair. The
Device name field can stay empty: the name chosen in the back office is used.
Scan the QR from the Vendora app
The phone's camera app is no use here: the QR does not open the app, it can only be read from the
Pair this device screen.
Check that the device is paired
As soon as the device has used the code, the wizard shows ““…” is paired” (1) and the list of settings
applied. The app shows ““…” is paired.” then its home screen (PIN sign-in for a register).
Expected result: the device appears in Settings › Devices, in its type's group, with the
Online status as soon as it has contacted the server. On the dashboard, the Pair your devices step of
“Getting started” progresses.

sections.heading: Install several devices at once: the installation kit
sections.text:
For an opening or an installer on site, the kit prepares in one go a preconfigured code per device,
valid for 7 days, on a sheet to print.
1. In Settings › Devices, click Prepare an installation kit, then New kit.
2. Add the planned devices with the buttons + Main register, + Register, + Floor phone,
+ Kitchen display, + Kiosk (1). For each line (2): Label on the sheet, Device name,
Quantity and the type's settings. Check the Server address (in the QR code).
3. The summary (3) shows the free slots in your plan. Click Prepare the kit.
If the kit plans more devices than your plan allows, a red banner (2) says so and
Prepare the kit stays grayed out:
4. The kit tracking shows the Paired devices progress (1). Click Print the sheet (2): an A4
page with, for each device, its QR, its name, its plain-text code and the instructions (you can also
save it as a PDF from the print window).
5. On site, for each device: Vendora app › Scan the QR code › aim at its QR on the sheet.
6. A lost sheet or a kit you no longer need: Revoke the kit (3) — unused codes are refused, devices
already paired stay active.
Confidential sheet
As long as its codes are valid, the sheet lets anyone pair a device to your store: destroy it once the
installation is finished, or revoke the kit.
Invalid pairing code — check what you typed.
(On the device.) The code typed matches no code: typo (the code uses neither O, 0, I,
nor 1). Type it again, or scan the QR.
Code expired or already used — generate a new one in the back office.
(On the device.) The code is more than 15 minutes old (7 days for a kit), has already been used, belongs to a revoked
kit, or the store has been archived. In the back office, click New code (the configuration is kept) or prepare a
new kit.
Code expired: generate a new one (the configuration is kept).
(In the back office.) The 15 minutes passed before the device scanned the QR. Click New code.
Server unreachable — check the URL and the network connection.
The device cannot reach the address in the QR code: it is not on the right network (guest Wi-Fi…), or the address is
your computer's (localhost) instead of the server's. Generate the code again with the right
Server address (in the QR code).
Invalid server URL — it must start with http:// or https://.
(Manual entry on the device.) Type the full address, e.g. http://192.168.1.20:8080. In the back office, the
same check shows “Invalid address: http(s)://hôte[:port]”.
The pairing code has 6 characters.
The code entered is incomplete or too long. The hyphen is optional.
QR code not recognized — scan the pairing QR shown in the back office.
The QR you aimed at is not a Vendora pairing QR (a receipt or menu QR…). Aim at the one in the wizard or on the kit sheet.
This code has no name chosen in the back office: give this device a name.
Enter a name in Device name on the pairing screen, then Pair.
Too many attempts — try again in a few minutes.
Too many wrong codes in a row. Wait a few minutes, then scan the QR rather than typing the code.
Restaurant plan limit reached: 6 sales device(s) (kiosks excluded). Upgrade to a higher plan or add an extra device (Subscription page).
(In the back office, when clicking Generate the code.) Your plan already has the maximum number of sales
devices (the plan name and the number vary; the back office workstation does not count). Revoke a device you no longer
use (Manage your devices) or contact Vendora. On the device, this case may
show as “Server error (HTTP_409) — try again.”. For a kit: “The kit exceeds the plan by … device(s): …”.
Account suspended or canceled: no new device can be paired. Contact Vendora.
The subscription is suspended: devices already paired keep selling, but no new one can be
added. See Manage your Vendora subscription and invoices. On the device: “Server error (HTTP_423) — try again.”.
This store is archived: put it back into service (Stores page) before pairing a device to it.
Put the store back into service in Settings › Stores, or choose another store.
Only the store owner designates the main register
Only the owner can add a
Main register. A manager adds a Register; the owner will designate it later from its detail sheet.
Pairing not saved: the device's secure storage is unavailable. Generate a new code in the back office and try again.
The device could not keep its access key (secure storage locked or full). Restart the device, generate a new code and start again.
The camera does not open on the device (“Camera denied”, “Camera unavailable”)
The app is not allowed to use the camera. On Android: Try again then Allow the camera; on
iPad / iPhone: Settings › POS › Camera. Otherwise, use manual entry of the address and the code.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Confirm your email address
- Choose the device role
- Manage your devices (rename, change role, replace, revoke)
- Supervise your kiosks and set up their payment terminal
- First day: from sign-up to the first sale

pages.title: Confirm your email address

sections.heading: Confirm your email address
sections.text:
After signing up you are already signed in and can start setting up your business. Vendora also sends you a welcome
email with a confirmation link valid for 24 hours, usable once: opening it proves the address really is yours. Until
you do, a few sensitive actions have to wait.

sections.heading: What waits for the confirmation, and what is never affected
sections.text:
Waits for the confirmation · Allowed right away
Adding a device (pairing code or kit) · Catalog, products, prices, taxes
Connecting an AI assistant · Settings, stores, floor plan
Creating an API key · Reports and the dashboard
Adding a paid option
Inviting or creating a team member
Selling is never affected
A register that is already paired keeps selling, syncing and closing its Z reports, whether the address is confirmed or not.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Spot the banner and the welcome email
On the dashboard, a Confirm your email address banner (1) reminds you which address the link was sent to and what is
on hold. Open your mailbox: the welcome message contains the link.
Nothing received? Click Resend the link (2): a new link is sent right away (one per minute, five per day at most).
Open the link you received
Click the link in the email. It opens signed in to your account:
- You are already signed in in this browser: the page confirms the address straight away.
- You are not: the sign-in page appears with the notice Sign in to confirm your email address. (1). Enter your address (2)
and your password: the confirmation happens by itself once you are signed in, without opening the link again.
Check that it is confirmed
Expected result: the page shows Your email address is confirmed… (1) and a button back to the dashboard, where
the banner is gone. You can now pair your devices, connect an AI assistant, create API keys, add options and invite
your team.

sections.heading: If you try before confirming
sections.text:
A pending action is refused with the message Confirm your email address first…: nothing is lost, open the link (or
Resend the link) and try again.

sections.heading: Special cases
sections.text:
- Account never confirmed: it is closed after 7 days. Nothing is deleted and the address becomes available again
for a new sign-up; if in doubt, contact Vendora.
- Existing accounts, invited members, businesses created by the Vendora team: nothing to do, their address already
counts as confirmed.
- Forgotten password: resetting your password with the link you receive also confirms the address and **signs out
your other sessions** (Sign in).
This link is not valid. Sign in and request a new link from the dashboard.
The link is incomplete (cut off when copied) or matches no email sent. Sign in, then click Resend the link in the
dashboard banner and open the latest email received.
This link has already been used. If your address is not confirmed yet, request a new link from the dashboard.
The link works only once. If your address is already confirmed, the page says so in green (“Your email address is
already confirmed”) and there is nothing else to do. Otherwise, Resend the link. (Some mail programs “open” links in advance to check them: that is sometimes the cause.)
This link has expired. Sign in and request a new link from the dashboard.
More than 24 hours have passed. Sign in, click Resend the link, and open the new email.
A link has just been sent: wait a minute before requesting a new one. / Too many resends today: try again tomorrow, or contact Vendora.
One resend per minute, five per day. Wait, or check your spam folder first; past the daily limit, try again tomorrow or
contact Vendora.
No email arrives
Check your spam folder, then click Resend the link if needed. Still nothing? A typo in the address entered at
sign-up is possible: contact Vendora, who will correct the address with you.
If you are signed in with a different account from the one that received the link, sign out, then open the link again from your email.
The link confirms the account it was issued for. Sign out of the current account, then open the link again: the sign-in
page will ask for the right account.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Create your Vendora workspace
- Sign in to the back office, forgotten password
- Pair a register or a phone
- Build your team: roles, invitations, PIN

pages.title: Create your Vendora workspace

sections.heading: Create your Vendora workspace
sections.text:
Signing up creates, in one go, your business, your owner account and your first store.
You choose how to start: the Free plan, with no time limit, or a 2-month trial of Commerce or Restaurant, **with
no payment method, whose days only count down from your first sale**
(Free trial: rules). You land directly in your back office, already signed in; a welcome email contains a link to open within 24 hours
to confirm your email address (it unlocks device pairing, API keys, your team…).
Sign-up in 20 seconds: name, email, password, activity, currency, and you're ready.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open the Create my workspace page
From the back office sign-in page, click Create my workspace (link “No account yet?”). The
Create my workspace page opens; you can change the language at the top (Français, English, العربية).
Choose how to start
At the top of the form, Your start offers two choices:
- Start for free: “Free plan for life: 1 store, 1 sales device, 300 products, 3 users. No credit card.” Ideal for a
small business that wants to take payments and print its Z report (The Free plan);
- Try Commerce or Restaurant for 2 months (selected by default): “All the plan's features, then you keep going for
free if you do not subscribe.” The …-day free trial badge then appears under the title.
You can move to a paid plan at any time; a trial that ends without a subscription brings you back to Free without
deleting anything.
Fill in the form
1. Business name: the name of your business (shown on the registers and receipts; you can change it later).
2. Email address: your sign-in ID.
3. Password (at least 8 characters) and Confirmation.
4. Your activity: Grocery, Restaurant, Clothing, Services or Generic. It prepares the right
screens (floor plan and kitchen for a restaurant, selling by weight for a grocery…) and the matching trial plan.
5. First store name (optional): left empty = same name as the business.
6. Currency and Time zone: check them carefully. The currency can no longer be changed after the first sale.
7. Business phone (at least 8 digits): the Vendora team calls you if needed during the trial. **Only one free trial
per number** over 12 months.
8. SIRET or tax ID (optional): same rule, one trial per tax ID over 12 months.
Click Create my workspace (the button is called Start for free if you chose the Free plan).
Land in the back office
Expected result: you are signed in and the Dashboard appears, with the Getting started list (1) —
the Activate your account step is already checked — and, for a trial, the trial banner (2): **Trial: your 60 days
start with your first sale. Without a sale, the trial closes on …** On the Free plan, there is no trial banner.
Now follow the Getting started list: Discover the dashboard,
then First day: from sign-up to the first sale.

pages.title: Getting started

sections.heading: Getting started
sections.text: Have you just opened your Vendora workspace? Follow these tutorials in order: within an hour, your business is ready to sell.

pages.title: Try the register in demo mode, without a server

sections.heading: Try the register in demo mode, without a server
sections.text:
Demo mode runs the app without a server and without an account, with a few dummy products. Nothing is
sent anywhere: it is a sandbox for discovering the screen or training someone before installation.
This is not a real register
Demo mode sales are never sent or counted: they appear neither in the back office nor
in the reports. To sell for real, pair the device
(Pair a register or a phone). To train the team on a paired
register, use training mode (dummy tickets) from the register instead.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Enter demo mode
1. Open the Vendora app on an unpaired device: the Pair this device screen appears.
2. Tap the discreet Demo mode without server link at the very bottom.
3. The Device role screen appears: choose Register. (Kiosk, Floor phone and
Kitchen display only show “Coming soon” in demo mode.)
Try the register (iPad / iPhone)
On iPad and iPhone, the demo is a real register with three products (Café express, Eau minérale 1 L, Sandwich thon)
and two dummy users:
1. Who are you?: choose Omar (owner, PIN 2468) or Karim (cashier, PIN 1357) and
enter the PIN.
2. Open session with an opening float (suggested: 100,000).
3. Make a sale: tap the products, Charge, choose the payment method. If a receipt printer is
connected, the receipt really prints.
The status bar stays Offline (“Demo mode without server”) and the counter of operations waiting to sync keeps growing:
this is normal, nothing is sent.
Try the register (Android)
On Android, the demo is more limited: Register — engine demo displays a calculated
sample cart (lines, 10% discount, VAT breakdown, change due), with no input. The
50,000-product catalog demo (target < 100 ms) button opens a sales grid with a very
large catalog, to gauge how fast search is; charging is disabled there.
To try a real sale on Android, pair the device to your workspace (free trial) and turn on training mode.
Leave demo mode
- iPad / iPhone: tap Leave the demo, at the top right.
- Android: tap Leave demo mode, at the bottom of the screen.
The app returns to the Pair this device screen. The role chosen in the demo is forgotten; the demo data stays
isolated and will never be sent.
I can't find “Demo mode without server”
The link only appears on the Pair this device screen, so on an unpaired device: a device already
linked to your store opens its work screen directly. It is disabled while a pairing is in progress.
Sales made in the demo do not appear in the back office
This is intended: demo mode has no server. Pair the device to sell for real.
“Coming soon” appears after choosing Kiosk, Floor phone or Kitchen display
Only the register is available in demo mode. Leave the demo, go back to Demo mode without server and choose Register.
(On Android, the placeholder shows “coming soon”.)

sections.text:
- Choose the device role
- Pair a register or a phone
- Register tutorials

pages.title: First day: catalog, team, device, first sale

sections.heading: First day: catalog, team, device, first sale
sections.text:
This page guides you in order, from an empty account to the first closed day. Each step points to the detailed
tutorial. The dashboard's Getting started list tracks your progress: when all its steps are checked,
you are ready.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Create your workspace (3 minutes)
Sign up choosing the right activity, the right currency and the right time zone (the currency can no
longer be changed after the first sale). → Create your Vendora workspace
Set up your catalog (15 to 30 minutes)
1. Check your VAT rates and the default rate (Catalog › VAT rates).
2. Import all your products at once from a spreadsheet: → Import your catalog from a CSV file.
Or create them one by one in Catalog › Products (New product button on the dashboard).
3. Restaurant: add the options (cooking levels, extras) and the combos. → Catalog tutorials
The Add your catalog step is checked at 20 active products.
(Restaurant) Floor and kitchen (15 minutes)
In the order of the Getting started list: Draw the floor plan, Set up prep stations
(kitchen, bar: who prepares what), Choose table checkout, Set up floor phones.
Each button in the list opens the right page. → Restaurant tutorials
Add your team (10 minutes)
Create one access per person: cashiers, waiters and kitchen staff with a PIN; managers by email invitation.
Also set your own PIN (Control › PIN & approvals): it approves sensitive actions at the register.
→ Build your team: roles, invitations, PIN · Manager PIN and approvals
Pair the register (5 minutes)
Settings › Devices › Add a device › Main register (or Register) › name › Generate the code, then
on the tablet: Vendora app › Scan the QR code. → Pair a register or a phone
Add the planned floor phones, kitchen displays and kiosks the same way. Optional: your logo and your colors
(→ Customize the appearance).
Make the first sale (5 minutes)
On the register:
1. Who are you?: choose your name and enter your PIN.
2. Open session: count the opening float and enter it.
3. Tap the products to fill the cart, then Charge: choose the payment method (cash, card…).
4. Sale recorded: the receipt prints (or is sent). The back office dashboard comes alive right away
(Live card), and the Ring up a first sale step is checked.
Details and special cases: Register tutorials.
Close the day (5 minutes)
At the end of the day, on the register: Close session, count the drawer, confirm. The Z report seals the
day (you can view it in Checkout and payments › Z reports). The Close a first day (Z) step is
checked. Finally, open a report (Insights › Sales reports) to check the last step.

sections.heading: After the first day
sections.text:
- Every morning, keep an eye on the dashboard: To handle block.
- Once a month: Tax compliance (archives), Subscription (invoices).
- Need help with setup? Rather than giving out your password, grant a
delegation to the Vendora team.
The register cannot find the server during pairing
The server address put in the QR code cannot be reached by the tablet. See
Pair a register — If it doesn't work.
An employee does not appear in “Who are you?” on the register
Their PIN is not set, or the register has not synced yet (less than a minute when online). Check in
Settings › Team that their PIN is Set ✓ and that they have access to this store.
The products do not appear on the register
They are inactive, or the register has not synced yet. See A product does not appear on the register.

sections.text:

- Try the register in demo mode

pages.title: Choose the device role

sections.heading: Choose the device role
sections.text:
Each device in the store plays one role, which sets its home screen. The role is chosen in the back office,
when you add the device: the app receives it from the server at pairing, so there is nothing to choose on the device.

sections.heading: The four roles
sections.text:
Role (back office) · On the device · For whom
Register / Main register · Sales, payments, returns, drawer, sessions and Z; PIN sign-in. The main register also takes payment for bills settled at the table. · Cashiers, managers
Floor phone · Order taking at the table, instant sending to the kitchen (and table checkout if you allow it). · Waiters
Kitchen display · The tickets of one or more prep stations arrive and move through their states. · Kitchen, bar
Kiosk · Self-service ordering by customers, in locked mode. · Customers

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Choose the role when adding the device
In Settings › Devices › Add a device, the first step, Type, is the choice of role. Choose it,
set the name (and the stations, zones or preset depending on the role), generate the code and pair the device.
→ Pair a register or a phone
On the device, after Pair, the app goes straight to the screen for its role (for a register: Who are you?).
The pairing screen's help text says so: “The device role (register, kiosk…) is set by the server.”
Change the role of a device already paired
- Kitchen display ⇄ Floor phone: from the device's detail sheet in the back office, Switch to …, then
the device switches on its own at its next sync (under a minute if it is online), without restarting or a new pairing.
→ Manage your devices
- Register or Kiosk: their role does not change (a register has its fiscal chain, a kiosk its orders). To
reuse the device differently: on the device, Unpair this device (confirmation then manager PIN; the
slot is freed on the server) and pair it again with a code of the right type. To replace a broken register with
another tablet: Replace this device.
The “Device role” screen (demo mode only)
The Device role screen (“Each device in the store has a role. Choose this device's role — it sets the home
screen.”) appears only in demo mode, without a server. It offers Register, Kiosk,
Floor phone and Kitchen display. Only Register can be used in demo mode; the others show “Coming soon”.
→ Try the register in demo mode
The device shows the wrong screen after a role change
The app switches at its next sync: the device must be online (check its card in Settings › Devices).
Offline, it keeps its old screen and switches as soon as it is back on the network.
Role change only possible between kitchen display and floor phone: a register (fiscal chain) or a kiosk (orders) is replaced
Revoke the device and pair it again with the right type, or use
Replace this device.
The app shows “Role not supported by this app.” (iPad / iPhone) or the raw role name with “à venir” (Android)
The device was paired with a code of a type this app does not handle (back office workstation, for example). Tap
Unpair (Unpair this device on Android) and pair it with a Register, Floor phone,
Kitchen display or Kiosk code.

sections.text:
- Pair a register or a phone
- Manage your devices (rename, change role, replace, revoke)
- Supervise your kiosks and set up their payment terminal

pages.title: Sign in to the back office, forgotten password

sections.heading: Sign in to the back office, forgotten password
sections.text:
The back office opens in a browser, on a computer or tablet. It is reserved for the owner,
administrators and managers; cashiers, waiters and kitchen staff sign in on the devices with their PIN.

sections.heading: Sign in
sections.text:
Enter your email and password
On the Sign in to the back office page, enter your Email address (1) and your Password (2), then
click Sign in (3). You land on the Dashboard.
The ? button at the top of the card, next to the language choice, opens this tutorial in a new tab (see
Contextual help).
The session stays open in this browser. To close it (shared computer): menu at the top right (your
initials) › Sign out.

sections.heading: Forgotten password
sections.text:
Request a link
On the sign-in page, click Forgot password? (4). Enter your account's Email address (1),
then Get the link (2).
The message (1) always appears, whether or not the address has an account (so nothing is revealed to a stranger). Open
the email “Vendora — choisissez un nouveau mot de passe” (choose a new password; the subject is in French). The link
is valid for 24 hours and can be used only once.
Choose the new password
The link opens the New password page, which reminds you of your account. Enter the **Password (at least 8
characters) (1), the Confirmation (2), then Save** (3) — grayed out as long as the two entries differ.
Expected result: “Your password has been changed. Sessions open elsewhere have been closed.” Click
Sign in.
Incorrect email or password.
The address or the password does not match. Check the Caps Lock key and the address (the one used at sign-up or
in the invitation). Otherwise, use Forgot password?. There is no lockout after several attempts.
The “choose a new password” email does not arrive
Wait a few minutes and look in your spam folder. Check the address you entered. After
3 requests within an hour, no more emails are sent for a while: wait an hour. An account that is still
only invited (invitation not accepted) does not receive a link: use the invitation email.
Link already used or replaced — request a new one (“Forgot password?”)
The link has already been used, or you have requested another link since (only the most recent one works). Click
Request a new link.
Link expired — request a new one (“Forgot password?”)
More than 24 hours have passed. Make a new request.
Unknown link: it may have been replaced by a newer link.
Use the link from the latest email received, or check that it was not cut off when you copied it.
Password: 8 characters minimum
Choose a longer password.
Unable to sign in: the server is not responding. Check your internet connection, then try again.
The Vendora server is not responding (internet connection down, maintenance). Try again in a few minutes. Do the
same for “Unable to send right now. Try again in a few minutes.” and “Unable to reset.”.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Create your Vendora workspace
- Accept an invitation
- Find your way around the back office

pages.title: Find your way: menu, displayed store, “Go to…”, theme, language

sections.heading: Find your way: menu, displayed store, “Go to…”, theme, language
sections.text:
All back office pages share the same frame: the menu on the left, and at the top the displayed store, the
Go to… search and your account menu.
“Go to…”: typing “clôture” (closing) then Enter opens the Z reports.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
The four landmarks on the screen
1. The menu: Dashboard, then the groups Insights, Catalog, Stock and purchasing,
Checkout and payments, Restaurant, Customers, Control and Settings. Click a group to
expand it; the groups you leave open are remembered. You only see the pages your role allows; a page outside
your plan carries the Plan badge. On a tablet or small screen, the menu opens with the ☰ button.
2. The displayed store: every page covers this store. The owner and administrators also have
All stores for overall views. Some pages only cover a single store: they say so
(“This page covers a single store: choose it here or in the header.”).
3. Go to…: the page search (next step).
4. Your account (your initials): language, theme, sign out.
Find a page with “Go to…”
Click Go to… (Z, VAT, stocktake) or press ⌘K (Mac) / Ctrl+K (Windows). Type a few letters (1):
accents and capitals don't matter, and common words work too (“z” or “z report” finds
Z reports). Choose with the ↑ ↓ arrows, open with Enter (2), close with Esc.
Without typing anything, the window offers your Recent pages, then All pages.
Change the language and the theme
Click your initials at the top right. The menu offers:
- Language (1): Français, English, العربية (right-to-left screen);
- Theme (2): Light, Dark (easier on the eyes in the evening) or System (follows the computer's setting);
- Sign out (3).
The choice is remembered on this computer. The back office in the Dark theme:
The language and theme of the registers are set separately, in Settings › Appearance.

sections.heading: The banners at the top of pages
sections.text:
Banner · Meaning
“Trial — … days left.” · Free trial in progress (Subscription).
“Payment pending…”, “Account suspended…” · Subscription status (Subscription).
“Vendora · … — delegation until …” · A member of the Vendora team is working under your delegation (Vendora access).
““…” is not included in your plan…” · The page depends on a module that is not in your plan.
“Change refused — …” · The server refused a change; the reason follows.
A menu page has disappeared, or I don't see “All stores”
Your role does not give access to this page or to the multi-store view (reserved for the owner and
administrators). See the roles in Build your team: roles, invitations, PIN.
The figures don't match what I expect
Check the displayed store at the top of the screen: the pages follow that choice.
⌘K / Ctrl+K does nothing
First click inside the page (not in the browser's address bar), then try again; or click
Go to… directly.
No page matches “…”.
Try another word (“ticket”, “stock”, “team”…) or browse the menu.

sections.text:
- Discover the dashboard
- Sign in to the back office
- Customize the appearance (logo, colors, kiosk)

pages.title: Discover the dashboard and the “Getting started” list

sections.heading: Discover the dashboard and the “Getting started” list
sections.text:
The Dashboard is the back office home page. From top to bottom: the Getting started list, the
Live view, the Today figures and the To handle items. It covers the store chosen at the top of
the screen (or all stores).

sections.heading: The “Getting started” list
sections.text:
Follow the setup steps
The card shows your progress (1) — … / … steps and the percentage — and the list of steps. A completed step
is checked; a step still to do (2) has a button that takes you to the right page.
Step · Done when… · Button
Activate your account · your account is active (from sign-up) · —
Add your catalog · at least 20 active products (progress “… / 20”) · Import a CSV
Invite your team · at least one member besides you (a pending invitation counts) · Invite
Draw the floor plan (restaurant) · at least one table · Open the floor plan
Set up prep stations (restaurant) · at least one station (kitchen, bar…) · Set up stations
Choose table checkout (restaurant) · the checkout rule is saved · Choose
Set up floor phones (restaurant) · at least one phone profile · Configure
Pair your devices · the planned devices are paired (at least one register); progress “Register 1/1 · …” (“Register: 2 paired for 1 planned” if you paired more than planned) · Add a device
Ring up a first sale · a sale is charged on a register · —
Close a first day (Z) · a Z report exists · See Z reports
Open a first report · you have opened the sales or margins report · Open reports
Open a first Z report (Gratuit plan, instead of the previous one) · you have opened the Z reports page (“Each day's Z report: sales, payments and VAT. Included in your plan, like today's dashboard.”) · See Z reports
The restaurant steps only appear if you have a store with the Restaurant profile. When everything is done:
“All set: happy selling!” and the card tucks itself away.
Collapse or hide the list
- Collapse (3): the card only shows the next step (1). Expand opens it again.
- Hide (4): the card disappears; the Show “Getting started” (… / …) button (1) brings it back.
These choices are remembered on the computer you use.

sections.heading: The rest of the dashboard
sections.text:
Live: your registers right now
Updated every 30 seconds (Refresh to force it). The Quick actions (1) — Add a device,
New product, Z reports —, then the tiles (2): Open sessions and their revenue, Current service
(tables and covers), Kitchen (lines sent but not ready, wait times), Kiosks, Devices online. The
Open register sessions and Devices cards detail who is open and who is offline.
Configuration alerts (3) flags what prevents service from running smoothly, with a Correct button:
main register without an open session, prep station without a screen or printer, category routed to no station,
kiosk without a preset…
Today: today's figures
Today's revenue (compared with yesterday and last week), Tickets, Average basket, Today's margin, the
Revenue by hour chart (today and D-7) and Today's top products. The Sales reports and Margins links go
further.
To handle: what needs your attention
Four cards: Integrity alerts (anomalies detected by the server on Z reports, sealed sales,
approvals), Stock alerts (out of stock, negative stock, below threshold), Supplier due dates (invoices overdue
or due within 7 days) and Anti-fraud (open alerts). All is well when each card shows a green check mark.
See Manager PIN and approvals,
Monitor anti-fraud, Tax compliance.
The “Getting started” list does not appear
It is reserved for the owner and administrators. Otherwise, it has been hidden: click
Show “Getting started”, or it is complete (Review “Getting started”).
A step stays “to do” even though I have done it
Check the condition in the table above (20 active products, a paired register, a synced
sale…), then reload the page.
Live view is reserved for this store's managers.
You are not a manager of the store chosen at the top of the screen: choose one of your stores.
Alerts unavailable (Manager role required on this store).
Same cause: switch stores, or ask the owner to give you the Manager role on this store.
Today's figures are unavailable.
The server did not respond. Click Refresh or reload the page. Do the same for “Live view unavailable.”.

sections.text:

pages.title: Order number, inactivity, kiosk unavailable

sections.heading: Order number
sections.text:
After payment (by card or at the counter), the Thank you! screen shows the order number (for example, K55-002): this is the number shown
on the kitchen display and at the register. The kiosk returns to the welcome screen automatically a few seconds later.
The number is issued by the store device that holds the local network hub (see
Store network): all the kiosks then share a single sequence for the
day — K-041, K-042, K-043… If the kiosk cannot reach the hub (Wi-Fi down, register switched off), the order
is not blocked: the kiosk uses a fallback number prefixed with its own code (e.g. K55-002), which cannot be mistaken
for another kiosk's. Rarely, if two orders from the same day still reach the server with the same number, the second
one gets a letter (K-042B); its ticket, already printed, is found at the register through its QR code.

sections.heading: Inactivity
sections.text:
If no one touches the screen for the preset's timeout (60 s by default), the kiosk asks Are you still there? with a
countdown (“Back to home in … s”). Yes, I continue resumes the order; otherwise, the cart is cleared and the
kiosk returns to the welcome screen.

sections.heading: Start over
sections.text: Start over at the top of the screen asks “Abandon the current order?” (1): Start over (2) clears the cart.

sections.heading: Kiosk unavailable
sections.text:
Kiosk temporarily unavailable — “Please order at the counter”: the kiosk was disabled in the back office (closing
time, kitchen problem). Reactivate it from its record in the back office.
The kiosk returns to the welcome screen too quickly
Increase the preset's inactivity timeout in the back office (15 s to 10 min).

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Pay at the kiosk
- Prepare the kiosk

pages.title: Kiosk

sections.heading: Kiosk
sections.text: The self-service ordering kiosk: preparing it, what the customer sees, payment and the technical mode.

pages.title: Technical mode: unlock, set up the terminal, exit the kiosk

sections.heading: Technical mode: unlock, set up the terminal, exit the kiosk
sections.text:
The kiosk has no visible staff button: you open the Technical screen with a hidden gesture and a manager
PIN.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Tap the top-left corner 5 times
Quickly tap the top-left corner of the screen 5 times (an invisible area). The Manager PIN dialog opens:
“Exit kiosk mode — manager approval required” (1). The manager types their PIN (2) and taps Approve.
Read the technical screen
The Technical screen shows Back to the kiosk (1); the status of sync, the kiosk, the printer, and Guided Access; the
Payment terminal section (2) (provider, mode, reader status) and Card payment (3) (“Available” or the reason
it is unavailable); and the Kiosk cash session.
Technical actions
Further down: Close the kiosk day (Z) (1), Sync now, Reprint the last ticket (2), **Unpair this
device (3). In a test environment, a Simulated terminal** also lets you use test cards.
Hardware diagnostics tests the kiosk's printer, beep, and connection to the server (see
Hardware diagnostics).
Online help opens this help center inside the app (Guided Access and pinning block the browser);
Close help returns to the technical screen.
Expected result: Back to the kiosk returns to the customer welcome screen.
The 5-tap gesture does nothing
Tap faster, right at the top-left edge (an area about 1.5 cm / 0.6 in square). It works on the welcome screen and during
an order.
Wrong PIN — 4 attempts left
Only a manager of the store can open the technical screen.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Prepare the kiosk
- Approve with the manager PIN
- Unpair a device

pages.title: Pay at the counter or by card on the kiosk

sections.heading: Pay at the counter or by card on the kiosk
sections.text: A complete order at the kiosk: dine in, lunch meal deal (starter, main with option, dessert), cart, card payment, order number.

sections.heading: Pay by card
sections.text:
Pay by card
In the cart, the customer taps Pay by card. The kiosk connects to the terminal (“Connecting to the terminal…”), then shows the
order number, the amount, and Insert or tap your card (1). Cancel cancels the payment.
Payment accepted
The screen shows Thank you!, Your order number (1) in very large type, and Payment accepted (2). The order goes to the
kitchen, and a ticket prints if the kiosk has a printer (“Keep your ticket, it carries your number”).

sections.heading: Pay on the terminal next to the kiosk
sections.text:
When the kiosk preset has payment set to On the card terminal (a standalone terminal placed next to the kiosk),
Order in the cart leads to Pay … on the terminal next to the kiosk (1), with the order number (2):
- terminal gateway active: “The kiosk continues as soon as the terminal confirms the payment”. As soon as a payment of
the right amount is received, the kiosk moves to Thank you! on its own and the order goes to the kitchen;
- I paid on the terminal (3) only appears if the preset allows Manual card terminal payment confirmation: the
customer cannot confirm alone, a manager's code is needed (see below). These manual confirmations
are checked during reconciliation;
- Pay at the counter (4): the customer pays at the counter after all, with their number.
Whether the payment is confirmed by the terminal or by hand (under a manager's code), the kiosk records a real sale,
with its receipt, and no longer just an order marked as paid. If the customer has paid but the sale cannot be recorded
(not enough stock, for example), they have nothing to pay again: see
Paid, but the sale could not be recorded.
With no payment by the end of the preset's Payment expiry (min) delay (10 minutes by default), the order expires:
it is canceled, nothing goes to the kitchen, and the kiosk returns to the welcome screen with the “Order expired…”
message (1), shown for 30 seconds or until the next customer.

sections.heading: The customer paid on the terminal: a manager's code
sections.text:
When the terminal does not confirm by itself, the customer taps I paid on the terminal. They cannot finish alone: a
manager on the team checks the payment and confirms it with their code. A confirmation that comes from the terminal
itself never asks for a code.
The customer calls a manager
The kiosk opens the Confirm the terminal payment window. The customer reads “Please call a staff member to confirm
your payment”. Cancel closes the window without recording anything and goes back to the payment screen. After a
while without any touch, the window closes by itself and what was typed is erased.
The manager checks the slip and enters their code
1. They read the slip printed by the terminal (“Manager: check the terminal slip, then enter your code.”).
2. If the slip carries a number, they copy it into Card slip number (optional) (“Copy the number printed on the
terminal slip, if there is one”; 40 characters at most). With no number, they leave the field empty: the payment is
then recorded with no reference.
3. They type their code on the keypad: dots appear, never the digits. It is the
manager PIN, and it must belong to a manager at least. **Confirm the
payment** becomes active from 4 digits.
Expected result: the window closes and the kiosk shows Thank you!, the order number and Payment done, then
the ticket prints as for any payment. The sale keeps a trace of the manager who confirmed and of the slip number typed.
When the code does not go through:
- wrong code: the dots empty and “Wrong PIN — 3 attempts left” appears; the slip number typed is kept;
- five failures: “Too many attempts: manager PIN locked until 14:35”; the keypad and Confirm the payment are
greyed out, only Cancel stays active;
- no manager with a PIN on the device: “No manager with a PIN on this register — set a PIN in the back office (PIN &
approvals) then sync”, as soon as the window opens.

sections.heading: Paid, but the sale could not be recorded
sections.text:
A rare case: the terminal has taken the customer's payment (or a manager has confirmed it), but the kiosk cannot record
the sale: not enough stock at payment time, the kiosk's cash day could not be opened, or an amount paid that differs
from the order's. The customer has nothing to pay again.
The customer is reassured
The kiosk shows no error: the Thank you! screen gives Your order number in very large type and the message
“Your payment has been received; you don't need to pay again. Show this number at the counter: the team will complete
your order.” The customer taps I noted my number (or waits for the automatic return to the welcome screen) and goes
to the counter. No ticket is printed: there is no sale to print a ticket for.
If the customer had already left the kiosk when the cash day or the server answers, nothing is shown on the kiosk: only
the register flags it.
The team records the payment at the register
The order becomes Already paid at the terminal: the register shows an alert that cannot be dismissed, and the back
office lists it in Kiosks. Staff record it without charging the customer again: see
An order already paid at the terminal.

sections.heading: Pay at the counter
sections.text:
With Pay at the counter, the order also goes to the kitchen, and the customer gets their number with **Show this
number at the counter** (1). At the register: Charge a kiosk order.
Pay at the counter is still offered even when the code fails (code locked, no manager available). It sends an
ordinary order to the register, which the register will have paid: if the customer has already paid on the terminal,
do not let them pay again, and get a manager to confirm their payment. This is a known limit.

sections.heading: In Tunisia
sections.text:
As long as the Tunisian tax module (NACEF) does not cover the kiosk, the kiosk of a Tunisian store only offers the
counter: before any payment, it shows “Payment at the kiosk is not available in this store yet: please pay at the
counter.” Nothing has been paid. In the back office, the preset's On the card terminal setting is refused for that
store (“Payment at the kiosk is unavailable in Tunisia until the NACEF module covers it: choose PAY_AT_COUNTER”). If your
store is in Tunisia, leave payment on At the counter in the preset; a preset already set to the terminal before this
change is not yet corrected everywhere.
Payment declined
The bank declined the card: Try again with another card, or Pay at the counter.
Payment terminal unavailable: please pay at the counter
The terminal is not responding, so the order can be paid at the counter. Staff can check the terminal in the
technical screen.
Card payment unavailable offline: please pay at the counter
The kiosk has lost its internet connection, and the terminal requires online authorization.
The order amount has changed: please pay at the counter
The order was changed during payment: the customer pays at the counter.
Order expired: the payment was not received in time. Please start your order again.
The customer did not pay on the terminal within the preset's delay. The order is canceled: they place it again. To
lengthen the delay: Settings › Appearance › Kiosk, Payment expiry (min).
Your payment has been received; you don't need to pay again. Show this number at the counter: the team will complete your order.
The customer has paid (the terminal confirmed it, or a manager did) but the sale could not be recorded (not enough
stock, cash day could not be opened, different amount). They do not pay again: they go to the counter with their number,
and the team records the payment (An order already paid at the terminal).
The payment could not be verified. Do not pay again: please call a staff member.
The terminal confirmed the payment, but the kiosk could neither record nor cancel it (no transaction number, for
example): it cannot verify it alone. The customer does not pay again. To prevent a second payment, the screen no longer
shows any button (no “Try again”, “Pay at the counter” or “Cancel”); it returns to the welcome screen after the kiosk's
inactivity delay. The order is not sent to the kitchen. A manager checks the payment on the terminal's statement before
serving the customer; if in doubt, contact Vendora support.
The payment must be confirmed by a manager. Please call a staff member.
The manager's code was not received in time for this order (it is only valid for a short moment). Tap **I paid on the
terminal** again and redo the entry.
Too many attempts: manager PIN locked until …
Five wrong codes in a row. Wait for the time shown. The customer must not pay again meanwhile: see **Pay at the
counter** above.
Payment at the kiosk is not available in this store yet: please pay at the counter.
Tunisian store: the kiosk does not take card payment yet (In Tunisia). The customer pays at the counter.
Printer unavailable: note your number
No ticket is printed: the customer writes down their number and taps I noted my number.

pages.title: Product page, options, meal deals, and cart on the kiosk

sections.heading: Product page and options
sections.text:
Tapping a product with options opens its page: groups marked Required (1) (doneness, side), add-ons with their
prices, quantity, and Add · … (2) with the total price. The button stays grayed out until all required choices
are made.

sections.heading: Meal deal
sections.text:
The meal deal is built step by step (“2 / 3”) (1): the customer taps one product per step (2); a dish with options
shows its choices within the meal deal; Your meal deal shows a summary. Add meal deal · … (3) adds it to the cart.

sections.heading: Cart
sections.text:
The Cart (1) lists the items (with meal deal details), the − / + quantity buttons, and the total. Depending on the preset, the customer taps **Pay at the
counter (2) or Pay by card (3); Edit goes back to the catalog, and Clear** removes
everything.
Your cart is empty
No products have been added: tap Edit to go back to the catalog.
This meal deal is no longer available
The meal deal was disabled in the back office while the order was in progress: choose individual items instead.

pages.title: The customer journey: welcome, language, dine in / takeaway, catalog

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Welcome and language
The customer taps the screen (Touch to order). They can change the language at any time with FR / EN / AR
at the top of the screen.
Dine in or takeaway
Where will you eat?: Dine in (1) or Takeaway (2). (This step does not appear if the preset turns it off.)
The catalog
The categories (1) scroll along the top (All products, Starters, Mains…). Featured products are shown first; a
meal deal (2) has its own badge. The Cart (3) stays visible; Start over cancels the order (after
confirmation).
Next: Product page, options, meal deal and cart.

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
A product does not appear at the kiosk
It is inactive, not sold in this store, or its category is hidden from the kiosk in the back office.

pages.title: Prepare the kiosk (preset, welcome screen, featured products, payment)

sections.heading: Prepare the kiosk (preset, welcome screen, featured products, payment)
sections.text:
The kiosk is a self-service tablet: customers build their order, choose dine in or takeaway, and pay by
card or at the counter. Its look and behavior come from a preset configured in the back office.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Set up the preset in the back office
In the back office, on the Appearance › Kiosk page (kiosk presets), set the welcome text (“Touch to order,” “Dine in or takeaway”), the **dine in /
takeaway step, featured products** (up to 12), banners, inactivity timeout (15 s to 10 min, 60 s by default),
and payment method: At the counter or On the card terminal. The Kiosks page then assigns a preset to each kiosk. For details, see
Customize the appearance (logo, colors, kiosk) and
Supervise your kiosks and set up their payment terminal.
The kiosk downloads the welcome image and banner images at the next sync and stores them on the
tablet, so they still display without an internet connection. A banner disappears automatically when its period ends; when a customer
taps a banner, the order opens directly on its category (or its product's category).
Pair the tablet as a kiosk
Generate a pairing code with the Kiosk role and the chosen preset, then pair the tablet (see
Pair). To accept card payments at the kiosk, set up its **payment
terminal** from the kiosk's record in the back office.
Check the welcome screen and lock the kiosk
The kiosk shows the preset's welcome screen (1) — with its welcome image and banners if it has any — and the
language options (2) (Français, English, العربية). Until the kiosk is locked, a reminder (3) is displayed:
- iPad: turn on Guided Access (Settings › Accessibility › Guided Access), then triple-click the side button
while in the app;
- Android: when the app opens, the tablet asks “Pin app?” — accept. The reminder changes to “Screen pinned”.
Unless the tablet is a dedicated device (device owner, set up with a device management tool), a system gesture
can unpin the app. For a full lock, have the tablet provisioned as a dedicated device; the reminder then shows
“Kiosk locked (dedicated device)”.
The kiosk also works on a phone (compact layout, handy for testing), but it is designed for tablets.
Expected result: the welcome screen is displayed and customers can no longer exit the app; staff use the
technical mode.
Kiosk temporarily unavailable
The kiosk was disabled in the back office (or has not received its preset yet). Customers see “Please order at
the counter”. Reactivate it from its record in the back office, then sync.
The welcome image or the banners are not displayed
The kiosk downloads the images at the first sync after the preset is saved (syncs run every 20 to 30 seconds). Check its
connection, then tap Sync now in the technical screen. A banner outside its
validity period is not displayed.
Screen not pinned: accept « Pin app »
Android: the pinning request was declined or dismissed. Go back to the kiosk's welcome screen (or restart the app) so
the request appears again, then accept it.
Payment terminal unavailable: please pay at the counter
The kiosk's terminal is not set up or is not responding, so the kiosk offers payment at the counter. Check the
terminal in the technical screen.
