pages.title: Set up a payment connector (card terminal, online payment)

sections.heading: Set up a payment connector (card terminal, online payment)
sections.text:
A payment connector links your registers to a provider: the register requests the payment, the customer pays (by
scanning a QR code, opening a link, or on a card terminal) and the confirmation comes back automatically. Each store
chooses its connectors in Checkout and payments › Payment connectors. The “manual confirmation” bank card (the
cashier confirms a payment made on a standalone terminal) is always available.
Three modes:
- Simulated: demo, no money changes hands — for training the team;
- Sandbox: the provider's test account, to check the connection;
- Production: real payments.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Checkout and payments › Payment connectors
One card per provider: Flouci (QR), Konnect, Paymee, Simulated QR (demo), TPE carte bancaire (bank card terminal).
1. the checkbox to enable the connector;
2. its type: QR / link or Terminal (and “unavailable here” if the chosen mode does not exist on this server);
3. the Mode;
4. the provider's credentials (secret fields show “Leave blank to keep”);
5. the publication status and Publish.
Under each description, the way the payment is confirmed: “confirmation by readback (the register queries the
provider)”, “confirmation by signed provider notification” or “automatic confirmation (demo)”.
Enable a connector and enter its credentials
1. Check the connector.
2. Choose the Mode.
3. In any mode other than Simulated, paste the credentials given by the provider (for example App token and **App
secret for Flouci; API key, Wallet (receiverWalletId) and Webhook secret for Konnect; Terminal
IP address, Port and Merchant contract number** for the bank card terminal). The help under each field tells you where
to find it.
Credentials are encrypted and never shown again: to keep them when you make a change, leave the field
blank.
Publish
Click Publish. If a required credential is missing, publishing is refused and the message says which one (1),
for the connector concerned (2):
Once the fields are filled in (or in Simulated mode):
Expected result: “Connectors published (version 1) — registers offer the active connectors from the next
checkout.” (1) and “Version 1 — 1 active connector(s)” (2).
Only checked connectors are offered
As long as nothing is published, the simulated QR is offered by default (“Never published — simulated QR only”)
and its card is already checked: it stays active when you first publish. Uncheck Simulated QR (demo) if you
no longer want to offer it to the registers.
On the register, the checkout screen now offers this provider (see Take a meal voucher, a tip, a provider payment);
each payment then appears in Provider payments.
Publication denied. Flouci (QR) (SANDBOX): “App token” required
In Sandbox or Production, the provider's secret credentials are required. Paste them (from your developer or merchant area at the provider), or switch back
to Simulated for a demo.
A connector shows “unavailable here”
The chosen mode is not offered by this server (for example, simulated gateways are disabled in production).
Choose another mode.
Only the store owner configures payment connectors
A manager sees the page as
read-only (“Read-only: only the store owner configures the connectors.”). Ask the owner.
The connectors were changed elsewhere: the latest version has been reloaded.
Someone published while you were editing. Redo your changes and publish.
The QR payment stays on “Waiting for customer” on the register
The customer has not finished paying, or the provider is not responding. See Card payment is declined or
stuck and Track provider payments.

sections.heading: Checkout and payments
sections.text: Follow the money from the back office: register sessions and Z reports, tips, discounts, pay at the table, payment connectors.

pages.title: Track and reconcile provider payments

sections.heading: Track and reconcile provider payments
sections.text:
When the register requests a payment from a provider (dynamic QR, link, card terminal), it is the Vendora server that talks
to the provider; the register tracks the status. At sync, each sale that carries a provider payment is
reconciled with the payment: amount, provider and confirmation are checked.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Checkout and payments › Provider payments
1. the summary: Reconciliation with no anomalies ✓, or N reconciliation anomaly(ies) in red;
2. Status: Waiting for customer, Confirmed, Cancelled, Expired or Declined;
3. Transaction: the provider's reference (useful for finding the payment on the provider's statement);
4. Reconciliation: Sale reconciled ✓, Anomaly (with the details), or “Sale not received yet”.
Each row also gives the date, the provider, the Reference (the receipt number), the amount and the
Refunded amounts.
Understand the statuses
- Confirmed + Sale reconciled ✓: everything is in order.
- Confirmed + “Sale not received yet”: the customer paid, the register has not synced the sale yet
(normal for a few minutes, or the register is offline).
- Canceled: the cashier abandoned this payment (customer left, other payment method) — no sale expected.
- Expired: the customer did not pay in time.
- Declined: the provider declined the payment.
A row shows “Anomaly”
The details under the badge say what does not match between the sale and the payment, for example: “Amount 33,00 € ≠
30,00 €”, “Provider FLOUCI ≠ KONNECT”, “Payment EXPIRED at the provider, not confirmed”, “Already used by sale …”, or
for a return “Return …: 15,00 € refunded at the register, 0,00 € confirmed by the provider”. Compare with the provider's statement
(Transaction column) and the sale in Register sessions, then sort it out with the cashier.
A “Confirmed” payment stays on “Sale not received yet”
The register that took the payment has not synced. Check that it is online (see A register no longer syncs).
If the register was reset before syncing, report it to support.
No supplier payments for this store.
No QR or terminal payment has been made yet. “Manual confirmation” card payments do not appear here.
Unable to load the supplier payments.
The server did not respond. Check your connection and reload the page.

sections.text:
- Set up a payment connector
- Check register sessions
- Register (device): provider payment (QR / card terminal)
- The Checkout and payments section

pages.title: Track and share out tips

sections.heading: Track and share out tips
sections.text:
The cashier enters the tip at checkout, in cash or by card, assigned to the seller, the table's server, another team
member with a register PIN, or the shared pot. It is
excluded from revenue and from the VAT base: it does not count in any sales indicator.
Checkout and payments › Tips keeps the register of tips.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Checkout and payments › Tips
1. Group by: Beneficiary, Service or Day;
2. the period From / To (empty = everything);
3. the table: Count, Total, Cash, Card, and the Total (excl. revenue) row;
4. Export CSV and Export PDF.
Shared pot groups the tips the cashier did not assign to anyone: share them out according to your own rules.
See tips by service
Click Service: one row per service (register session), readable without any technical identifier (1) — the date,
the opening and closing times (“ongoing” while the register is still open), then the register, the manager (who
opened the session) and the session number. Handy for sharing the pot between those who worked that service.
The sales of a session (Checkout and payments › Cash sessions, open a session) also show the Tip (not revenue)
column: amount, beneficiary and method (“Lina · Card”).
Export the register
Export CSV downloads the table on screen (pourboires-<regroupement>-<du>-<au>.csv). Export PDF downloads
pourboires-<store>.pdf, ready to print or archive: the store's logo (or else its trading name), the store name, the period, the cash / card totals, then a
Par bénéficiaire table (1) and a Par service table (2), whatever the grouping on screen.
Tips also appear on every Z report, in the Tips (excluded from revenue) section (see
Read Z reports). Cash tips are in the drawer: they are counted in the
session's expected cash.
No tips in this period (registers send them at sync).
No tip was entered in the period, or the registers have not synced yet. Widen the dates. To enter a tip at the
register, see Take a meal voucher, a tip, a provider payment.
Tips does not appear in the menu, or shows the “Plan” badge
The page belongs to the Tips module of your plan (see Settings › Subscription).
Unable to load the tips report.
The server did not respond. Check your connection and reload the page.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Read and download Z reports
- Register (device): take a tip
- The Checkout and payments section

pages.title: Read and download Z reports

sections.heading: Read and download Z reports
sections.text:
The Z report is the frozen snapshot of a register session at closing. Each register numbers its Z reports
with no gaps (Z 1, Z 2…) and chains them together with a SHA-256 fingerprint: a Z is never edited, it is
archived. The server re-checks every Z at sync.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Checkout and payments › Z reports
1. the chain status: Chain intact ✓ (or N integrity anomaly(ies) in red) and the number of reports;
2. the columns: No., Register, Session, Closure, Revenue incl. VAT, Discrepancy, Integrity;
3. a non-zero discrepancy appears in red;
4. Integrity: OK, or Anomaly (hover over the badge to read the details).
Read the details of a Z and download it
Click a row. The Z report no. 8 details show:
- PDF (1): downloads rapport-z-8-….pdf (with the store's logo at the top, if it has one), to send to your accountant;
- the session, the opening and closing, then the Sales, Revenue incl. VAT, discounts, voids, returns (2);
- Revenue by payment method and VAT by rate (base excl. VAT and VAT collected);
- Tips (excluded from revenue), if any, by employee;
- Cash: opening float, each cash in / cash out with its reason and comment (3), expected, counted and
Discrepancy (4), followed by the Reason entered by the cashier;
- Sealing: the SHA-256 fingerprint, re-checked in your browser (5), and the Z it is chained to. Since this change, the register also signs the Z and Vendora checks the signature.
No Z reports received for this store (registers send them at sync).
No register has closed a session yet, or the register has not synced since closing. Check on the register
(see Close the register and read the Z report).
The “Anomaly” or “N integrity anomaly(ies)” badge appears
The server detected a problem in this register's Z chain. The Z details list “Integrity anomalies detected by the
server:” with one sentence per anomaly and its technical code, for example: “One or more Z reports are missing
before this one: no. 8 expected, no. 9 received.” (NUMBER_GAP) or “The Z report's content no longer matches its
fingerprint: it was changed after closing.” (HASH_MISMATCH). Nothing has been changed or deleted and there is
nothing for you to change: if a number is missing, keep the register switched on and connected, then contact Vendora
support with the register and the report number. A Z can also be reported when its signature cannot be checked (BAD_SEAL_SIGNATURE) or when it does not match the sales received from this register (CONTENT_MISMATCH): keep the register connected so it sends everything, then contact support if the gap remains; the report is kept as it is. All the anomalies and what they mean:
Reading an integrity anomaly.
The fingerprint does not match the content: this Z report may have been altered
Your browser recomputed the fingerprint and did not get the same one: the content displayed does not match the
sealed Z. Reload the page; if the message remains, report it to support.
Local verification unavailable (insecure context)
The browser only checks the fingerprint over a secure connection (https). The server check did take place
(Integrity column).
PDF export failed.
The PDF could not be generated. Try again; check your connection.

sections.text:
- Check register sessions and discrepancies

pages.title: Check register sessions and discrepancies

sections.heading: Check register sessions and discrepancies
sections.text:
A register session runs from opening (with the opening float) to closing (cash count and Z report).
The registers send every opening, sale, cash movement and closing to the server; *Checkout and payments ›
Register sessions* brings them together. The X report is recomputed there by the server: you can follow a
session in progress without going to the register.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Checkout and payments › Register sessions
In the menu, open Checkout and payments (1) then Register sessions (2).
Read the list and the discrepancies by cashier
1. the From / to and Cashier filters (Clear filters to show everything again);
2. Discrepancies by cashier: for the sessions closed in the period, attributed to whoever opened them — number of
sessions, Short, Over, Cumulative discrepancy and Largest shortage; a negative discrepancy is a
shortage;
3. open sessions at the top of the list (open badge);
4. for each closed session: the closed badge (or closed · forced) and its discrepancy, in red if it is not
zero.
Each row shows the register and the session number, the cashier, the opening and closing times, the number of
sales and the Z number.
Open the X report of a closed session
Click a session. The X report appears on the right:
1. Sales: count, Revenue incl. VAT, discounts, voids, returns, then Revenue by payment method;
2. Cash: Opening float, cash in and cash out with their reason, Expected (what should be in the
drawer), Counted at closing;
3. Discrepancy = counted − expected.
Below, Session sales lists each sale: Store no. (assigned by the server on receipt) and
Ticket no. (printed by the register, even offline), time, payment, total, and Tip (not revenue): amount,
beneficiary and method (“Lucas (salle) · Card”, “Shared pot · Cash”), “—” without a tip.
Follow a session in progress
Click the open session: the header shows “Current session · computed by the server at 23:12” (1) and the sales
already received (2). The expected cash tells you what should be in the drawer right now.
The X report only contains what the register has already synced. The X printed at the register (see
Cash in / cash out and the X report) may include a few more sales if the register is offline.
What to do about a discrepancy?
1. Review the session's cash outs (supplier purchase, bank deposit…): a movement forgotten at the register
often explains the discrepancy.
2. Read the reason entered by the cashier at closing: it appears on the Z report
(Read and download Z reports).
3. A cashier who is often Short: check how change is given and how the cash is counted at the end of the shift.
A closed Z is never edited: the discrepancy stays recorded as is.
No sessions pushed for this store.
No register in this store has sent a session yet. Check that a register is paired and that it synced after
opening its session (see Open the register with its opening float and A register no longer syncs).
No sessions for these filters.
No session matches the date or cashier filters: click Clear filters.
A session shows “closed · forced”
The register recorded a forced closing, outside the usual closing flow. The Z exists; check the cash count with
the cashier.
I don't know what a cash out in the X report corresponds to
Each movement shows its reason in plain words (“Cash supplier purchase”, “Bank deposit”, “Change top-up”,
“Other cash in”, “Other cash out”, “Correction”), followed in parentheses by the comment entered by the cashier.
Without a comment, ask the person who was running the register for details (their name appears in the session).
X report unavailable.
The server could not compute the report. Reload the page; if the message persists, check the connection.

sections.text:

- Register (device): cash in / cash out

pages.title: Set up the receipt and the scale (header, footer, weighing)

sections.heading: Set up the receipt and the scale (header, footer, weighing)
sections.text:
Checkout and payments › Receipt and scale sets what is printed in the header and footer of all the store's
receipts: sales, voids, X and Z reports, pre-bills. A field left blank is not printed. The same page declares the
scale labels (EAN-13 barcodes starting with 2x) the register can read.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Checkout and payments › Receipt and scale
1. the table of contents: Ticket legal identity, Branding areas, Scale labels;
2. the Ticket legal identity card;
3. the Receipt preview, updated as you type;
4. the version badge (“Never published — no details printed” at first).
Fill in the legal identity
Fill in (1) Legal name, Address, Phone, the tax identifier, the trade register and
Receipt footer message. The preview (2) shows the result. The labels follow the store's country:
Store country · Fields · Printed on the receipt
Tunisia · Tax ID, Trade register (RNE) · « MF : … », « RNE : … »
France · EU VAT number, Trade register (RCS) · « N° TVA : … », « RCS : … »
The country comes from the store's tax compliance settings (or, if none, its currency): there is nothing to choose.
Mandatory information
The receipt body (lines, amounts, VAT, number, session, seller) and the required legal notices are generated by
Vendora and cannot be changed. Here you only set the header and the footer.
Customize the header and footer
Branding areas card:
1. Logo in header: the monochrome version of the logo set in Settings › Appearance;
2. Welcome message (header) and Legal mentions (footer), 200 characters at most;
3. Social networks: Add a network, choose Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, WhatsApp or Site, then
the handle (3 networks at most) — printed « Instagram : @identifiant »;
4. Online receipt QR on the receipt: the customer scans it to find their receipt.
Declare the scale labels (selling by weight)
If a scale labels your products (grocery, butcher, cheese shop), its barcodes use the format
PP IIIII VVVVV K (1): prefix, item code, weight in grams or price, check digit. The register finds the product by
its scale code (PLU) or by the prefix and item code saved as its barcode (e.g. 2100123).
- “Weight” prefixes (2): prefixes whose variable part is a weight;
- “Price” prefixes (3): prefixes whose variable part is a price.
Separate multiple prefixes with commas. 20 (internal codes) and 29 (loyalty cards) are reserved.
- Item code on the label (4): 4, 5 or 6 digits, depending on your scale's setting (5 for most models); the
value takes up the remaining digits and the format shown updates to match (PP IIII VVVVVV K for 4 digits).
This setting is specific to each store. The products' scale code (PLU) stays at 5 digits: a 4-digit item code is
padded with a zero.
The product itself is set to “by weight” with its scale code in the catalog (see Sell by weight and scale codes).
Publish
Click Publish at the bottom of the page.
Expected result: “Profile published (version 1) — registers print it after their next sync.”
(1); the preview (2) shows the final receipt.
Print a test receipt on the register to check (see Connect and set up the receipt printer).
Only the store owner can fill in the receipt's legal identity.
A manager sees the page as read-only (“Read-only: only the store owner edits this profile.”).
Sign in with the owner account.
Publication denied. Scale prefix “20”: 21 to 28 expected (20 = internal codes, 29 = loyalty cards)
Scale prefixes range from 21 to 28. Other possible refusals: “A scale prefix cannot be both “weight” and “price””,
“8 scale prefixes at most per type”.
Publication denied. Social network handle required (40 characters at most)
A social network row has no
handle. Fill it in or click Remove. Likewise, each field has a maximum length: “Legal name of 64
characters at most”, “Address of 120 characters at most”…
The profile was changed elsewhere: the latest version has been reloaded.
Someone published while you were editing. Redo your changes on the reloaded version.
The logo does not print
Check that a logo is set in Settings › Appearance and that Logo in header is checked; the printer must be
able to print images (see Connect and set up the receipt printer).
The register does not recognize the scale label
Check that the label prefix (first 2 digits) is declared under the right type (weight or price), that you have
published, and that the product's barcode is indeed “prefix + item code”.

pages.title: Meal vouchers: tracking and remittance slips

sections.heading: Meal vouchers: tracking and remittance slips
sections.text:
Meal vouchers (paper or card) are taken at the register with the Meal voucher method. The register limits the
amount to the eligible items and to the store's cap, and never gives change. The server re-checks every
sale. Checkout and payments › Meal vouchers totals, day by day, what you must send to the voucher clearing
center.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Accept meal vouchers (once, by the owner)
In Restaurant › Pay at the table, Sales policy card (Checkout settings link at the top of the
Meal vouchers page):
1. check Accept meal vouchers;
2. enter the Cap per ticket (empty = no cap) — in France, the legal cap is 25 € per day;
3. Publish sales policy.
Expected result: “Sales policy published (version 1) — registers apply it at their next sync.”
On the register, the Meal voucher tile at checkout shows “Eligible: … · cap: … · allowed: …” (see
Take a meal voucher). The MV badge marks eligible
products on the ticket lines and on table bills (waiter phone, tablet, register in Tables mode); the **Meal
voucher** line of the X and Z reports totals the vouchers taken per session.
Track the amounts to hand over
Open Checkout and payments › Meal vouchers:
1. Remittance slip (CSV): the file to attach to your remittance;
2. the store and the period (7 days, 30 days, This month, or From / to);
3. To hand over, Sales paid with meal vouchers and Anomalies;
4. Per day: date, store, number of sales, amount, and the total;
5. Checkout settings: the shortcut to the previous step.
Handle anomalies
The Anomalies card lists the sales where the meal voucher exceeded what was allowed when the server re-checked them (1):
date, ticket, cashier, voucher amount (Title column), Allowed amount and Reason. The sale stays
recorded: check it with the cashier.
The possible reasons:
- “Meal vouchers are not accepted in this store”:
the store did not accept vouchers at the time of the sale — see the first step;
- “No item on the receipt is eligible for meal vouchers”: check “Eligible for meal vouchers” on the products concerned;
- “Meal voucher limited to … (eligible items: …, limit: …): pay the rest with another method”: the voucher exceeds the cap
or the eligible part of the ticket.
No sale paid with meal vouchers over the period.
Nothing was paid with meal vouchers on these dates. Widen the period (30 days).
The “Remittance slip (CSV)” button is grayed out
There is no day to hand over in the chosen period.
The register refuses the meal voucher or limits it
The register applies the same rules as the server re-check: the store must accept vouchers, the items must be
eligible, and the cap applies. The register's message says which rule is blocking (see Take a meal voucher).
Report unavailable.
The server could not compute the report. Change the period or reload the page.

pages.title: Organize categories

sections.heading: Organize categories
sections.text:
Categories are the tabs of the sales screen (“Starters”, “Drinks”…). They can be nested up to **three
levels deep**: Drinks › Soft drinks, or Grocery › Teas › Green teas. The color and icon style the
category buttons on the register. Every change is sent to the registers.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Catalog › Categories
The table shows the tree (subcategories are indented under their parent), the number of products, and the order.
New category (1) creates a top-level category; each row (2) has the buttons (3) Edit,
+ Subcategory, and Delete.
Create a category or a subcategory
Click New category, or + Subcategory on the parent row. Fill in:
1. Name — required;
2. Filed under — the parent category (“— Root —” for the top level);
3. Order — the category's rank in lists (smallest numbers first); see “In what order categories appear” below;
4. Color — the category button on the register (No color to reset it to neutral);
5. Icon — an emoji (🥤, 🍊, 🍰…), 16 characters at most.
Click Save.
Check
A banner confirms “Category “Jus de fruits” created.” (1) and the category appears in the tree, with its
color and icon.
To move a category (and its whole branch), click Edit and change Filed under.
Delete a category
Click Delete. If the category contains products, choose where to put them (1): another
category or “— No category —”, then confirm with Delete “…” (2). Cancel (3) closes without doing anything.
Products are never deleted along with the category.
In what order categories appear
Everywhere, categories follow the same rule: first the order you entered (smallest numbers first), then the name,
ignoring capitals, accents and typographic punctuation. Example: “Épices” sorts with the “E”s, between “Entrées” and
“Fromages”. This is the order of the back office, the online menu and the kiosk (iOS and Android); it does not
place the buttons on the register's sales screen. Whether the category comes from your own entry or from an assistant
proposal (Creating or editing a category),
the rule is the same.
Category name is required.
The Name field is empty.
Three category levels at most
The parent category is already at the third level. File the new category one level higher. Variant when
moving: “Three category levels at most (including subcategories)” — the moved branch would become too deep.
A category cannot be placed inside its own branch
You are trying to file a category under one of its own subcategories. Choose another parent.
The category contains 2 subcategory(ies): move or delete them first
A category can only be deleted after its subcategories have been moved (Edit button › Filed under) or deleted.
Category used by …: remove it first
The category is used elsewhere (sales screen, modifier group, preparation stations, kiosk preset), named
in the message. Remove it from that place, then delete it.
Unknown destination category
The category chosen to receive the products has just been deleted elsewhere. Reload the page and choose another destination.
Manager role required
Managing categories requires the Manager role or higher. Ask the owner to change your role in Settings › Team.

pages.title: Barcodes: enter, scan, generate internal codes

sections.heading: Barcodes: enter, scan, generate internal codes
sections.text:
A barcode lets you add an item at the register without searching for it. Two cases:
- the item already has a code on its packaging (EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC): copy it or scan it into the product record;
- the item has none (homemade, bulk, clothing…): generate a Vendora internal code (EAN-13 starting with 20) and print it on a label.
Each code can identify only one product.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Enter or scan the code on a package
Open the product, click the Barcode field (1), scan the packaging with the scanner (or type the
digits), then click Save.
For numeric codes of 8, 12 or 13 digits, Vendora checks the check digit (the last digit). A
typo is rejected, and the message shows the correct last digit (1):
Other codes (letters, Code 128…) are accepted as is.
Generate internal codes for products without a code
Open Catalog › Labels. Check Without barcode only (1) to see only products without a
code, select the products that need a code (2), then click Generate internal codes (3) in the 1. Missing codes block.
The banner confirms “2 internal code(s) generated — sent to the registers at the next sync.” (1).
Generated codes show the internal badge.
Expected result: each chosen product has a unique EAN-13 starting with 20, ready to scan as soon as you
print it (see Print price labels).
Check at the register
Once the register has synced, scan the item: it is added to the ticket. If nothing happens, see below.
Save denied. Invalid check digit: the last digit should be 2
The code you entered contains an error (often two swapped digits). Read the code on the packaging again or scan it.
The digit quoted is the one that would make the code valid — don't replace it “blindly”: if the rest is wrong, the code will not match any package.
Save denied. Codes starting with 20 are reserved for generated internal codes
EAN-13 codes starting with the internal prefix are assigned by Vendora. Leave the field empty and use
Generate internal codes on the Labels page.
Save denied. Barcode already used by another product
The barcode you entered is already assigned to another product. Search for the code in *Catalog ›
Products* to find that product, then correct one of the two.
Generation denied.
The server could not generate the codes (connection, permissions). Try again; if the message persists, check that you have the Manager role.
Excel turned the code into 3.76E+12 during an import
See Import your catalog: set the column to Text format before pasting the codes.
Scanning adds nothing at the register
The register may not have received the code yet (sync), or the product is inactive or not available in
this store. For a product with variants, the code is on the variant, not on the parent.

pages.title: Create and edit a product

sections.heading: Create and edit a product
sections.text:
A product is a line on your menu or an item on your shelves: a name, a price including tax, and a VAT rate.
Every save is sent to the registers, which receive it at their next sync (within a few
seconds if they are online).
Product limit
On the Free plan, you can have 300 active products. Beyond that, creation is refused; your existing products stay sellable and editable. Archiving a product (unchecking Active (visible at the register)) frees a place.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Catalog › Products
In the left menu, open Catalog, then Products. The list shows all your products.
Click New product (1). Use the search (2) to find an existing product and click its name (3) to
open it.
Enter the name, price, and VAT
- Name (1): as it will be printed on the receipt (“Caesar Salad”, “Ground Coffee 250 g”). Required.
- Category (3): places the product on the sales screen. Optional (“— No category —”).
- Reference (SKU) (2): your item code (ENT-005, CAF-250), optional but unique within the business (upper
and lower case are the same). It finds the product in the list, at the register (search) and in the
CSV import.
- Barcode (4): optional; see Barcodes.
- Selling price (major currency unit) (5): the price including tax paid by the customer, in euros (13.5 or 13,50).
- VAT (6): the default rate is suggested; change it if needed (for example, 20% for alcohol). Manage rates opens the list of rates.
Set the sales and stock options, then save
- Availability (1): All stores (default) or This store only (local product, if you have several stores). You can only choose this when you create the product.
- Stock tracking (2): uncheck it for a prepared dish or a service (no quantity to track). For a tracked product, choose its Stock unit — Piece, Kilogram (kg) or Litre (L) —, the unit of its stock and of the recipe sheets that use it as an ingredient (a product sold by weight is always in kg).
- Active (visible at the register) (3): leave it checked to sell the product.
- Eligible for meal vouchers (4): check it for food items that can be paid with meal vouchers.
Click Save (5).
Further down you will find the advanced options: Sold by weight, Scale code (PLU), Expiry tracking
(see Sell by weight). They only appear if one of your stores uses them
(based on its profile, or set in Stores › Modules); otherwise, a note tells you so.
Check in the list
You return to the list, where the product appears with its price, VAT, and Active status (1).
Expected result: the product appears on the registers at their next sync, in its category.
Edit a product
Click the product's name in the list: the Edit product page opens with the same fields.
Make your changes, then click Save. Only the changed fields are sent.
An existing record also has Change history (1) (who changed what and when, in the
audit log) and Back to products (2). Further down: variants, store prices, recipe sheet, combo, and images.
Remove a product from sale (archive)
Products cannot be deleted, because their sales history must be kept. To stop selling it, **uncheck Active
(visible at the register) (1), then click Save**. It disappears from the registers but stays in the reports; check the
box again to put it back on sale.
300 products in the Gratuit plan — Commerce makes them unlimited. Archive a product or change plan.
You have reached your plan's active-product limit (the number and plan names vary). Archive a product you no longer sell or move to a paid plan (The Free plan).
The name is required.
The Name field is empty. Give the product a name.
The sale price must be a positive number.
The price is empty, negative or unreadable. Type only the number, without a symbol: 13,50.
Choose a VAT rate.
No rate is selected (usually because there is no default rate). Choose one, or set a default
rate in VAT rates.
Changed elsewhere — reload.
Someone (or another tab) changed this product while you were editing it. Click **Reload
record**, then make your change again.
Save denied. Barcode already used by another product
The barcode (or, with “Scale code already used by another product”, the scale code) is already assigned to another
product: find it using the product list search, then change one of the two codes.
Save denied. Reference already used by another product
Another product already has this reference (caf-250 and CAF-250 are the same). Look it up in the product list
(the search also reads references) and change one of the two. A badly formed reference (;, #, more than 64
characters…) is flagged under the field: “Letters, digits, space, - _ . / (64 characters max).”.
Save denied. Invalid check digit: the last digit should be …
The EAN / UPC barcode contains a typo. See Barcodes.
Save denied. Manager role required for this store
You are not a manager of the store chosen for a local product. Ask the owner to give you this role
in Settings › Team, or create the product for All stores.
Save failed. Try again.
The server did not respond (connection lost, session expired). Check your connection and try again; reload the page if needed.
The product does not appear on the register
Check that it is Active, that it is available in this store (see Prices and availability by
store) and that the register is online: it receives changes at its
next sync.

pages.title: Print price labels

sections.heading: Print price labels
sections.text:
The Catalog › Labels page generates an A4 sheet as a PDF. Each label shows the product name,
its price including tax, and its EAN-13 barcode, which can be scanned at the register.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Catalog › Labels
The search (1) filters by name or code; the checkbox at the top of the table (2) selects all displayed products; the
right-hand panel (3) has two steps: 1. Missing codes and 2. A4 sheet.
Choose the products
Select the products (or click their rows). The N selected counter updates.
A product without a barcode shows the none badge: first generate its internal code (step **1. Missing
codes**, see Barcodes) Printing stays grayed out as long as a code is missing.
Products with variants are not listed themselves: their variants (“T-shirt — M”…), each with its own price
and barcode, are listed instead.
Set up the sheet and print
- Template (2): 24, 40, or 65 labels per page, to match your sheets;
- Start at cell (3): to reuse a partly used sheet, enter the first empty cell.
Click Print the sheet (PDF) (4).
The PDF downloads, and the banner confirms “Sheet of 2 label(s) generated (template 40, starting at slot 5).” (1).
Print the PDF
Open the PDF and print it at 100% (actual size): turn off “Fit to page,” or the labels
will be misaligned. Before using your label sheets, print a test on plain paper and hold it against a label sheet up to the light.
Expected result: the labels line up with the cells, and each code scans at the register.
The Print the sheet (PDF) button is grayed out
No product is selected, or a selected product has no barcode (“Generate the missing codes
first.”). Generate the internal codes, or uncheck those products.
Start position between 1 and 40
The starting cell exceeds the number of cells of the chosen template. Enter a cell between 1 and the number of labels per page.
No product selected
Select at least one product before printing.
Label sheet rejected.
The server could not produce the PDF (connection issue, expired session, or no store selected). Reload the page and try again.
The labels are misaligned when printed
Print at 100% with no scaling, and check the template (24, 40, or 65) and the A4 paper size in the printer settings.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Barcodes: enter, scan, generate internal codes
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Export your catalog (backup, spreadsheet)

sections.heading: Export your catalog (backup, spreadsheet)
sections.text:
The export creates a catalogue.csv file with one row per product and its Vendora ID. It is the
best starting point for changing many prices at once, and a good backup to keep before a major change.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Catalog › CSV import / export
The Export catalog block is on the left. Optionally choose:
1. Category — “All” or a single category (its subcategories are included);
2. Status — All, Active, or Inactive;
then click Export CSV (3).
Open the file
The browser downloads catalogue.csv to your Downloads folder. Double-click it to open it directly in Excel, LibreOffice, or
Numbers (semicolon-separated, UTF-8 with BOM so accented characters display correctly).
Column · Content
id · Vendora ID. Do not change it: it is what lets the import update the right product.
sku · Your item reference (empty if there is none); it also finds the product on import.
name · Product name
category · Category path, levels separated by > (Boissons > Softs)
barcode · Barcode (empty if there is none)
salePrice / purchasePrice · Selling price including tax / purchase price, decimal comma (16,50)
taxRate · VAT rate in % (10, 5,5)
trackStock, active, mealVoucherEligible · oui / non (yes / no): stock tracking, active, meal vouchers
soldByWeight, scaleCode · sold by weight (oui / non) and scale code (PLU, 5 digits)
trackExpiry, expiryAlertDays · expiry tracking (oui / non) and alert N days before the use-by date
Expected result: a file like this one, exported from the demo business:
Sample export (Le Petit Bistrot, demo)
The 34 active products of a fictional restaurant, with their IDs, references (BOI-001…), nested categories (Boissons > Cafés), prices, and
VAT. Useful for seeing exactly what an export looks like; its id values only exist in the demo business.
(Optional) Edit and re-import
Change prices, names, or statuses in the spreadsheet, save the file in CSV format (not .xlsx), then follow
Import your catalog from a CSV file: the preview shows
each change before it is applied.
What the export does not contain
Variants (axes), modifiers, combo steps, recipe sheets,
store prices, images, and stock quantities are not included in the file. They stay
unchanged when you re-import it.
Export failed.
The server did not respond (connection lost, session expired). Reload the page and try again.
Excel shows the barcodes as 3.76E+12
Excel reformats long numbers. Before re-importing, set the barcode column to Text format, or open
the file via Data › From Text/CSV and choose Text for that column.
The whole file is in a single column
Your spreadsheet app expects commas as separators. Use Data › Text to Columns (Excel) or choose the ; separator when opening (LibreOffice).
Manager role required
Exporting is limited to the Manager, Administrator, and Owner roles.

sections.text:
- Import your catalog from a CSV file
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Recipe sheet for a dish

sections.heading: Recipe sheet for a dish
sections.text:
The recipe sheet lists the ingredients of one portion: 1 beef patty, 1 bun, 40 g of cheddar, 200 g of
fries. Each time the dish is sold, the register deducts these quantities from stock; the dish itself is no longer tracked in stock.
The block also calculates the cost price, the food cost (cost ÷ price excl. VAT), and the margin per portion.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Prepare the ingredients
Create each ingredient as a product (Create and edit a product) with
Stock tracking checked, and choose its Stock unit: Piece for a counted item (bun, portioned patty),
Kilogram (kg) for a weighed item (cheese, fries), Litre (L) for a liquid (oil, cream). Ingredients **sold by
weight are always in kg. Uncheck Active** so an ingredient does not appear at the register, and group them in an
“Ingredients” category, for example. Their costs come from your goods receipts (Stock and purchasing): per kg, per
litre or per piece depending on the unit.
Add the ingredients to the dish
Open the dish, scroll down to the Recipe sheet block, and type an ingredient's name in **Add an ingredient
(stock-tracked product)** (1). Click the suggestion (2). Repeat for each ingredient.
Enter the quantities per portion
In Quantity per portion, type the quantity in the unit shown next to it (1): piece for a counted ingredient
(1), g or kg for an ingredient by the kilo (40 g), cl, ml or L for a liquid (2 cl).
Changing the unit converts the quantity already typed (40 g → 0.04 kg). The Unit cost (per kg, per L or per
piece) and Cost columns fill in, and at the bottom (2), Cost price, Selling price excl. VAT, Food cost,
and Margin per portion update as you type. Click Publish the sheet (3).
Check that it is published
The banner confirms “Version 1 published and sent to the registers: each sale now takes its ingredients out of
stock.” (1) and the Version badge (2) appears. Version history keeps every published version.
Expected result: each burger sold deducts 1 patty, 1 bun, 40 g of cheddar, 200 g of fries and 2 cl of sauce
from the store's stock; the Food cost report (Restaurant) tracks ingredient costs.
To delete the recipe sheet, remove all the ingredients and publish: “Recipe removed (version N): the dish is an ordinary product again.”
The “unknown cost” badge appears instead of the unit cost
The ingredient has no cost yet in this store (no goods receipt). Record a goods receipt
with its purchase price. Costs shown are those of the store selected at the top of the screen.
An ingredient is not suggested in the search
Only products with stock tracking are suggested. Open the ingredient, check Stock tracking, and save.
Quantity of “Cheddar affiné (kg)”: a positive number, in the chosen unit (e.g. 150 g, 2 cl, 1 piece)
The quantity is empty, zero, or invalid. For 40 g of an ingredient by the kilo, type 40 with the g unit (or
0.04 with kg).
The ingredient shows in pieces although it is weighed (or the other way round)
Its Stock unit is wrong. Open the ingredient, choose Kilogram (kg), Litre (L) or Piece, save, then
come back to the recipe sheet. Recipe sheets created before units existed received a unit deduced from the
ingredient's name (“Cheddar (kg)” → kg, “Oil (L)” → L, otherwise piece): check it. Note that the saved quantity does
not change: 1 piece becomes 1 kg; correct the quantity in the sheet and publish again.
“…” belongs to another store.
The ingredient is a local product of another store. Use an ingredient available in the dish's store.
Publishing failed.
The server did not respond, or the sheet was changed in the meantime. Reload the page and try again.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Create and edit a product
- Create a combo (set menu) with steps
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Create a combo (set menu) with steps

sections.heading: Create a combo (set menu) with steps
sections.text:
A combo sells several products for one price: “Kids Menu = 1 main + 1 drink + 1 dessert”. It is
made up of steps (Main, Drink, Dessert…), each with its own choices and a minimum / maximum number of choices.
A choice can have a surcharge (+1 € for ice cream). Each chosen product keeps its own preparation station,
stock, and VAT; the combo itself does not track stock.
Turning “Menu enfant” into a combo: three steps, a whole category, a surcharge, publication.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open the combo product
First create the product that will hold the combo (see Create and edit a product):
its selling price is the combo's base price. Open it, scroll down to the **Combo (set
menu) block, and click Turn into a combo** (1).
This button is not available for products sold by weight or with variants (“A product sold by weight or with variants cannot be a combo.”).
Build a step
An empty first step appears. For each step:
1. Step name — “Main”, “Drink”… (60 characters at most);
2. Minimum / Maximum — how many choices the customer makes. 1 / 1 = one required choice; 0 / 1 = optional step (“Dessert?”); 2 / 2 = two choices;
3. the choices table — product, Catalog price, Surcharge; the X removes a choice;
4. the tools for adding choices:
- Add a whole category: choose the category, then Add whole category (its active products, except combos, products sold by weight, and products with variants);
- Or search for products: type a name, check the product, then Add selection (n) — you can
run several searches in a row, and all checked products are added;
- Same surcharge for all choices + Apply to all (once there are at least two choices).
Several searches, one click to add
Check “Nuggets”, then type “croque” and check “Croque-monsieur”: the button shows **Add
selection (2)** and adds both products.
A combo has no Variants or Recipe sheet: these sections disappear from its record (its cost and
stock come from the chosen products).
Add the other steps and the surcharges
Click Add a step (12 steps at most) and repeat. Each step's arrows move it up or down
(or drag the ⋮⋮ handle); the trash icon deletes it.
For a paid choice, type the amount in its Surcharge box (1): 1 or 0,80.
On the right, What the customer sees summarizes the combo as it will appear at the register and on the kiosk:
Save the combo
Click Save combo. The banner confirms “Combo published (version 1), sent to registers and
kiosks.” (1); the Version badge (2) goes up each time you publish.
Expected result: in the product list, the Combo badge appears; at the register, tapping the combo
opens its steps one by one. Version history (at the bottom of the block) lists every published version.
To turn it back into an ordinary product, click Remove combo, then Confirm removal.
Add at least one choice.
A step has no product. Add choices or delete the step (trash icon).
At least one step must be required (minimum ≥ 1).
All steps have a minimum of 0: the combo could be sold empty. Set at least one step to minimum 1.
The maximum exceeds the number of choices.
The step asks for more choices than it offers (maximum 3 for 2 products). Lower the maximum or add products.
The minimum exceeds the maximum.
The minimum must be less than or equal to the maximum. Other messages for the same field: “The minimum cannot be
negative.” and “The maximum must be at least 1.”
Name the step.
A step has no name. Related message: “Two steps have the same name.” — rename one of them.
Surcharge for “…”: a positive amount (e.g. 1 or 0.80).
The surcharge box contains something other than a positive amount. Leave it empty for a choice with no surcharge.
“…” is a choice of the combo “…”: no combo inside a combo.
This product is already offered in another active combo, so it cannot become a combo itself. Create a
separate product for the combo. The reverse case shows: ““…” is a combo: no combo inside a combo.”
“…” has variants: choose the variants themselves.
A product with variants cannot be a choice: add its variants (“T-shirt — M”, “T-shirt — L”…).
The same applies to ““…” is sold by weight: not possible in a combo.”
“…” belongs to another store.
A store-specific combo can only offer products available in that store.
Combo changed elsewhere in the meantime: reload to start from the latest version (your unpublished changes will be lost).
Someone published the combo while you were editing it. Click Reload, then make your changes again.
Publishing failed.
The server did not respond. Check your connection and click Save combo again.

pages.title: Import your catalog from a CSV file

sections.heading: Import your catalog from a CSV file
sections.text:
Do you have your menu or items in a spreadsheet, or a file from a supplier? The CSV import creates
missing products, updates existing ones, and creates categories along the way. Nothing changes until
you have reviewed the preview and clicked Apply.
The import in 20 seconds: choose the file, read the preview, apply.

sections.heading: Prepare the file
sections.text:
The easiest way is to start from an export of your catalog (step 2), edit it in your spreadsheet, and re-import it.
You can also start from one of the sample files below.
Column · Accepted French header · Content · Example
id · identifiant · The product's Vendora ID (from the export). Leave empty for a new product. · 1deb3a3c-…
sku · référence, réf, code article · Your item reference (1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, space, - _ . /), unique within the business — upper and lower case are the same. Optional. · CAF-250
name · nom, désignation, libellé · Product name. Required for new products. · Croissant
category · catégorie · Category path, levels separated by > (3 levels at most). Created if it does not exist. · Boissons > Chaudes > Thés
barcode · code-barres, EAN · Barcode (EAN-13, EAN-8, and UPC-A are validated; any other text is accepted as is). · 3760999000012
salePrice · prix de vente TTC, prix de vente, prix · Sale price including VAT (all taxes included) in currency units, with a comma or period. A “prix de vente HT” (excluding VAT) header is refused. Required for new products. · 12,50
purchasePrice · prix d'achat · Purchase price (for margins). · 4,20
taxRate · TVA, taux de TVA · Rate in %, which must exist in your VAT rates. Empty = default rate. · 10 or 5,5
trackStock · suivi du stock · oui / non (also yes, vrai, 1…). Default: yes. · non
active · actif · oui / non. An inactive product no longer appears at the register. Default: yes. · oui
mealVoucherEligible · titre-restaurant · oui / non: can be paid with meal vouchers. Default: no. · oui
soldByWeight · vendu au poids · oui / non: sold by weight (the selling price is then the price per kg). · oui
scaleCode · PLU, code balance · Scale code of 1 to 5 digits (padded on the left), unique in the catalog. · 123
trackExpiry · péremption · oui / non: expiry tracking (batch and use-by date at receiving) — requires stock tracking. · oui
expiryAlertDays · alerte DLC · Alert N days before the use-by date, from 0 to 365. Default: 30. · 7
Key rules:
- Separator: semicolon ; (used by Excel in French) or comma ,. It is detected automatically from the header row.
- How Vendora finds a product: by its id; otherwise by its reference (sku, upper and lower case are the
same); otherwise by its barcode; otherwise, the row creates a new product. The easiest way to update a
supplier's file: a référence column with your item codes.
The name is never used to find a product: two “Croissant” rows without an id or barcode create two products.
- Empty cell = value unchanged for an existing product. Columns missing from the file are not changed either.
- The import never touches stock (quantities are managed in Stock and purchasing).
- Up to 10,000 rows per file.
- The sale price is always including VAT. A supplier's file is often priced excluding VAT: work out the VAT-inclusive price in your spreadsheet before importing. A “prix de vente HT” header is refused with this reminder.
- VAT of a new product: the rate must exist in your VAT rates; an empty cell = your default rate, which the preview shows (“default rate”).
- VAT of an existing product: changing it is allowed, but the preview lists it in a box and you must tick a confirmation box before applying. Giving a product the rate it already has changes nothing, even if that rate is no longer in your list.
- Product with variants: its VAT and its variants' VAT are set on the product page, never by CSV. The other columns of a variant (found by its id) can still be edited; creating variants by CSV is not possible.
- Stores: in a business with several stores, you choose the store for the new products (step 3). A store that has overridden a product's VAT or price keeps its value: the preview says so.

sections.heading: Sample files
sections.text:
Simple catalog (bakery-café)
Eight products and three categories (Viennoiseries, Pâtisseries, Boissons fraîches), headers in French:
référence;nom;catégorie;code-barres;prix de vente TTC;prix d'achat;TVA;suivi du stock;actif. Each product has its
reference (VIE-001, PAT-001, BOI-001…): imported again later with other prices, the file updates the same
products. The drinks have a barcode and stock tracking; the pastries do not. Imported as is: 8 products and 3 categories created.
Nested categories
Shows category paths: Boissons > Chaudes > Thés, Épicerie fine > Confitures… Each missing
level is created (3 levels at most). Only four columns: name;category;salePrice;taxRate — the others
use their default values. Uses the 10% and 5.5% rates: if they do not exist in your account, see
If it doesn't work.
Update by identifier
What an update looks like: the id column identifies the product, and only filled cells change.
Row 2: new selling price (2,20); row 4: new name; row 5: product deactivated (active = non).
The IDs in this file belong to the demo business: if you import it as is, each row
shows “id inconnu : …” (unknown ID). For your own updates, use the IDs from your export.
File with errors (for practice)
Eleven rows, nine of them deliberately wrong: the preview shows one error per row (see step 5) and
will not apply the file. A safe way to learn how to read the report.
Product limit
On the Free plan, the catalog has at most 300 active products. If the file would create more, the preview says so and the Apply button stays grayed out: the import would be refused as a whole and nothing would be imported. Remove rows, archive products (uncheck Active) or move to a paid plan. Updates to existing products do not count.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Catalog › CSV import / export
In the left menu, open Catalog (1), then CSV import / export (2).
Shortcut: type “csv” in the Go to… search at the top of the screen.
(Recommended) Export the current catalog
The page has two parts: Export catalog (1) and Import a file (2).
Optionally choose a category and a status, then click Export CSV to get catalogue.csv, with
the right columns and each product's id. It is the best template — and a backup before you change anything.
Re-importing an export without changing it changes nothing
Every row shows “Unchanged”. So you can export, adjust a few prices, and re-import the whole file.
Choose the file: the preview appears
Before the file, look at the New products for list (it appears as soon as you have more than one store):
- All stores (default): the products created are sold everywhere. Not possible if your active stores do not all share the same currency and country.
- One store: the products created are sold only in that store, in its currency. This is mandatory when your stores have several currencies or countries (for example one in France and one in Tunisia): otherwise every creation is refused and a banner asks you to choose a store. Choose one, then click Analyse again: the file is kept, no need to choose it again. Only the stores you are responsible for are offered.
Products that already exist keep their scope and currency.
Then click CSV file and choose your file. It is analyzed without changing anything. The report shows:
1. the summary: creations, updates, unchanged, errors, and the categories that will be created;
2. one line per row in the file (numbered as in the spreadsheet, with the header as row 1), with the planned action and the details of the changes;
3. the Apply button, which shows the number of new products and updates.
For an update, the Details column shows each changed value as before → after:
If there are more than 20 unchanged rows, the Hide unchanged rows box is checked automatically so you only see what changes.
For each product created, the preview shows what you will really get: the VAT rate (name from your rates, then the percentage, for example “TVA normale 20 % — 20 % (default rate)” when the cell was empty), the VAT-inclusive price in the product's currency and, above the table, “Prices incl. VAT in EUR — for all stores” (or “… — for” the chosen store). A price of 0 gets the note “Sale price is 0”: it is not an error, but check it.
If the file changes the VAT of existing products, a box “This file changes the VAT of existing products” lists each product (“Name: 19 % → 7 %”). Sales already made keep their rate; the new VAT applies to future sales. The Apply button stays grayed out until you tick “I confirm the VAT change of … products”.
Notes on a row: “{store} keeps its overridden VAT (… %)” or “{store} keeps its overridden price (…)” mean a store has its own value, which the import does not touch. The “Specific to store {store}” badge marks a product created for a single store: you can change it only if you are responsible for that store (otherwise the row is an error from the preview).
Apply
If everything looks right, click Apply (… new, … update(s)). The whole file is applied
at once (never partially), and a message confirms the result:
Expected result: the products appear in Catalog › Products, and on the registers at their
next sync (within a few seconds if they are online). The import is recorded in the audit log: every product and category written carries the mention “CSV import “file””, and the import's own entry keeps the list of VAT changes.
If there are errors: fix and re-import
If even one row has an error, nothing is applied: the red banner (1) says so, each
faulty row explains why (2), and the Apply button stays grayed out (3). Fix the file in your spreadsheet,
save it, then choose it again to get a new preview.
This file would add … product(s) too many: your plan is limited to … active products. The import would be refused as a whole and nothing would be imported. Remove rows, archive products or change plan.
Shown in the preview. The file would create more products than your plan allows. Nothing was imported. Remove creation rows, archive products you no longer sell, or move to a paid plan (The Free plan).
Import refused, nothing was imported: … product(s) over the limit. 300 products in the Gratuit plan — Commerce makes them unlimited. (… active, … more with this file.)
Same cause, when applying (the catalog changed since the preview). Nothing was imported: shorten the file or archive products, then run the import again.
VAT rate 10 % not in the list
The rate in the VAT column does not exist (or is disabled) in your rates. Two solutions: add it in
Catalog › VAT rates, or empty the cell to give the product your default rate.
Same message with another rate (“taux de TVA 7 % absent du référentiel”…). Write the rate as a percentage:
10, 5,5 or 20 % — not 0,10.
unreadable VAT rate: …
The VAT cell does not contain a number between 0 and 100 (e.g. dix, 10/20). Enter a single rate in digits.
no default VAT rate
The VAT cell is empty and no rate is marked “default”. In Catalog › VAT rates, choose
a default rate, or fill in the VAT column.
sale price required to create a product
The row creates a product (no id or known barcode) but the selling price column is empty. Enter the
price including tax. If you meant to edit an existing product, add its id (taken from the export) or its barcode.
name required to create a product
Same case for the name: a creation needs a name. Often an empty or half-filled row at the bottom of the file: delete it.
unknown id: …
The id does not match any product in your catalog: an id copied from another business (like the sample
update file), truncated by the spreadsheet, or made up. Take the ids from a recent export, or **empty the
id cell** so the row creates the product (or finds it by its barcode).
sale price: 2 decimal place(s) at most (1,999)
Too many decimals for the currency (2 for the euro, 3 for the dinar). Round it: 2,00. The same message exists for the purchase price.
sale price unreadable: …
The price is not a positive number: currency symbol attached (12€), text, negative number. Keep only the number: 12,50.
stock tracking: yes or no expected (peut-être)
The yes / no columns (stock tracking, active, meal vouchers) accept oui, non, yes, no, vrai, faux, 1, 0. Nothing else.
Invalid check digit: the last digit should be 8
The EAN / UPC barcode has a typo: its last digit (the check digit) does not match the others.
Check the code on the packaging. Watch out: Excel often turns long codes into 3,761E+12 — set the
column to Text format before pasting the codes.
barcode … already on row 9
The same barcode appears twice in the file. Each barcode identifies a single product: delete the duplicate or correct the code.
barcode … already used by “…”
This barcode already belongs to another product in your catalog (named in quotation marks). If it is the same
product, add its id to the row; otherwise, correct the code.
reference … already on row 4
The same reference appears twice in the file (upper and lower case are the same: caf-001 = CAF-001). Each
reference identifies a single product: delete the duplicate or change the reference.
reference … already used by “…”
This reference already belongs to another product in your catalog (named in quotation marks) while the row points
to a different product (by its id or barcode). If it is the same product, remove the id or barcode from the row;
otherwise, choose another reference.
reference: 1 to 64 characters (letters, digits, space, - _ . /) (…)
The reference contains a refused character (;, #, *, quotes…), starts with a sign, or is longer than 64
characters. Keep letters, digits, spaces and - _ . /: CAF-250, 12/B, THE.VERT_100.
Codes starting with … are reserved for generated internal codes
EAN-13 codes starting with this prefix are assigned automatically by Vendora to products without a code.
Leave the cell empty: an internal code can be generated from the product record.
same product as row …
Two rows identify the same product (same id, or same barcode). Merge them into a single row.
category “…”: three levels at most
Categories nest on three levels at most (Boissons > Chaudes > Thés). Shorten the path.
Unknown column(s): …
A header column is not recognized (typo, extra column such as “Stock” or “Description”).
Rename it with one of the headers in the table above, or delete it. The whole file is rejected as long as it remains.
At least one name, id, sku (reference) or barcode column is required
Without any of these four columns, Vendora can neither create nor find a product. Check that the **first
row** of the file contains the headers (not a title or an empty row).
Empty file: the first line must contain the headers
The file is empty or starts with an empty row. Delete the rows above the headers.
File too long: 10,000 rows at most
Split the file into several files of fewer than 10,000 rows each (keeping the header row in each one) and import them one at a time.
Accents display incorrectly (“Ã©”, “�”) in the preview
The file is not saved in UTF-8. In Excel: File › Save As › CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited); in LibreOffice: check Edit filter settings, character set Unicode (UTF-8),
separator ;. Then re-import it (no products were changed, since you had not applied the import).
Everything is in a single column, or “Colonne(s) inconnue(s)” lists the whole row
The separator is neither ; nor , (often a tab, in a .txt or .tsv file). Save it again in CSV format.
… row(s) with errors (the catalog may have changed since the analysis): fix the file and run the import again
Between the preview and the click on Apply, the catalog changed (a colleague edited a product, another import
went through) and some rows are no longer valid. Nothing was applied: choose the file again for an up-to-date preview.
The catalog has changed since the analysis (rows 4, 9): analyse the file again, nothing was written.
Between the preview and Apply, a product or a permission changed (a colleague edited a product, another import went through, your role no longer covers a store). The numbers are the rows concerned. Nothing was written: click Analyse again to see what changed, then apply.
This file was analysed before a server update: analyse it again before applying it.
The preview dates from before a Vendora update. Nothing is written: analyse the file again.
The sale price is written including VAT: rename the column “Prix de vente TTC”.
The file header says “prix de vente HT” (or “prix HT”). Vendora only reads VAT-inclusive prices: work out the VAT-inclusive price in your spreadsheet (price excl. VAT × (1 + VAT rate)), rename the column Prix de vente TTC, and import again.
This business has stores in several currencies or countries: choose the store for the new products (they will be sold only in that store).
Every creation is refused until a store is chosen, because “all stores” would give a wrong currency or rate for some of them. Choose a store under New products for, then Analyse again. Updates to existing products are not affected.
No active store: create or reactivate a store before creating products.
All creations are refused: a created product needs an active store to know its currency. Create or reactivate a store in Settings › Stores.
Store “…” is archived: choose another store for the new products.
The chosen store was archived since the analysis. Choose another store under New products for. The message “Manager role required on store “…” to create products there” means you are not responsible for that store: choose one you are responsible for, or ask an administrator.
The VAT of a product with variants is set on its product page.
The row changes the VAT of a product that has variants, or of a variant. Put the current rate back in the file (or empty the cell), then set the VAT from the product page (Catalog › Products).
Product specific to store …: Manager role required on that store
The row changes a product created for a single store that you are not responsible for. Remove the row or ask the store's manager (or an administrator) to run the import. A row that changes nothing about that product is never refused.
The name contains an invisible character
A new or changed name is refused if it contains an invisible character (zero-width space, line break…), a quotation mark (“The name cannot contain quotation marks”) or more than 120 characters (“Name too long: 120 characters at most”). Such names would be printed on the receipt. Retype the name by hand in the spreadsheet. A name you do not change is never refused.
Apply stays grayed out although there is no error, and a “VAT changes” box appears
The file changes the VAT of existing products: tick “I confirm the VAT change of … products” after reading the list. If that is not intended, fix the VAT column in the file (or empty it: an empty cell changes nothing on an existing product).
Import already applied
This preview has already been applied (double-click, or two tabs open). Check the result in Catalog › Products; do not apply it again.
Manager role required
Import and export are limited to the Manager, Administrator, and Owner roles. Ask a manager to do it,
or ask the owner to change your role in Settings › Team.
The file could not be parsed.
The server did not respond (connection lost, session expired). Check your connection, reload the page and try again.
Do the same for “The import could not be applied.” and “Export failed.”
Products are created twice instead of being updated
Without an id, reference or barcode, a row always creates a product (the name is not used to find a product).
Start from an export to get the id values, or give your products a reference. You can deactivate duplicates that were already created in Catalog › Products.

sections.text: Everything you sell: products, categories, VAT rates, options (modifiers), combos, variants, import from a spreadsheet, and labels.

pages.title: Search, filter, activate / deactivate products

sections.heading: Search, filter, activate / deactivate products
sections.text:
The Catalog › Products page lists everything your registers can sell. It shows 10 products per page,
sorted by name.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Search for a product
Type a few letters of the name, the reference or the barcode in Search by name, reference or barcode… (1):
the list filters as you type and is not case-sensitive. A product's reference is shown in small type under its name
(“Ref. CAF-250”). The counter (2) shows how many products were found;
the Status column (3) tells you whether a product is Active or Inactive.
Filter by type or availability
Once you have at least one combo, an All types filter (1) appears: choose Combos or **Simple
products. If you have store-specific products, a second filter offers All stores / Local products**.
The badges next to the name summarize the product: Combo (2), By weight, N variant(s),
Expiry, Local: (store).
Browse pages
If you have more than 10 products, use Previous / Next at the bottom of the table (1). Search always
covers the whole catalog, though.
Activate or deactivate a product
Open the product (click its name), check or uncheck Active (visible at the register) in the **Sales and
stock section, then click Save**. An inactive product disappears from the registers at their next sync but
keeps its history (see Create and edit a product).
To deactivate many products at once, export the catalog, enter non in the active column,
and re-import the file (Import your catalog).
Expected result: the Status column shows Inactive for the product.
No matching products.
The search or filter returns no results. Clear the search, set the filter back to All types, and check
the spelling. To search by barcode, enter the exact code (or part of it).
Could not load
The list could not be loaded (connection lost, session expired). Reload the page; sign in again if needed.
A product with variants has no barcode in the list (“—”)
For a product with variants, the list shows “—”: each variant has its own barcode (see
Products with variants).

- Export your catalog
