pages.title: Offer options: modifiers and add-ons

sections.heading: Offer options: modifiers and add-ons
sections.text:
A modifier group groups options together: “Doneness” (rare, medium rare, medium, well done), “Sauce,”
“Burger add-ons” (bacon +1,50 €)… When the waiter adds a matching product, the register or floor
phone shows the group. A required group must be filled in before the order can be sent to the kitchen;
add-on prices are added to the line price.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Catalog › Modifiers
On the left is the list of groups (1) with their rule (“1 required choice,” “up to 3 choices”) and the number
of options and products. Click a group to open it and see Minimum choices / Maximum choices (2) and its
Options (3).
Create a group and its options
Click New group, then:
1. the group Name, as waiters will see it (“Sauce salade”);
2. Minimum choices and Maximum choices: 1 / 1 = one required choice (doneness); 0 / 2 = up to two optional choices; removals (“No onion”): 0 / number of options;
3. the Options: a name and, for a paid add-on, a price (1,50). An empty price or 0 = free. Add an option adds a row; the X removes it.
Choose the products
There are two ways, which you can combine:
- Included categories: all products in the category, including those created later;
- Affected products (1): check the products one by one (2).
Leave Active (offered in the dining room) checked, then click Save. Archived products, badges and categories are
explained below, in Archived products, attachments with no effect, and categories.
Check
The banner confirms ““Sauce salade” saved (version 1) — sent to the registers at the next sync.” (1).
The History section keeps every version (who and when).
Expected result: at the register, adding a Salade César opens the sauce options; parmesan adds 1,50 € to the line.
To stop offering a group without losing it, uncheck Active (offered in the dining room) and save.

sections.heading: Archived products, attachments with no effect, and categories
sections.text:
In Affected products, three cases deserve an explanation.
- An archived product stays attached. If you archive a product that belongs to a group, the group keeps it: saving the
group for another reason (name, add-on price) does not silently remove it. It is shown with the Archived badge and can
still be unchecked: to really remove it, uncheck it and save. An archived product that is not attached is not offered in
the list.
- Some attachments have no effect. They are never refused: the product can still be checked, but a badge tells you where
the options will (or will not) be offered.
Badge · What it means
“Options are chosen on each variant” · A product with variants (size, flavour…): attach the group to its variants, not to the parent product.
“A combo offers the options of its choices” · A combo never offers options on itself: not at the register, not at the kiosk, not in the online menu, not in online ordering. Options are chosen on the products that make it up (attach the group to those products).
“Not offered at the till or kiosk” · A product sold by weight does not open an options choice at the register or at the kiosk. Dining-room order taking still offers them today: current behaviour, expected to change.
- A category does not cover its subcategories. A group attached to the “Mains” category applies to products filed
directly in “Mains” (and their variants), not to those in “Mains › Burgers”. Attach the subcategory as well, or check
the products one by one. The rule is the same on the register, the kiosk, dining-room ordering, the online menu and online
ordering.

sections.heading: In what order are the groups shown?
sections.text:
When a product has several groups (“Cuisson,” “Accompagnement,” “Sauces”…), they appear in the same order on the iPhone / iPad
register, the Android register, the kiosk, table ordering, the online menu and online ordering: the order in which they were
created; when that is equal, by name, ignoring capital letters and accents (“Épices” sorts with the “E”s). The cart line
label follows the same order.
Current limit: there is no screen yet to change this order, and the back-office list sorts groups by name: it can
therefore differ from what the customer or waiter sees. This is not a display error.

sections.heading: An add-on follows the product's VAT rate
sections.text:
An add-on is sold at the VAT rate of the product it is added to. Advice: if an option has a different tax nature
(an alcoholic drink as an add-on to a dish, for example), sell it as a separate product with its own rate rather than
as an add-on. This advice does not replace your accountant's opinion.

sections.heading: An add-on price is capped
sections.text:
An option's price cannot exceed 10,000,000.00 € (1,000,000.000 DT in Tunisia). The rule applies to the options
you create or whose price you change; an option already saved is left alone until you touch it.

sections.heading: When the assistant proposes a group
sections.text:
Your AI assistant can propose creating a group or editing one (extra prices, options, number of choices, deactivation); you
read and approve it in the back office, and the group changes as if you had saved it by hand. It does not attach the group
to products in that proposal: that is done here, under Products concerned, or by a separate proposal, **Attach or detach a modifier
group**. Details:
Creating or editing a modifier group
and Attaching or detaching a modifier group.
The assistant is then stricter than this screen: it refuses a parent with variants, a combo, a product sold by weight and an
archived product, which you can tick here with a badge.
Save denied. “Sauce salade”: add at least one option
A group needs at least one option with a name. Other rules of the same kind:
““…”: the minimum exceeds the maximum”, ““…”: maximum at least 1”,
““…”: maximum greater than the number of options”,
““…”: duplicate option “…””, ““…”: an option has no name”,
““…”: negative price for “…””. Fix the field mentioned.
Save denied. The group has no name
Give the group a name.
Invalid price: a positive number, e.g. 1,500.
An option's price is not a positive number. Type only the amount, without “€”: 1,50.
This group was changed elsewhere: the latest version has been reloaded.
Someone else saved this group at the same time. The latest version is now displayed: make your change again and save.
This surcharge is too high (maximum …).
An option's price is above the cap. The message states the maximum in the shop's currency (1,000,000.000 DT for a Tunisian
shop); when the currency is not known it only says “This surcharge is too high.” The faulty option is outlined in red and
your entry is kept: correct that price (a real add-on is far lower, 1,50) and save again.
This group was just created elsewhere: the list is up to date. Check before saving again.
Another device or tab has just saved this same new group. Nothing is lost: the list has already been reloaded and what
you typed is kept. Check whether the group that was created suits you; if you save again, a second group is created.
The group does not appear at the register on a product
Check that the group is Active, that the product (or its category) is checked, and that the register has synced.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Create a combo (set menu) with steps
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Add photos to a product

sections.heading: Add photos to a product
sections.text:
A photo helps your team find the right button and makes products more appealing on the kiosk. The first image is the main
image: registers keep a thumbnail of it so they can display it even when offline.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open the product and scroll down to Images
In Catalog › Products, click the product name, then scroll to the
Images section at the bottom of the record. A reminder of the rules (1): PNG, JPEG or WebP, 5 MB max, 10 images. Click Add images (2).
Choose one or more photos
Select your files (you can pick several at once). They upload one at a time, and “Sending…”
is shown during the upload. There is nothing to save: images are stored as soon as they finish uploading.
- The Main badge (1) marks the main image.
- The Main button (2) under another image makes it the main image.
- Remove (3) deletes the image.
Check the thumbnail
Back in the product list, the thumbnail (1) appears next to the name.
Expected result: the registers and kiosks show the main image after their next sync — including on the sales screen's quick buttons (wide tile, or any tile on a tablet), even offline.
Photos that look good
Photograph the product on its own, from the front, against a plain background; a square image (for example, 800 × 800 px) looks best
on buttons. There is no need to upload multi-megabyte photos: they are resized automatically.
WebP photos (often those from supplier websites) are accepted as they are: Vendora converts them for the
registers and kiosks.
…: Format not accepted (HEIC): PNG, JPEG or WebP accepted
The file is in another format, named in parentheses: HEIC (iPhone photo), GIF, AVIF, BMP, TIFF, SVG, PDF…
Convert it to JPEG (on iPhone: Settings › Camera › Formats › Most Compatible; on a computer: “Export as JPEG”).
…: Image too large (5 MB at most)
Reduce the photo (size or quality) before uploading it. Above 5 MB, the message can also be
“File too large (5 MB max)”.
…: Image too small (at least 64 px per side)
The image is tiny (often an icon copied from a website). Use a larger photo.
…: Unreadable image
The file is damaged or is not really an image (for example, a renamed extension). Reopen it in a photo app and save it again as JPEG.
…: 10 images at most per product
Remove an image before adding another one.
The Images section does not appear
It only appears on a product that has already been saved. Create the product first, then reopen it from the list.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Create and edit a product
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Prices and availability by store

sections.heading: Prices and availability by store
sections.text:
The catalog is shared by all your stores. The Prices by store section of a product record lets you set
exceptions: a higher price downtown, a different VAT rate, or a product that is not sold in one
store. Any field left empty uses the product's value. It is also useful with a single store to temporarily
take a product off sale without editing the record.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open the product and the Prices by store section
Open the product from Catalog › Products and scroll down to the Prices by store section: one row per
store. In the store's row:
1. Selling price — empty = product price (shown grayed out); otherwise, this store's price including VAT;
2. VAT — “Inherited (10%)” or another active rate;
3. Available — uncheck it so this store's registers no longer offer the product;
4. Save — saves the row.
Check
The banner confirms “Le Petit Bistrot (démo): saved and sent to the store's registers.” (3). The row shows the
overridden badge (1); Restore (2) clears the exception and goes back to the product's values. A product that is not
available shows the not sold badge.
Expected result: only this store's registers sell the product at this price (or no longer offer it).
Create a product for a single store
If you have several stores, the New product form includes an Availability option (1): All stores
or This store only (then choose the store). A local product only exists in that store: other stores cannot
sell it or receive it by transfer. You make this choice when you create the product.
Later, an owner or administrator can make it available to all stores with the **Make available in all
stores button on the record (this cannot be undone). In the list, these products show the Local: (store)** badge.
Vendora refuses the extension (nothing is changed) in three cases:
- a store of the business does not have the same currency as the product: its price and VAT rate only hold for one currency;
- a store belongs to another tax country than the original store: the product's VAT rate only holds for one country;
- the product has variants (or is a variant): they would stay specific to the original store.
Archived stores do not count. The message names the stores concerned. Instead, create the product separately in the other store (with its price, currency and VAT rate). The same rule applies when the AI assistant proposes the extension (see Approving the assistant's proposals).
The price cannot be negative
Enter a positive price, or clear the field to use the product's price.
VAT rate 7 % not in the list: add it in Catalog › VAT rates
The chosen rate no longer exists or has been deactivated. Add it or reactivate it in VAT rates.
Manager role required on this store.
You are not a manager of this store, so its row is grayed out. Ask the owner.
Store archived
The store is archived: its prices can no longer be changed.
Store “…” does not use this product's currency (EUR): a product can only be extended to all stores if every one of them has the same currency.
The product is sold in a different currency from one of the business's stores. It cannot become shared: create it separately in the store named, with its price in that currency. A store you no longer use can be archived (store settings): it then stops blocking the extension.
Store “…” belongs to a different tax country than “…”: the product's VAT rate only applies to one country.
The VAT rate on the record is that of the original store's country. Create the product separately in the store named, with the rate of its country.
“…” has variants: they would remain specific to the original store. Variants cannot be extended to all stores.
A product with variants cannot be extended to all stores. Create the product (and its variants) separately in the other store.
“…” belongs to the store …: it does not exist in this store
A local product can only be set for its own store.
Prices by store unavailable.
The section could not load. Reload the page.

sections.text:
- Create and edit a product
- Manage VAT rates
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Control discounts granted at the register

sections.heading: Control discounts granted at the register
sections.text:
At the register, a discount can be applied to a line or to the whole receipt, as a percentage or a fixed amount. The
Catalog › Discounts page sets two thresholds per store: above either one, the register requires a reason and a
manager PIN, even offline. The server recalculates every discount and flags those that exceed the threshold
without a valid approval.
No automatic promotions
Vendora does not support scheduled promotions yet (“buy 2, get the 3rd free,” happy hour). Discounts are
applied manually at the register; loyalty discounts come from the loyalty program tiers.
For a long-term price reduction, change the product's price (or its price in a store).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Catalog › Discounts and choose the store
Choose the store at the top of the page. The badge (4) shows “Never published — default thresholds” or the
published version. The defaults are 10% and 20 €.
1. Percentage threshold — for example, 10%;
2. Amount threshold — for example, 15 € (empty = default of 20 €);
3. Reasons offered above the thresholds — one reason per line; “Other” asks the cashier for details.
Edit and publish
Change the values: the Effective threshold line (1) sums up the rule (“Effective threshold: 10 % or 15,00 € — whichever is exceeded
first.”), and the bottom bar (2) shows Unpublished changes. Click Publish thresholds.
The banner confirms “Thresholds published (version 1) — registers apply them at the next sync, even offline afterwards.” (1).
Expected result: at the register, a 12% discount (or an 18 € one) requires a reason and a manager PIN; a 5% discount goes through without approval.
Review the discounts granted
The Discounts granted section (1) totals the store's discounts: count, amount discounted, number **over the
threshold, and anomalies** (threshold exceeded without a valid approval). The table lists each discount: date, receipt,
line or whole receipt, discount, amount, approver and reason, cashier, and status (OK or anomaly).
Read-only: only the store owner publishes the thresholds.
Only the owner can set thresholds. A manager can view the page and the report but cannot publish.
If a manager tries to publish, the message is “Only the store owner publishes discount thresholds.”
The sales policy was changed elsewhere: reloaded.
Someone else published in the meantime (or changed the store's checkout settings). The page now shows the latest version: make your changes again.
No discounts synced for this store.
No discount has been granted yet, or the registers have not synced. Discounts appear as soon as the registers send their sales.
Publication denied.
The server rejected the request or did not respond. Check the values (percentage between 0 and 100) and your connection.

sections.text:
- Set up a loyalty program
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Manage VAT rates (default, reassignment)

sections.heading: Manage VAT rates (default, reassignment)
sections.text:
When your workspace is created, the list is pre-filled with the rates for your store's country (in France:
20%, 10%, 5.5%, 2.1%, and 0%). A product can only use an active rate from this list. When a legal
rate changes, add the new rate, then move the products to it: past sales keep their original rate.
The VAT rate is your responsibility
Vendora applies the rate you choose. If in doubt (takeout, alcohol, mixed products…),
ask your accountant.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Catalog › VAT rates and check the list
Each rate shows its name, value, number of products using it, and status. The Default rate (1)
is suggested for every new product and used during import when the VAT column is empty. The
Products column (2) shows how many products use this rate. The buttons (3) are Rename, Default,
Deactivate / Reactivate, and Move products to….
A restaurant usually picks 10% as the default, a grocery store 5.5%, and a retail shop 20%. Click
Default on the appropriate row.
Add a rate
At the bottom of the page, in the New rate section, enter a clear Name (1) (“TVA DOM 8,5 %”) and the Rate (%) (2) as a
percentage (8,5), check Default (3) if needed, then click Add (4).
Move products to another rate
On the old rate's row, open Move products to… (1) and choose the new rate. Confirm
the message “Move the N product(s) from “…” to “…”? Registers will receive the new rate.”.
A banner shows “N product(s) moved to “…”.”.
For a single product, just change the VAT on its record.
Deactivate an unneeded rate
Deactivate removes the rate from the available choices (product record, import). A rate that is still in use must first have
all its products moved (previous step). Reactivate puts it back in the list.
Expected result: only the rates you need appear in the VAT list on product records.
The rate 10 % already exists (“TVA intermédiaire 10 %”)
The same rate can only exist once. Use the existing one (rename it if you don't like the name).
If it is deactivated, the message ends with “: reactivate it”: click Reactivate.
Name and rate (between 0 and 100%) required.
The name is empty, or the rate is not a number between 0 and 100. Enter the rate as a percentage: 5,5 (not 0,055).
5 product(s) use this rate: move them to another rate first
You cannot deactivate a rate still carried by products. Use Move products to…, then deactivate.
The default rate cannot be disabled: first choose another default rate
Click Default on another rate, then deactivate this one.
A disabled rate cannot be the default rate
Reactivate the rate before making it the default rate.
The target rate is disabled
The rate you are moving products to was deactivated in the meantime. Reactivate it or choose another one.
Only the owner and admins can edit this reference data.
Managers see this banner instead of the buttons: the page is read-only. If the server enforces the same rule,
the message is “Administrator role required”. Ask the owner.

sections.text:
- Prices and availability by store (a different rate in a single store)
- Create and edit a product
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Products with variants (size, color, flavor)

sections.heading: Products with variants (size, color, flavor)
sections.text:
An herbal tea in three flavors and two package sizes, a T-shirt in S / M / L and two colors: instead of creating each
item by hand, you describe one or two axes, and Vendora creates every combination (3 × 2 = 6 variants).
Each variant is a full product, with its own price, barcode, and stock.
Two axes (Parfum, Format), Generate variants, then the price and barcode of one variant.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open the parent product
In Catalog › Products, open the product, then scroll down to the Variants section, which has the axes (1) and
Generate variants (2).
Describe the axes and generate
- Axis 1 (e.g. Size): the axis name (“Parfum”) and its Values, separated by commas (“Verveine, Camomille, Menthe”);
- Axis 2, optional (e.g. Color): a second axis (“Format”: “50 g, 100 g”).
Click Generate variants. Limits: 20 values per axis, 100 variants maximum, and no “/” in a value.
Each variant starts with the parent's price and is named like “Tisane bio — Verveine / 100 g”.
Set the price and barcode of each variant
The table lists the variants: Label (2), Name, Selling price (3), Barcode, Status.
Change a row's price or barcode, then click that row's Save (4). The banner
confirms “Variant “Verveine / 100 g” saved.” (1). Open shows the variant's full record
(image, stock, prices by store…).
What changes on the parent
On the parent's record, Barcode shows “Set on each variant” (1); the same applies to selling by weight
and the scale code. The parent's price (2) is used as the starting price for new variants.
In the product list, the parent shows the 6 variant(s) badge (1):
Expected result: at the register, tapping the product prompts you to choose a variant; scanning a variant's barcode adds it directly.
Add or remove a value later
Edit the axis values (add “Tilleul”, remove “Menthe”), then click Generate variants again.
New combinations are created; existing ones keep their price and barcode. Removed combinations
are archived after confirmation (“N variant(s) will be archived (…): they disappear from the
registers, their history is kept. Continue?”): they remain visible, grayed out, with the Archived status.
Axis “Parfum”: at least one value
The axis has a name but no values. Other messages: “Axis name required”, “Axis “…”: 20 values at most”,
“Two axes with the same name”, “1 or 2 variant axes (e.g. size, color)”.
A value cannot contain “/”
The “/” separates the axes in variant names. Write “1 L” rather than “1/2 L” (or “demi-litre”).
100 variants at most per product
The two axes multiplied together exceed 100 (e.g. 20 sizes × 6 colors). Create several parent products (one per range).
A product sold by weight cannot have variants
Uncheck Sold by weight on the parent, or create separate products. Likewise: “A variant cannot have its own variants”. The Variants section does not appear on a product sold by weight anyway.
The sale price must be a positive number.
The price entered on a row is not a number. Type 7,90.
Variant changed elsewhere — reload the product.
The variant changed in the meantime (another tab, an import). Reload the page and make the change again.
The variants could not be generated.
The server did not respond. Check your connection and try again.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Barcodes: enter, scan, generate internal codes
- Print price labels
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Sell by weight and scale codes

sections.heading: Sell by weight and scale codes
sections.text:
A product sold by weight has a price per kilo: the register weighs the item (with a connected scale or a manually entered weight)
and calculates the price. The scale code (PLU) links the product to the item number in your label-printing scale:
when you scan the label printed by the scale, the register finds the product and reads the weight (or price)
encoded in the barcode.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Spot products sold by weight
In Catalog › Products, products sold by weight show the By weight badge (1); the
Barcode column shows their scale code, such as “PLU 00101” (2); the price shown (3) is the price per kilo.
Make a product sellable by weight
Open the product (or create it), then in Sales and stock:
1. check Sold by weight (price per kg);
2. if you have a label-printing scale, enter the Scale code (PLU): 1 to 5 digits, matching the number in the scale (101 is saved as 00101).
The price field label changes to Sale price per kg (major currency unit) (1): enter the price of one kilo including VAT.
Click Save.
Expected result: at the register, the product prompts for a weight; scanning a scale label with PLU 00101 adds it directly with its weight.
How the register reads a scale label
Scales print an EAN-13 of the form PP IIIII VVVVV K: a prefix PP, the item code IIIII (your
5-digit PLU), a value VVVVV, and a check digit. By default, prefixes 21, 22, 23 indicate a weight
in grams and 24, 25, 26 a price in cents. Prefixes 20 (Vendora internal codes) and 29 (loyalty
cards) are reserved. Example: 2100101012501 = item 00101, 1,250 g.
What is not compatible with selling by weight
A product sold by weight cannot have variants or become a
combo, and cannot be a combo choice.
Scale code: 1 to 5 digits expected
The code contains letters, spaces, or more than 5 digits. Type only the scale's item number.
Save denied. Scale code already used by another product
The scale code (PLU) you entered is already assigned to another product. Find the product that uses it (search for
“PLU” in the list), change one of the two codes, then save again.
Save denied. A product with variants has no barcode, scale code or sale by weight: they are set on each variant
On a parent with variants, these settings are made on each variant (open it from the Variants section). However,
a variant cannot be sold by weight (“A variant is not sold by weight”): for bulk goods in several
flavors, create one product sold by weight per flavor.
The scale label is not recognized at the register
Check that the PLU programmed in the scale is exactly the product's Scale code, that the scale prints
an EAN-13 starting with 21 to 26, and that the register has synced since the change.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Barcodes: enter, scan, generate internal codes
- Create and edit a product
- All catalog tutorials

pages.title: Manage customer tabs (store credit)

sections.heading: Manage customer tabs (store credit)
sections.text:
Basic and advanced customer credit
Basic customer credit is included in every plan, Free included: credit sales within the limit (set on the customer record), payment at the register, balance visible on the customer record. The Customers › Customer tabs page (open tabs, reminders) belongs to advanced customer credit, included in the Commerce plan: on Free, it is hidden and shows Included in Commerce. An open tab can always be paid at the register.
A tab is the account of a customer who pays later. At the register, a sale “on credit” requires an identified
customer; above their limit, a manager PIN is required. Payments are taken at the register and are included
in the Z report. The back office is where you set limits, track debts, and send reminders.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Set a customer's limit
By default, the limit is 0: no tab allowed. Open the customer's record (Customers › Customers), enter a
Tab limit (1), then click Save.
Enter the limit in your business currency: 50 for a limit of 50 €.
Track open tabs
Open Customers › Customer tabs to see the customers who owe money, oldest debts first.
1. No movement for at least: 0, 7, 30, or 60 days, to focus on dormant debts;
2. the totals: number of tabs, amount due, tabs over the limit;
3. for each customer: Due, Limit, Oldest debt, Last payment, No movement, Reminder;
4. Send reminders (n): bulk reminder.
A red row (“exceeded”) flags a tab above its limit: this can happen when two registers that were offline
sync. It is flagged, never canceled.
Send a reminder
In the Reminder column, click the channel (Email, WhatsApp, SMS). A reminder is only sent through a
channel the customer has accepted (consents on their record) and for which you have their contact details;
otherwise the line shows “No consent to send”. The banner confirms “Reminder sent to … (…).” (1) and the date of the last reminder appears (2).
Send reminders (n) sends reminders to all reachable customers at once, through their preferred channel: “N reminder(s)
sent · N without email or consent · N failed.”
Read a customer's tab, write it off
On the customer's record, the Customer tab section shows the amount due and the limit (1), then the **Tab
ledger (2): Sale on credit, Payment (cash / card), Write-off, Return (credit note)**.
To write off an unrecoverable debt (3), enter an amount and a reason (required), then click Write off.
The entry is logged (“Tab written off: … — still owed …”). Enter the amount the same way as the limit, in your business currency (12,50).
Expected result: the payment collected at the register lowers the amount due and appears in the ledger after sync.
The Customer tabs page is missing from the menu
On the Free plan, the Customer tabs page (open tabs, reminders) is hidden: it belongs to advanced customer credit, included in Commerce. The limit is still set on the customer record, the balance stays visible there, and credit sales and payments still happen at the register. See The Free plan.
No consent to send
The customer has not accepted any channel, or you don't have the matching contact details (no email address for Email).
Check the consent box on their record if they gave consent, and add their email address or phone number.
…: reminder not sent — ….
The reminder was refused (reason shown after the dash):
channel not accepted, missing contact details, or sending impossible. It is recorded but not sent.
Tab settled: nothing to remind
The customer has paid everything in the meantime. Reload the page.
Amount between 1 and the amount due (…)
The amount to write off is more than what
the customer owes (or is 0). See the note on entering amounts.
Reason required
A write-off must have a reason (“Customer left without a forwarding address”…).
Negative tab limit
The limit must be 0 (no tab allowed) or a positive amount.
The tab is refused at the register
The limit is 0 (“no tab allowed”), the tab is blocked, or the limit has been reached: above it, the register asks for a manager PIN.
Raise the limit on the customer record if needed.

sections.text:
- Create and find your customers
- Analyze your customers (customer tab aging)
- All customer tutorials
- The Free plan

pages.title: Merge duplicate customers

sections.heading: Merge duplicate customers
sections.text:
The same customer can end up with two records: one created at the register with their cell phone number, another in the back
office with a different number. Two records with the same phone number are merged automatically. Other cases —
same email or same name with different phone numbers — are listed here for review: a manager decides, and nothing is
merged automatically.
Search for duplicates, keep Martin Dubois's record, dismiss a false duplicate.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Customers › Customer duplicates
The tabs (1) To review, Merged, and Dismissed sort the pairs. New records are compared automatically;
Search all records (2) reruns the comparison across all your customers (“N new likely duplicate(s).”).
Each pair shows the reason (3): Same email or Same name.
Compare the two records
Each record (1) shows the phone number, email, creation date, number of sales, points, and tab. Usually, keep the most complete
or the oldest record — the phone number of the record you keep becomes the customer's phone number.
Merge: Keep this record
Click Keep this record (2) under the record to keep. A dialog asks for confirmation — “Merge ‘M. Dubois’ into
‘Martin Dubois’?” (1) — and reminds you that merging is permanent: it cannot be undone. Click **Merge
permanently (2); Cancel** changes nothing.
The other record is merged into the kept record with its sales, points, tab, and cards, and the registers are updated.
The banner confirms “‘M. Dubois’ merged into ‘Martin Dubois’: sales, points and tab combined.”
If they are not the same person (two different “Claire Fontaine”s), click Not a duplicate (3): the pair moves to
Dismissed and will no longer be suggested.
The Merged tab keeps a history of each merge, with the kept record marked Record kept (2):
Check the combined record
In Customers › Customers, the kept record now combines the purchases and points of both records (1); the other
record has disappeared from the list (2).
Expected result: one record per customer on every register, once they sync.
No duplicates to review.
No pairs are waiting for review. Click Search all records to run the comparison again.
Already handled elsewhere — list reloaded.
A colleague merged or dismissed this pair at the same time. The list is now up to date; there is nothing else to do.
One of the two records has already been merged or anonymized
One of the records no longer exists in this form. Reload the page.
Managers only.
Only managers, administrators, and owners can merge records (the server message is “Manager role required to approve a merge”).
I merged the wrong records
A merge cannot be undone. Create a new record for the affected person (with their own phone number) and, if
needed, correct the points with an adjustment and a reason (see Loyalty).
Two records with the same number are not suggested
This is expected: two records with the same phone number are merged automatically during sync. Check that the number was
entered with its country code (+33…) — see Create and find your customers.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Create and find your customers
- All customer tutorials

pages.title: Create and find your customers

sections.heading: Create and find your customers
sections.text:
Customer records are used for loyalty, customer tabs, and email receipts. It is shared by all your stores and can
be created here or at the register (even offline). The phone number identifies the customer: two records with
the same number are merged automatically.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Customers › Customers
On the left is the customer list, with the most recent buyers first. Each row shows the phone number, last
purchase date, total spent, number of purchases, points, and, if applicable, the Customer tab.
1. Search: a name, the last 4 digits of the phone number, or a card code;
2. New customer;
3. Likely duplicates: see Merge duplicate customers.
Create a record
Click New customer and fill in Name (1), Phone (2), Email (3), and Notes (4)
(allergies, preferences…). Click Create (5).
Country code
A number entered without a country code (06 12 34 56 78) gets your business's country code: +33 for a business in
France (or using euros), +216 in Tunisia. For a foreign customer, type the full number with its country code
(+32 470 12 34 56).
The banner confirms “Customer “…” created — available on the registers at the next sync.” (1).
If the number already exists, Vendora blocks the duplicate: the red banner “Phone already used by Martin Dubois” (1)
appears at the top of the page, and the form offers Open record (2):
Find a customer and read their record
For example, type 3040 (the last digits of the number) in the search box (1) and click the customer. The record shows how
long they have been a customer, the number of purchases and the total (2), then the editable fields (3): name,
phone, email, Tab limit and notes. After making changes, click Save (“Record saved.”).
Further down: Loyalty (points and history), Customer tab, Customer QR (shown at the register,
recognized even offline), Digital receipts, and Recent purchases.
Cards and consents
- Cards (1): Assign a card creates a loyalty card with a unique code that can be scanned at the register; Revoke deactivates it (for a lost card).
- Consents (2): check Email, SMS, or WhatsApp only if the customer has agreed to be contacted through that channel. Without consent, no receipt or reminder is sent to them.
Export or anonymize (GDPR)
At the bottom of the record:
- Export data (JSON) (1): downloads all the data Vendora holds about the customer, so you can give it to them on request;
- Anonymize (2): permanently erases the name, phone number, email, notes, and cards; sales stay in the history without a name. You are asked to confirm. This cannot be undone.
Expected result: the record shows “Customer anonymized” and can no longer be edited.
Invalid phone number
The number is not recognized. Enter it in international format, with the country code: +33 6 12 34 56 78.
Phone already used by Martin Dubois
A record already exists with this number. Click Open record instead of creating a second one.
Customer name: 2 to 80 characters
The name is too short (a single letter) or too long.
Tab not settled (…): collect the payment or write it off first
You cannot
anonymize a customer who owes money. Collect their payment at the register, or write off the tab
(see Manage customer tabs), then anonymize.
Customer anonymized: the record can no longer be edited
Anonymization is final. If the customer comes back, create a new record for them.
No digital receipts (sales appear when registers sync).
Sales linked to the customer and their receipts arrive when the register syncs. For a sale to be linked, the
customer must be identified at the register at the time of the sale.
Manager role required
Customer records in the back office are only available to
managers, administrators, and owners.

pages.title: Set up a loyalty program

sections.heading: Set up a loyalty program
sections.text:
Customers identified at the register earn points on the net amount paid. Once they reach a tier, the register
offers to redeem points for a discount. The program applies to all stores and works offline.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Customers › Loyalty and set the earning rule
In the Earning rule block:
1. check Loyalty program active;
2. 1 point for … EUR paid: 1 = one point per euro (the example below updates: “A purchase of 25,90 € earns 25 point(s).”);
3. Points expiry in months: 12 = points older than one year expire (oldest first); 0 = never;
4. Redeemable points: in all stores or in the store where they were earned;
5. Text printed on the receipt: a line printed under the points balance (80 characters max).
Define the reward tiers
In Reward tiers, click Add a tier (3) for each level, then:
- From: the number of points required;
- Reward: Discount in EUR (amount) or Discount in %;
- Value: 5 (€) or 10 (%);
- Limit: for a percentage, the maximum discount in euros (empty = no limit);
- Label (ticket, register): what the cashier and the customer see (“5 € offerts”).
Remove deletes a tier. You need at least one tier to activate the program.
Publish
Click Publish (top right). The banner confirms “Program published (version 1) — registers in every store apply
it at the next sync.” (1); the badge (2) changes from “never published” to “version 1”.
Expected result: at the register, an identified customer earns points on every sale; once they have 100 points, the register offers them “5 € offerts”.
View and adjust a customer's points
On a customer's record (Customers › Customers), the Loyalty section shows the balance and the next tier (1)
(“Only 5 pts to go for 5 € off”), and the **Points
ledger (2): Earned, Redeemed, Expired, Adjustment, Taken back (return)**.
To correct a balance (goodwill gesture, mistake), enter ± points and a Reason (required), then click
Adjust points (3). An adjustment is added as a logged entry; it never overwrites the balance.
(Optional) Expire points right away
The server expires points once a day. The Expire due points button (Expiry block) runs the calculation
immediately: “N point(s) expired for N customer(s).” or “No points to expire.”.
At least one tier to activate loyalty
Add a tier before publishing an active program.
Duplicate tier identifiers
The program received contains two tiers with the same
identifier (a program published by an external integration, for example). Delete the duplicate tier, then publish
again. A double-click on Add a tier now creates two separate tiers.
Two tiers with the same threshold
Two tiers require the same number of points.
Change one of the thresholds.
Tier “5 € offerts”: invalid reward
The value is zero, or a percentage is above
100 %. Other messages: “Tier “…”: points threshold strictly positive”, “Amount per point strictly positive”.
Only the owner publishes the loyalty program.
Only the owner can publish; the page is read-only for everyone else (“Read-only: only the owner publishes the program.”).
The program was changed elsewhere: reloaded.
Someone else published in the meantime. The latest version is now displayed: make your changes again and publish.
Zero adjustment
Enter a number of points other than 0 (use a negative number to remove points).
A customer does not earn points
They must be identified at the register before payment (phone number, card, or customer QR), and the program
must be active and published. An anonymous sale earns no points.

pages.title: Analyze your customers (loyal, needing follow-up)

sections.heading: Analyze your customers (loyal, needing follow-up)
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Customer reports are part of full reports, included in the Commerce plan and higher plans. On the Free plan, the page is hidden and shows Included in Commerce; customer records and history stay available.
For a given period (the last 30 days by default), the Customers › Customer reports page summarizes the visits and value
of identified customers, loyalty, and customer tabs. The figures cover all your stores.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Choose the period and read the Customers tab
Set From / to (1). The tabs (2) are Customers, Loyalty, and Customer tabs. The Customers tab shows (3):
- Active customers (including returning customers, who came at least twice);
- New records created during the period;
- Identified sales: the share of receipts linked to a customer — the number you want to grow;
- Identified revenue.
Below is the Top customers table: purchases, revenue, average basket, and last purchase (phone numbers masked).
Export CSV / Export PDF (4) download the current tab.
Loyalty tab
Indicators (1): Points earned, Points redeemed, Expired · reversed, Outstanding to date (outstanding
points and the number of customers who have any). Largest points balances (2) lists the customers to remind that a
reward is waiting for them.
Customer tabs tab
Indicators (1): Due to date (customers and limits exceeded), Credit sales, Settlements · losses,
Reminders sent. Customer tab aging (2) groups debts by the age of the oldest one: follow up on the oldest ones
first from Customer tabs.
Expected result: you know who to follow up with, and whether the share of identified sales is growing month over month.
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
No identified purchases in this period.
No sales were linked to a customer on these dates. Widen the period, and remember to identify the customer at the
register (phone number, card, or customer QR) before taking payment.
PDF export failed.
The server could not produce the PDF. Try again; the CSV export is still available.
Today's figures do not appear
Sales arrive when the registers sync. An offline register sends its sales when it is back online.

pages.title: Contextual help “?” in the back office and the apps

sections.heading: Contextual help “?” in the back office and the apps
sections.text:
No need to hunt for the right tutorial: from any back office page or from a device, one click opens the help page
that matches what you are doing. The help center opens in a new tab, so nothing you are typing in the back office
is lost.

sections.heading: In the back office
sections.text:
The “?” button at the top of every page
At the top right of every page, just before your name, the round ? button (tooltip Help for this page) opens
the tutorial for the page on screen: on Catalog › CSV import / export, it opens
Import your catalog from a CSV file; on Settings › Kiosks,
Monitor your kiosks; on the Dashboard,
Discover the dashboard, and so on for every page.
With the keyboard: the Tab key reaches it like the other header buttons; screen readers announce it as “Help for this
page (new tab)”. The label follows the back office language (French, English, Arabic).
The “?” button before you sign in
The pages you open without being signed in also have their ? button (1), at the top of the card, right after
the language choice: Sign in to the back office and Forgot password open
Sign in to the back office, Create my workspace opens
Create your workspace, the invitation page opens
Accept an invitation, and the delegation page opened from the
Vendora console opens Vendora access.
In Arabic, the card header is mirrored: the ? moves to the left of the language choice.
The “Help center” link in the menu
At the bottom of the left menu, Help center opens the home page of this site: search and sections. The
Getting started card on the dashboard also offers “Need a step-by-step guide?” with two links: **First day with
Vendora (First day) and Help center**.
The “Learn more” links in messages
Some frequent messages carry a Learn more link that leads straight to the solution:
- errors from the catalog CSV import → the “If it does not work” section of
Import your catalog from a CSV file;
- account banners (trial, payment pending, suspension) and the “Change refused” banner →
Account suspended, end of trial.
For all other messages: Back office error messages (index).

sections.heading: On devices: “Online help”
sections.text:
Open help from the device
The Online help entry opens, in the device's browser, the section for its role:
Device · Where to find Online help · Section opened
Register · Who are you? screen (above Unpair this device), and Register menu › Hardware diagnostics · Register
Floor phone · Who are you? screen, and once signed in, More actions (“⋯”) on the floor plan › Online help (see The phone menu) · Floor phone
Kitchen display · Screen settings menu, after Store network · Kitchen display
Kiosk · technical screen (5 taps at the top left, then manager PIN), before Unpair this device · Kiosk
Same location and same label on iPad / iPhone and on Android. The entry does not appear in demo mode. On the kiosk,
help is deliberately available to staff only (technical screen), never to customers.
On the kiosk, help opens inside the app (not in the browser): the iPad's Guided Access and the Android tablet's
screen pinning prevent opening another app. Only help center pages are displayed there; Close help returns to the
technical screen. Without Internet access, the app shows “Help unavailable: check the device's Internet
connection.”
The “?” button opens a page that doesn't quite match
Some pages are covered by several tutorials (the product page, for example: variants, combos, photos, selling by
weight…). The “?” opens the main tutorial; the others are listed in its See also section and on the section page.
You can also use the search at the top of the help center.
Nothing opens when I click
The browser may be blocking new tabs for this site: allow them, or right-click ›
Open link in new tab. On a device, check that it has Internet access; on a kiosk in locked mode
(Guided Access, screen pinning), exit the lock first.

pages.title: A register no longer syncs

sections.heading: A register no longer syncs
sections.text:
First, don't worry: nothing is lost. Vendora works offline. The device keeps selling, taking payments and sending orders to
the kitchen; everything it does is kept on the device and sent to the server as soon as the connection comes back.
An operation refused by the server is never deleted either.

sections.heading: The symptom
sections.text:
The status pill at the top right of the device screen does not go back to Up to date:
Pill · What it means
Offline or Offline · … · The device cannot reach the server. The number shows the operations waiting to be sent.
… pending (and not going down) · The device is online but its uploads do not go through.
… rejected · The server refused one or more operations.
Attention · The device time is wrong, or the device has not been able to sync for a long time. A banner says which.
If the whole screen shows Register revoked, the device was revoked in the back office: see step 4.
On the kitchen display, the banner shows “Offline — last sync …”. In the back office, this device's sales do not
reach the reports and the Settings › Devices page shows an old Last contact.

sections.heading: Likely causes
sections.text:
1. No Internet on the device (Wi-Fi off, router restarted, mobile data used up).
2. Server unreachable from the store network (firewall, guest network blocking it, temporary outage).
3. Device revoked in the back office, or device key not recognized after a reset.
4. App too old: the server requires a more recent version (see “Update required” on the device).
5. Rejected operations: the server refused a specific operation (session already closed, user removed from the team…).
6. Wrong device time: the device date or time is more than 5 minutes away from the server's.
7. Device offline for a long time: 7 days without sync or 10,000 operations waiting (critical alert at 21 days or
50,000).

sections.heading: Step-by-step checks
sections.text:
Tap the pill and read the Sync window
The window shows “Last synced at …” (“Last synced 22 days ago” after 24 hours, or Never synced) and “… events to
send”. Tap Sync now.
Expected result: the pill shows Sending… then goes back to Up to date. If so, it was a temporary outage:
nothing else to do.
Check the device connection
Open a web page on the device or, on the register, run Register menu › Hardware diagnostics and then the server
test. A “Server unreachable: …” result gives the cause after the colon (“connection refused”, “timed out”,
“host not found”, “no network connection”). Reconnect to the store Wi-Fi, restart the router if needed. See
Hardware diagnostics (scanner, drawer, beep, server).
Read the device banner
A red or yellow banner gives a precise cause:
- “The server refuses uploads from this register: device key not recognized. Pair the device again (new code in the
back office) — sales are kept here.” → generate a new code in the back office and pair again.
- “Update required: minimum version …” → update the app
(“Update required” on the device).
- “Last sync more than 72 h ago — only managers can sign in” → the device has been offline for more than three days:
only managers can sign in to it until the connection is restored.
- “Device time is wrong: … min behind the server” (or “ahead of”) → open the device settings (Date & Time), turn on
automatic time or fix the time. Sales continue meanwhile; the banner goes away at the next sync.
- “Sync is behind: …” (orange) or “Sync is critical: …” (red) → the device has not been able to send for too long.
Reconnect it to the Internet (step 2): everything is sent automatically. At the critical level, the next manager who
signs in on the device gets the “Register not synced” alert. Nothing is ever deleted or blocked.
Register revoked: go back to pairing
When the device was revoked in Settings › Devices, it shows the Register revoked screen at its next sync.
The operations it made before the revocation were sent to the server and are waiting for a manager's review
(Control › Sync, quarantine). The title follows the device: Register revoked on a register, Kiosk revoked
on an ordering kiosk, Device revoked on a kitchen display or a floor phone; what to do is the same. A revoked kiosk
no longer pins the screen.
1. If the screen says “… still have to be sent”, connect the device to the Internet, then tap Try sending again:
nothing is deleted until everything has been sent.
2. Tap Back to pairing, then pair the device with a new code created in the back office
(Pair the register, phone, kitchen display or kiosk). It starts
again with a new identity (session no. 1, new Z report no. 1).
If a register session was open on the device, close it in the back office (forced close).
Handle rejected events
If the pill shows “… rejected”, tap View rejected events: each row gives the operation and the reason. They are
never resent or deleted: a manager handles them in the back office, in Control › Sync (accept or refuse the ones
in quarantine, understand the final rejections). See Handle rejected sync events.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.text:
- Network outage: keep selling. Everything is sent automatically when the connection comes back; Sync now
speeds it up.
- Wrong time: fix the device date and time (automatic time).
- Device revoked or key not recognized: pair it again with a new code. If you can avoid it, do not unpair it
before its sales have been sent (see Unpair a device).
- Version too old: update the app.
- Rejections: have a manager decide on them in the back office.
Never synced
The device has just been paired and has not finished its first sync: wait a few seconds, or tap Sync now. If it
stays like this, check the connection (step 2).
Device time is wrong
The device date or time is more than 5 minutes away from the server's. Fix it in the device settings (**Date &
Time**, automatic time). Sales made meanwhile are kept and accepted.
Register revoked
The device was revoked in the back office: follow step 4 to go back to pairing.
The register is online, but tables and kitchen tickets do not pass from one device to another
Devices in the same store also talk to each other directly over the store Wi-Fi. Check that they are on the same
network: see Store network: local hub and main register.
A register's sales do not appear in the back office reports
Reports only contain what the registers have sent. Check the register's pill, then the
Register sessions page.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Sync: status, sync now, rejected events
- Handle rejected sync events
- Manage your devices (rename, change role, replace, revoke)
- Account banners: trial, offline, account suspended

pages.title: Account suspended, end of trial

sections.heading: Account suspended, end of trial
sections.text:
Selling never stops because of the subscription. Whatever the state of the account, your registers, floor phones
and kitchen displays keep taking payments and sending orders to the kitchen. What changes is what you can do in the
back office.

sections.heading: The symptom: the banners
sections.text:
A banner appears at the top of every back office page (and at the top of the devices), in the language of the screen:
Banner · State · What is blocked
“Trial — … days left.” · Free trial · Nothing.
“Your trial is over: you keep going for free.” · Trial ended without a plan: Free plan · Nothing is blocked or suspended; paid modules are hidden and the Free plan limits apply (My trial is over).
“You have … days left to choose your register or subscribe.” · Free plan with too many devices · Nothing for 15 days; after that, registers not kept become read-only (Choose the register that stays active).
“Payment pending: please settle your Vendora subscription. Sales continue.” · Invoice overdue · Nothing for now: settle it before the suspension.
“Account suspended: the back office is read-only. Sales continue. Contact Vendora.” · Suspended · Any change in the back office; pairing new devices.
“Cancellation scheduled for ….” · Cancellation requested · Nothing until that date.
“Subscription canceled: export your data before ….” · Canceled · Devices revoked; back office read-only, export possible for 90 days.

sections.heading: Likely causes
sections.text:
1. End of the trial without a plan: this is not a suspension, you move to the Free plan
(My trial is over).
2. Unpaid invoice (status To pay or Overdue).
3. Suspension decided by Vendora after a prolonged non-payment.
4. Cancellation requested by the owner.

sections.heading: Step-by-step checks
sections.text:
Open Settings › Subscription
The banner's View subscription link takes you there. The Plan card gives the state (Trial, Active,
Payment pending, Suspended, Canceled) and the trial end date or next invoice date. See
Manage your Vendora subscription and invoices.
Find the invoices to pay
Invoices card: the To pay or Overdue rows. The PDF button opens the invoice (bank transfer
references).
Settle or contact Vendora
Pay the pending invoices, or contact Vendora from the Subscription page to choose a plan at the end of the trial,
reactivate a suspended account or withdraw a cancellation. The banner disappears as soon as Vendora has recorded the
payment.
Cancellation: export your data
During the following 90 days, export what you need: reports, accounting exports, tax archives
(Accounting exports, Tax compliance).
Tax data is kept for 6 years.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.text:
Pay the pending invoice(s) (or choose a plan at the end of the trial). In the meantime, keep selling: nothing is
lost, everything the registers do is sent normally.
Change refused — Read-only account (subscription suspended or canceled): sales continue on your registers. Contact Vendora from the Subscription page.
Any change in the back office is refused while the account is suspended or canceled. Settle the subscription.
Account suspended or canceled: no new device can be paired. Contact Vendora.
Shown when you generate a pairing code. Devices already paired keep working.
Read-only register: your plan includes fewer registers than you have. You can still check out the current cart, close the session and print the Z report. To sell here again, pick this register in the back office (Devices page) or subscribe to a higher plan.
This is not a suspension: on the Free plan, only one register stays active. See
The register on the Free plan.
Page restricted to the owner and admins.
A manager does not see the subscription: tell the owner when the banner appears.
“Multiple stores” is not included in your plan: existing data remains viewable; creating and configuring require a plan that includes it.
This is not a suspension: the page depends on a module that is not in your plan (the module name varies). Contact
Vendora to add it.

sections.text:
- Manage your Vendora subscription and invoices
- Account banners: trial, offline, account suspended
- My trial is over
- Back office error messages (index)

pages.title: Cash discrepancy at closing: what to do?

sections.heading: Cash discrepancy at closing: what to do?
sections.text:
At closing, the register compares the Counted amount in the drawer with the Expected cash: opening float + cash
collected − change given ± cash ins and cash outs. The difference is the Variance (negative = money is missing,
positive = there is too much). A discrepancy does not prevent you from closing, but it must be explained, and it
stays recorded forever on the Z report.

sections.heading: The symptom
sections.text:
In the Close session no. … window, the Variance is shown in red and the **Comment (required: non-zero
variance)** field must be filled in; without a comment, the register answers “Comment required: variance of …”.

sections.heading: Likely causes
sections.text:
1. Counting error (notes stuck together, coins forgotten in a compartment).
2. Change error during service.
3. Cash movement not entered: supplier purchase paid in cash, bank deposit, change top-up.
4. Wrong payment method entered: a sale paid by card recorded as cash (or the other way round).
5. Opening float entered incorrectly at opening.

sections.heading: Step-by-step checks
sections.text:
Recount before closing
Recount the drawer calmly, notes then coins. Correct the Counted amount (€): the discrepancy is recalculated live.
Read the X report again
Before closing, open the X report (register menu): opening float, cash collected, cash ins and outs, expected
amount. A forgotten cash out? Record it now (Cash out, with its reason); the expected amount is updated. See
Cash in / cash out and the X report.
Check the payment methods
In Session sales, look for a “Cash” sale that should have been “Card” (compare with the card terminal total). A
wrong sale is corrected with a void or a return, with a manager PIN
(Void a ticket, process a return with or without a receipt).
Justify and close
If a discrepancy remains, write what you know in the comment (“Change error”, “Bread purchase paid in cash not
entered”…) then Close. The reason appears on the Z report. See
Close the register and read the Z report.
(Manager) Follow discrepancies in the back office
Checkout and payments › Register sessions: the Discrepancies by cashier table gives, over the period, the
sessions Short and Over, the Cumulative discrepancy and the Largest shortage. Click a session to see
its X report. See Review register sessions and discrepancies.
Discrepancies that keep coming back for the same person trigger a Recurring cash variances alert in
Control › Anti-fraud (Monitor anti-fraud).

sections.heading: Solution
sections.text:
- An explained discrepancy (change error, forgotten movement): note it in the comment; from now on, enter each
cash out when it happens.
- An unexplained or recurring discrepancy: the manager compares the sessions in Register sessions, checks
voids and returns, and sets the alert threshold in anti-fraud.
- A closed Z can never be changed: you do not “correct” a discrepancy afterwards, you explain it.
Invalid counted amount
The counted amount is empty or unreadable: type a number, with a comma for the cents.
Only … or a manager can close this session
The session was opened by another cashier: only that cashier or a manager can close it.
A session shows as “closed · forced” in the back office
The register recorded a forced closing, outside the usual flow. The Z exists; check the cash count with the cashier.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Open the register with its opening float
- Read and download Z reports
- Daily summary (the day's cash discrepancies by email)

pages.title: The printer does not print

sections.heading: The printer does not print
sections.text:
A failed print never blocks a sale. The ticket waits in the device's print queue and is sent again
automatically when the printer comes back. So you can keep serving while you look for the cause.

sections.heading: The symptom
sections.text:
- After a sale: “Printer unreachable — retrying automatically”, “Ticket pending — queue: …” or
“Printing failed (…) — reprint from the history”.
- In the register menu: Print queue (… pending).
- On the kitchen display: a banner “… Follow the tickets on this screen.”.
- On the kiosk: “Printer unavailable: note your number”.
- The kitchen ticket comes out twice, or comes out nowhere.

sections.heading: Likely causes
sections.text:
1. Printer switched off, out of paper or cover open.
2. Printer on a different network from the device (guest Wi-Fi, IP address changed after a router outage).
3. No printer set up on this device (the setting is specific to each device).
4. Kitchen tickets: no device has This device prints kitchen tickets, or several have it; or the product is not
routed to any station.

sections.heading: Step-by-step checks
sections.text:
Look at the printer
Switched on? Error light? Paper? Cover properly closed? Press its paper feed button: if nothing comes out, the problem
is with the printer itself (see its manual).
Test from the device
On the register: Register menu › Hardware diagnostics, printer test, or Printer settings › Test ticket.
“No printer configured”: set it up first
(Connect and set up the receipt printer).
Check the network address
Network printer: print its configuration page (printer button held down at startup, depending on the model) to read
its IP address, then compare with Printer settings. Search the network finds it if the device is on the same
Wi-Fi. Possible messages:
- “No printer answers on port 9100”: printer switched off, on another network, or not a network printer;
- “No local network: connect the register to the store Wi-Fi”: the device is not on the Wi-Fi;
- “Invalid address or port (port 1–65535)”: wrong entry.
Tip: reserve a fixed IP address for the printer in your router settings, so it never changes again.
Empty the print queue
Once the printer is back, the queue restarts by itself, in order. Otherwise, open Print queue in the register
menu: reprint, redirect to another printer, or abandon a ticket with a reason. See
The print queue (retry, redirect, abandon).
Kitchen tickets: check the routing
- Only one device in the store must have This device prints kitchen tickets checked (otherwise each ticket
comes out twice).
- In the back office, Restaurant › Prep stations: the product's category must be routed to a station, and the
station must have its printer. See Create prep stations and route products.
- On the phone, a kitchen ticket can be reprinted from the table: see
Send to the kitchen, mark as served, reprint a ticket.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.text:
- Hardware (paper, cover, power): fix it, the queue restarts by itself.
- Network: put the printer and the device back on the same Wi-Fi, correct the address, set a fixed IP in the router.
- Missing setting: set up the printer on each device that must print.
- Urgent customer receipt: send it by email, WhatsApp or SMS
(Send the receipt by email, WhatsApp or SMS; reprint a ticket).
Drawer not opened: printer unreachable
The cash drawer is opened through the printer: if the printer does not answer, neither does the drawer. Fix the
printer; in the meantime, open the drawer with its key.
No other printer configured
To redirect a ticket, you need a second printer set up on the device.
No paired printer.
Android, Bluetooth: first pair the printer in Android's Bluetooth settings, then come back to Printer settings.
Reprint not possible: batch unknown to this device or station without a printer
The ticket was sent from another device, or the station has no printer. Reprint from the device that sent it, or set
up the station's printer in the back office.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Connect and set up the receipt printer
- The print queue (retry, redirect, abandon)
- Hardware diagnostics (scanner, drawer, beep, server)
- Order number, inactivity, kiosk unavailable

pages.title: Troubleshooting / FAQ

sections.heading: Troubleshooting / FAQ
sections.text: An error message, a register that no longer syncs, a printer that stays silent? The solutions are here.

pages.title: Back office error messages (index)

sections.heading: Back office error messages (index)
sections.text:
A message appears in red under a form, in a banner or in a dialog? Look it up below (or type a few words of the
message in the help center search, at the top of the page). Each row gives the likely cause and the tutorial that
explains the solution step by step.
Messages are sorted alphabetically by their first word, as displayed in English, ignoring quotation marks and accents.
Messages received by third-party software through the public API stay in French: they are listed with their exact
French text, sorted with the others, and the Cause column gives their meaning. The parts that
change from one case to another (product name, number, name of your plan) are replaced with … or shown with an
example from the demo business.

sections.heading: Message families
sections.text:
Before looking for a specific message, recognize its family: what to do is often the same.
The message contains… · What it means · What to do

pages.title: “Update required” on the device

sections.heading: “Update required” on the device
sections.text:
When Vendora upgrades the server, a version of the app that is too old is no longer accepted: it would not understand
the new information sent by the other devices. The device then keeps selling offline, but it no longer syncs until
the app is updated.

sections.heading: The symptom
sections.text:
- The status pill stays on Offline, and the Sync window (or the banner) shows:
“Update required: minimum version … — the app keeps working offline, sync is paused”.
- In the back office, Settings › Devices shows an old app version and a Last contact that no longer changes.
- In Control › Sync, rejections “event version unknown to the server” may
appear.

sections.heading: What still works, what is suspended
sections.text:
Keeps working · Suspended until the update
Sales, payments, receipts, closing and Z · Sending sales to the server (they wait on the device)
Sending to the kitchen over the store network · Receiving new products, prices, PINs
PIN sign-in (managers only after 72 h without sync) · Back office reports for this device

sections.heading: Step-by-step checks
sections.text:
Read the minimum version required
Tap the pill: the message gives the minimum version. Compare with the installed version (device settings › Apps ›
Vendora, or the version column in Settings › Devices in the back office, see
Manage your devices (rename, change role, replace, revoke)).
Check that the sales are safely kept
The Sync window shows “… events to send”: these are your sales, kept on the device. **Do not unpair and do not
delete the app**: an update keeps them, deleting the app would lose them.
Update the app
Outside peak hours (an update takes a few minutes):
- iPad / iPhone: App Store › your profile › Updates › Update (or the TestFlight link provided by Vendora);
- Android: Google Play › Manage apps › Update (or the file provided by Vendora for managed devices).
Reopen the app and sign in with your PIN.
Expected result: the pill shows Sending… then Up to date; the pending sales are sent automatically.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.text:
Update the app on the device concerned (each register, phone, kitchen display and kiosk has its own version).
Consider turning on automatic app updates in the app store, overnight. If no update is offered, contact Vendora: the
required version may not be published for your device yet.
Last sync more than 72 h ago — only managers can sign in
The device has not synced for more than three days (because it has not been updated): only managers can sign in to
it. Update it as soon as possible. See PIN refused or locked, manager degraded mode.
After the update, the device asks to be paired again
The app was deleted and reinstalled instead of being updated. Pair it with a new code
(Pair the register, phone, kitchen display or kiosk). Sales not sent
before the deletion can no longer be recovered from the device: report it to Vendora.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- A register no longer syncs
- Sync: status, sync now, rejected events
- Handle rejected sync events

pages.title: The card payment is declined or stuck

sections.heading: The card payment is declined or stuck
sections.text:
Vendora takes card payments in two ways: with a standalone card terminal (you type the amount on the card terminal,
then tap Accepted or Declined on the register), or with a connected terminal or QR payment (payment
connector: the register or kiosk waits for the provider's answer). **The sale is only recorded once it is fully
paid**: a decline never creates a half-paid sale.

sections.heading: The symptom
sections.text:
Message · Where · Meaning
“Card payment declined — choose another method.” · register · The card terminal declined (or Declined was tapped).
“The card exceeds the total by … — no change on card.” · register · Card amount higher than the amount left to pay.
“Provider unavailable — charge by manual confirmation (card).” · register · The connected provider does not answer.
Waiting for customer / Expired / Declined · register (provider payment) · The customer did not confirm in time, or the provider declined.
“No open cash session — open a session before charging.” · register · No open session.
“Payment declined” · kiosk · The bank declined the card.
“Payment terminal unavailable: please pay at the counter” · kiosk · The kiosk terminal does not answer.
“Card payment unavailable offline: please pay at the counter” · kiosk · No Internet, and the terminal requires online authorization.
“The order amount has changed: please pay at the counter” · kiosk · The order changed during the payment.

sections.heading: Likely causes
sections.text:
1. Declined by the bank (limit, blocked card, wrong code): nothing to do with Vendora.
2. Card terminal offline (battery, Wi-Fi, terminal not paired with the provider).
3. Payment connector set up incorrectly, or in Simulated / Sandbox mode instead of Production.
4. No Internet for a payment that requires online authorization (QR, connected terminal).

sections.heading: Step-by-step checks
sections.text:
With the customer: offer another method
A bank decline cannot be “forced”. Offer another card, cash, or several methods (part by card, the rest in cash). See
Charge: cash, card, several methods.
Standalone card terminal: look at the terminal slip
Tap Accepted only if the card terminal approved the payment. If in doubt (outage during the transaction), check the
last slip or the terminal history before trying again: you will avoid charging the customer twice.
Connected payment (QR, terminal) stuck waiting
Let the customer finish, or cancel and start again. If the provider no longer answers, the register offers
“Provider unavailable — charge by manual confirmation (card).”: charge with the card terminal and Accepted. See
Take a meal voucher, a tip, a provider payment.
Kiosk: check the terminal
The kiosk offers Pay at the counter: the customer keeps their number and pays at the register
(Charge a kiosk order). Staff check the terminal in the
kiosk technical screen, and its setting in the back office in
Settings › Kiosks › Payment terminal (Supervise your kiosks and set up their payment terminal).
(Manager) Check the connectors and the payments
- Checkout and payments › Payment connectors: Production mode and credentials filled in
(Connect a payment connector).
- Checkout and payments › Provider payments: each QR or terminal payment, its status and its matching with the
sale; an “Anomaly” row flags a difference to settle
(Track and reconcile provider payments).

sections.heading: Solution
sections.text:
- Bank decline: another payment method.
- Terminal or provider down: standalone card terminal + Accepted (manual confirmation), or payment at the
counter for the kiosk; report the outage to the manager.
- Wrong setting: the owner corrects the connector in the back office.
- Suspected double charge: compare the terminal statement with the Provider payments page; refund on the card
terminal if needed (Void a ticket, process a return with or without a receipt).
Only the store Owner configures payment connectors
A manager sees the connectors read-only. Ask the owner.
The simulated terminal is not allowed in production.
The simulated terminal is only for testing: choose the real provider of the kiosk terminal.
Reader ID required outside simulation
In Sandbox or Production, enter the reader ID given by the provider.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Pay at the register or by card on the kiosk
- Payment connectors
- Provider payments

pages.title: PIN refused or locked, manager degraded mode

sections.heading: PIN refused or locked, manager degraded mode
sections.text:
On the devices, everyone signs in with their PIN (4 to 6 digits), set in the back office. The PIN is checked on the
device itself, even without Internet: that is why a PIN changed in the back office is only known to the device after
it syncs.

sections.heading: The symptom and its cause
sections.text:
Message on screen · Cause
“Wrong PIN — 4 attempts left” · The PIN typed does not match. After 5 errors, it is locked for 5 minutes.
“PIN of … locked until …” · Too many errors on this PIN: wait until the time shown.
“Too many attempts: manager PIN locked until …” · Same thing for the manager PIN requested for a discount, a return…
“The PIN has 4 to 6 digits” · PIN too short or too long.
“First sync… users and their PINs are coming from the server.” · The device has just been paired: wait a few seconds.
“No user with a PIN on this register — set PINs in the back office (Team), then sync” · Nobody has a PIN for this store.
“Unknown or deactivated user — sync the register” · The person was deactivated or removed from the store.
“Last sync more than 72 h ago — only managers can sign in” · Degraded mode: the device has not reached the server for more than 3 days.
“No manager with a PIN on this register — set a PIN in the back office (PIN & approvals), then sync” · An action requires a manager PIN, but no manager has a PIN known to the device.

sections.heading: Step-by-step checks
sections.text:
Check that you chose the right name
On Who are you?, tap your name before typing the PIN: a correct PIN typed under a colleague's name is refused.
See Sign in with your PIN and switch user.
PIN locked: wait or have the PIN reset
The lock lasts 5 minutes. If you forgot your PIN, a manager resets it in the back office in Settings › Team
(member page, reset the PIN), see Build your team: roles, invitations, PIN. Then, on the
device, tap the pill then Sync now: the new PIN is known.
Degraded mode: restore the connection
After more than 72 hours without sync, for security, only managers can sign in (“Degraded mode: only managers can sign
in”) and the manager PIN is checked against the local copy (“Last sync more than 72 h ago — manager PIN in degraded
mode”). A manager signs in to continue service; restore the Internet connection, then sync. See
A register no longer syncs.
Manager PIN not found
A manager sets their PIN in Control › PIN & approvals (My PIN section), then the device is synced. See
Manager PIN and approvals (cash outs, drawer, discounts…) and
Approve with the manager PIN.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.text:
- Typing error: type it again slowly, under your name.
- Forgotten PIN or repeated lock: a manager resets the PIN in the back office, then Sync now.
- Member deactivated: check with your manager (reactivation in Settings › Team).
- More than 72 h offline: a manager signs in; restore the connection.
Creation denied. PIN already used in this store, choose another one
In the back office: each PIN is unique within a store (it is what identifies the person). Choose another one.
Approval expired — ask for the manager PIN again
The manager PIN was entered, but the action was not completed in time. Start the action again and ask for the PIN
again.
The PIN works on one register but not on another
The other device has not received the PIN yet (offline) or belongs to another store, where you are not a member.
Sync it; check your stores in Settings › Team.

sections.text:
