- Kiosk technical mode

pages.title: A product does not appear on the register

sections.heading: A product does not appear on the register
sections.text:
Registers work on a local copy of the catalog (that is what lets them sell without Internet). A product created or
changed in the back office therefore reaches the device at its next sync, and only if it can be sold in this
store.

sections.heading: The symptom
Likely causes
sections.text:
1. The register has not synced yet since the product was created or changed.
2. The product is inactive (Active (visible at the register) box unchecked).
3. The product is not sold in this store (Available box unchecked in Prices by store), or it is a
local product of another store.
4. It is active but missing from the grid of the sales screen (the search finds it, the tiles do not).
5. The barcode scanned is not the one recorded (or it belongs to a variant).

sections.heading: Step-by-step checks
sections.text:
Sync the register
On the register, tap the status pill then Sync now. If the pill stays on Offline, see
A register no longer syncs.
Check that the product is active
In the back office, Catalog › Products: search for the product; the Status column must show Active.
Otherwise, open it and check Active (visible at the register), then Save. See
Search, filter, activate / deactivate products.
Check its availability in the store
In the product page, Prices by store block: the Available box must be checked for the register's store (a
product that is not available carries the not sold tag). A product created with This store only only exists in
its own store. See Prices and availability by store.
Check the sales screen
The register search finds the product but it is missing from the grid? Add it to the layout in **Checkout and
payments › Sales screen** (Build the sales screen). For the kiosk, check the
preset (Prepare the kiosk).
Check the barcode
Compare the code printed on the item with the one on the product page (or on each variant for a product with variants).
See Barcodes: enter, scan, generate internal codes.

sections.heading: Solution
sections.text:
Fix the cause found in the back office, then Sync now on the register. For many products at once (activation,
availability), use the CSV import: “Import applied: … Registers receive them at the
next sync.”
The product appears, but at the wrong price
A store-specific price (Prices by store block) takes priority over the product price; an automatic discount may
also apply. See Prices and availability by store and
Control discounts granted at the register.
The product is on the register but does not reach the kitchen
Its category is not routed to any station. See
Create prep stations and route products.
Manager role required for this store
You are not a manager of the register's store: you cannot change its availability. Ask the owner.

sections.text:

pages.title: Install the kitchen display and choose its stations

sections.heading: Install the kitchen display and choose its stations
sections.text:
The kitchen display replaces (or complements) paper tickets: orders sent from the floor and the register arrive
there instantly, station by station. It uses a dark theme and can be read from a distance.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Choose the stations
After pairing, the screen asks Which stations does this screen show?. Tap one or more stations (2) (with
their Target time), or All stations (1) for a pass view that gathers the whole kitchen. Tap
Show this station / Show … stations (3).
Check the header
The header shows the station displayed (here All stations), the sync status (“Live in store”),
and the number of tickets and late tickets. In pass view, the Filter by station bar (1) isolates one station; “Chef: …”
(2) shows who is at the stove.
Expected result: the tickets of the chosen stations appear; “No tickets waiting” when everything has been served.
With several stations selected (here Cuisine and Bar), the title lists them (1), the chips count each
station's tickets (2) and every ticket shows its station and target time: the beer goes to Bar (3), and the steak
for the same table to Cuisine (4).
To change stations later: Screen settings › Choose stations. If the station is assigned in the back office
(“Stations assigned by the back office”), change it in Restaurant › Prep stations (the station's Kitchen display
list).

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
Same choice on an Android tablet: each station is shown by its name (“Cuisine”, “Bar”).
No preparation station: set them up in the back office (Preparation stations), then sync.
Create the stations (Kitchen, Bar…) in the back office (Create prep stations), then sync the screen.
… lines without station
Some products aren't linked to any station, so they don't reach any screen. A manager routes their category (or the
product itself) to a station in the back office.

pages.title: Target times, late tickets, set aside and recall

sections.heading: Late tickets
sections.text:
Each station has a target time (e.g. Kitchen 15 min, Bar 5 min). Past that time, the ticket switches to Late (2)
(alert color) and the header counts the late tickets (1) (“1 late”).

sections.heading: Set aside
sections.text:
For a ticket to prepare later (dessert, a table that isn't ready yet), tap Set aside (tray icon). It leaves the queue
and goes to the Set aside (…) panel (1); Resume (2) puts it back in the queue.

sections.heading: Recall
sections.text:
Moved to Ready too quickly? Recall (2) (back arrow) returns the ticket to the previous step (1)
(Preparing).
All tickets go late
The station's target time is too short: a manager adjusts it in the back office (Create prep stations and route
products).
A ticket has disappeared
It may be Set aside: open the panel at the top right. Or it was marked Served from the floor
phone.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Move tickets forward
- Kitchen display settings

pages.title: Move tickets forward (start, ready, served, voids)

sections.heading: Move tickets forward (start, ready, served, voids)
sections.text:
Each ticket shows the table (or the kiosk order number), the round, the number of guests, the elapsed time, and
the products with their options and the kitchen note. A single large button moves the ticket forward one step:
Start → Ready → Served.
On iPad: the table T5 ticket arrives, Start, then Ready.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Read the incoming ticket
At the top: Table T5 (1) and the timer since it was received. Under each product, its options (2) (“Saignant ·
Purée”) and the note (“Sans sel”). Tap Start (3).
Preparing, then Ready
The ticket switches to Preparing (1). When the round is plated, tap Ready (2): the waiter gets an alert on their
phone.
Served
The ticket is Ready (1); once the plate has left, tap Served (2): the ticket leaves the screen. The waiter can
also mark it served from their phone.

sections.heading: Voids
sections.text:
When the floor voids a line or a bill (with a manager's PIN), a VOID ticket arrives at the station:
take the dish out of production.

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
A ticket doesn't arrive
Check the station shown (Screen settings › Choose stations) and that the product is routed to this station in the
back office. Check “Live in store” in the header (see Store network).
…. Follow the tickets on this screen.
The station's ticket printer is down: follow the orders on the screen in the meantime.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Target times, late tickets, set aside and recall
- Send to the kitchen (floor phone)

pages.title: Kitchen display

sections.heading: Kitchen display
sections.text: The kitchen or bar screen: receive tickets, move them forward, keep an eye on prep times.

pages.title: Screen settings (landscape, network, change station, who is cooking?)

sections.heading: Screen settings (landscape, network, change station, who is cooking?)
sections.text:
Tap the Screen settings icon (at the top right):
- Who is cooking? (1): tap your name; the header shows “Chef: …”. Nobody clears the name. No PIN
is required: it's just for the team's information.
- Lock in landscape (2) / Unlock orientation: prevents the screen from rotating when touched.
- Store network (3): status of the real-time link with the other devices (see
Store network).
- Choose stations (4): goes back to the station choice, which also contains Unpair this device.
- Hardware diagnostics: tests the beep and the server connection (see
Hardware diagnostics).

sections.heading: On Android
sections.text:
Stations assigned by the back office
This screen's station is assigned in the back office: change it in Restaurant › Prep stations (the station's
Kitchen display list).
The screen goes to sleep during service
Set the tablet's auto-lock to “Never” (system settings) and keep it plugged in.

pages.title: Compare your stores

sections.heading: Compare your stores
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Store comparison is part of full reports, included in the Commerce plan and higher plans (several stores require the Custom plan). On the Free plan, the page is hidden and shows Included in Commerce.
All your stores over the same period, ranked by the chosen indicator. The revenue change compares against the
previous period of the same length (the last 7 days against the 7 days before, and so on).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Insights › Store comparison
Choose the period (Today, 7 days, 30 days, This month or dates), then:
1. the ranking indicator: Rank by: Revenue, Tickets, Average basket, Margin, Margin rate;
2. the group totals: revenue, tickets, average basket, margin rate;
3. the ranking: rank, store, revenue and Share of the total, tickets, average basket, margin, rate, Revenue change
(green when rising, red when falling) and Top product.
If a store is selected in the header, all stores are still compared and that one is highlighted. Stores in
different currencies are shown in separate tables, with no conversion.
Export CSV: Rang ; Magasin ; Devise ; CA ; Part ; Tickets ; Panier moyen ; Marge ;
Taux de marge ; Évolution du CA ; Produit phare.
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
Only one store appears
You only have one store, or your role only covers one store. An additional store depends on your
plan (Settings › Subscription).
Change “—” for a store
No sales in the previous period (recent store): no comparison is possible.
Margin “—”
No product sold has a known cost: see Track your margins.

pages.title: VAT e-reporting of sales to consumers (France)

sections.heading: VAT e-reporting of sales to consumers (France)
sections.text:
Your sales to consumers, aggregated per day and per VAT rate (never the ticket details), are
sent to the tax authorities through an accredited platform. The schedule depends on your VAT regime:
every ten days (standard regime: from the 1st to the 10th, from the 11th to the 20th, from the 21st to the end of
the month), monthly (simplified regime) or every two months (VAT exemption). A period with no sales is sent
as “none”; a sale arriving after a transmission triggers a correction.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Set up e-reporting (once)
In Insights › E-reporting (France), click Settings:
1. Company VAT regime: Standard regime — sent every ten days, *Simplified regime — sent
monthly* or VAT exemption — sent every two months (ask your accountant);
2. Accredited platform: the one you have a contract with; No platform (sending impossible) as long as
nothing is chosen;
3. First day sent: earlier periods stay “Before activation”;
4. check Send each elapsed period automatically (every hour).
With several stores, a regime per store is possible (empty = company regime). The SIREN is
taken from the accounting exports. Click Save.
Track the periods
Choose the Month (2) with the arrows or the picker. At the top, three counters (1): To send,
Rejected, To correct; below, Periods to handle over the last twelve months (click one to open it).
For each store, the Transmission periods table (3) gives the period, its status, the number of sales,
the base excl. VAT, the VAT, the last transmission (initial, correction or resend, revision, date, platform
reference) and the XML button.
The statuses: Before activation, In progress (period not over), To send, **Awaiting the
platform, Accepted, Rejected, To correct**.
Under the periods, Aggregates per day and per rate shows what is (or will be) sent, with Sealed closure
(Yes / Not yet) for each day:
Send and handle a rejection
Sending is automatic if it's enabled. To send right away, click Send the elapsed periods (4): “… transmission(s)
sent and accepted.” or “Nothing to send: all elapsed periods are up to date.”
A Rejected period shows the reason given by the platform: fix the cause (often the SIREN or the
contract with the platform), then click Resend on the row: “Resend accepted (revision 2).”

sections.heading: The file sent
sections.text:
E-reporting for a ten-day period (XML)
The demo grocery store's initial transmission for the October 21–31, 2026 period (fictitious SIREN).
File named ereporting-<SIREN>-<début>-<fin>-r<révision>.xml.
Tag / attribute · Content
<EReportingB2C version="1"> · Root, namespace urn:vendora:ereporting:b2c:1.
<Siren> · Company SIREN.
<Store id="…"> · Store identifier and name.
<Period start end regime> · Period dates (inclusive) and regime (REEL_NORMAL, REEL_SIMPLIFIE, FRANCHISE).
<Transmission revision kind generatedAt> · Revision (1, 2…), type (INITIAL, CORRECTION, RETRY), generation date.
<Currency> · EUR.
<Nil> · true if the whole period has no sales (“none”).
<Day date salesCount> · One day of the period and its number of sales (empty if no sales).
<Vat ratePermille baseHtMinor vatMinor ttcMinor> · Per rate: rate in ‰ (55 = 5.5%), base excl. VAT, VAT and total incl. VAT in cents.
<Totals baseHtMinor vatMinor ttcMinor> · Period totals, in cents.
Sending is disabled: aggregates are computed but nothing is sent to the accredited platform.
Check Send each elapsed period automatically in Settings and save.
SIREN required: enter it in the accounting settings
Enter the SIREN in Accounting exports › Chart of accounts (“To be entered in the accounting exports” link).
Choose an accredited platform before enabling sending
The platform is set to “No platform”: choose yours, or uncheck sending.
E-reporting is only for stores on the FR fiscal module (France)
B2C e-reporting applies to France. A store outside France or in another currency (“E-reporting is only for
stores kept in euros”) is ignored.
A transmission was rejected by the platform: fix it and resend, no period may be missing.
Read the reason under the rejected period, fix it, then Resend.
Sales arrived after an accepted transmission: a correction will go out with the next sending.
A register synced sales late: there's nothing to do, the correction goes out on its own (or click
Send the elapsed periods).
Only a rejected transmission can be sent again (status …)
The period is not
rejected: there is nothing to resend.
E-reporting: Owner or Administrator role required
Only the owner and administrators can set up and send e-reporting.
E-reporting unavailable.
The server didn't respond: reload the page.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text: - Export for your accountant (journals and FEC)

pages.title: Export for your accountant (journals and FEC)

sections.heading: Export for your accountant (journals and FEC)
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Accounting exports (FEC, sales and payment journals) are included in the Commerce plan and higher plans. On the Free plan, the page is hidden and shows Included in Commerce. The tax archive, however, is always available, whatever the plan (Tax compliance).
Vendora produces daily summary entries per store: each day, one sales entry
(broken down by VAT rate) and one receipts entry (by payment method), followed, when there were any, by a tips
entry and a cash movements entry (cash added to or taken out of the drawer). Voided sales are
excluded, returns deducted, cash net of change given. Show this page to your accountant once to
agree on the account numbers, then export every month.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Insights › Accounting exports
Choose the store (header) and the period (This month by default), then:
1. the Sales journal or Receipts journal tab;
2. the check: number of Entries, Total debit, Total credit and Balance (“✓ balanced”);
3. Export CSV: the journal displayed;
4. Download the FEC: the fiscal year chosen in the list next to it.
Check the VAT and the entries
In the sales journal, VAT breakdown gives, for each day and each rate, the base excl. VAT, the VAT and
the total incl. VAT — everything you need to prepare the VAT return. Under the breakdown, Entries details each
line (date, entry no., account, label, debit, credit).
The Receipts journal debits one account per payment method and credits the customer account. The same day
then shows:
- “Tips on …”: tips received in cash and by card as debit, the tips account (467100 “Tips payable to
staff”) as credit. They stay out of revenue and VAT: never in the sales journal.
- “Cash movements on …”: the drawer (Cash account) as debit for cash added, as credit for cash taken out;
opposite, one account per reason — Change top-up and Bank deposit on 580000 (internal transfers),
Cash supplier purchase on 401000, Other cash in and Other cash out on 471000 (suspense
account). A correction uses the account of the movement it corrects.
Each entry is balanced and numbered in sequence (CA-000001 receipts, CA-000002 tips, CA-000003 cash
movements…), in the CSV as in the FEC.
Set up the chart of accounts (once)
Click Chart of accounts:
1. SIREN (for the FEC file): 9 digits;
2. Sales journal (code, VT by default);
3. Receipts journal (CA by default) and Customer account (411000);
4. a sales account and a VAT collected account per rate, and one account per payment method.
A field left blank uses the default account shown in gray (707000, 445710, 530000 cash,
511200 card, 511300 meal vouchers…);
5. the Tips account (467100 by default);
6. under Cash movement, the offset account of each reason (blank: 471000, suspense account).
Tips (not revenue) are credited to the tips account; the drawer is the Cash account of the payment methods
table.
Click Save: “Chart of accounts saved.”
Download the FEC
Choose the fiscal year, then Download the FEC. The file, named <SIREN>FEC<YYYYMMDD>.txt
(e.g. 123456789FEC20261231.txt), contains both journals of the fiscal year for all your stores, in the format
expected by the French tax authorities.

sections.heading: Example files
sections.text:
Generated from the demo businesses (fictitious SIREN 123456789): sales journal of the grocery store, receipts journal and FEC of the restaurant (with tips and cash movements).
Sales journal
One entry per day and per store: the customer account as debit (incl. VAT), then for each rate the sales
account (excl. VAT) and the VAT collected account as credit.
Receipts journal
One entry per day and per store: one account per payment method as debit, the customer account as credit.
Column (CSV) · Content
Journal · Journal code (VT, CA).
Date · Day of the sales (DD/MM/YYYY).
N° écriture · VT-000001, CA-000001… (one entry = one day of one store).
Compte, Libellé du compte · According to your chart of accounts.
Pièce · Document reference: journal code + date (VT20261028).
Libellé · “Ventes du 28/10/2026 — Magasin” (sales of 10/28/2026 — store name).
Débit, Crédit · Amounts, decimal comma.
Devise · EUR…
FEC (accounting entries file)
The demo restaurant's FEC for the 2026 fiscal year: 18 tab-separated columns, amounts with a decimal
comma.
Column (FEC) · Content
JournalCode, JournalLib · VT Ventes (sales), CA Encaissements (receipts).
EcritureNum, EcritureDate · Entry number and date (YYYYMMDD).
CompteNum, CompteLib · Account and label.
CompAuxNum, CompAuxLib · Empty (no subsidiary account).
PieceRef, PieceDate · Document reference and date.
EcritureLib · Entry label.
Debit, Credit · Amounts.
EcritureLet, DateLet · Empty (matching done by the accountant).
ValidDate · File generation date.
Montantdevise, Idevise · Empty (everything is in euros).
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
Enter the company's SIREN in the accounting settings
The FEC needs the SIREN: open
Chart of accounts, enter it, save.
The SIREN has 9 digits
Enter the 9 digits of the SIREN (spaces are accepted),
not the SIRET (14 digits).
Invalid account number: “…”
An account must contain only digits and letters (3 to
20 characters), with no spaces or dots.
The two journals must have different codes
The sales and receipts journal codes
must differ (e.g. VT and CA). An empty code gives “Journal code required”.
The FEC concerns French businesses: stores must use euros (current currency: …)
The FEC is reserved for stores kept in euros. Export the CSV journals instead.
Accounting exports: Owner or Administrator role required
Only the owner and administrators can use accounting exports. The same goes for the chart of accounts settings
(“Accounting settings: Owner or Administrator role required”).
“unbalanced” in the check
A day's debit and credit don't match (VAT rounding, incomplete sale). Don't send the file as
is: report it to support with the date concerned.

pages.title: Insights

sections.heading: Insights
sections.text: Your business figures: dashboard, sales reports, margins, stock, accounting exports.

pages.title: Track your margins

sections.heading: Track your margins
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Margin tracking is part of advanced stock, included in the Commerce plan and higher plans. On the Free plan, the page is hidden and shows Included in Commerce; your purchase prices are kept.
Margin = selling price excl. VAT − weighted average cost recorded at the time of the sale. A new purchase price
therefore never changes past sales. The average cost on the date of the sale is the one used: a sale made
offline before a delivery, and sent afterwards, keeps the cost from before the delivery. The margin rate =
margin ÷ revenue excl. VAT. The PDF shows the store's logo (or else its trading name).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Insights › Margins
Choose the period (same filters as the sales reports), then read:
1. Revenue excl. VAT, Cost, Margin, Margin rate for the period;
2. one row per product: quantity, revenue excl. VAT, cost, margin, rate; unprofitable badge below the chosen threshold;
3. Unprofitable only keeps only the flagged products;
4. the “unprofitable” threshold is set in Report settings (link on the page and in the menu).
By category
Select By category to compare your departments:
Handle unknown margins
A product sold with no purchase price and no average cost is left out of every rate: it is listed separately under
Unknown margin. Enter its purchase price (Catalog › Products) or receive an order: the following sales
will have a margin (past sales stay unknown).
Restaurant bill shares (equal split or balance) are not products: they stay under Unknown margin, grouped on
one Bill shares (no product) line. For the margin of the dishes, settle the bill by items.
Export
Export CSV (columns: Produit or Catégorie, Quantité, CA HT, Coût, Marge, Taux,
Non rentable; unknown margins at the end of the file) or Export PDF.
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
No sales with a known cost in this period.
No sales in the period, or no product sold has a cost: see the “Handle unknown margins” step.
A product's margin doesn't change after a purchase price increase
This is by design: the cost is recorded at the time of the sale. Sales made after receiving goods at the new price
will have the new margin.
PDF export failed.
Try again; if the message persists, reload the page.

sections.text:
- Set up reports (unprofitable threshold)
- Read your sales reports
- Value your stock
- The Free plan

pages.title: Stock reports: turnover, losses, dormant products

sections.heading: Stock reports: turnover, losses, dormant products
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Stock reports are part of full reports, included in the Commerce plan and higher plans. On the Free plan, the page is hidden and shows Included in Commerce; the Stock page and low-stock alerts stay available.
Stock reports are computed from the stock log, for a
single store (the one in the header, or the one chosen on the page). Five tabs.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Stock value at a date
Stock value tab (1): the value As of the chosen day (handy for December 31), the number
of Products without cost (2), and the details per product with its WAC (weighted average cost). The value
uses the weighted average cost on that date (or, failing that, the purchase price): the value at December 31 no
longer moves when a more expensive delivery arrives in January. The PDFs show the store's logo (or else its trading
name). Export CSV / Export PDF (3)
export the tab displayed.
Turnover
Turnover = quantity sold ÷ average stock (start and end of period). The higher it is, the faster the product
sells; low turnover signals too much stock.
Dormant products
Products with No sale for N days (1) that are still in stock, with the Tied-up value (2).
The default number of days is set in Report settings.
Options: run a promotion, return it to the supplier, or stop ordering it.
Losses and theft
The Value lost over the period, by reason (breakage, expiry, damaged, theft…) and by product. It includes
losses recorded on the Stock page and on the register, and expired lots written off.
Inventory discrepancies
A summary for each validated stock count: date, products adjusted, and the value of the Gain,
Loss and Net (negative net in red).
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
Report unavailable.
The server didn't respond, or you don't have access to the store: reload the page and check the chosen store.
You don't have access to this store
You aren't a manager of this store: choose one of your stores.
Empty period: the start must be before the end
The start date is after the end date: correct From / to.
Value at 0 or “unknown cost” for a product
The product has neither a receipt nor a purchase price: enter its purchase price. Negative stock is valued at 0.

sections.text:
- Value your stock and enter opening stock
- Set up reports
- The Free plan

pages.title: Read your sales reports (period, products, sellers)

sections.heading: Read your sales reports (period, products, sellers)
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Sales reports are part of full reports, included in the Commerce plan and higher plans. On the Free plan, the page is hidden and shows Included in Commerce; today's sales stay on the dashboard and Z reports stay available.

sections.heading: First: today's dashboard
sections.text:
When you open the back office, the Dashboard shows the current day for the selected store: Live block
(open register sessions and their revenue, devices online, kitchen, kiosks; updated every 30 s),
Today block (today's revenue compared with yesterday and last week, tickets, average basket, margin, revenue by
hour, top products) and To handle (integrity alerts, stock alerts, supplier due dates, anti-fraud).
The dashboard in 15 seconds: Live, Today, top products, To handle.
For another period or more detail, go to the sales reports (Sales reports button at the top
of the dashboard).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Insights › Sales reports
In the menu, open Insights (1) then Sales reports (2).
Choose the period and read the figures
1. Filters: the store (the one in the header, or “All stores”), a quick period (Today,
7 days, 30 days, This month) or From / to dates, and whether amounts are shown Incl. VAT or excl. tax;
2. The analysis axes (tabs);
3. the totals: Revenue, Tickets, Average basket;
4. the table: quantity, tickets, revenue and Share of the total; click a header to sort;
5. the exports.
Revenue = sales minus returns, voided sales excluded, counted by store day. The note “Data up to
date at …” shows the last sync received; if a register hasn't synced recently, its name
is flagged (“devices not synced recently: …”) and its latest sales are still missing.
Change the axis
The tabs: By product, By category, By seller, By device, By payment,
By hour, By store, By sale type (counter, table service, kiosk…), By combo.
For example, By payment (1) splits revenue between cash, card, meal vouchers… (2) — useful for
reconciling with the bank:
By hour shows peak hours (handy for staff scheduling):
With several stores, choose All stores in the header (1) and the By store tab (2):
For a detailed ranking of stores (change, margin, top product), see
Compare your stores.
Export
- Export CSV: the table displayed (columns: the axis, Quantité, Tickets, CA, Part) — file ventes-<axe>.csv.
- Export PDF: the same report, laid out, with the store's logo at the top (or else its trading name; “All stores”: the brand logo).
- Export details (CSV): one row per item sold in the period (see below). For a large volume,
“Large export: being prepared in the background, it will appear below once ready.”: the file appears
in Background exports, with a Download button when the status is Ready.
Sales details (extract)
Extract (40 rows) of the details exported from the demo grocery store (file lignes-de-vente-<date>.csv).
Column · Content
Date · Date and time of the sale (DD/MM/YYYY HH:MM:SS).
Ticket · Ticket number on the register.
Magasin, Appareil, Vendeur · Where and by whom (store, device, seller).
Type · Vente (sale) or Retour (return).
Statut · Annulée for a voided sale, empty otherwise.
Produit, Catégorie, Quantité · The item sold.
Brut, Remise, Net TTC · Amount before discount, discount, amount paid.
TVA, Taux TVA · VAT amount and rate (5,5, 20).
Coût unitaire · Purchase cost used at the time of the sale (basis for margins).
Devise · EUR…
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
No sales in this period.
No sales synced on these dates for this store. Widen the period, check the store in the header,
and check that the registers are online (Settings › Devices).
“No data received from the registers” or “devices not synced recently: …”
A register hasn't sent its sales for a while (offline, switched off). Its sales are kept on the
device and will arrive when it reconnects. See A register no longer syncs.
The report's revenue doesn't match the Z total
The report counts by store day, voided sales excluded, returns deducted; a Z covers a register
session, which can run past midnight. Compare over the same range, or read the Z reports in Checkout and payments › Z reports.
PDF export failed.
The server didn't respond: try again. Do the same for “Unable to export the details.”

pages.title: Receive the daily summary

sections.heading: Receive the daily summary
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
The daily summary email is part of full reports, included in the Commerce plan and higher plans. On the Free plan, the page is hidden, shows Included in Commerce, and the email is no longer sent; your settings are kept.
Every evening, at the chosen time (store time), an email sums up the day: revenue, tickets,
average basket, margin, top 5 products, cash discrepancies and open anti-fraud alerts. It is sent **only once
a day** and retried automatically if it fails.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Insights › Daily summary and set up sending
1. check Send the summary every day;
2. choose the Sending time (after closing, e.g. 9 pm);
3. enter the Recipients, separated by commas (you, your partner, your accountant…);
4. Stores: check those to include — none checked = all;
5. Send: One combined email for all stores or One email per store;
then click Save: “Settings saved.”
Send a test
Click Send a test now (after saving the recipients): “Test sent: 1 email(s).”
(1). The Recent sends table (2) lists each send: day, store, number of attempts, status
(Sent at … or Failure with the reason).
Expected result: the email arrives within a minute. Not received? Check your spam folder and add
the sender to your contacts.
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
At least one recipient is required to enable the summary
You turned on sending without any recipient: add at least one address.
Invalid address: …
The address shown is mistyped (space, extra comma, missing @). Correct it.
No recipients
The test goes to the saved recipients: save the list first.
Test: … sent, … failed — …
Some emails could not be sent; the reason follows the dash. Check the address concerned.
Read-only: only the owner and administrators can change these settings.
Your role (Manager) lets you see the settings, not change them.
Settings unavailable.
The server didn't respond: reload the page. Do the same for “Unable to save.” and “Unable to send.”

pages.title: Set up reports (thresholds, unprofitable products)

sections.heading: Set up reports (thresholds, unprofitable products)
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Report settings are part of full reports, included in the Commerce plan and higher plans. On the Free plan, the page is hidden and shows Included in Commerce; your thresholds are kept.
These thresholds are specific to each store (choose it in the header or on the page).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Insights › Report settings
1. “Unprofitable” threshold (margin rate, %): a product is flagged unprofitable when its margin rate is
at or below this threshold (0%: sold at a loss or with no margin; 15% to be alerted earlier) — used
by the margins page;
2. Dormant product after (days without a sale) — used by the Dormant products tab of the
stock reports;
3. Food-cost drift flagged above (%): tolerated gap between a dish's actual cost and the cost on its
recipe sheet (Food cost page, restaurants);
4. Save: “Settings saved.”
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
Margin threshold between -100% and 100%
Enter a rate between −100 and 100.
“Dormant” delay between 1 and 3650 days
Enter a number of days between 1 and 3650.
Food cost drift threshold between 0 and 100%
Enter a percentage between 0 and 100.
Read-only: only the owner and administrators can change these settings.
Your role (Manager) doesn't let you change them: ask the owner.
Settings unavailable.
The server didn't respond: reload the page. Do the same for “Unable to save.”

pages.title: Manage your Vendora subscription and invoices

sections.heading: Manage your Vendora subscription and invoices
sections.text:
The Settings › Subscription page summarizes your contract with Vendora. It stays available even if the account is
suspended. To change plans, contact the Vendora team: they apply the change immediately, with no
interruption.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Settings › Subscription
During the trial, the Trial — … days left. banner (1) appears at the top of every page; its
View subscription link takes you here. The page has four cards:
- Plan (2): its name, its state (Trial, Active, Free, Payment pending, Suspended,
Canceled), its monthly price excl. VAT (yearly: 2 months free), the extra devices, and the end of the trial or
the date of the next invoice (payment by bank transfer). On the Free plan: Free, with no time limit and “No
invoice: the Free plan is never billed.” (The Free plan);
- Usage (3): Sales devices used out of the plan's maximum, Stores and, when your plan limits them,
Active products and Users (active or invited). The back-office workstation does not count as a sales device;
- Modules (4): what is included (✓) and what is not (padlock, not included);
- Subscription options: your active options (extra device, kiosk, AI assistant…), their monthly price and the
Add an option list (Add an option to your subscription);
- Invoices (5): your Vendora invoices and credit notes.
- Free trial (6), during the trial: counter start (first sale), end date, 3rd-month offer and trial scope; at the
end of the trial, “Your trial is over: you keep going for free.” and, if you have extra devices, the **Choose my
register** button. See Free trial and My trial is over.
Download an invoice
In Invoices, each row shows the Number (a store credit badge marks a credit note), the Date, the
Period, the Amount and the State (To pay, Paid, Overdue, Canceled by credit note). The
PDF button opens the invoice in a new tab, where you can save or print it.
Which currency are you billed in?
The currency depends on your business's country, set when you subscribe: a business in Tunisia is billed **in
dinars (three decimals, for example 39.000 TND), a business in France or elsewhere in euros (€29.00**).
The plan price, extra devices, invoices, credit notes and payments all use this currency. It only changes with a new
subscription (a plan change requested from Vendora).
Add or remove an option
In the Subscription options card, you add an extra device or the AI assistant yourself (Add button,
then Add to my subscription); the other options (kiosk, e-reporting, priority support) show **On request: contact
the Vendora team. The AI assistant is free for 3 months the first time: its line carries the Free until …**
badge.
An option added mid-month is billed pro rata on the next invoice. When you remove one (Remove, then **Remove the
option), the window only announces a prorated credit** if there really is one: never on the Free plan without an
invoice, during the trial or during the AI assistant offer.
Removed during its 3 free months, the AI assistant stays active until the end of the offer, free of charge: its
line shows Active until … and a Keep the option button that cancels the removal. On that date, your “AI
Assistant” keys are suspended (nothing is deleted). After the offer, the removal is immediate. Full details:
Add an option to your subscription.
Understand limits and modules
- Sales devices at the maximum: nothing is cut off, but no new device can be paired
(“Beyond the plan: nothing is cut off, but no new device can be paired.”). Revoke a device you no longer need
or add an extra device yourself (Subscription options card).
- Kiosks: they have their own limit and do not count as sales devices. Each kiosk needs the Kiosk option,
added by the Vendora team (Custom: no limit). Exception: a Restaurant trial includes 1 kiosk; once you subscribe,
it stays in service but needs the Kiosk option (Kiosks).
- Stores at the maximum: creating a store is refused (Manage your stores).
- Active products at the maximum: “Limit reached: archive a product or change plan to create new ones. Your
existing products stay sellable.” A CSV import that would go over the limit is refused as a whole.
- Users at the maximum: “Limit reached: deactivate a member or change plan to invite a new one.” The owner and
pending invitations count.
- Free plan with too many devices (end of trial): 15 days to choose the register that stays active
(Choose the register that stays active).
- Module not included (suppliers, loyalty, advanced stock, full reports, accounting export…): the page stays
visible in the menu with the badge of the plan that includes it (Commerce, Restaurant or Sur mesure); if
you open it, the Included in Commerce screen (or the plan concerned) replaces it. The data stays intact and reappears when you subscribe.

sections.heading: Account banners
sections.text:
These banners are shown in the back office language.
Banner (at the top of pages) · What it means
“Trial: your … days start with your first sale. Without a sale, the trial closes on …” · Trial opened, counter not started yet.
“Trial — … days left.” (and “Subscribe before …: your 3rd month is free.”) · Free trial in progress, with no payment method.
“Your trial is over: you keep going for free.” · Trial ended without a plan: the business moves to the Free plan, with no read-only period or suspension (My trial is over). Shown for 30 days.
“You have … days left to choose your register or subscribe.” · Free plan with too many sales devices: choose the register that stays active (Manage your devices).
“Your kiosk is not included in the Free plan: it will be unavailable in … days. Your registers are not affected.” · Only the Restaurant trial's kiosk is over the limit: nothing to choose, it stops at the end of the 15 days unless you subscribe with the Kiosk option (Only the kiosk is over the limit).
“Payment pending: please settle your Vendora subscription. Sales continue.” · An invoice is overdue. Everything works; pay it.
“Account suspended: the back office is read-only. Sales continue. Contact Vendora.” · Registers keep selling, but the back office no longer allows changes.
“Cancellation scheduled for ….” · Your subscription will stop on that date.
“Subscription canceled: export your data before ….” · You have 90 days to export your data (reports, accounting exports, fiscal archives).
Change refused — Read-only account (subscription suspended or canceled): sales continue on your registers. Contact Vendora from the Subscription page.
The account is suspended or canceled: every change in the back office is refused, but your registers take
payments normally. Pay the To pay or Overdue invoices, or contact Vendora.
“Multiple stores” is not included in your plan: existing data remains viewable; creating and configuring require a plan that includes it.
The page you are opening depends on a module that is not in your plan (the module name varies). Contact Vendora to
add it.
300 products in the Gratuit plan — Commerce makes them unlimited. Archive a product or change plan.
Product limit reached (the number and plan names vary). Archive a product or change plan. Same case for users: “3
users in the Gratuit plan — Commerce makes them unlimited. Deactivate a member or change plan.”
Account suspended or canceled: no new device can be paired. Contact Vendora.
Same cause: settle the subscription to pair new devices.
Page restricted to the owner and admins.
Managers do not see the subscription.
Subscription unavailable.
The server did not respond. Reload the page.

pages.title: Authorize Vendora assistance (delegated access)

sections.heading: Authorize Vendora assistance (delegated access)
sections.text:
Never give your password, not even to Vendora. To have your account configured (importing your menu,
drawing the floor plan, installing the devices…), grant a delegation: a specific member of the Vendora team
gets access limited to the scopes you choose, for 14 days at most, revocable in one click, and every one
of their changes is listed on this page.
A delegation never gives access to payments, tax settings, API keys, the subscription, account ownership,
customer data or PINs.
Granting a 3-day delegation for the catalog and the dining room.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Settings › Vendora access and fill in the delegation
In Configuration delegations:
1. Vendora member's email: the address your contact gave you (or select them from Vendora member if they
have helped you before).
2. Duration (days, 14 at most): the time needed for the setup, 7 days by default.
3. Scopes: check only what is needed:
Catalog (products, categories, modifiers, VAT, discounts, labels, menu import),
Team (invitations and roles; each employee chooses their own password and PIN),
Dining room (floor plan, floor phones), Kitchen (prep stations),
Devices (devices, pairing codes, kiosks), Appearance (themes, logo, sales screens, receipt).
4. Reason (required): what you are asking for, e.g. “Setup: menu and floor plan”.
5. Click Grant delegation.
Expected result: “Delegation granted to … until …”.
Track the delegation
Each delegation appears below the form with its state (1) — Active, Expired or Revoked —, its
scopes, its end date, its reason and the number of session(s) and change(s). The history details
each session opened and each change (time, action, page concerned).
During a session, the Vendora member always sees the banner “Vendora · … — delegation until … · limited access,
every change is visible to the owner.” and only the pages within their scopes.
Revoke a delegation
Once the work is done, or if you change your mind, click Revoke (2). There is no confirmation. Expected result:
“…'s delegation revoked: their access is cut off immediately.”
If you do not revoke it, the delegation ends automatically on its end date.
Check support sessions (read-only)
Separately from delegations, the support team can view (never change) your data during a support
session: with a reason, for 60 minutes at most. Each session is listed in Support sessions (read-only):
who, when, why, and the list of Data accessed (stores, devices, users, register sessions,
Z reports, sales, alerts).
No active Vendora team member with this email
The address does not belong to a
member of the Vendora team (typo, personal address, former employee). Check it with your contact.
Check at least one scope
Check at least one box in Scopes. The
Grant delegation button stays grayed out while the email, a scope or a reason of at least 5 characters is missing.
Duration: from 1 to 14 days
A delegation lasts 14 days at most. For a longer
project, grant a new one when it expires.
Reason required (e.g. “setup: menu and floor plan”)
Write what you are handing
over to Vendora: it will appear in the history.
Only the owner grants or revokes a delegation.
You are an administrator: only support sessions are visible to you. Ask the owner.
Delegation already revoked
It has already been cut off (double click, or from
another tab). Reload the page.
Incomplete delegation link: reopen the back office from the Vendora console.
This message is for the Vendora member: they opened the delegation page without going through their console. The
other messages on this page (“Link expired or already used…”, “Delegation expired or revoked by the owner.”)
mean that their link is more than 60 seconds old or that you revoked the delegation.
Delegations unavailable.
The server did not respond. Reload the page. Do the same for “Could not grant the delegation.” and “Unable to revoke.”.

pages.title: Monitor anti-fraud

sections.heading: Monitor anti-fraud
sections.text:
Vendora continuously reads what the registers do — discounts, lines removed before payment, voided receipts and
bill lines, drawer opened without a sale, sales — and session closings. When a threshold is crossed, an
alert is raised (checks run about every 15 minutes) and, if you turned this on, managers are
notified by email. You handle an alert by entering a reason, and it stays on record.
An alert is not an accusation: it is a signal to check (giving change to a delivery driver is a perfectly good
explanation for a drawer opening).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Control › Anti-fraud
Choose the store and the period (1): Last 7 days, Last 30 days or Last 90 days. The By cashier table (2)
shows for each person: Sales, Discounts, Voids, Drawer openings, Register discrepancies,
Off hours sales, Stock discrepancies, and a Score: OK, To watch or Critical, with the rule
involved and the number of alerts. The most problematic column is highlighted.
Below, Open alerts (3) lists what is waiting for a decision.
Review the evidence
Each alert sums up what happened (e.g. “Camille (caisse): 4 drawer openings without a sale on 07/11 (threshold 3/day)”, the name being the person or device), its date and the number of pieces of evidence. Click Evidence: the list (1) shows each event involved,
with the time, the device and the reason entered on the register.
Cross-check with the approvals log (who approved?) and, if needed, talk it
over with the person.
Acknowledge or reject the alert
- Acknowledge: the alert is justified and you have handled it (explanation obtained, instruction given).
- Reject: false alert (unsuitable threshold, normal situation).
In both cases, enter the Reason (1) — required — then confirm.
Expected result: “Alert acknowledged: “…”.”. View handled alerts shows the history: decision, author,
date and reason.
(Owner) Set the thresholds and opening hours
In Thresholds and opening hours, click Show. For each rule (1), check Active and set the
Threshold (and the Window for recurring variances):
Rule · Threshold expressed in · Default
Frequent discounts · discounts / day / cashier · 10
Discounted amount · % of the cashier's daily revenue · 10 %
Voids and removals · voided lines or receipts / day / cashier · 10
Drawer opened without sale · openings / day / user · 3
Recurring cash variances · variance amount per session, number of sessions with a variance, rolling days · 5 € · 3 sessions · 30 days
Out-of-hours sales · out-of-hours sales tolerated / day · 0
Check Notify managers by email (2) to receive the alerts (and the products that fell below their stock
threshold). Fill in the Opening hours for each day (empty = closed): without any hours, the “out-of-hours
sales” rule is inactive. Click Publish thresholds.
“Thresholds published (version …): they apply from now on; past days are still judged with the thresholds of the time.”
Reason required to handle an alert
Write a reason before confirming; the button stays grayed out while the field is empty.
Alert already handled
A colleague handled it before you. Reload the page and check View handled alerts.
Read-only: only the store owner changes the thresholds.
Thresholds are reserved for the owner. Managers view and handle alerts.
Closing before opening (hh:mm – hh:mm)
For a given day, the closing time must be
after the opening time. For a service that ends after midnight, close at 23:59.
Settings changed in the meantime: current version 3, received 2
Someone published
thresholds while you were editing them (the numbers vary). Reload the page and start again.
“Anti-fraud” is not included in the Restaurant plan. Contact Vendora to add it.
The module is not part of your plan. See Manage your subscription.
No alert appears even though a threshold was just crossed
Rules are evaluated about every 15 minutes, and only on what the registers have already synced.
Wait, and check that the rule is Active.

pages.title: Manage your devices (rename, change role, replace, revoke)

sections.heading: Manage your devices (rename, change role, replace, revoke)
sections.text:
The Settings › Devices page shows all the devices of a store, sorted by type, with their live state.
Each card opens the device's details page: that is where you rename, configure, replace or revoke it.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Read the device list
Open Settings › Devices and choose the store. Devices are grouped: Registers (1),
Floor phones, Kitchen displays, Kiosks. Each card shows:
- Online (contact less than 3 minutes ago; 5 minutes for a kiosk) or Offline — the same rule as the
Kiosks and Live pages, shown under the page title;
- Last contact (“Just now”, “17 min ago”, “Never”) and the app version;
- badges: Main register, Session no. … open, Prints for others, Station: …, Preset: ….
The Offline filter (2) shows only devices that are not responding: handy for spotting a tablet that is switched off.
Open the details page: rename, main register, printing
Click a card. The details page shows the last contact, the app version, the pairing date and,
for a register, the open session.
- Name (1): edit it, then Rename. The device takes the new name at its next sync.
- Main register (2), for a register: Make it the main register (owner only). Bills
paid on floor phones go into this register's session.
Prints the tickets of the other devices: only one device per store; checking it here removes it from the device that had it.
- For a kitchen display: Stations displayed, then Save the stations; for a kiosk: its Preset;
for a floor phone: its Floor profile.
- Replace this device (3) and Revoke (4): see the next steps.
Change the role of a kitchen display or a floor phone
Only these two types can swap roles. In the details page, in the Role section (1), click
Switch to Floor phone (or Switch to Kitchen display), then confirm with Change role.
Expected result: “Role changed: … The device switches on its own at its next sync, without restarting; the
server already applies the new role.” No need to touch the device: if it is online, it shows the screen of its new
role in under a minute (2); switched off or offline, it switches as soon as it is back on the network.
The person who was signed in on a phone that becomes a kitchen display is signed out (the kitchen display has no
sign-in) and preselected as the display's cook. A kitchen display that becomes a phone releases
its stations; a phone that becomes a kitchen display must then be given its stations.
A register (fiscal chain, sessions, Z reports) or a kiosk (orders) never changes role: replace it instead.
Replace a broken or swapped-out device
Broken tablet, new phone: on the old device's details page, click Replace this device.
The wizard opens directly on Settings: the new device will take over the name, the role and the settings
(stations, main register, preset, printing) (1). Generate the code and pair the new device as
usual; the old one is revoked automatically as soon as the new one is paired.
For a register (2), the new device starts its own fiscal chain (numbering from zero):
close the old register's session if it is still open. A replacement does not count as an extra
device in the plan.
Revoke a lost, stolen or returned device
On the details page, click Revoke. The browser asks for confirmation (“Revoke “…”? The device will be refused
at its next connection; sales it already made remain valid.”), then a Reason (optional).
The device is refused as soon as it contacts the server. Revoked devices are listed in Revoked (1), at
the bottom of the page, with the date and the reason.
Sales already synced remain valid. Sales made offline before the revocation, then
sent afterwards, are set aside for a decision in Control › Sync
(Handle rejected events). A revocation is final: to reuse
the device, pair it again.

sections.heading: Choose the register that stays active
sections.text:
The Free plan keeps a single sales device active (register, floor phone or
kitchen display; kiosks have their own limit and are never part of this choice). If your business has more, for example at the end of a trial, the Active devices card
appears at the top of Settings › Devices.
1. For 15 days, all your devices keep selling. The banner **You have N days left to choose your register or
subscribe. appears in the back office (Choose my register and View subscription** links) and on the
registers.
2. In the Active devices card, tick the register to keep. Each row shows the name, type, store and **Last
contact**; the counter “1 of 1 chosen” shows where you stand.
3. Click Confirm my choice, then confirm in the Confirm the choice of active devices window (“Staying active: …
The other devices will become read-only at the end of the 15-day period…”).
Expected result: “Choice saved (…). The other devices become read-only at the end of the 15-day period: they finish
their sale, session and Z, and keep syncing.” You can change this choice as long as you have extra devices. Only the
owner and administrators choose.
Without a choice, at the end of the 15 days, Vendora keeps the most recently used sales device active (last
contact). The card says so: “Automatic choice: at the end of the 15-day period, Vendora kept the most recently used
sales device active. You can change this choice below.”
Devices not kept have the Read only badge, the one that stays has the Active badge. A read-only register **no
longer opens a new sale, hold or session, but it finishes the current cart, closes** its session, prints its
Z report and keeps syncing: nothing is lost
(The register on the Free plan). A subscription reactivates all
devices at their next sync. Remember to revoke devices you no longer use.

sections.heading: Only the kiosk is over the limit
sections.text:
End of a Restaurant trial without subscribing: your sales devices fit in the Free plan, but the trial's kiosk
is not included. There is nothing to choose: your registers stay active and show no banner. The back office shows
“Your kiosk is not included in the Free plan: it will be unavailable in N days. Your registers are not affected.” and
the Kiosks outside the plan card replaces Active devices: the kiosk carries the Not included badge, then
Unavailable at the end of the 15 days (it then shows “Kiosk temporarily unavailable”). A subscription with the
Kiosk option puts it back in service (Supervise your kiosks).
When your sales devices are also over the limit, the Active devices card lists kiosks separately, with no
checkbox: they have their own limit (Included if an option covers them, Not included otherwise).
Your kiosk is not included in the Free plan: it will be unavailable in … days. Your registers are not affected.
Only the Restaurant trial's kiosk is over the limit: nothing to choose, your registers carry on normally. Subscribe to a
plan with the Kiosk option to keep it (Only the kiosk is over the limit).
You have … days left to choose your register or subscribe.
Your plan keeps fewer sales devices than you have. Choose the one that stays active in the Active devices card
(see above) or subscribe to a paid plan.
Choose 1 to 1 sales device(s) (Gratuit plan).
You ticked too many devices, or none. Keep as many as the plan allows.
Owner and administrators only
A manager sees the Active devices card but cannot confirm the choice: ask the owner.
No extra device: all your sales devices stay active.
You revoked devices or subscribed in the meantime: there is nothing left to choose.
A device stays “Offline”
The device is switched off, asleep, or has no network. It keeps selling offline and will catch up on everything when
it reconnects. Check the device's Wi-Fi; if it stays offline for a long time, see
A register no longer syncs.
Role change only possible between kitchen display and floor phone: a register (fiscal chain) or a kiosk (orders) is replaced
Use Replace this device, then pair a device of the right type, or add a
new device.
Device revoked: its role can no longer change
A revoked device can no longer be
edited. Pair it again as a new device.
Read only: only the owner chooses the main register.
You are a manager or an administrator: ask the owner to choose the main register.
The payment policy (phone's own session) does not use a main register.
Your pay-at-the-table setting makes each phone take payments in its own session: the main
register is not used. See Restaurant › Pay at the table.
“…” remains the main register: designate another one to replace it
You cannot remove
the main register role without choosing another one: open the new register's sheet and
click Make it the main register.
Device name required
The name is empty. Same case for “Device name: 60 characters maximum”.
Manager role required in this store.
Only managers, administrators and the owner manage this store's devices. Ask the owner
to give you this role (Team).
Action not possible.
The server did not respond. Reload the page and try again.

pages.title: Customize the appearance (logo, colors, kiosk)

sections.heading: Customize the appearance (logo, colors, kiosk)
sections.text:
The Settings › Appearance page sets the look of your devices: button colors, logo at the top of the register and on the
receipt, light or dark mode, language, kiosk welcome screen. Anything required by law (mandatory receipt information,
Z report, checkout flow) can never be customized.
With nothing set here, a device shows the store name and the default colors of its profile (grocery, restaurant…)
as soon as it is paired. If you rename the store, the devices follow at their next sync.
Each setting can be inherited: a store then uses the brand setting (shared by all your stores)
or, failing that, the default values of its profile. You only customize what needs to differ.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Settings › Appearance
Choose the store. The table of contents (1) links to the four sections: Store theme, Brand (all stores),
Kiosk — presets, Per-device settings. On the left, the theme editor (2); on the right, the Previews (3)
of the register, the kiosk and the receipt, updated as you type.
Add your logo
In Logo (6), click Upload and choose your file (PNG, JPEG or WebP, 2 MB at most). It is published
right away: “Logo published — … Registers show it at the next pull.”. Vendora prepares a color version
for the screen and a black-and-white version for the thermal receipt. Change replaces it; Remove goes back to showing the
name as text.
Choose colors, mode, name and language
- Primary color (1): main buttons (products, CHARGE). Secondary color (2): secondary
buttons and banners. Uncheck inherited, then pick the color from the swatch or type its #RRGGBB code.
- Mode (3): Light, Dark, System (follows the device) or Inherit.
- Display name (4): the name at the top of registers and receipts. Empty = brand name, otherwise store name.
- Register language (5): French (default), English or العربية (RTL) (right-to-left screen,
amounts in digits 0-9).
Look at the Previews: the Text on primary line shows the contrast; AA ✓ means the text stays
readable. If the color is too light, Vendora switches the text to black and says so.
Publish the theme
Click Publish theme. Expected result: “Theme published (version …) — registers apply it at the next sync (≤ 30 s).” (1)
In System mode, the register follows the tablet's light / dark setting live, without restarting or signing in
again: same session, light screen (1) then dark (2) as soon as the iPad switches to dark appearance. A window that is
already open (open session, register menu…) also changes live, including when you publish another mode.
Changed your mind? Restore previous version republishes the previous theme.
(Multiple stores) Set up the shared brand
The Brand (all stores) card gives the colors, the Brand name and the Brand logo used by
each store whose field is “inherited”. A store logo always takes precedence over the brand logo.
Click Publish brand.
Set up the kiosk welcome screen (preset)
A kiosk preset combines the look and behavior of a kiosk. In Kiosk — presets, click
Edit (or New preset):
- Welcome text (1), “Touch to order” by default;
- Payment (2): At the counter or On the card terminal (with Manual card terminal payment confirmation if needed);
- Inactivity (s) (3): back to the welcome screen after 15 to 600 seconds without any action;
- Payment expiry (min) (4), offered when payment is On the card terminal: an order left unpaid on the
terminal expires after this delay (1 to 120 minutes, 10 by default);
- Ask dine-in / takeaway, Welcome image, up to 5 Banners.
Click Publish preset, then assign it to the kiosk (next step, or at pairing).
Adjust a specific device
Per-device settings overrides the theme for a single device: a kitchen display in Dark, a kiosk in
Arabic… For each device: Mode, Language, Kiosk preset, Sales screen and, for a register,
Home screen (Automatic — tables / direct sale, Tables (floor plan), Direct sale). Click
Publish on its row. If the store's Tables module is inactive (Stores › Modules),
the register always opens on the sale screen: the column then shows Direct sale (Tables module inactive).
Logo too large (2 MB max).
Resize the image (512 × 512 pixels is enough) or save it as JPEG. Server variant: “Logo too large (max 2 MB)”.
Accepted formats: PNG, JPEG or WebP.
The file is an SVG, a GIF, a HEIC, a PDF… Export it as PNG from your software (PNG keeps transparency). Server
variant: “Format not accepted (SVG+XML): PNG, JPEG or WebP accepted”.
Logo too small (at least 32 px per side)
Use a larger image (ideally 512 pixels
per side). The same rule applies to kiosk images.
Unreadable image
The file is damaged or is not really an image. Open it and save it again as PNG.
Primary color in #RRGGBB format.
The color code must start with # followed by 6 characters (digits or letters A to F), e.g. #2F5D50.
The same applies to the secondary color and the brand (“Colors must be in #RRGGBB format.”).
Main button text adjusted to black (AA contrast ≥ 4.5:1).
This is not an error: your color is light, so the button text switches to black to stay readable. The theme
is published normally.
Server: Primary color close to the alert red: risk of confusion with voids
Just a
warning: on the register, red signals voids. Prefer another shade if your team might
get confused.
This theme was changed elsewhere: the latest version has been reloaded, reapply your changes.
A colleague published in the meantime. Your unpublished changes are lost: redo them, then publish.
Equivalents: “The brand was changed elsewhere…”, “Preset changed elsewhere — list reloaded, reopen it.”.
No previous version to restore
The theme has only been published once: there is nothing to restore.
Restricted to the owner and administrators.
Only the owner and administrators publish the appearance. Managers can view it.
The register has not changed color
The register applies the theme at its next sync (less than a minute if it is online). Also check the
Per-device settings: a mode or language set on the device takes precedence over the store theme.
Payment at the kiosk is unavailable in Tunisia until the NACEF module covers it: choose PAY_AT_COUNTER
The store is in Tunisia and the NACEF module does not cover the kiosk yet: On the card terminal payment is refused
when the preset is saved. Choose At the counter; the kiosk then only offers the counter
(In Tunisia).

pages.title: Get an automatic daily summary

sections.heading: Get an automatic daily summary
sections.text:
Every morning at 8 a.m., yesterday's summary and what to order: you can ask your assistant to prepare it on its own,
without having to ask the question yourself.
This is a feature of your assistant, not of Vendora
Vendora does not send any summary and does not schedule anything. It is your assistant (Claude, ChatGPT…) that, at
the time you chose, asks Vendora the question and then answers you. Its availability, its limits and the names of its
menus depend on the plan you have with it and change from time to time: what you read here explains the approach,
not a guaranteed menu path. If in doubt, check the assistant's own help ("scheduled tasks" or similar).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Check that the question works by hand
A scheduled request is only worth something if the question already works. In a conversation with your assistant, ask
first, for example: "Give me the summary of my day." then "What should I order this week, by supplier?". If the
answer is right, move on; if not, see Connect your AI assistant.
Ideas for questions, by type of business and moment of the day, are in What to ask your assistant.
Ask for the schedule, in one sentence
In a conversation with your assistant, describe what you want in plain words, with the time, the frequency,
the store and your time zone. For example:
Every morning at 8 a.m. (Paris time), give me yesterday's summary for Épicerie Lumière (démo), then tell me what to order today, by supplier.
As far as we know, assistants then propose a name, a schedule and instructions: read them through (time,
frequency, store) before confirming. If your assistant cannot schedule a request, or if your plan does not allow it,
it will tell you: the feature is then not available with it.
Check, adjust, stop
- Find the task. Look, in the assistant or in its help, for where to see your scheduled requests ("scheduled
tasks", "scheduled" or a similar name): the place, its name and even whether it exists depend on the assistant and
on your plan.
- Try it without waiting for tomorrow. If the assistant offers to run it right away, do it once.
- Change or stop it. Change the time, pause it or delete it from there, if the assistant allows it.
- See what was read. In Vendora, Settings › AI assistant › Assistant activity shows what the assistant read, and
at what time: a reading at 8 a.m. confirms that the task did run.
Expected result: in the morning, the assistant's answer is waiting for you, with the period and the time of the data recalled.
Nothing arrives in the morning
Find the task in the assistant (where it lets you see scheduled requests): it may be paused, or set to a different time than planned (time
zone). Depending on the plan, the assistant may also run only if its app is open: read the description of the feature
in its help.
The assistant says it cannot reach Vendora
In Vendora, open Settings › AI assistant and click Test the connection. If access was removed or has expired,
connect again from the assistant. Assistants stopped by the emergency stop read nothing until the owner restores
access.
The figures look incomplete
Look at the time of the data in the answer and check that the tills are online: a till that has not synchronised may be
missing from yesterday's summary.
