sections.text:
- Connect your AI assistant
- What to ask your assistant

pages.title: Supervise your kiosks and set up their payment terminal

sections.heading: Supervise your kiosks and set up their payment terminal
sections.text:
The Settings › Kiosks page groups all your self-service ordering kiosks: their live state, their card
payment terminal and their statistics. The kiosk content (welcome screen, featured products, payment method
offered) comes from its preset, set in Settings › Appearance › Kiosk; the kiosk screen itself is
described in the Kiosk section.
Linking a payment terminal to the kiosk, then disabling and re-enabling it remotely.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Read the state of the kiosks
1. the counters Kiosks online (out of the total), Offline or unavailable, Disabled;
2. State: Online (the kiosk contacted the server less than 5 minutes ago — same rule as the Devices and Live pages), Offline, Unavailable
(the kiosk declared itself unavailable) or Disabled, with the last contact: “seen just now”,
“seen 3 min ago”, “seen 2 h ago”, then “seen on 05/11/2026” after more than a day;
3. Printer (OK, Error, Offline, None) and Lock mode (tablet lock mode active or not);
4. the assigned Preset; you also get the app Version, the Last order and the Terminal;
5. the Deactivate / Reactivate and Payment terminal actions.
The list refreshes every 30 s (checkbox); Refresh reloads it right away.
Link a payment terminal
Click Payment terminal on the kiosk's row. The panel reminds you (1): “Without a terminal, the kiosk
offers payment at the counter: the customer pays at the register with their order number.”
2. Terminal provider: Simulated terminal (test), Stripe Terminal, Viva Wallet or Nepting;
3. Mode: Simulated (no money, for trying it out), Sandbox (the provider's test account) or
Production; for any mode other than Simulated, also enter the Reader ID assigned by the provider;
4. Save.
Expected result: “Payment terminal of “Borne entrée (démo)” saved.” (1), and the
Terminal column (2) shows the provider and its mode.
On the kiosk, the customer then sees Pay by card (see Pay at the register or by card on the kiosk). Remove (in the panel)
deletes the terminal: “The kiosk will no longer offer card payment: the customer will pay at the counter.”
Read the conversion statistics
Further down, Conversion statistics:
1. the period (From / To, then Apply);
2. Sessions (customers who touched the screen), Orders and their amount, Conversion rate, Average basket,
Dine-in / takeaway;
3. Where customers drop off: Home, Catalog, Cart, Payment, and the share of Confirmed orders;
4. Per kiosk: the same figures, kiosk by kiosk.
Many drop-offs at the Catalog? Feature your best sellers in the preset. At Payment? Check the
terminal. A “Manual terminal confirmations to reconcile” banner appears if payments were confirmed by hand
on the kiosk: check them against the terminal statement, or reconcile them in the next step.
Standalone terminal and reconciliation
Is your card terminal standalone (placed next to the kiosk, with no link to it)? The **Standalone terminal and
reconciliation block ties its payments to the orders of the kiosks whose preset has payment set to On the card
terminal**.
Terminal gateway (owner or administrator):
1. the gateway's status — Active once enabled with Enable the simulated gateway;
2. the Webhook address, the Signature header and the Secret, to copy into the terminal's settings. The
secret is shown in full only once, when the gateway is enabled (“Gateway secret, shown only once: copy it now
into the terminal's settings.”), then masked;
3. Deactivate and Renew the secret (the old secret stops working immediately).
The simulated gateway is for demonstrations and trials: no real terminal model is connected yet, and it is not
offered on the production server (“Production server: the simulated gateway is not offered.”).
With the gateway active, each payment notified by the terminal confirms the matching order on its own: the kiosk moves
to Thank you! and the order goes to the kitchen, with no action from the customer. Each confirmed payment (by the
terminal or by hand) creates a real sale with its receipt. If the sale is impossible although the customer paid (not enough stock, for
example), the order becomes already paid at the terminal and waits to be recorded at the register: see the next step.
Reconciliation compares, day by day, the payments confirmed by the kiosks with the terminal statement:
1. Day to reconcile, then Reconcile now to record the result (“Reconciliation recorded: no gap.”);
2. Confirmed by the kiosks, Of which manual confirmations, Terminal statement and **Gap (confirmed −
statement)**;
3. the banner: “No gap: every confirmed order matches a payment on the statement.” or “Gap to check: …”;
4. the line-by-line detail: Reconciled, Different amount, Confirmed, missing from the statement (the case
of a manual confirmation with no payment) On the statement, with no confirmed order or Paid, sale to record (the terminal took the payment, the sale is
still to be recorded at the register; the reason shows under the badge), with the source
(Manual confirmation or Terminal notification);
5. outside production, Simulate a payment (Order number, Amount paid) plays the terminal's part, for a
trial.
The previous day is reconciled automatically. A finished day that still has a gap alerts the managers (in the
register's alerts: “Kiosk payments: gap with the terminal”) and the block says so: “Managers were alerted on …”. An
order left unpaid expires after the preset's delay (Payment expiry (min), see
Customize the appearance); it shows as Expired (unpaid) in
Follow the current service, Closed bills.
Follow the terminal payments to record
When a customer paid on the terminal but the sale could not be recorded at the kiosk (not enough stock, cash day could
not be opened, different amount), the Kiosks page flags it. There is nothing to do here for the customer: they paid
and do not pay again.
1. the To record at the register tile (1), among the counters, with the number of payments (it only appears if there
are any);
2. on the kiosk's row, the “1 payment(s) to record” badge (2);
3. the Terminal payments to record (n) section (3), with the banner “These orders were paid on the kiosk terminal,
but the sale could not be recorded. Record them at the register without charging the customer again.” and a table:
Order, Kiosk, Amount, Terminal transaction (or “no reference”) with its origin — **Confirmed by the
terminal or Confirmed by hand by a manager —, Reason** (“Not enough stock at payment time”, “The kiosk's
cash day could not be opened”, “Order amount differs from the payment” or “Other reason”) and Time;
4. the collapsed Already handled, last 30 days (n) list (4): the payments already settled, with their state
(“Recorded”, “Canceled”, “Merged”, “To record” or “Other status”).
This page does not let you record the payment: a register does it, under its operator's name
(An order already paid at the terminal). The kiosk's
page updates once the register has recorded the payment.
When the customer's payment was confirmed by hand (manager's code), the line says so: **Confirmed by hand by a
manager**, and “no reference” if the manager typed no slip number. Match it against the terminal's statement. A payment
that a register has recorded is also logged in the
Technical events journal (“Terminal payment not recorded”, then “Terminal
payment settled”).
Two extra marks on a line. A line may carry:
- the red badge “Also taken by a till that was unaware of this payment (older version or not yet synchronised): check for
a double payment”: a till has also taken this order although the customer had already paid at the terminal. **Check for a
double payment** on the terminal's statement;
- the note “Refunded at the terminal: amount (reference)” (the reference reads “reference …”, or “no reference”): a manager declared that the terminal refunded this payment. Match
it against the terminal's statement.
Both marks appear in the Payments at the terminal to record section as well as in the collapsed Already handled
list. There is no button yet to declare a refund from the back office: it will come later. The page only shows
refunds that have already been declared; they are also logged in the
Technical events journal (“Terminal payment ignored by a
till”, “Terminal refund outside a sale”).
Disable a kiosk remotely
Deactivate asks for confirmation: “It will show “Kiosk unavailable” at its next contact with the
server; orders already confirmed remain valid. You can re-enable it here.”
Expected result: “Kiosk “Borne entrée (démo)” disabled.”; the state changes to Disabled and the button
becomes Reactivate.
No kiosk paired
Add a kiosk from Settings › Devices (“Kiosk” type, choosing a preset as you go), or assign a
preset later in Settings › Appearance › Kiosk. See Prepare the kiosk.
A kiosk is “Offline” or “Unavailable”
Offline: it has not contacted the server for 5 minutes or more (tablet switched off, asleep, app
closed, Wi-Fi down). Unavailable: it responds, but has declared itself out of service (for example, a printer
error); the Printer column helps with the diagnosis. Orders placed offline come through when it reconnects.
Reader ID required outside simulation
In Sandbox or Production, enter the reader ID assigned by the provider (e.g. tmr_… or serial
number). Other possible refusals: “The SIMULATED provider goes with the SIMULATED mode (and only it)”,
“Reader ID too long (120 characters max)”.
The simulated terminal is not allowed in production.
On the production server, the simulated terminal is not offered (“Production server: the simulated terminal is
not offered.”). Choose your terminal's real provider.
Reserved for the owner or an administrator.
A manager sees the terminal read-only (“Read only: only the owner and administrators can configure
the payment terminal.”). Ask the owner.
Kiosk limit reached: 2 kiosk(s) (Restaurant plan and “Kiosk” options). Revoke a kiosk or add the “Kiosk” option with the Vendora team.
This message appears when you add a kiosk in Settings › Devices: kiosks have their own limit, separate from
registers and phones. Each kiosk needs a Kiosk option (the Commerce and Restaurant plans include none; only the Restaurant trial includes one); an extra
device is not enough. With no kiosk planned at all: “No kiosk is included in the … plan: add the “Kiosk” option with
the Vendora team (help center).” Revoke an unused kiosk or ask the Vendora team for the option
(Add an option).
1 kiosk in service / 0 included — add the Kiosk option with the Vendora team. Nothing is cut off, but no new kiosk can be paired.
Settings › Subscription page, after subscribing to the Restaurant plan at the end of a trial: the trial kiosk stays
in service, but the plan includes no kiosk. Ask the Vendora team for the Kiosk option: the 1st option covers this
kiosk, a 2nd one lets you pair another (Subscription options).
After the trial, the kiosk shows “Kiosk temporarily unavailable”
The Restaurant trial ended without a subscription: on the Free plan, the kiosk counts as an extra device. It kept
taking orders for 15 days, then stopped. Subscribe to a plan with the Kiosk option: it resumes at its next sync
(My trial has ended).
Read-only: only the owner and administrators set up the terminal gateway.
A manager sees the gateway but cannot enable it, deactivate it or renew its secret. Ask the owner.
An order paid on the terminal stays pending on the kiosk
Check that the gateway is Active, that the terminal sends its notifications to the Webhook address with the
right Secret (a wrong signature is rejected), and that the amount paid is exactly the order's: a different amount
is not confirmed automatically: it shows as Different amount in the reconciliation and, the customer having paid, the order
appears in Terminal payments to record with the reason “Order amount differs from the payment”. An offline kiosk does not
receive the confirmation: what remains is manual confirmation (if the preset allows it) or payment at the counter.
The “Terminal payments to record” section appears
A customer paid on the terminal, but the sale could not be recorded. They have nothing to pay again. Check each line's
Reason, then have the payment recorded at the register. If the line stays, the register has not recorded the payment
yet or is not synced (A register no longer syncs).
Payment at the kiosk is unavailable in Tunisia until the NACEF module covers it: choose PAY_AT_COUNTER
The store is in Tunisia and the NACEF module does not cover the kiosk yet: the preset's On the card terminal payment
is refused. Choose At the counter; the kiosk then only offers the counter.
Reserved for the store's managers.
Only the store's managers, administrators and owner supervise the kiosks.
Configuration changed in the meantime
Someone changed the kiosk at the same time as you. Click Refresh, then try again.
Could not disable.
The server did not respond. Reload the page and try again. Do the same for “Could not re-enable.” and
“Unable to save the payment terminal.”.

pages.title: Connect your AI assistant

sections.heading: Connect your AI assistant
sections.text:
Already use Claude or ChatGPT? Link it to your business and ask questions as you would to a deputy:
"How did my day go?", "What should I order this week?". The assistant fetches the figures from Vendora and
answers in plain words. It reads your figures and can propose actions, but nothing is applied without a manager's approval (see
Approve the assistant's proposals), and your customers' data is never given to it without your
explicit consent.
Everything happens in Settings › AI assistant, a page reserved for the owner and administrators. It also works on a
phone.
Email address to confirm
Connecting an AI assistant requires the owner's email address to be confirmed: see Confirm your email address.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Activate the AI assistant option
The AI assistant is an option of your subscription: €7 excl. VAT per month in France, 15 DT in Tunisia, **free
for 3 months** the first time (once per business). It is included in the Custom plan and is not offered on the Free
plan (“Available with Commerce”).
1. Open Settings › Subscription, Subscription options card, and click Add next to AI assistant
(3 months free badge) — or Activate the option in the AI assistant block of Settings › API keys.
2. The window says “Free for 3 months, then … / month excl. tax.”: confirm.
3. The AI assistant line appears in Active options with “… this month”, the Free until … badge and
“then … / month”.
Seven days before the offer ends, Vendora emails the owner. You have nothing to do to keep the option. It is
billed in arrears: the invoice covering the end of the offer does not include it, the next one carries the
days since the offer ended, then the full month.
Don't want it any more? Click Remove in Active options. During the 3 free months, the assistant **stays
active until the end of the offer, free of charge: the line shows Active until … and a Keep the option** button
(also in the AI assistant block of Settings › API keys) cancels the removal. On that date, your “AI Assistant”
keys are suspended. After the offer, the removal is immediate. Either way, your keys and connected assistants are
suspended (the key shows Suspended), without deleting anything: reactivate the option at any time and they
resume immediately. Details:
Add an option to your subscription.
Already had the assistant before November 2026?
You received the option with 3 months free from its launch, and an email told you so: your connections keep working
without interruption.
Connect
Open Settings › AI assistant. The Connector address block (1) gives the address to provide to your assistant.
Click Copy the address (2). On a computer, a QR code (3) repeats the same address; on a phone, only the
Copy the address button is offered, first.
Then follow the three steps in your assistant's block:
- Connect Claude: in Claude, open Settings › Connectors › Add custom connector, paste the address and click
Connect. Vendora's Connect an assistant page opens: sign in if asked, choose the stores and data families to
share, then Allow. The details of that screen are in Connect an AI assistant in one click.
- Connect ChatGPT (beta): in ChatGPT, Settings › Connectors, turn on developer mode, create a custom connector,
paste the address and choose OAuth authentication. This route has not yet been tried end to end: menu names may
differ.
The connector added to your Claude account then works on all your devices, phone included.
Trial environment
On Vendora's trial environment the service goes to sleep when unused: the first call can take a minute. Later calls are fast.
Test the connection
In the Test the connection block, click the button of the same name. Vendora checks that the connector responds,
without sending any data from your business, and shows a single message:
- All good: your assistant can reach Vendora.
- Your plan does not include the AI assistant. with a link to your subscription.
- AI assistants are stopped: emergency stop or suspension by Vendora (see below).
- The service is not responding. Try again in a minute: on the trial environment, this is often the service waking up.
A second test within 10 seconds is refused: A test was just run: try again in … seconds.
Ask your first questions
The To get started block offers the questions for your type of business (restaurant, grocery, bakery, shop),
arranged by moment of the day: in the morning, at the end of the day, at the end of the week, at the end of the month.
Press Copy next to one of them, then paste it into the conversation with your assistant. With several stores,
questions for comparing your stores are added. When several types of business are possible, buttons let you choose:
for example Grocery and Bakery for a grocery, or one button per store type with All stores when they
differ. If your store type has no list, the block says so and shows exactly these five general questions:
You want to… · Ask
The summary · "Give me the summary of my day."
Know what to order · "What should I order this week, by supplier?"
Understand your margin · "Why has my margin been falling for a month?"
Check the till · "Are there any cash discrepancies this week?"
Check the store · "Are all my tills online?"
All the questions are also gathered in What to ask your assistant. To receive them
every morning without asking, see Get an automatic daily summary.
Read the answers well
- The period is always recalled ("from Monday 2 to Sunday 8 November"). If it is not the one you wanted, specify it.
- The time of the data is given. If a till has not synced, the assistant warns you: the figures may be incomplete.
- The figures come from Vendora, calculated as in your reports. If in doubt about an important decision, open the
matching report: an assistant can be wrong in its commentary.
Choose what the assistant can propose
An assistant reads your figures; it can also propose actions, which you then approve (see
Approve the assistant's proposals). The What the assistant can propose
block (1), reserved for the owner and administrators, lists eight families of actions: Catalog, Stock, Purchases,
Restaurant, Customers, Settings, Devices, Anti-fraud. Each one says what it covers, the actions the assistant will be able
to prepare in it, and the last change.
Today, four actions exist: Change a selling price and Make a product available or unavailable (Catalog),
Prepare a purchase order (Purchases) and **Handle an
anti-fraud alert (Anti-fraud). The other families show “No action is open in this family for now”. Everything is off
until you tick something. Tick the families you want, then click Save**.
Make a product available or unavailable is in the Catalog family, next to the price change: ticking the Catalog
family authorizes both.
- Allowing a family here grants it to no assistant: you then tick it each time you connect an assistant or create a
key (next steps).
- Removing a family deletes nothing: the assistant can no longer propose anything in that family, and proposals
already made remain to be decided.
- During a Vendora support session, the block can be read but not changed: only the owner and administrators set it,
from their own session.
Follow what the assistant reads
Further down the same page:
- Connected assistants: each assistant connected in one click, with who connected it, since when, on which stores
and data families. A badge says what it can do: Read only (it can propose nothing) or Read and proposals (with,
under “Proposals:”, the families of actions granted). Remove access (after confirmation) cuts it off from its next
request.
- Assistant activity: the last 50 reads, in plain words ("Claude read the sales of 10/11 of Le Petit Bistrot
(demo)"), with the originating assistant or key. The Assistant list lets you follow just one.
Connect a developer tool (optional)
The Keys for integrators block is collapsed: open it only if a developer must connect Claude Code or a script
with a key rather than through the one-click connection. Click Create a key, name it, choose the stores and data
families. The Customers family (personal data) is unticked: tick it only if truly needed.
A key proposes nothing by default. For it to be able to propose, tick Assistant proposals in the **Prepare
proposals block (1), then, under Proposal families (2), the families granted to this key: with no family ticked,
the key cannot propose anything** (“No family ticked: this key will not be able to propose anything.”). If the business
does not allow any family yet, the form says so: allow some first in What the assistant can propose. The key list has a
Proposals column: the granted families, or “No proposal”.
A family needs the matching read access: if you tick “Catalog” as a proposal family without the “Catalog” read in
Data the key can read, a warning tells you (the actions of the family that require it will not be proposable).
The key's secret is shown only once, with the Claude Code command ready to copy
(claude mcp add --transport http vendora … --header "X-API-Key: …"). Click Copy the command, then
I have saved the secret. Secret lost: create another key and revoke the old one.
Third-party software keys (online shop, accounting…) stay in Create API keys.
Cut off access
- One assistant: Remove access in Connected assistants. It can no longer read anything, right now.
- All assistants: the Emergency stop block (Stop all AI assistants), reserved for the owner, cuts off
at once the assistants connected in one click and the integrator keys. Every block of the page switches to
Stopped; Restore access puts them back in service. An administrator sees the button greyed out, with the explanation.
Every removal and every stop is recorded in the audit log.

sections.heading: What the assistant sees, and does not see
sections.text:
It can read (if you allow it) · It can never
Sales, average tickets, payment methods · Take payments, refund, send, pay or publish anything; apply a proposal without a manager's approval
Margins, food cost, purchase prices · Read PIN codes, passwords, keys
Stock, alerts, stocktakes, losses · Change fiscal data (it can only read them)
Purchase orders, supplier invoices · See the stores you have not ticked
State of the tills and kiosks · Read your customers' names and contact details, except with explicit permission
Vendora only passes your data to the assistant that you connected. What it does with it afterwards depends on its
own terms and on your settings there: check them.

sections.heading: What it knows about your catalog
sections.text:
For a product, the assistant sees its category, whether it belongs to the whole business or to a single store,
its stock-outs and its prices store by store (detailed for up to six stores; beyond that, it tells you so). It can also
list your categories and your active VAT rates, and it knows today's date in each of your stores: "yesterday" and "this
week" therefore land in the right place, even across different time zones.
An access limited to some stores does not see the products that belong only to the other stores. It cannot find
them, count them, or read their price or purchase cost.
A few questions to try:
- "What is the croque-monsieur's category, and is it sold in all my stores?"
- "Which products are out of stock, store by store?"
- "Is the tarte tatin priced the same everywhere?"
- "Which categories do I have, and which VAT rates are active?"
- "What is today's date in my stores?"
Reserved for the owner and administrators.
The page is reserved for the owner and administrators. A store manager does not see it in the menu: ask the owner to
make the connection.
AI assistant access is not included in your plan. Contact Vendora to add it.
The AI assistant option is not active: the page shows no connection block. On a paid plan, add the option
yourself in Settings › Subscription (step “Activate the AI assistant option”); on the Free plan, move to Commerce.
The page message still says “Contact Vendora”, but that is no longer necessary.
One-click connection is not available on this server for now. The integrator keys, further down, remain usable.
One-click connection is off on this server. The integrator keys remain usable; contact Vendora to turn it on.
The service is not responding. Try again in a minute.
On the trial environment (the message then adds “on the trial environment, the first call can take a minute”), the service falls asleep after a period of inactivity: wait a minute then test again. If the
message persists, check your Internet connection, then contact Vendora.
A test was just run: try again in … seconds.
Only one test is accepted every 10 seconds. Wait for the delay shown.
AI assistants are stopped (emergency stop). No assistant can read your data until the owner restores access.
The owner has turned on the emergency stop: they click Restore access in the Emergency stop block. Variant:
"Vendora has temporarily suspended AI assistant access for all businesses": nothing to do on your side, try again later.
The assistant says it cannot reach Vendora, or asks to reconnect
Check the pasted address (copy it again with Copy the address), then click Test the connection. Access may have been removed,
or expired (one year at most): connect again from the assistant.
The connection page says “request expired or already handled”
The request is valid for only 10 minutes and once: start the connection again from the assistant. See
Connect an AI assistant in one click.
The figures look incomplete, or the assistant answers off the mark
Look at the time of the data and check that the tills are online. Specify the store and the period, or ask the
assistant to “use Vendora”.
You lost your phone or shared access by mistake
Click Remove access for the assistant concerned, or Stop all AI assistants if in doubt.

pages.title: Create API keys (integrations)

sections.heading: Create API keys (integrations)
sections.text:
An API key is a password meant for a program: your ordering website, your accounting software,
a dashboard or an AI assistant uses it to read (or change) your Vendora data. By default it gives access to
all the stores in the business; you can limit it to some stores and to some data families.
Create one key per application: you can cut one off without affecting the others.
Email address to confirm
Creating an API key requires the owner's email address to be confirmed: see Confirm your email address.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Create the key
Open Settings › API keys and click New key. Fill in:
1. Key name: the software that will use it (e.g. “Ordering website”).
2. Rate limit (requests per minute): 10 to 6,000, 600 by default. Requests beyond that are throttled.
3. Expiry (optional): the key stops working after this day (at 23:59:59).
4. Key type: choose Full access (READ / WRITE) or Read access limited to data families: in the second case, under Data the key can read, check only what the software needs (e.g. “Accounting” and “Fiscal” for an accountant), and under Stores uncheck All stores to keep only some stores.
5. Scopes (full access): Read only (READ), checked by default, is enough to view data; Read and write (WRITE) also lets the program create and change data (e.g. a website that creates orders). Check it only if the provider requires it.
Click Create key.
Copy the secret (only once)
The Key secret (1), which starts with vd_live_, is shown only once (2). Click Copy (3)
and pass it on to the software or the provider through a secure channel (not by unencrypted email or text message). Then click
I have saved the secret.
Lost the secret? It cannot be shown again: create a new key and revoke the old one.
Track and revoke your keys
The Keys list (1) shows for each key its Prefix (the start of the secret, so you can recognize it), its Scopes,
its Limit, who created it, when it was Last used and its Status (Active, Revoked, Expired,
Expires on …, Suspended).
A still-valid “AI Assistant” key is Suspended when assistant access is cut off; the reason is written below it:
“AI Assistant option removed: add it back to reactivate the key”, “Emergency stop on (Settings › AI Assistant)” or
“Assistant access suspended by Vendora”. Nothing is deleted: the key works again as soon as access returns.
An assistant's key carries the AI assistant badge; a limited key shows its stores (“Stores: …”) and, under
Scopes, the data families it can read.
To cut off access (end of contract, leaked secret, abandoned software): Revoke, then confirm. The program
is refused immediately; this is final.
The provider can find the technical documentation through the OpenAPI documentation button (How to call the API
card).
AI assistants have their own page
Connecting Claude or ChatGPT, connected assistants, assistant activity, the emergency stop and creating a key for a
developer are now in Settings › AI assistant, not here. The AI assistants card of this page only points you
there (Open Settings › AI assistant). Assistant keys already created stay listed under Keys, with the
AI assistant badge, and you can still revoke them.
See Connect your AI assistant.
Stay within your plan quota
Your Vendora plan sets the number of active keys and the maximum rate per key: the … plan card (2) at the
top of the page shows your usage (“2 of 5 active key(s)”) and the maximum rate (“Maximum rate per key: 1200 requests per
minute”). The Rate limit field (3) shows the allowed range (“Between 10 and 1200”).
Beyond that, Vendora refuses the creation with a clear message (1). When all the keys of the plan are in use, the
New key button is greyed out: revoke a key you no longer use (its slot is freed at once) or upgrade your plan
(Settings › Subscription). A plan change never cuts off an existing key.
For reference: Essentiel 1 key (600 requests per minute at most), Commerce 3 keys and Restaurant 5 keys (1,200), Sur
mesure unlimited (6,000).
Follow this month's usage
The API usage card shows this month's calls against your plan's quota (“3,250 / 5,000 calls · 65 %”), the
reset date, then, depending on your country, the spending cap (France, changed with Change the cap) or the
pack balance (Tunisia), and the Last 6 months. A banner warns you at 80% and 100%. In Tunisia, when the quota
is used up but a pack is left, the card shows “Included quota used up — … prepaid calls left”: calls carry on against
your packs. Calls from AI assistants do
not count. Everything is explained in API quota and pay-as-you-go.
The status of the AI assistant option
The AI assistant block shows with a badge whether your “AI Assistant” keys can be used:
Badge · What it means
Free until … · The option is active and free until that date, then billed if you keep it.
Billed … / month · The option is active and on your subscription.
Included in your plan · Custom plan: nothing extra to pay.
3 months free · The option has never been taken: Activate the option button.
Active until … · The option was removed during the 3 free months: the assistant stays active, free of charge, until that date, then your “AI Assistant” keys are suspended. Keep the option button to cancel the removal.
Keys suspended · The option was removed: your keys and connected assistants are refused, but nothing is deleted. Activate the option button to reactivate them immediately.
Available with Commerce · Free plan: the AI assistant requires a paid plan. See my subscription button.
Activate the option opens the Activate the AI Assistant option? window (“Free for 3 months, then … / month
excl. tax.” the first time); after confirming: “AI Assistant option activated.”. See
Connect your AI assistant and
Add an option to your subscription.
Key name required
Give the key a name (80 characters at most: “Key name: 80 characters at most”).
At least one scope
Check Read only (READ), Read and write (WRITE), or both.
Rate limit between 10 and 6000 requests per minute
Enter a value between 10 and
6,000 (600 is fine in most cases).
Expiry date already passed
Choose a future date, or leave the field empty for a key
with no expiry.
Clé d'API inconnue, révoquée ou expirée
(Message received by the connected software, in French: “Unknown, revoked or expired API key”.) The key was revoked,
has expired or was copied incorrectly. Check its status here; create a new one if needed.
Clé en lecture seule : écriture refusée
(Message received by the software, in French: “Read-only key: write refused”.) It is trying to change data with a
Read only key. Create a key with Read and write (WRITE) if it is really necessary, then revoke the old one.
Limite de 600 requêtes par minute atteinte
(Message received by the software, in French: “Limit of 600 requests per minute reached”.) It calls Vendora too
often. Ask the provider to slow down, or create a key with a higher limit.
Essentiel plan limit reached: 1 active API key(s). Revoke a key or contact Vendora to upgrade your plan.
All the keys of your plan are active. Revoke an unused key, or ask for a higher plan. The plan name and the number
depend on your subscription. Variant: “The public API is not included in the … plan” (no key in the plan).
Rate limit of the Restaurant plan: 1200 requests per minute at most per key.
The limit entered exceeds your plan's maximum: enter a value within the range shown under the field
(“Between 10 and 1200”).
Restricted to the owner and administrators.
Managers do not have access to API keys.
The key could not be created.
The server did not respond. Reload the page and try again. Do the same for “Unable to revoke.”.
Choose at least one store, or “All stores”.
You unchecked All stores without checking a store: check at least one, or check All stores again.
Cette clé n'a pas la portée … nécessaire pour cette lecture.
(Message received by the software or the assistant.) The key does not cover the requested data family; the message
names the missing scope (e.g. customers:read for customers). If the access is intended, create a new key and check
that family under Data the key can read, then revoke the old one.
Magasin introuvable ou non autorisé pour cette clé
(Message received by the software or the assistant.) The key is limited to some stores and the request is about
another one. Variant for business-wide data: “Cette clé est limitée à certains magasins …”. Create a key for the right
store, or one without a store restriction.
Une clé « Assistant IA » ne peut rien créer ni modifier directement : les modifications se font au back-office Vendora ou sur la caisse.
(Message received by the assistant.) An assistant never changes data directly: it can only read and, if a family of
actions is granted to it, propose an action that a manager approves (see
Approve the assistant's proposals). When a family is granted, the message adds “Elle peut seulement préparer une proposition, qu'un responsable valide avant toute application.” (it can only prepare a proposal that a manager approves before anything is applied). Make the change yourself in the back office or on
the till, or approve its proposal.
L'accès des assistants IA est coupé pour ce commerce (arrêt d'urgence).
(Message received by the assistant.) The emergency stop is on: the owner lifts it with Restore access in
the Emergency stop block of Settings › AI assistant. Variants: “L'accès des assistants IA est suspendu par Vendora pour tous les
commerces” (nothing to do on your side, try again later) and “L'accès des assistants IA n'est pas inclus dans la
formule …” (change plan in Settings › Subscription or contact Vendora).
Activez l'option Assistant IA : l'accès des assistants IA n'est pas actif pour ce commerce (formule …).
(Message received by the assistant, in French.) The AI assistant option was removed or never taken: click
Activate the option in the AI assistant block; the keys work again from the next request. On the Free plan:
“Disponible avec Commerce : l'accès des assistants IA n'est pas inclus dans la formule Gratuit de ce commerce. …”.
Unknown or already removed connection
Access for this assistant was already removed (by you in another tab, or by another administrator). Reload
the page: the Connected assistants block of Settings › AI assistant is up to date. Same for “Could not remove access.”.

pages.title: Tax compliance: integrity, closures, archives

sections.heading: Tax compliance: integrity, closures, archives
sections.text:
Every sale is sealed by the register at the moment it is completed, even offline: a fiscal number with no gaps
and a fingerprint that chains it to the previous one. The server re-checks everything. Daily, monthly and
annual closures add up a perpetual total that is never reset to zero. Nothing sealed can be changed:
an anomaly triggers an alert, never a rewrite.
The Control › Tax compliance page lets you see this for yourself and provide the documents requested during an
audit.
Always available, whatever the plan
Closures, integrity checks and tax archives work on every plan, the Free plan included: an archive can be generated and downloaded even when accounting exports (FEC) are not included.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Control › Tax compliance
Choose the store. The table of contents links to the Tax module, Integrity, Closures,
Tax archives (and Technical log) sections.
- Tax module (1): the country and the module applied (in France: “France — art. 286-I-3° bis CGI (NF525)”), the
Download the certificate (PDF) button and the status of the Settings — Locked (real sales issued) as soon
as the first real sale is made.
- Integrity (2): Chains intact ✓ when everything is consistent, with the number of Sealed records (sales, returns and voids), the last
fiscal number of each register (chain OK), the Z reports with anomalies and the status of the closures
(chain OK, perpetual total consistent). If something is inconsistent, the badge becomes
Anomalies detected: see Reading an integrity anomaly.
The certificate (PDF) is the document to give to your accountant or to the tax authority when they ask for it.
View and generate closures
Daily closures are generated automatically after midnight. In Closures, choose
Daily, Monthly or Annual (1). Each row shows the Period, the Grand total for the
period, the Perpetual total since opening, the Fingerprint and the Link (the fingerprint of the previous
closure) (3). PDF exports the displayed list.
If closures are missing (for example, the server was down for a night), the owner clicks
Generate due closures (2): “… closure(s) generated.” or “All due closures have already been generated.”.
Produce a tax archive
The tax archive is a ZIP file in an open format (CSV + manifest + notice in French) that can be checked
without Vendora, locked by a chained fingerprint. This is what you hand over during an audit.
The ventes.csv file (one row per sale, return or void) has five more columns: the record type, the signing algorithm,
the signer identifier, the signature and the canonical content (what was signed). A cles_publiques.csv file
added to the archive gives the registers' public keys: with it, an inspector can check the signatures without Vendora.
Sales from before this change have no signature: their columns are empty. Voids appear there with the type VOID. The
rapports_z.csv file gains four columns: the algorithm, the signer, the signature and the **canonical
content** of the signed Z report; they are empty for a Z report from before the change.
1. Choose the period: From and to. It must be closed (ending yesterday at the latest) and each of its
days must have its daily closure.
2. Click Generate archive. The archive is prepared in the background: the banner “Archive … → … requested: being
generated, the download link will appear in the list.” appears and its row shows the In progress… badge (1).
For a long period (a year of a large business) this can take a few minutes: you can leave the page, the archive
keeps going.
3. Without reloading the page, the row fills in. Expected result: “Archive … → … generated (hash …).”; the row (1)
shows the date, size, Fingerprint and Previous (the fingerprint of the archive before it: archives are
chained).
4. Click Download (2) on its row and keep the file in a safe place.
If generation fails, the row shows Failure and the reason under the period (for example missing closures): fix
the cause, then click Generate archive again.
Recently opened business
The suggested period starts on the 1st of the previous month, or on the store's first day if that is more recent. A
period that starts earlier is moved up to that first day: the start date shown on the archive's row
is the real one.
Follow purges of detail older than 6 years
The law requires keeping sales detail for 6 years. After that, Vendora can purge this detail (the lines and
payments of each sale) to lighten the database, but only if it is covered by a sealed tax archive whose
fingerprint is checked again just before. Closures, the perpetual total, Z reports, the technical log and
archives are never purged: the reference archive stays downloadable and is authoritative.
Under Tax archives, the Detail purges (over 6 years) part lists each purge: the date, the purged Period (1),
the deleted Volumes (2) and the Reference archive (3). As long as nothing has been purged, it shows “No purge:
all sales detail is kept. …”.
Each purge is also written to the Technical event log (JET) with the Detail purge badge (1): period and
volumes. The reference archive is shown in the purges table, just above.
The purge is automatic and daily; you have nothing to do. So that a year can be purged one day, generate its archive
(for example every year, after the annual closure).

sections.heading: Reading an integrity anomaly
sections.text:
When the server finds an inconsistency, the Anomalies detected badge (1) replaces Chains intact ✓ and the
Anomalies to report block (2) says in plain words what is wrong: the sale (fiscal number and receipt) or the Z
report concerned, the register, one sentence per anomaly and, in small print, its technical code.

sections.heading: On a sealed sale
sections.text:
What the page shows · Technical code · What it means
“The sale's content no longer matches its fingerprint: it was changed after sealing.” · HASH_MISMATCH · The server recomputed the sale's fingerprint: it is not the one the register sealed.
“The sale's sealed content cannot be read.” · UNREADABLE · The sealed record sent by the register cannot be read back.
“The number of the sale received is not the one that was sealed.”“The lines or totals of the sale received are not the ones that were sealed.”“The return received does not match the sealed return (missing reason or different original sale).”“The signer identifier of the envelope differs from the one in the signed content. The sale is kept as it is.” · CONTENT_MISMATCH · The sale received by the server and its sealed record do not say the same thing. The last sentence: the signer identifier is inconsistent. The sentences specific to a card payment at the kiosk and to a void are in On a card payment at the kiosk and On a void.
“The sale was sealed by a different register from the one that sent it.” · DEVICE_MISMATCH · The register written in the seal is not the one that transmitted the sale.
“The sealed total (…) does not match the total recomputed by the server (…).” · ENGINE_MISMATCH · The server redid the sale's calculation and does not get the sealed total.
“… sale(s) missing before this one: fiscal no. … expected, no. … received.”“Fiscal number already used or received out of order: no. … expected, no. … received.” · SEQUENCE_GAP · The register's fiscal numbering has a gap, or a number arrived twice or out of order. It may be a sale the register has not sent yet.
“The sale does not link to the register's previous sale (broken chain).” · BROKEN_LINK · Each sale carries the fingerprint of the previous one; here, that link does not match.
“The sale should have been signed by the register and is not. It is kept as it is.”“The sale's signature does not match its content: the sale may have been changed after it was signed. It is kept as it is.”“The sale was signed with a different key from the register's. It is kept as it is.”“The sale's signature could not be checked: the server does not know the register's key. This is not proof of a change. The sale is kept as it is.”“The sale is signed with a method the server does not recognise: its signature could not be checked. It is kept as it is.”“The sale is not signed although the register was already signing previous sales. It is kept as it is.” · BAD_SEAL_SIGNATURE · The register signs each sale and each return with the device key, and the server checks the signature. In all six cases the sale is kept as it is. Only the second sentence points to a possible change; the fourth only means the server could not check.

sections.heading: On a card payment at the kiosk
sections.text:
A kiosk only records a payment through a sealed, signed sale on its own chain. When the customer pays on a standalone
terminal, that sale comes from the terminal's confirmation (with its transaction number) or from a manager's manual
confirmation, under their code (the manager's code at the kiosk):
the sealed payment of that second sale then carries the trace of the code granted and of the manager who gave it. Vendora judges the sale on its sealed
content: if anything does not hold, it is kept as it is and reported under the code CONTENT_MISMATCH, with one
sentence per cause.
What the page shows · What it means
“The card sale at the kiosk was recorded without a transaction reference although the terminal confirmed the payment. It is kept as it is: match it against the terminal's statement.” · A payment confirmed by the terminal must carry its transaction number; it is missing. (A manual confirmation may have no reference: that is not an anomaly.)
“The card payment at the kiosk was confirmed by hand, but no manager code granted to this kiosk for this order was found. The sale is kept as it is: check who confirmed the payment, then match it against the terminal's statement.” · The sale cites a manager code that the server cannot find for this kiosk and this order.
“The manager code cited by this card sale at the kiosk was used for several orders: every sale that cites it is flagged, and there is no telling which one is the right one. The sale is kept as it is: check who confirmed each payment, then match them against the terminal's statement.” · A manager code is only good for one order: if several cite it, every sale that cites it is flagged, and there is no telling which one is the right one.
“The manager code cited by this card sale at the kiosk was granted outside the time of the payment. The sale is kept as it is: check who confirmed the payment, then match it against the terminal's statement.” · The code was granted more than 90 seconds before the payment, or more than 5 seconds after it.
In the last three cases, the payment did take place: it is the check of the manager's code that did not hold. Change
nothing: check with the team who confirmed the payment, then match the sale against the terminal's statement
(kiosk payment reconciliation).
Kiosk sale outside the allowed form. A kiosk only takes card payments, at the terminal, with no change,
discount, tip, customer or user. When a kiosk sale falls outside that form, it is reported under the code
CONTENT_MISMATCH by one of the sentences below. Each one ends with the same sentence: “The sale is kept as it is and
counted in turnover, with no stock movement and no order settlement: a manager decides in the sync quarantine.” (for a
return: “The return is kept as it is and reduces turnover, with no stock movement and no order settlement: …”).
A void is the exception: its sentence has its own ending and is given in full. For a sale that combines several
deviations, see the “several reasons” row and the list of reasons under the table.
What the page shows · What it means
“Kiosk sale with no order: it is not linked to any kiosk order. …” · The sale matches no order placed at the kiosk.
“Kiosk sale not paid by card: a kiosk only takes card payments, at the terminal. …” · The payment is not a card payment.
“Kiosk sale with change given: a kiosk does not give change. …” · The sale carries change given.
“Kiosk sale with a discount: a kiosk does not give discounts. …” · The sale carries a discount.
“Kiosk sale with a tip: a kiosk does not take tips. …” · The sale carries a tip.
“Kiosk sale linked to a customer: a kiosk does not link customers. …” · The sale is linked to a customer.
“Kiosk sale with a credit note, an override or loyalty points: a kiosk does not apply any. …” · The sale applies a credit note, an override or loyalty points.
“Return recorded by a kiosk: a kiosk does not refund. …” · A return came from the kiosk; it reduces turnover.
“Void recorded by a kiosk: a kiosk does not void. The void is kept as received, with its fiscal number, and flagged: check with the team why the kiosk voided this sale.” · A void (code VOID) came from the kiosk. It is kept as received, with its fiscal number; ask the team why the kiosk voided this sale.
“Kiosk sale recorded under a user's name: a kiosk sells without a user. …” · The sale is under a user's name.
“Simulated kiosk sale received in production: it counts in turnover although no money was taken. … To correct it, make a return at the register.” · A kiosk test sale reached a real shop: no money was taken.
“Kiosk sale outside the accepted form for several reasons: discount · tip. It is kept as received and counted in the figures, with no stock movement and no settlement of the order: a manager decides in the synchronisation quarantine.” · The sale combines several distinct deviations: the sentence lists them all, separated by “·” (here a discount and a tip).
“Kiosk sale outside the allowed form. …” · General sentence, for any other reason.
Reasons listed by the “several reasons” sentence, in the page's words: no order · not paid by card · change given ·
discount · tip · customer attached · credit note, override or loyalty points · return · user name · simulated sale ·
voiding · other deviation.
The sale is kept and counted in turnover (a return reduces it). Its stock movement and the order settlement, for
their part, wait for a manager's decision in the synchronisation quarantine, where
they appear under the label “payment or stock movement of a kiosk sale outside the allowed form: the sale is kept and
flagged, a manager decides. Accepting records the stock movement or settles the order; rejecting sets them aside, the
sale stays recorded and the order stays open”. The sale itself is never corrected: to correct it, make a return at the
register.

sections.heading: On a Z report
sections.text:
The register signs every Z report with the device key and Vendora checks the signature, as for a sale. A Z report from before this change is not signed and is not reported for that reason alone.
What the page shows · Technical code · What it means
“The Z report's content no longer matches its fingerprint: it was changed after closing.” · HASH_MISMATCH · The server recomputed the Z report's fingerprint: it is not the one the register declared.
“One or more Z reports are missing before this one: no. … expected, no. … received.”“Unexpected Z report number: no. … expected, no. … received.”“The number written in the Z report is not the one announced by the register.” · NUMBER_GAP · The register's Z report numbering has a gap or an inconsistency. It may be a Z report the register has not sent yet.
“A Z report with this number was already archived for this register: the second one was not recorded.” · DUPLICATE_NUMBER · Two different Z reports carry the same number; only the first one received is kept.
“The Z report does not link to the register's previous Z report (broken chain).” · BROKEN_LINK · Each Z report carries the fingerprint of the previous one; here, that link does not match.
“The Z report was issued by a different register from the one that sent it.” · DEVICE_MISMATCH · The register written in the Z report is not the one that transmitted it.
“The Z report received cannot be read: it could not be archived.” · UNREADABLE · The content sent by the register cannot be read back.
“The signer identifier in the envelope differs from the one in the signed content of the Z report. It is kept as it is.”“The Z report does not match the sales received from this register: the last sale it announces (fiscal no. …) was not received or does not have the same fingerprint. … The report is kept as it is: check that the register has sent everything, then contact Vendora support if the gap remains.”“The Z report does not match the sales received from this register: … record(s) are missing between fiscal no. … and no. … of the session. …”“The Z report does not match the sequence of sales received from this register: records from this register are missing or differ. …” · CONTENT_MISMATCH · The Z report announces the end of the register's sales chain (first and last fiscal numbers of the session, fingerprint of the last one); what Vendora received does not match. First sentence: the envelope's signer differs from the one in the signed content. The next three: the last announced sale was not received or has a different fingerprint, or records are missing in the session. The report is kept as it is.
“This kiosk's Z report declares an opening cash float, although a kiosk only takes card payments. …”“This kiosk's Z report declares expected or counted cash, although a kiosk only takes card payments. …”“This kiosk's Z report declares a cash variance, although a kiosk only takes card payments. …”“This kiosk's Z report declares a cash float, cash or a variance, although a kiosk only takes card payments. …” · CONTENT_MISMATCH · A kiosk's report (or session) declares a cash float, cash or a variance: a kiosk has no cash drawer. Last sentence: another case of the same kind. Each sentence ends with: “The report and the session are kept as they are: a manager checks what the kiosk actually took.”
“The Z report should have been signed by the register and is not. It is kept as it is.”“The Z report's signature does not match its content: the report may have been changed after it was signed. It is kept as it is.”“The Z report was signed with a different key from the register's. It is kept as it is.”“The Z report's signature could not be checked: the server does not know the register's key. This is not proof of a change. The report is kept as it is.”“The Z report is signed with a method the server does not recognise: its signature could not be checked. It is kept as it is.”“The Z report is not signed although the register was already signing previous reports. It is kept as it is.” · BAD_SEAL_SIGNATURE · The same six cases as for a sale. In all of them the report is kept as it is. Only the second sentence points to a possible change; the fourth only means the server could not check.
For a kiosk, this Z report is kept as it is and reported: a kiosk has no cash drawer, so no cash float, cash or
variance means anything for it. A manager checks what the kiosk actually took.

sections.heading: On a void
sections.text:
Voiding a ticket at the register produces a separate sealed record, signed by the register: it takes the **next
fiscal number** (the original sale keeps its own) and changes neither the X nor the Z, whose totals stay what they were.
If Vendora finds that a void does not match the sale it voids, it is reported, under the code
CONTENT_MISMATCH, with one of the sentences below (one per cause), and kept as it is:
What the page shows · What it means
“The void of sale no. … has no sealed link, although the register seals its voids. The sale stays as it was received: contact Vendora support, giving the register and this number.” · The void received has no sealed record (the chain link), although registers produce one for every void.
“This sale had already been voided: a second void was received. It is kept as it is.” · The same sale is voided a second time.
“This sale had already been refunded by a sealed return: its void was received afterwards. It is kept as it is; what remains of a refunded sale is returned through a return.” · The sale had already been refunded, even in part; what remains is returned through a return.
“The total, discount or VAT of the void received are not the opposite of those of the voided sale. It is kept as it is.” · The void's amounts and VAT are not the opposite of the sale's.
“The void received has no sealed reason, or its origin or number are not those of the envelope. It is kept as it is.” · The void's reason is not sealed, or its origin or number differ from the envelope's.
A void reported before this change, whose cause was not recorded, keeps the original general sentence: “The void
received does not match the voided sale or its sealed record: …”.
What to do is below: change nothing, then contact support. At the register, a sale that has **already been refunded,
even in part, can no longer be voided**; see Void a ticket, process a return.

sections.heading: Payments received at the kiosk terminal, sale to record
sections.text:
When the customer paid on the terminal but the sale cannot be recorded at the kiosk (not enough stock, cash day could
not be opened, different amount), the fact is never lost: it is written to the technical events journal (JET) under
the label Terminal payment not recorded (as a warning): “Terminal payment not recorded: order no. …, amount,
reference … (or “no reference”). Confirmed by the terminal (or Confirmed by hand by a manager), paid on …. Cause: …”.
Once a register has recorded that payment, the JET adds Terminal payment settled: “… the sale fiscal no. … (receipt
…) was recorded by the device …”, with the time of the original payment. The Kiosks page
lists these payments while they remain to be recorded.
For now, two things are not delivered: the printed Z report and the server's daily closing do not yet flag
these payments to record (only the register's closing warns); and an amount paid that differs from what was due has no
way out at the register yet.

sections.heading: Kiosk payments: other technical journal events
sections.text:
Three types of the technical events journal (JET) concern payments made at a kiosk's terminal:
Type · What the page shows · What you do
Terminal payment ignored by a till (red badge) · “A till that was unaware of the terminal payment (older version or not yet synchronised) acted (“…”) on order no. …, already paid at the kiosk terminal (amount, reference): risk of double payment. Check that the customer did not pay twice.” · Check for a double payment: compare the order with the terminal's statement. The Kiosks page also flags the order concerned.
Terminal refund outside a sale · “Terminal refund declared outside a sale by a manager: order no. …, paid …, refunded … (total …), reference ….” followed by “The order no longer needs to be recorded.” or “Left to record: ….” · Match the refund against the terminal's statement, using the reference.
Kiosk payment refused by a manager (warning) · “A manager refused the fact “…” held in quarantine: …. Note: …”, with “Decision made from a till.” when the decision came from a till. · Nothing to correct: the refused payment stays readable in the quarantine of the synchronisation. If in doubt, match it against the terminal's statement.

sections.heading: What to do
sections.text:
1. Do not change anything. Nothing has been changed or deleted: sealed data stays exactly as it was received, and
there is nothing for you to change, on the register or in the back office.
2. If a number is missing (SEQUENCE_GAP, NUMBER_GAP) or if a Z report does not match the sales received
(CONTENT_MISMATCH on a Z report), keep the register concerned switched on and connected: it sends what has not
arrived yet. If the gap remains, go to the next step; the report is kept as it is.
3. Contact Vendora support with the register, the number concerned (the sale's fiscal number and receipt, or the
Z report number) and the technical code.
Special cases.
- “Could not be checked” signature (“… the server does not know the register's key …”): this is not proof of a
change, only a statement that the server could not check the signature. The sale stays recorded; report it to support
with the register concerned.
- Card sale at the kiosk with no transaction reference, or confirmed by hand with a manager code that was not found,
was used for several orders or was granted outside the time of the payment: match the sale against the terminal's statement,
as in the kiosk payment reconciliation (the sentences in detail).
- At present, the register signs sales, returns and voids, and its Z reports; a record or a Z report that is not
signed although the register was already signing previous ones is reported as above. Checking the chain on the
register itself and the “integrity compromised” screen are not delivered yet.
A reported anomaly stays on record, even once its cause is understood: this is intended, the log is never rewritten.
The same sentences appear in Checkout and payments › Z reports (Anomaly badge, details, and the report's PDF,
in French), on the dashboard (Integrity alerts card) and in the Technical event log (JET), under the
Sealing anomaly label.
An “Archive of a previous pairing” line in the log? It appears when a register (or another device) **re-paired to a
different store** has set aside, on the device, the data of its previous pairing. Nothing from the former business is
sent to this store: the line only says that an archive exists. It is not an anomaly and there is nothing to do.
An “Export of a pairing archive” line in the log? A manager exported, from a register, the archive of a
previous pairing (with their code). The line holds no content from the former business. It is not an anomaly and
there is nothing to do. An “Archive record rejected” line means an archive fact (its type, PairingArchiveCreated
or PairingArchiveExported, is named in the line) was not in the accepted form: its content was not kept; tell support
if it keeps happening.
Missing daily closures (7/37): generate the due closures before archiving
Some days of the period do not have a daily closure yet (the figures vary: 7 closures found out of
37 days). Click Generate due closures, then Generate archive again.
Nothing to archive before the store's first day (…): choose a period that ends on or after this date.
The whole chosen period is before the store was opened in Vendora. Choose an end date on or
after the day shown.
The detail from … to … was purged after 6 years: download the existing reference archive instead of generating a new one.
The detail of this period has already been purged: a new archive would be incomplete. Download the archive shown as
Reference archive in Detail purges (over 6 years).
Archive being generated: try again in a moment.
The archive is not ready yet (In progress… badge). Wait until the Download button appears on its row.
This archive could not be generated: start the generation again.
Generation failed (Failure badge, reason under the period). Fix the cause shown, then click Generate archive
again. If the reason is “Internal error during generation (…).”, try again later, then contact Vendora if it keeps
failing.
Period not closed: the end must be before today
An archive only covers finished days. Choose an end date no later than yesterday.
Invalid period
The end date is before the start date. Swap them.
Certificate only available for stores subject to the French tax module
The PDF certificate only exists for the France module (NF525). For another country, contact Vendora.
The “Anomalies detected” badge replaces “Chains intact ✓”
The server found an inconsistency (a missing number, a fingerprint that does not match, a Z report with anomalies).
Nothing has been changed or deleted, and there is nothing for you to change: read the Anomalies to report block,
write down the register, the number and the technical code, then contact Vendora support. See
Reading an integrity anomaly. The alert also appears on the
dashboard, in the Integrity alerts card.
Owner or Administrator role required
Generating closures or archives, and downloading an archive, is reserved for the owner and administrators.
Archiving denied.
The server did not respond. Reload the page and try again. Do the same for “Generation denied.”,
“Download failed.” and “Tax configuration unavailable.”.

pages.title: Connect an AI assistant in one click

sections.heading: Connect an AI assistant in one click
sections.text:
You add the Vendora connector in your assistant (Claude on the web or on a phone, Claude Code,
ChatGPT); the assistant then opens the Connect an assistant page of your back office. There you choose what
you share, then you go back to the assistant: there is no key to copy. The assistant reads your figures;
it can only propose actions if you tick that, and nothing is applied without a manager's approval.
Your customers' data is never shared.
Email address to confirm
Connecting an AI assistant requires the owner's email address to be confirmed: see Confirm your email address.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Start the connection from the assistant
In your assistant, add the Vendora connector (Vendora gives you its address) and start the connection.
Your browser opens the back office: sign in as usual if asked, then the **Connect an
assistant** page appears by itself.
Never open this page from a link received by email or message: it must only appear right after
you started the connection.
Check who is asking for access
The box at the top (1) gives the assistant's name, its Domain and the address you will be sent back to after
you answer. The Verified badge marks an assistant known to Vendora (Claude, ChatGPT).
A Not verified badge means the name and domain are the ones the assistant declares itself: only allow
if you have just started this connection, and decline at the slightest doubt.
Choose the stores and the data
Under Which stores? (2), keep All my stores, or untick it to tick only some stores.
Under Which data? (3), tick the kinds of data you need:
- Sales and reports: products, prices, receipts, revenue and reports.
- Stock: stock quantities, movements and stocktakes.
- Purchases: suppliers, orders, receptions and purchase invoices.
- Devices: the store's tills, printers and screens, and their status.
- Anti-fraud: control alerts. It is never ticked in advance.
- Settings: theme, receipt, floor plan, stations, sales screen and loyalty program of your stores. No customer or employee data.
Under Prepare proposals, the Assistant proposals box (never ticked in advance) allows the assistant to file
proposals. The Which actions? block then lists the families of actions your business allows (Catalog, Purchases,
Anti-fraud…), with the actions they contain: none is ticked by default, and the assistant only gets those you tick.
Nothing is proposed for an unticked family.
A yellow warning helps you forget nothing:
- family ticked without the main box: “Also tick “Assistant proposals” above: without it, the ticked families are not
granted.”;
- main box without a family: “No family ticked: the assistant will not be able to propose anything.”;
- missing read access: a family often needs a read access. For example, for “Catalog”, also tick “Sales and reports”
under Which data?; for “Purchases”, “Purchases”; for “Anti-fraud”, “Anti-fraud”. Without it, the actions of the
family that require it cannot be proposed.
If your business does not allow any family yet, the block says so: the owner allows some in Settings › AI assistant
(see Connect your AI assistant).
On a phone, the page shows the same choices one below the other.
Allow or decline
Click Allow (5): the message “Access allowed. Returning to your assistant…” appears and you go back
to the assistant, which can now answer your questions. Decline shares nothing and also takes you back to
the assistant.
A request is valid for 10 minutes and can only be used once. After that, start the connection again from
the assistant.
Remove access later
The assistant appears in Settings › AI assistant, Connected assistants block. Remove access cuts it off from
its next request; the Emergency stop block cuts off all assistants at once. See
Connect your AI assistant.
This connection request has expired or was already answered. Start the connection again from your assistant.
The request is more than 10 minutes old, or you already answered it (in another tab, for example). Go back to
the assistant and start the connection again. Same for “Unknown connection request.” and “Incomplete connection
link.”.
Only the owner and administrators can connect an assistant. You can decline the request.
Your account (manager, cashier…) cannot share the business's data. Click Decline, or ask
the owner to make the connection with their account.
This assistant could not be identified. For safety, the connection is cancelled. Try again from your assistant.
Vendora could not read the assistant's identity document. Try again from the assistant; if it keeps happening, the
problem comes from the assistant, not from your account.
The return address requested by this assistant is not recognised. For safety, the connection is cancelled and you are not sent to that address.
The assistant asks to send you back to an address it did not declare. Do not go on: it may be an
attempt to deceive you. Start the connection again from an assistant you trust.
This connection request is not valid. For your safety, you are not sent back to this assistant. Start the connection again from your assistant.
The assistant sent an incomplete or incorrect request, and Vendora does not know it: you stay on Vendora instead of
being sent back to it. Nothing was shared. Start the connection again from an assistant you trust; if it keeps
happening, the problem is on the assistant's side.
This connection request was opened in another browser. For your safety, it cannot be accepted here. Start the connection again from your assistant, on this device.
The link you opened comes from a connection started elsewhere: on another device, in another browser, or by someone
else. If someone sent you this link, do not go on: it may be an attempt to deceive you. Otherwise, start the
connection again from the assistant and answer in the browser that opens, without copying the link elsewhere.
Too many connection requests in a short time. Wait a minute, then start the connection again from your assistant.
Wait a minute before starting the connection again.
AI assistants are stopped for this business (emergency stop). The owner can restore access in Settings › API keys.
The emergency stop is active: the owner clicks Restore access in the Emergency stop block of Settings › AI assistant, then
you start the connection again. Variant: “Vendora has temporarily suspended AI assistant access for all
businesses” (nothing to do on your side, try again later).
Choose at least one kind of data.
Tick at least one box under Which data?. Likewise, “Choose at least one store, or “All my
stores”.”: tick a store or tick All my stores again.
Could not allow access. Try again.
The server did not answer. Check your Internet connection and click again; if the request expired in the
meantime, start the connection again from the assistant. Same for “Could not decline. Try again.” and “Could not
display the connection request.”.
