pages.title: Build your team: roles, invitations, PIN

sections.heading: Build your team: roles, invitations, PIN
sections.text:
Each team member has their own access: their sales are signed in their name, and what they can do depends
on their role. On the registers, people sign in with a personal PIN (4 to 6 digits), even without internet.

sections.heading: Roles
sections.text:
Role · For whom · What they can do
Owner · You · Everything, including the subscription, the main register, policies and transfer of ownership. Only one per business.
Administrator · Partner, trusted accountant · The whole back office for all stores, except decisions reserved for the owner.
Manager · Store manager, floor supervisor · Back office for their stores: catalog, team (roles up to Manager), devices, reports. Approves sensitive actions at the register with their PIN.
Cashier · Register · Sell, open and close the register. Discount above the threshold, return, drawer: with a manager's PIN.
Waiter · Floor · Take orders on the floor phone.
Kitchen · Kitchen, bar · The kitchen display.
Only the owner, administrators and managers have access to the back office (and must therefore be invited by email).
User limit
On the Free plan, the team has at most 3 users, owner included; pending invitations count too. Beyond that, the invitation is refused. Deactivating a member or canceling an invitation frees a place; existing members stay active. The counter is on Settings › Subscription (Users (active or invited)).
Email address to confirm
Inviting or creating a team member requires the owner's email address to be confirmed: see Confirm your email address.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Settings › Team
Choose the store. The table lists the members with their Role (1), the status of their Register PIN (2) —
Set ✓, To be redefined or None — and their Status (Active, Disabled, Invited — expires on …).
The action buttons (3) are at the end of each row.
Add a member with a PIN (registers only)
For a cashier, waiter or cook who only uses the store's devices. In Add a member:
1. Leave With a register PIN (registers only) checked (1).
2. Fill in Name, Email, Role and Register PIN (2) — 4 to 6 digits, different from those of colleagues
in the store. The email is required, but no message is sent to it.
3. Click Add (3).
Expected result: “… added — their PIN reaches the registers at the next synchronization (≤ 30 s).”
Tell them their PIN in person.
Invite a member to the back office by email
For a store manager, an administrator — or anyone who should choose their own password and PIN:
1. Check By email invitation (back office access — link valid for 72 h) (1).
2. Fill in Name, Email and Role (2). If you have multiple stores, check Also in … to give them access to the others.
3. Click Invite (3).
Expected result: “Invitation sent to … — valid 72 h.” (1) and a row Invited — expires on … (2). The
person receives the email “Invitation à rejoindre le back-office” (sent in French: “Invitation to join the back
office”) and follows Accept an invitation.
Link lost or expired: Resend invitation generates a new link (the old one stops working).
Invitation sent by mistake, or the person is no longer coming: Cancel invitation. “…'s invitation canceled —
the link received by email no longer works.”; the row changes to Disabled.
Change a role, reset a PIN
- Change role: choose the new role in the list (1), then Confirm. The registers apply it at the
next sync. A manager can assign roles up to Manager; only the owner or an
administrator can appoint an Administrator.
- Reset PIN: an employee forgot their PIN, or it shows To be redefined? Enter the new PIN (1)
then Confirm; “…'s PIN reset.”.
- Deactivate: for someone who leaves. The member is signed out of the registers at the next sync, and their PIN is
erased; their sales remain signed in their name. There is no confirmation.
(Owner, administrator) Reactivate a disabled member
An employee comes back, or an invitation was canceled by mistake: on their Disabled row, click
Reactivate (1). Only the owner and administrators see this button; the operation is recorded in the
audit log.
- Member with a register PIN or back office access: they become Active again, but without a PIN (erased
on deactivation). “… reactivated — set a new register PIN so they can sign in on the registers again.”; the
New PIN field opens right away (2): enter it, then Confirm.
- Canceled invitation, never accepted: the invitation is sent again with a new 72 h link: “…'s invitation
renewed — new link sent to …, valid for 72 h.”.
(Owner) Register inactivity timeout and transfer of ownership
At the bottom of the page:
- Register security — inactivity timeout (1): with no activity for this long, the register returns to
“Who are you?” (the current sale is kept). Enter the Time (minutes, 1 to 240) then
Publish time limit; the registers apply it at their next sync. Default: 5 minutes.
- Transfer ownership (2): choose the New owner (a member invited by email who has activated
their account), enter Your password, then click Transfer ownership and confirm. You become an
administrator.
3 users in the Gratuit plan — Commerce makes them unlimited. Deactivate a member or change plan.
Your plan's user limit is reached (the number and plan names vary). Deactivate a member who left, cancel an unneeded invitation or move to a paid plan (The Free plan).
Creation denied. PIN already used in this store, choose another one
Each PIN is unique within a store (it is what identifies the person on the register). Choose another one.
The same message appears when resetting a PIN (“Reset denied. …”) or in My PIN.
Creation denied. Email already in use
This address already has a Vendora account (in your business, deactivated, or elsewhere). Use another address.
The same message appears for an invitation (“Invitation denied. Email already in use”).
The PIN must be 4 to 6 digits.
Digits only, from 4 to 6. The Add button stays grayed out until the PIN, the name and the email are valid.
Invitation denied. You cannot invite a Administrator (a role above yours) to this store
A manager cannot invite or appoint anyone above Manager. Ask the owner. Variant when changing
a role: “Role change denied. You cannot assign the Administrator role”.
Invitation created for …, but the email was not sent (provider not configured): use “Resend” later.
The invitation exists but the email could not be sent. Click Resend invitation a little later; if
the problem persists, contact Vendora.
Deactivation denied. Member already deactivated
The member was deactivated in the meantime (from another computer, for example). Reload the page: their row shows
Disabled; Reactivate puts them back in service.
Reactivation denied. Reactivation reserved for the owner and administrators
A manager cannot reactivate a
member. Ask the owner or an administrator. Variant: “Reactivation denied. Member already active” — they were reactivated in the meantime: reload the page.
Invitation canceled — ask for a new invitation
(Seen by the invited person when opening an old link.) Their invitation was canceled. Reactivate on their row sends them a new link.
Role change denied. You cannot change your own role
You cannot change your own role. The owner's role only changes through Transfer ownership.
No member can take over ownership in this store: you need a member invited by email who has activated their back office access.
First invite the person by email, wait for them to activate their account, then come back to transfer ownership.
Incorrect password
(Transfer of ownership.) The password you entered is not yours. Type it again.
Read-only: only the store owner changes this timeout.
The inactivity timeout is reserved for the owner.
Policy changed in the meantime — value reloaded, check it and republish.
Someone published a timeout while you were editing it. Check the displayed value and publish again.
Unable to load the team.
The server did not respond. Reload the page.

pages.title: Free trial: rules and end of trial

sections.heading: Free trial: rules and end of trial
sections.text:
The free trial is real use of Vendora: receipts, Z closures and tax features are complete, with no watermark, and
no payment method. Your registers are never cut off, neither during nor after the trial. At sign-up, you can
also choose Start for free: you start directly on the Free plan, with no
trial.

sections.heading: The rules at a glance
sections.text:
Rule · Detail
Counter start · At your first real sale (not at sign-up).
Length · 60 days from the first sale (the exact length for your market is shown on the Subscription page), at most 90 days after sign-up.
Trial without a sale · Closed 30 days after sign-up (an email warns you 7 days before).
Scope · 1 store, 3 selling devices — and 1 kiosk for a Restaurant trial —, the trial plan's modules; white label and multi-store after subscribing.
Offer · Subscription before D+30 of the counter: your 3rd month is free (discount on the invoice).
End of trial · Without a subscription, you keep going for free on the Free plan: no read-only period, no suspension, nothing is deleted; paid modules are hidden and you get 15 days to choose the register that stays active.
One trial per business · Only one trial per phone number and per SIRET / tax ID over 12 months.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Follow your trial
A banner at the top of every page (1) shows the trial status: Trial: your … days start with your first sale. before
the first sale, then Trial — … days left. Subscribe before …: your 3rd month is free. The Free trial card on
Settings › Subscription (2) shows when the counter started, the end date and the trial scope. For a Restaurant trial, it reads “During the trial:
1 store, 3 selling devices and 1 kiosk, …”: you can pair an ordering kiosk on top of your
3 selling devices.
Read the trial emails
Vendora writes to you in your store's language (French, English or Arabic):
- D+1: welcome and the 3 steps to get started (catalogue, register, first sale);
- D+3: if your catalogue is empty, we import it for you;
- D+7: help with the first receipt, if no sale has been made yet;
- 7 days before closing a trial that is still without a sale;
- D+30 of the counter: review of your reports; D+50: choose your plan (yearly gives 2 months free);
D+58: last reminder;
- at the end of the trial: “Your trial is over: you carry on for free”.
An email that no longer applies (catalogue already imported, sale already made) is not sent.
At the end of the trial: you keep going for free
If you have not subscribed by the end of the trial, your business moves to the Free plan: 1 store, 1 sales device,
300 products, 3 users. The banner shows Your trial is over: you keep going for free. The back office can still be
edited and your registers keep taking payments and syncing.
Nothing is deleted: paid modules (stock counts, batches, full reports, accounting export, loyalty…) are hidden and
reappear with their data as soon as you subscribe. If you had several registers, you have 15 days to choose the one
that stays active. Everything is explained in My trial is over.
To keep everything, choose a plan with the Vendora team (View subscription link), ideally before the end of the
trial.
Restaurant trial: what happens to the kiosk?
A Restaurant trial includes 1 kiosk, on top of the 3 selling devices. At the end of the trial:
- you subscribe to the Restaurant plan: the trial kiosk stays in service, but the plan includes no kiosk. The
Subscription page shows “1 kiosk in service / 0 included — add the Kiosk option with the Vendora team.” Ask the
Vendora team for the Kiosk option: the 1st option covers the trial kiosk, a 2nd option lets you pair
another one (Subscription options). Nothing is billed automatically;
- you carry on with the Free plan: the kiosk counts as an extra device. It keeps taking orders for 15 days,
then shows Kiosk temporarily unavailable until you subscribe with the Kiosk option
(My trial has ended).
A Commerce trial includes no kiosk.
Your trial is over: you keep going for free.
The trial ended without a plan: you are on the Free plan. See My trial is over for
what changes. The banner disappears after 30 days, or as soon as you subscribe.
A free trial was already opened with this phone number or tax ID less than 12 months ago: contact Vendora to subscribe directly.
At sign-up: a trial was already opened with this phone number (1) or this SIRET / tax ID less than a year ago (2).
Contact Vendora to open your workspace directly on a plan.
Gratuit plan limit reached: 1 sales device(s) (kiosks excluded). Upgrade to a higher plan or add an extra device (Subscription page).
After the trial, the Free plan no longer accepts a new sales device beyond the first one. Devices already paired keep
working for 15 days; choose the one that stays active (Manage your devices).

pages.title: My trial is over

sections.heading: My trial is over
sections.text:
Your trial has ended and you have not chosen a paid plan yet: you keep going for free. Your business moves to the
Free plan, with no time limit. There is **no read-only period and no
suspension**: your registers keep taking payments and the back office can still be edited.

sections.heading: What does not change
What changes
sections.text:
Before (trial) · Now (Free)
All the features of the plan you tried · Paid modules are hidden (Included in Commerce screen); their data reappears when you subscribe
Several sales devices · 1 sales device: 15 days to choose the one that stays active
1 kiosk (Restaurant trial) · No kiosk: the kiosk counts as an extra device; it takes orders for 15 more days, then shows Kiosk temporarily unavailable
Unlimited products and users · 300 products and 3 users: what exists stays, only creating more is refused
Receipt with no extra line · Powered by Vendora line at the bottom of the receipt

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Read the end-of-trial message
You receive an email “Your trial is over: you carry on for free” (only once, in your store's language). For 30 days,
the back-office banner reminds you: Your trial is over: you keep going for free.
On Settings › Subscription, the Plan card has the Free badge and the Free trial card says: “Nothing is
deleted: paid modules are hidden and reappear, with their data, as soon as you subscribe.”
Choose the register that stays active (if you have several)
Did you have more than one sales device? They all keep selling for 15 days. The banner **You have N days left to
choose your register or subscribe. appears in the back office and on the registers; the Free trial** card offers
the Choose my register button.
Choose the register to keep in Settings › Devices: see
Choose the register that stays active. Without a choice, after 15 days
Vendora keeps the most recently used device. The others become read-only: they finish the current cart, close
their session and print their Z report, but no longer open a new sale
(The register on the Free plan).
Get everything back: subscribe
To get the modules and devices back, contact the Vendora team from Settings › Subscription. As soon as the plan is
recorded, hidden pages reappear exactly as they were, the limits are lifted and read-only registers are
reactivated at their next sync.
Did you have a kiosk during a Restaurant trial? The Restaurant plan includes no kiosk: also ask for the Kiosk
option (Subscription options). The kiosk then resumes at its next sync.
You have … days left to choose your register or subscribe.
You have more sales devices than the Free plan keeps. Choose your register before the deadline (**Choose my
register** link) or subscribe.
Kiosk temporarily unavailable
(On the kiosk.) Your Restaurant trial kiosk has gone past the 15-day grace period of the Free plan, which includes no
kiosk. Nothing is deleted: subscribe to a plan with the Kiosk option to bring it back into service.
A page I used during the trial has disappeared
It belongs to a paid module (stock counts, batches, full reports, accounting export, loyalty…). The data is kept and
comes back when you subscribe. See The Free plan.
My account was read-only or suspended at the end of an earlier trial
Accounts whose trial ended before the Free plan existed move to Free automatically: the read-only period and the
suspension are lifted, with nothing lost.

pages.title: The Free plan

sections.heading: The Free plan
sections.text:
The Free plan lets you run a small business without paying, with no time limit and no credit card: you take
payments, print your Z report and follow today's sales. It is never billed. You get there in two ways: by choosing
Start for free at sign-up, or automatically at the end of a trial without a subscription
(My trial is over).

sections.heading: What is included
sections.text:
Free plan
Stores · 1
Sales devices · 1 (register, floor phone or kitchen display), plus the back office on a computer; a paid extra device is possible (€7 or 10 DT per month)
Active products · 300 (archived products do not count)
Users · 3, owner included (active or invited)
Selling · Checkout, returns, printed receipt, receipt by email or QR code, full offline mode
Register · Register sessions, X and Z reports, tax archive
Catalog · Products, categories, barcodes, sale by weight, CSV import and export
Basic stock · Stock quantities, stock log, low-stock alerts
Customers · Customer record and history
Basic customer credit · Credit sales within a limit, payment at the register, balance visible on the customer record
Reports · Today's sales (dashboard) and Z reports
Appearance · Logo, colors, French / English / Arabic
API · 1,000 calls per month, then stopped until the next month (API quota)

sections.heading: What requires the Commerce plan
sections.text:
These features stay visible in the menu on the Free plan, with a Commerce badge (or Restaurant, Sur mesure: the plan that includes them). If you open their page, the Included in Commerce screen appears
instead: “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you
subscribe.”
- Advanced stock: stock counts, batches and expiry dates,
stock value, margins;
- Full reports: sales reports, stock reports,
customer reports, daily summary email,
store comparison, report settings;
- Accounting export: FEC and journals;
- Advanced customer credit: the Customer tabs page (open tabs, reminders);
- Loyalty, Suppliers and purchasing, Anti-fraud: visible in the menu with the Plan badge.
The floor plan, kitchen display, floor phones and tips require the Restaurant plan; several stores and white label,
the Custom plan. The AI assistant, kiosks and the other options require a paid plan: on the Free plan, only
the Extra device option is offered (Add an option).
The tax archive is always available
Whatever your plan, your closures and tax archives are generated and downloaded as usual
(Tax compliance).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
See your plan and your limits
Open Settings › Subscription. The Plan card shows the Free badge, Free, with no time limit and “No
invoice: the Free plan is never billed.” The Usage card shows where you stand: Sales devices, Stores,
Active products and Users (active or invited).
When a limit is reached
Nothing is cut off: your existing products, users and devices keep working. Only creating more is refused:
- 301st product: “300 products in the Gratuit plan — Commerce makes them unlimited. Archive a product or change
plan.” Archiving a product frees a place;
- 4th user: “3 users in the Gratuit plan — Commerce makes them unlimited. Deactivate a member or change plan.”
Deactivating a member frees a place (Team);
- a CSV import that would go over 300 products: refused as a whole, nothing is imported
(Import your catalog);
- 2nd sales device: pairing is refused (Manage your devices), unless you add an
extra device in Settings › Subscription: you are then billed for that line only, from the day you add it. A
kiosk is not possible on the Free plan (it requires the Kiosk option): a Restaurant trial kiosk takes orders
for 15 more days, then shows Kiosk temporarily unavailable.
The “Powered by Vendora” line on the receipt
On the Free plan, every printed sales receipt ends with the line Powered by Vendora (in French on a
receipt printed in French), centered, after the legal notices and the tax area (never inside them). The online
receipt (QR code or email) has the same line in its footer.
It does not appear on the Z report, kitchen tickets or training-mode receipts. It disappears as soon as you move to a
paid plan, from the next receipt (an offline register removes it as soon as it receives the new plan).
Move to a paid plan
To lift the limits, contact the Vendora team from Settings › Subscription (the View subscription link in the
banners and on the Included in Commerce screens). The change is immediate, with no interruption:
- the product, user and device limits are lifted;
- pages marked with a badge open with their data (batches, loyalty records, earlier stock counts);
- a read-only register is reactivated as soon as it syncs;
- the line on the receipt disappears.
300 products in the Gratuit plan — Commerce makes them unlimited. Archive a product or change plan.
You already have 300 active products. Archive the products you no longer sell
(Search, filter, activate / deactivate products) or move to Commerce.
3 users in the Gratuit plan — Commerce makes them unlimited. Deactivate a member or change plan.
The owner and pending invitations count. Deactivate a member or cancel an unneeded invitation.
A page has disappeared from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
The page depends on a paid module. Your data is not deleted: it reappears when you subscribe. A manager sees “Ask the
business owner to choose a plan that includes it.”

pages.title: View the audit log

sections.heading: View the audit log
sections.text:
The audit log keeps a record of every change in your business, made in the back office or on the
registers (after sync): who, when, what, with the value before and after. It is never erased.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Control › Audit log and filter
The most recent entries are at the top. Filter with:
1. Type: what was changed (Product, Category, VAT rate, User, Device, Store theme, Floor
plan, Fraud alert, API keys…);
2. Action: Creation, Edit, Publication, Price change…;
3. Author: a team member (registers appear as Register (sync), automatic
processes as System);
4. From / to: the period;
5. Item: the identifier of a specific item.
The store chosen at the top of the screen also filters the log. Clear filters shows everything again.
Read an entry in detail
Each row shows the Date, the Author, the Item (type and identifier), the Action and a summary of the
Changes (“Name: … → …”). Click Details (2): the Before and After blocks show the full
values. For a change that came from a register, the details also show “From synchronized event …”.
Click an item's identifier to see the full history of that item; for a product, Open takes you
to its product page. Entries are loaded 100 at a time: Oldest shows the next ones.
Export
Export CSV downloads journal-audit.csv (separator ;, columns Date, Auteur, Type, Élément, Action, Détails),
readable in Excel or LibreOffice. The export contains the rows loaded on screen: filter first, and click
Oldest as many times as needed to go back in time.
No entries for these filters.
The filters are too restrictive (or the store chosen at the top of the screen is not the right one). Click
Clear filters or choose All stores.
A change made on a register does not appear
It appears once the register syncs. If the register is offline, the change comes through when it reconnects.
A type or action is displayed in an unusual form (“Some new action”)
All known items and actions have a proper label (for example “API key”, “Revocation”, “Vendora
delegated access”). A brand-new item, added by a Vendora update, may be displayed for a few days in a
temporary raw form that is still readable: this is not an error.
Unable to load the log: check your connection, then reload the page.
The server did not respond. Reload the page. If you are not a manager of the store, access to the log is denied
(“Manager role required”).

pages.title: Manage your stores (create, edit, archive)

sections.heading: Manage your stores (create, edit, archive)
sections.text:
A store is a point of sale: it has its own devices, registers, stock and reports. The catalog,
customers and team, on the other hand, are shared by all the stores in the business. Your first store was created when you
signed up; this page lets you add more, correct them and archive those that close.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Settings › Stores
In the left menu, open Settings then Stores (1). The table (2) lists your stores with their
Profile, Currency, Time zone and State (Active or Archived). Below it, the
New store card (3) lets you create one.
The Devices link on a row opens that store's devices directly.
Edit a store
Click Edit: the row becomes editable (1). Change the name, profile, currency or time zone, then
click Save (2) — or Cancel.
- The profile (Restaurant, Grocery, Clothing, Services, Generic) adapts the screens offered: floor plan and
kitchen for a restaurant, sale by weight for a grocery store…
- Modules — product fields: the Variants, Sold by weight and scale and Expiry (lots, use-by dates)
checkboxes set which fields are shown on the product page. By default, they follow the profile (Clothing: variants;
Grocery: weight and expiry; others: none). As the catalog is shared, a field is shown as soon as one active store uses
it, and a product that already uses it always keeps it. Changing the profile adds its fields without removing yours.
- Modules — dining room: the Tables (floor plan) checkbox gives the store's registers the **Tables | Direct
sale** switch (if the floor plan has at least one table). Ticked by default for a restaurant; tick it for a grocery
store with a terrace, untick it for a restaurant without table service. Registers apply it at their next sync; a table
bill that is still open remains reachable until it is paid.
- The currency can no longer change after the store's first sale: choose it carefully from the start.
- The time zone sets the time on receipts, closures and reports.
Check the lists before saving
When editing, check that Profile, Currency and Time zone show the store's current values
before clicking Save; correct them if needed.
Expected result: the green banner “Store “…” saved.”.
Create a new store
In New store, fill in the Name (1), the Profile (2), the Currency (3) and the Time zone (4),
then click Create store (5).
Expected result: “Store “…” created. You can pair its devices.” The store appears in the
table and in the store selector at the top of the screen. It shares the catalog and the team; then add
its devices (Add a device) and, if needed, give your
employees access to this store (Team).
The number of stores depends on your plan. If the limit is reached, a red banner says so and nothing is created:
Archive a closed store (or return it to service)
When you have at least two active stores, an Archive button appears on each row. The browser
asks for confirmation: “Archive “…”? Its data stays viewable; no device can be paired with it any more.”
Before archiving: revoke the store's devices (Manage your devices) and
finish its ongoing stock transfers. An archived store remains visible (sales, Z, reports); the
Return to service button reactivates it.
Restaurant plan limit reached: 1 store(s). Contact Vendora to add more.
Your plan does not allow another store (the plan name and the number vary). See
Settings › Subscription and contact the Vendora team to move to a
multi-store plan. The same message appears when you return an archived store to service.
Currency can no longer change after the store's first sale
A sale has already been completed in this currency: it is locked to keep receipts, Z reports and accounting
consistent. If the currency really is wrong, create a new store with the right currency and archive the old one.
The last active store cannot be archived
A business always has at least one active store. First create the new store, then archive the old one.
First revoke this store's active devices: …
Registers or other devices (named in
the message) are still active. Revoke them in Settings › Devices, then archive.
First finish this store's ongoing transfers: …
Stock transfers (numbers listed)
leave from or arrive at this store. Receive or cancel them in Stock and purchasing › Transfers.
Store name required
The name is empty. The same applies to “Store name: 80 characters maximum”: shorten it.
Owner and administrators only
Managers see the stores but cannot create or edit them. Ask the owner.
Unable to create.
The server did not respond (connection lost, session expired). Reload the page and try again. Do the same for
“Unable to save.”, “Unable to archive.” and “Unable to restore.”.

pages.title: Add an option to your subscription

sections.heading: Add an option to your subscription
sections.text:
An option is added to your plan without changing it: one more device, a kiosk, the AI assistant… Each option has
its monthly price, in your country's currency, and its own line on the invoice. Everything happens in
Settings › Subscription, Subscription options card.

sections.heading: The options and their price
sections.text:
Option · France · Tunisia · Who adds it?
Extra device (one more register, floor phone or kitchen display) · €7 excl. VAT / month · 10 DT / month · You, from the Subscription page (also on the Free plan)
AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT connected to your business) · €7 excl. VAT / month · 15 DT / month · You; 3 months free the first time
Kiosk (per ordering kiosk) · €19 excl. VAT / month · 29 DT / month · The Vendora team
E-reporting (transmission through the approved platform, Commerce plan) · €5 excl. VAT / month · — · The Vendora team (France only)
Priority support (evenings and weekends) · €9 excl. VAT / month · 20 DT / month · The Vendora team
An option with no price in your country is not offered to you: e-reporting does not appear for a business in Tunisia.
It is included in the Restaurant plan and in Custom (France); the AI assistant is included in Custom. In those
cases, the page shows Included in your plan instead of the button.
Email address to confirm
Adding a paid option requires the owner's email address to be confirmed: see Confirm your email address.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open the Subscription options card
Open Settings › Subscription. The Subscription options card has two parts:
- the Active options table: Option, Quantity, Price per month, Added on, and the Remove button
(options you manage yourself) or the mention with the Vendora team; below, “Options total: … excl. tax /
month”;
- the Add an option list: each option with its price excl. tax / month and, depending on the case, the
Add button, the mention On request: contact the Vendora team., the Included in your plan badge, or the
reason why it is not available.
The Priority support badge appears at the top of the card when this option is active.
Add an extra device or the AI assistant
1. For a device, choose the quantity in the field next to the button (several at once if needed).
2. Click Add. The Add …? window recalls the price, for example: “1 × Extra device at €7.00 per month, i.e.
€7.00 excl. tax / month more. The device limit goes up immediately; the proration for the rest of the period
appears on your next invoice.”
3. Click Add to my subscription. A confirmation message appears.
The effect is immediate: the device limit in the Usage card goes up, and your registers receive the new right
at their next sync. For the AI assistant, the window says “Free for 3 months, then … / month excl. tax.”: see
Connect your AI assistant.
Ask for a kiosk, e-reporting or priority support
These options are added with the Vendora team: contact it from the help center. It turns them on from its
console; they immediately appear in Active options, with the mention with the Vendora team. Removal also goes
through the team.
Kiosks have their own limit, separate from sales devices: the Free, Commerce and Restaurant plans include **no
kiosk, each kiosk needs a Kiosk option (Custom: no limit). An extra device therefore does not** let you pair a
kiosk, and a kiosk does not take a register's place. Kiosks paired before this change keep working.
The only exception: the Restaurant trial includes 1 kiosk. When you subscribe to the Restaurant plan, that kiosk
stays in service but is no longer included: you need the Kiosk option. The 1st option covers the trial kiosk;
to pair another kiosk, ask for a 2nd option. Nothing is billed automatically: the Vendora team adds the option.
See Free trial.
Understand proration
An option added mid-month is billed to the day for the rest of the period: this proration is carried over to
your next invoice, one line per addition (for example “Prorata : Borne × 2 ajoutés le … (18 j sur 30)”). The
pending amount is shown under the list.
- On yearly billing, options follow the same rule as the plan: 10 months paid for 12.
- An option's price is frozen on the day it is added: a catalog change does not modify it.
- During the trial, an option is not billed; if the trial ends on the Free plan, it is removed.
Remove an option
Click Remove on the option's line, then Remove the option. A removal is never retroactive:
- Extra device: one device fewer, but nothing is unpaired. If all your devices are in use, Vendora refuses the
removal: revoke a device first in Settings › Devices, otherwise you would keep
it without paying for it.
- Kiosk (with the team): kiosks already paired stay active, but no new kiosk can be paired beyond the new limit.
- AI assistant, during the 3 free months: the assistant stays active until the end of the offer, free of
charge (“The assistant stays active until …, free of charge, then your "AI Assistant" keys will be suspended (nothing
is deleted). You can keep the option until then.”). The line then shows Active until … and a Keep the option
button that cancels the removal (“The removal is cancelled: free until …, then … / month excl. VAT.”); on that date,
your “AI Assistant” keys are suspended.
- AI assistant, after the offer: the removal is immediate; your “AI Assistant” keys are suspended and
connected assistants refused. Nothing is deleted, and adding the option again reactivates them immediately.
The confirmation window announces “a prorated credit appears on your next invoice” only if there is one: when an
invoice already covers the current month and included this option. On the Free plan without an invoice, during the
trial or during the AI assistant's 3 free months, there is nothing to refund, and the window does not say so.

sections.heading: On the Free plan
sections.text:
Only the extra device is offered: it lets you keep two sales devices without moving to Commerce. You are then
billed for that line only (€7 or 10 DT per month per device), from the day you add it. The other options show
“… is not available on the Free plan: upgrade to Commerce to add it”. See The Free plan.
… appareils de vente appairés pour une limite de … après ce retrait : révoquez d'abord un appareil (page Appareils)
(Message currently shown in French.) All your extra devices are in use. Revoke the device you no longer use
(Manage your devices), then remove the option.
“…” is not available on the Gratuit plan: upgrade to Commerce to add it
The option requires a paid plan (the option name varies). Only the extra device is offered on the Free plan.
1 kiosk in service / 0 included — add the Kiosk option with the Vendora team. Nothing is cut off, but no new kiosk can be paired.
On the Subscription page, under the Kiosks meter. Most often: you subscribed to the Restaurant plan after a trial,
and the trial kiosk stayed in service without being included. Nothing is cut off; ask the Vendora team for the
Kiosk option (one option per kiosk in service, one more to add another).
No kiosk is included in the Commerce plan: add the “Kiosk” option with the Vendora team (help center).
(When pairing a kiosk.) Your plan includes no kiosk. Ask the Vendora team for the Kiosk option. If you already
have kiosks: “Kiosk limit reached: … kiosk(s) (… plan and “Kiosk” options). Revoke a kiosk or add the “Kiosk” option
with the Vendora team.”
“E-reporting” is not offered in your country (France only)
E-reporting through the approved platform is a French obligation: the option only exists for a business in France.
Variant: “… comes with the Commerce plan (included in Restaurant and Custom)”.
“AI assistant” is already active
The option is already in Active options. For a device: “…: 100 at most (… already)”.

pages.title: Manager PIN and approvals (cash outs, drawer, discounts…)

sections.heading: Manager PIN and approvals (cash outs, drawer, discounts…)
sections.text:
Some register actions are sensitive: taking money out of the drawer, opening it without a sale, reprinting a Z,
comping a line, giving a discount above the threshold, a return… The cashier can only perform them with a **manager's
PIN, entered on the register. The PIN is checked on the spot, even without a network, then checked again by the server**:
each approval is recorded in the approvals log.

sections.heading: Actions that require a manager's PIN
sections.text:
Action · How it appears in the log
Cash out · Cash out
Opening the drawer without a sale · Drawer opening
Reprinting a Z report · Z report reprint
Voiding a line already sent to the kitchen · Void of a sent line
Canceling a bill · Bill cancellation
Comped line · Line comped
Discount above the threshold, return / refund, voiding a receipt, training mode, loss / breakage, sale beyond stock, tab above the limit, customer attached after the sale · under their technical code (DISCOUNT, SALE_REFUND, SALE_VOID, TRAINING_MODE, STOCK_LOSS, NEGATIVE_STOCK, CREDIT_OVER_LIMIT, SALE_CUSTOMER_ATTACH)
A manager, an administrator or the owner who is signed in on the register can perform these actions without entering an extra PIN.
These are the default settings. The owner can waive the PIN for small cash outs, small returns, **voiding a
sent line and loss / breakage** (see Set the manager PIN thresholds below): the action is then done without a
PIN, but is still recorded in the log, marked No PIN.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Control › PIN & approvals
The page has three parts: My PIN (1), your own register PIN; for the selected store, the number of approvals
and, if there are any, a red … anomaly(ies) badge (2), the Manager PIN thresholds (3) and, further down, the
approvals log.
Set or change your PIN
In My PIN, type the New PIN and the Confirmation (4 to 6 digits, identical), then Save.
The PIN must be different from your colleagues' PINs in the store; otherwise:
Choose another one. Expected result: “PIN saved — registers receive it at the next sync (≤ 30 s), then it
can be used offline.”
Never share your PIN: each approval is recorded in your name. If an employee forgot their PIN, see
Reset PIN.
Review the log and spot anomalies
Each row shows the Date, the Action, the Reason entered on the register, who it was Approved by, the Operator
(the signed-in cashier, or “— (register without user session)”) and the Server check (1).
An action done without a PIN because the store waives it shows No PIN under Approved by, with its amount and
the threshold (“€20.00 ≤ €50.00”), and Below threshold under Server check; the “… without PIN (under the
threshold)” counter adds them up.
OK: the server confirmed that the approver was indeed allowed to approve. An anomaly (2) flags a
questionable approval: nothing is erased or corrected; it is up to you to investigate (who knew this PIN? has the
person's role changed?). Anomalies also appear on the dashboard, in the Integrity alerts card.
Set the manager PIN thresholds
The Manager PIN thresholds card (owner only; a manager sees it read-only) sets, for the selected store, when a
manager's PIN is required:
- Cash out: PIN above (1) an amount — 0 = PIN for every withdrawal (default setting). With €50, a €20
withdrawal goes through without a PIN, a €200 one asks for it;
- Return / refund: PIN required checkbox and the amount above which the PIN is asked (2); unticked, no return
asks for it;
- Voiding a line sent to the kitchen and Loss / breakage: PIN required yes / no (3); without a PIN, the register
only asks for the reason.
Discounts and opening the drawer are recalled at the bottom, unchanged (4). Click Publish thresholds (5).
Expected result: “Thresholds published (version …) — registers apply them at the next sync, even offline
afterwards.”
Set the discount threshold
The threshold above which a discount requires a manager's PIN is set in Catalog › Discounts, in the
Thresholds and reasons card (owner only): Percentage threshold (1) and Amount threshold (2) — exceeding
either one is enough — and the list of reasons offered to the cashier. Click Publish thresholds.
Selling beyond available stock is set in Restaurant › Pay at the table (matching checkbox).
PIN already used in this store, choose another one
The PIN identifies the person on the register: it is unique per store. Choose another one.
PIN must be 4 to 6 digits
Digits only, from 4 to 6. The Save button stays grayed out as long as the two entries differ.
Approver with role Waiter (Manager or above required)
An action was approved with the PIN of someone who is not a manager (here a waiter) — often because their role
has changed since, or because an offline register had not yet received the change. Check with the team;
change the person's PIN if needed. Variants: “Approver has no role in this store”,
“Unreadable approver: …”.
On the register: “Invalid PIN” or “PIN locked, try again later”
The PIN entered does not belong to a manager of the store. After 5 errors, entry is blocked for one minute. Check that
your PIN shows Set ✓ in Settings › Team and that the register has synced since.
On the register: “No PIN set for this user”
The manager does not have a PIN yet: they set it here, in My PIN.
Read-only: only the store owner publishes the thresholds.
(Manager PIN thresholds card and Discounts page.) Thresholds are reserved for the store owner.
The thresholds were changed elsewhere: reloaded, make your change again.
Someone published the thresholds while you were editing them: the card now shows their version. Make your change
again, then Publish thresholds.
Unreadable amount: digits only, 0 or more.
Type a positive amount (“50” or “12.5”) or 0. Publish thresholds stays grayed out while an amount is unreadable.
Unable to load the approvals log.
The server did not respond, or you are not a manager of this store (“Manager role required”). Reload the page.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Build your team: roles, invitations, PIN
- Monitor anti-fraud
- View the audit log

pages.title: Approve the assistant's proposals

sections.heading: Approve the assistant's proposals
sections.text:
Your AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT…) reads your figures and can also propose actions: “prepare my order from Fresh
Market”, “align this price”. It changes nothing itself: it files a proposal that you read, then approve or
decline. Nothing is applied without a manager's approval.
Today the assistant can propose several things: a draft purchase order, a price change, the **handling of an
anti-fraud alert (acknowledging or dismissing it) and a product's availability** (making it unavailable or putting it
back on sale), correcting a product's record and withdrawing a product from sale or putting it back (actions subject to activation, see below), creating a product (action subject to activation, see below), extending a product to all stores (action subject to activation, see below) changing the price of several products at once (action subject to activation, see below) creating or editing a category (actions subject to activation, see below) and creating or editing a modifier group (actions subject to activation, see below) attaching or detaching a modifier group (action subject to activation, see below) editing the sales screen (action subject to activation, see below), correcting stock after a count and recording a stock loss (actions subject to activation, see below) and receiving a sent purchase order (action subject to activation, see below). They all appear on the same screen, in the same order. An
approved purchase order stays a draft: it is never sent to the supplier, you send it yourself from **Purchase
orders**.

sections.heading: Where to see the proposals
sections.text:
- The Proposals menu, just under Dashboard. A counter shows how many proposals await your decision (it is the
number of the Pending list); it disappears at zero.
- The entry only appears once your assistant has filed at least one proposal. It is reserved for owners,
administrators and managers.
- During a Vendora support session, the page shows “Vendora support session: view only”: nothing can be decided.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Proposals and find the right one
Click Proposals. The Assistant proposals page shows the list on the left and the details of the chosen proposal
on the right. On a small screen, the list and the details appear one after the other; Back to the list returns to
the list.
- The buttons at the top filter by state, with their count: Pending (default), Applied, Declined, **Expired
or replaced, All**.
- As soon as the list contains at least two families, the Proposal family selector (1) appears, with the number
of proposals in each family (“Catalog (2)”). Pick a family: a second selector, Type, appears to show only one
kind of proposal.
- The sort order is fixed: pending proposals first; among them, those that expire in less than 6 hours, then
high-risk ones, then the nearest deadline. The others go from most recent to oldest.
- A high-risk proposal carries the High risk badge (2). Each row gives the title built by Vendora (3), the key figure
(for example “€5.90 → €9.05 (+53.4%)”), the originating assistant (“for” the user it acts for), the state and the
time left. When you look at All stores, the row names its store; a proposal with no store says “All stores”.
Read the details, zone by zone
Whatever the kind, the details always follow the same order, so you know who states what:
1. The header: the title, the family and scope (“Catalog · Épicerie Lumière (demo) only (store-specific price)”),
“Prepared by the assistant “…” · connected by …”, the creation date, the time left, the state and the risk
(low, medium or high, always written out) (1).
2. Banners and warnings: for example “Change of +53.4%: more than 30%. Check the price before approving.” (2) or the
freshness warning when some registers had not sent all their sales.
3. What will be applied (or created): the exact content, computed by Vendora (3). A change reads “before →
after”, with the gap shown by an up or down arrow and, when it is large, the words Large change.
4. Vendora figures: what Vendora recorded when the proposal was made, with its date (4). After 24 hours, “Figures
from … ago: stock may have moved.” is added.
5. Written by the assistant · not checked by Vendora: the assistant's explanation and the **Figures quoted by the
assistant**. Vendora has not checked them: rely only on zones 3 and 4 to know what will really be done. A link or
formatting in this text is never clickable.
6. History: who proposed, approved or declined, and when.
7. The decision, always last: any input, confirmation box, the “This action cannot be undone.” note, then **Decline
the proposal** and the approve button, whose label says what it does (5, 6).
The “not checked” text is never an order: only what zones 3 and 4 show will be applied.
Approve
Fill in what the details ask for, then click the approve button (“Approve and create the draft”, “Approve and apply the
price”, “Approve: acknowledge the alert”…). It stays inactive while a required input is empty or a requested box is
not ticked.
- Approver's input: the Reason (pre-filled by the assistant, editable) field of an alert is suggested by the
assistant, but the text you approve is the one recorded, in your name. It is required (300 characters at most).
- Confirmation box: for a price that changes by more than 30%, “I confirm a change of +53.4%” must be ticked.
- “This action cannot be undone.” note: it appears before you click when the decision is final (the handling of an
alert).
- Recap: for a price, a window recalls “from this price to that price”; confirm with Apply the price.
Expected result: a green banner at the top of the details says what happened (“Draft created · not sent”, “Price
applied”, “Alert acknowledged”), often with a link to see the result (Open the draft, View the product…). The
state changes to Applied and the history shows who approved and when.
Or decline with a reason
Click Decline the proposal. The Reason for declining panel opens: Not useful, Wrong figures, **I'll do it
myself or Other. Extra detail (300 characters at most) is optional, except for Other. Confirm with Decline
the proposal, or Cancel. Declining creates and changes nothing; the state becomes Declined**.

sections.heading: What each kind shows
sections.text: The four kinds use the same zones; only the content of zone 3 changes.

sections.heading: Purchase order
sections.text:
Zone 3 is a table (Product, Unit cost excl. tax, Quantity, Total excl. tax); if a cost is unknown, the
total is called partial. Zone 4 gives, for each product, the Stock, the Threshold, Sold in 30 days and
Already ordered. “Draft not sent: you will send it yourself, from the back office.” It is approved by the store's
manager.

sections.heading: Price change
sections.text:
Zone 3 shows “Selling price incl. tax: before → after” in large type, the gap, “VAT unchanged (5.5%)” and “Sales already
made keep their price.” Only the price changes: never the VAT, never the product's availability; the store's own
settings are kept. Registers receive the new price at their next sync.
The scope is written in the header: a single store (approved by that store's manager) or **All stores (company
price), in bold, approved by a manager (Manager, owner or administrator). The company price is decided in the back
office**: registers show it read-only, with the “Back office” badge and the “Decided in the back office” card.

sections.heading: Handling an anti-fraud alert
sections.text:
The assistant can only propose handling an anti-fraud alert (Anti-fraud page), never
a fiscal integrity or stock alert. Zone 3 is called Alert to handle: rule, summary, person concerned, date,
Proposed decision and the View the alert link. See the inputs above: the reason you approve is the one recorded.

sections.heading: Product availability
sections.text:
You tell your assistant “no more apple tart tonight” (or “no more tart or chocolate fondant”): it files a proposal to
make those products unavailable in the store. “Put the tart back” puts it back on sale the same way. **Nothing is
removed from sale before a manager approves. A proposal covers at most 20 products**, all in the same direction (all
removed, or all put back on sale).
Zone 3 shows “Sale in this store: On sale → Unavailable” in large type (1), then “This store's price and VAT are
unchanged.”, “Orders already taken are not changed.” and “Stays unavailable until a manager puts it back on sale.” (2).
Zone 4 recalls the availability recorded by Vendora (3). For several products, zone 3 is a Product / Today / After
table and the button reads “Make 3 products unavailable”.
Approve. Click Make unavailable (or Put back on sale for a return to sale; for several, “Make 3 products
unavailable”). A window recalls what will happen: “« Tarte Tatin » will no longer be offered at Le Petit Bistrot (demo):
registers, waiter phones and kiosks at their next sync, online menu right away.” No input or box is required; confirm with
Unavailable (or On sale).
Expected result: the state becomes Applied and a green banner announces “Product made unavailable · View the
product” (or “Product put back on sale”), above the What was applied block. **This banner only appears right after
your approval**: if you reopen the proposal later, it is replaced by “Approved by … · View the product” and the history
keeps who approved and when.
What this changes, and what it does not:
- Price and VAT do not change. A store's own price or own VAT is kept as is; only availability moves. In the product
record, Prices by store block, the store's line shows “not sold” and the Available box is unticked.
- The product stays unavailable until it is put back on sale, which you ask for the same way: nothing puts it back on
sale by itself.
- The online menu follows right away. Registers, floor phones and kiosks receive it at their next sync.
- A sale in progress is not changed. A line already in the register's cart stays sellable until the app is
restarted; on restart it is removed with the message “Session restored after restart · 1 item removed from the catalog”.
Orders already taken are not changed.
What the assistant declines, explaining why (no proposal is then filed):
- a product already in the requested state (“is already unavailable in this store” or “is already on sale”);
- the opposite request of a proposal already waiting for a manager: the pending proposal is not replaced; a manager
can decline it, then the assistant files another;
- a product with variants, or a variant: its availability is set in the back office, not by the assistant;
- an archived product (it is no longer sold);
- any price or VAT request through this action: it only touches availability. A price is requested with the “Change a
selling price” action;
- several products with the same name (it asks you to be more specific), or more than 20 products at once.
A group is all or nothing. If a single product of the request is refused (for example “Mousse au chocolat” already
unavailable), the whole request is refused and no product is sent: the assistant says which one to remove, then asks
again with the others. At approval it is the same: if one product of the group changed since the proposal, the whole
proposal is out of date and nothing is applied.
Out of date. The proposal says what changed, in a single box, with the conclusion “Nothing was applied. Ask your
assistant for a new proposal.” Examples: “« Fondant au chocolat » has been unavailable in this store since the
proposal.”, “« Île flottante » has been archived since the proposal, and 1 other.”, “The record of « Café gourmand » in
this store was modified since the proposal, and 1 other.” (a price, VAT or availability changed by hand since). The block
is then titled What was proposed.

sections.heading: Correcting a record, withdrawing a product from sale
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
This box applies to both actions of this section: “Edit a product” and “Withdraw or restore a product”. They are
authorized separately in Settings › AI assistant (Catalog family), once they are open for your account.
Correcting a record. You say “rename the almond croissant” or “put it in Viennoiseries, purchase cost €0.62”: the
assistant files a “before → after” proposal. The assistant can propose:
- the name (120 characters at most);
- the category (or No category to remove it);
- the barcode;
- the purchase cost (in a single currency: if your stores do not share just one, the assistant explains and proposes
nothing);
- stock tracking;
- meal voucher eligibility.
All the changes to one product fit in a single proposal: a new request on the same product replaces the one
that is waiting. Each changed field is a “before → after” line in zone 3, followed by notes (“Sale price and VAT
unchanged.”, “Receipts and sales already recorded keep the old name.”, “The margins and stock value shown will use this
cost from now on.”, “This product's stock will no longer be tracked: alerts and restocking will not see it.”).
What the assistant can never propose with this tool: the sale price (ask for it with “Change a sale price”),
the VAT (never, here or anywhere else), variants: a product with variants, or a variant, is edited in the back
office. It does not touch the reference, scale code, weight, expiry, online menu or allergens either.
A barcode cannot be removed: the assistant can propose another one, not erase it. It also refuses:
- a barcode already used by another product;
- a code starting with 20 to 29: those prefixes are used for scale labels and the store's internal codes; such a code
could make an already printed label sell under the wrong product;
- a product withdrawn from sale (put it back on sale first);
- a category or product that is not found or ambiguous (the assistant asks you to be more specific).
Withdrawing a product from sale, or putting it back. “We no longer sell the tuna sandwich” gives a **Withdrawal from
sale proposal; “put it back in the catalog” gives Back on sale. The product disappears (or comes back) in all
stores: registers, kiosks and online menu. The detail shows “On sale → Withdrawn from sale”, the remaining stock** if
any (it no longer counts in the stock value), and states that sales in progress that contain the product are paid as
usual. Putting a product back on sale counts again toward your plan's product limit: if it is reached, approval
is refused and the proposal stays pending. It is reversible: withdraw, then restore.
Do not confuse it with today's out-of-stock.
Product availability · Withdrawal from sale
When · A dish is missing tonight, in one store · The product is no longer sold
Scope · One store · All stores
Effect · It leaves the sales list until it is put back on sale · It disappears from the sales catalog
Tool · “Make a product available or unavailable” · “Withdraw or restore a product”
Decided in the back office. These proposals are decided here only. On the register and the waiter phone they are
listed and readable in full with the Back office badge, with no button (see
Approve a proposal on the register).
Meal vouchers. If the change touches eligibility, the proposal adds a note: “From approval, this product can (or can
no longer) be paid with meal vouchers, under the conditions of the French Labour Code (art. R3262-4). Sales already made
do not change.” Eligibility is your responsibility: only certain food products qualify. Vendora does not check
compliance.
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is applied, if the record changed in the meantime.
A single box says so, for example “The record of “Almond croissant” was modified since the proposal.”, ““Tuna sandwich”
was withdrawn from sale since the proposal.”, “The category “Viennoiseries” no longer exists.”, “Barcode … now belongs to
another product.” or ““Tuna sandwich” now has variants: its record is edited in the back office.”. Then ask your
assistant for a new proposal.

sections.heading: Creating a product
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “add the almond croissant at €1.80 in Viennoiseries”: the assistant files a New product proposal, at **high
risk**. The product does not exist until a manager approves. The assistant can propose:
- the name (1 to 120 characters);
- the category (optional);
- the selling price incl. VAT;
- the barcode (optional);
- the purchase cost (optional);
- stock tracking (on if the assistant does not mention it);
- the VAT rate (optional, see below).
Company product or store product. With no store named, the product belongs to the company: “All stores”. If you
name a store, it is specific to that store, and only a manager of that store can approve it. The scope and currency
are written under the title (“All stores · EUR”). The assistant is never asked for the currency: it is the store's; for a
company product, it is the single currency of your stores, and if you have several the assistant explains it and proposes
nothing. An assistant whose access is limited to some stores must always name the store.
The VAT rate, decided by you. The rate applies to every sale of the product: the proposal highlights it.
- The assistant names a rate. It must exist and be active in your business. The VAT line shows it as “name —
percentage” (“TVA réduite 5,5 % — 5.5%”). The percentage is always calculated by Vendora from the rate's value,
never read from its name. It is shown that way even when the name already contains the percentage (“TVA réduite 5,5 % — 5.5%”): this is intended, the percentage after the dash is always the one actually applied. The confirmation box quotes it: “I confirm the creation of “Jus d'orange pressé” at 3,50 €
incl. VAT, at the rate “TVA réduite 5,5 % — 5.5%”.” If that rate differs from the one most active products in the
category use, a warning says so: “Most other products in “Viennoiseries” are at … Check that the named rate suits
this product.”
- The assistant names no rate (the most frequent case). The VAT line says “To be chosen by the manager in the back
office” and a VAT rate field (“Choose the rate”) lists the active rates of your business, from the highest
percentage to the lowest, 0% last. None is preselected and none is given as “default”: the choice is yours. The **Create the
product button stays inactive until the rate is chosen and the box is ticked**. The box text does not repeat the
chosen rate (“… with the VAT rate I chose above.”): re-read the list before ticking.
- Never 0% from the assistant. If it names 0%, the request is refused (“The assistant cannot propose a 0% rate.
Propose the product without a rate: the manager will choose it at approval.”). You can choose “Exonéré 0 % — 0%” from
the list yourself; the detail then reminds you “The 0% rate only suits products exempted by law.” (for a Tunisian store
it adds “A sale under tax suspension is declared on the sale, not on the product.”).
- No rate in your business. The assistant proposes nothing and tells you to open Catalog › VAT rates: the rates
are created the first time it is opened (see VAT rates). Do it once.
The assistant will not be able to change the rate of a product afterwards: that is done by hand on the record.
What the assistant declines, explaining why (no proposal is then filed):
- a name already taken by a product on sale (it suggests editing the record or the price instead) or by a product
withdrawn from sale (it suggests putting it back on sale);
- a price of 0 or too high; an empty name, one over 120 characters, or one containing quotation marks or an
invisible character;
- a barcode already used by a product, or one that starts with 20 to 29 (reserved for scale labels and internal
codes);
- a category that is not found or ambiguous (it asks you to be more specific);
- variants: a product with variants is created in the back office. Sale by weight, meal vouchers, expiry,
the online menu, allergens and other settings are not proposed: once the product exists, set them on its record.
Decided in the back office. Like a record correction, this proposal is decided here only. On the register and the
waiter phone it is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge, with no button (see
Approve a proposal on the register).
Approving. Choose the rate if asked, tick the box, click Create the product. The product is created as if you had
entered it by hand; it counts toward your plan's product limit (if it is reached, approval is refused and the proposal
stays pending).
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, a “Product created” banner appears with the View the product
link, and the VAT line states where the rate came from: “… · Rate chosen by the manager” or “… · Rate named by the
assistant, confirmed by the manager”. The product reaches registers, waiter phones and kiosks **at their next
synchronization. It is reversible**: withdraw it from sale (through the assistant or by hand).
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is created, if in the meantime a product with the same
name was created (“A product “Tarte au citron” now exists.”), if the rate was deactivated (“The rate “TVA réduite 7 % —
7%” is no longer active.”), if the category no longer exists, if the store was archived or if the barcode now belongs to
another product. If a rate is deactivated while you are choosing, approval is refused and the proposal stays pending:
choose another rate. When it is out of date, ask your assistant for a new proposal.

sections.heading: Extending a product to all stores
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “put the house cookie from the station store in all stores”: the assistant files an Extend to all stores
proposal, at medium risk. It concerns a product that is specific to one store (it exists only in that store, see
Prices and availability per store): once the proposal is approved, it becomes a
product of the business, sold in all stores. The assistant only proposes the product (name, barcode or
reference): it cannot change its price, its VAT rate or its name.
Who approves. Only the owner or an administrator can approve this proposal, like the **Make available in all
stores button on the product record. The manager of the original store sees** it in the list, but if they click the
button they get “You do not have the role to approve this proposal.”: nothing is changed and the proposal **stays
pending** for an owner or an administrator.
Approving. Read the detail, tick the confirmation box (“I confirm extending “Cookie maison” to all stores; this
choice is final.”), then click Extend to all stores. This choice is final: a product extended to the business never
becomes specific to a store again.
What changes.
- The product appears on the registers, waiter phones and kiosks of all stores, at their next synchronization, **at the
selling price and VAT rate of its record**: the detail quotes them (“Current selling price”, “VAT rate of the
record”). The prices and rates specific to the original store stay specific to that store; if the original store has
any, a note says so. Each store can then change its price or make it unavailable.
- The stock stays that of the original store: the other stores start from zero.
- If stores have an online menu, the product will be offered there too.
- Sales already recorded do not change.
A product with the same name already exists in another store. This is not a refusal: a warning says so (“A
product with the same name is already specific to: “Centre”, “Port”. Both will appear in those stores.”). After the
extension, withdraw the old product from those stores if you no longer want it.
What the assistant refuses, explaining why (no proposal is filed then):
- a product that is already shared by all stores (“… is already available in all stores: there is nothing to
extend”);
- a product withdrawn from sale: put it back on sale first;
- a product with variants (or a variant): it cannot be extended, its variants would stay specific to the original store;
- a store with another currency or another tax country: the price and VAT rate of the record only hold for one
currency and one country. Archived stores do not count;
- a name already used by a business product (“A product “…” already exists for all stores: extending it would create a
duplicate visible everywhere. Rename one of the two in the back office, then propose again”);
- an assistant whose access is limited to some stores: only an all-stores access can propose extending a product,
since the effect reaches every store.
Decided in the back office. On the register and the floor phone, the proposal is listed and readable in full with
the Back office badge, with no button (see Approving a proposal on the register).
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, a “Product extended to all stores” banner appears with the **View the
product link. It is final**: unlike a withdrawal from sale, nothing can undo it.
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is extended, if in the meantime the product
disappeared, was extended by hand (“… is already available in all stores.”), was withdrawn from sale, received variants,
had its record modified (“The record of “…” was modified since the proposal.”), if a product with that name exists for
all stores, or if a store with another currency or tax country appeared (“The store “…” does not use this product's
currency (EUR).”). Once the product is extended, the other pending proposals on that same product (correction,
withdrawal, price) also become out of date: ask your assistant for them again.
Known limit. An archived store does not block the extension; if you later reopen a store with another currency, it
will still receive the product. Check your stores' currency before extending.

sections.heading: Changing several prices at once
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “raise all the coffees by €0.10 at the bistro” or “lower the pastries by 5% in all stores”: the assistant files one
Change a selling price proposal that lists 1 to 100 products, from one store or from the whole company. It has **three
ways to prepare it: a new price for each product; the same increase or decrease as an amount (“+ €0.10”); the same increase
or decrease as a percentage (“−5%”, from −90% to +100%). In the last two cases Vendora calculates** each new price from the
price currently in force for each product, to the nearest cent (millime for the dinar), with no commercial rounding: −5% on €2.10
gives €1.995, rounded to €2.00. The products are those on the assistant's list: it cannot target a category without naming the
products one by one, and you read the list.
What the screen shows. The title gives the number of products. A table gives, for each product, the price before and after, the
change as a percentage, the margin rate before and after (the rate is the price excluding tax minus the cost, divided by the
price excluding tax; “—” when the product has no purchase cost) and, where needed, a flag. Lines that deserve your attention are
flagged with a written reason: “Below cost” (the price excluding tax after is lower than the cost) first, then **“Large change
(+35.7%)”** (more than 30%). Warnings put numbers on it (“2 products change by more than 30%”, “1 product falls below its cost”), and
“Cumulative change in unit prices” gives the sum of the changes with its sign: “+€1.85” for an increase, “−€0.55” for a decrease. In the
back office, the Flagged lines tab shows what to watch first and the All lines tab shows them all (in alphabetical order, not
flagged first); a filter finds a product. On the register, a preview of five lines (flagged first) is followed by “See the N lines”.
Who approves, and where. A group for one store is decided in the back office or on that store's register and floor phone, **under
a manager PIN (see Approving a proposal on the register). A group for the whole
company (“All stores”) is decided in the back office only: registers show it read-only with the Back office** badge.
The confirmation box. From two products, approval requires ticking the box, for example “I confirm the new prices of 12 products
(cumulative change +€1.85), including 2 over 30% and 1 below cost.”: without it, the Apply the 12 prices button stays inactive and the
server refuses (“The confirmation box is missing: nothing was applied.”). For a single product no box is required (the screen shows one above
30%), as for a simple price change. On the register you tick the box, then enter the PIN.
Resale at a loss: flagged, never blocked. A price below cost is not refused: the line is flagged and a note reminds you that
selling a product resold as is below its purchase price may be prohibited (resale at a loss), with exceptions. The cost shown is
a Vendora estimate (the store's average cost, otherwise the purchase cost of the record): check it against your purchase invoice.
The decision, and the legal rule that applies to your business, remain yours.
What changes, and what does not. Only the selling price changes, in the stated scope (one store: its store price; the whole
company: the record's price); registers receive the new prices at their next sync. VAT does not change, sales already recorded keep their
price, and so do orders already entered (a basket put on hold takes the new price when recalled). **A price specific to a store stays
specific: in a company group, a note says so (“1 product has its own price in some stores: that price does not change.”). Think of the
shelf labels**: Vendora does not change them, and a note reminds you.
All or nothing. The prices change all together, or not at all: if a single product is a problem at approval time, nothing is applied.
The proposal becomes stale when, since it was filed, a product's price has changed (“The price of ‘Pommes Gala (kg)’ changed from €3.20 to
€3.30 since the proposal (and 1 other product). Nothing was applied.”), a product was withdrawn, a product gained variants, the **store was
archived, or a store with another currency appeared** (company group). Ask your assistant again.
What the assistant refuses, explaining why (no proposal is then filed):
- a product with variants, or a variant: the price is changed on each variant, not in a group;
- in a company group, a product specific to a single store; in a store group, a product specific to another store;
- products in different currencies, or a company group while a store uses another currency (one group per currency);
- more than 100 products, or the same product twice;
- an unchanged, zero or negative price, or one above the ceiling; a percentage outside −90% to +100%;
- an assistant whose access is limited to some stores when it targets the whole company.
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, with the “Prices applied” banner and the View the products link.

sections.heading: Creating or editing a category
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “create a category Desserts”, “rename Hot drinks to Coffees and teas”, “put the pastries in Bakery” or “put the
desserts first on the kiosk”: the assistant files a Create a category or Edit a category proposal. A proposal
concerns a single category. To edit it, the assistant can rename it, move it into another category or **to the
top level, and change its order: a number, or “first” / “last”** (Vendora then works out the number when you
approve). A category's colour and icon cannot be proposed: they are set in Catalogue › Categories.
What the screen shows. The title gives the action and the category (“Create a category · Ice creams”). The category is
named by its path, from the highest level to the lowest: “Menu › Desserts”, or “Top level” for a category with no
parent. The What will be created block (or What will be applied for an edit) lists the Name, Placed in and
Position lines: for an edit each line shows before → after, and the list summarises “3 changes” when there are
several. The position reads “1 of 5” (or “First · 1 of 5”): it is the category's rank among those at the same level.
The notes, each with an information icon, say what approving changes and does not change; Vendora's figures give the
number of products in the category, its subcategories and the categories at the same level.
Who approves, and where. A manager (Manager, owner or administrator) decides it in the back office only. On the
register and the waiter phone the proposal is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge, with no
button (see Approve a proposal on the register). **There is no
confirmation box**: the risk is low and everything can be undone (rename or move again; an empty category can be deleted
in Catalogue › Categories).
What changes, and what does not.
- The order applies to the kiosk, the online menu and the back office, not to the buttons on the register. The
register's sales screen puts each button at a fixed place in its grid: changing a category's order does not move them.
A note on the screen says so.
- Renaming also changes the name in the reports by category, including for past periods (reports read the current
name).
- Moving a category takes its products and its subcategories with it. The preparation stations and modifier groups
linked to the category stay the same.
- Sales already recorded do not change.
- A created category is empty: you put products in it from their product page. In the online menu it appears as soon
as a product is placed in it.
- The registers receive the change at their next sync.
One order rule, everywhere. Categories are sorted by the order you chose (the number in the Order column, smallest
first), then by name, ignoring capitals, accents and typographic punctuation: “Épices” sorts with the “E”s, and “L’apéro”
(typographic apostrophe) like “L'apéro”. It is the same rule in the back office, the online menu and the iOS and Android
kiosk, whether the category comes from a proposal or from your own entry.
What the assistant refuses, explaining why (no proposal is then filed):
- a name already taken by another category, wherever it is in the tree (the back office accepts duplicates, the
assistant does not: it finds categories by name); changing only the capitals of a category's name is accepted;
- more than three levels of categories, subcategories included;
- a category placed in its own branch (in one of its own subcategories);
- an empty name, one over 120 characters, with an invisible character or with quotation marks;
- a category that cannot be found, or is ambiguous (two categories with the same name: the assistant offers you the list);
- a request with no change (same name, parent and order);
- an assistant whose access is limited to some stores: a category applies to all stores.
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is applied, if since it was filed the category **was
deleted (“This category no longer exists.”), renamed, moved or reordered** (“The category “Fromages” was modified since
the proposal.”), if the parent category disappeared, if the move became impossible (three levels, or into its own branch),
or if the name is now taken (“A category “Glaces” now exists.”). Ask your assistant for it again.
Limits.
