- The position shown is the one at the time of the proposal: if other categories have moved since, it may have
changed. “First” and “Last” remain true at approval, because Vendora recalculates them then.
- The assistant does not delete categories: deletion is done in Catalogue › Categories.
- “Put this product in the Desserts category” is a proposal to edit the product (see “Correcting a record”), not the
category; for several products the assistant files one per product.
- No colour, no icon, no store: a category is the same for all stores.
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, with the “Category created” or “Category edited” banner and the **View the
categories** link.

sections.heading: Creating or editing a modifier group
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
A modifier group gathers a product's options (“Cooking”, “Sauces”, “Burger extras”…, see
Offering options). You say “create a Sauces group”, “make the bacon 1.50 €”, “add
Pepper sauce at 0.80 €” or “the cooking choice becomes mandatory”: the assistant files a Create a modifier group or **Edit
a modifier group proposal. A proposal touches a single group. To edit one, the assistant can change an option's extra
price, add, rename or remove options, change the number of choices** (minimum and maximum), rename the group,
and deactivate or reactivate it. It does not attach the group to products or categories: a group created this way is
not yet offered with any product, attach it in Catalog › Modifiers or ask the assistant to (see
Attaching or detaching a modifier group). It does not propose a VAT rate and deletes no
group (deletion does not exist: you deactivate it). A group applies to all stores.
What the screen shows.
- Creation: the What will be created block gives the Name and the Choice (“1 optional choice”, “Up to 2
choices”, “1 required choice”, “Between 1 and 2 choices”…); the The group after approval table lists each Option
with its Extra price (“Free” when there is none). The list summary reads, for example, “Up to 2 choices · all free” or
“Up to 3 choices · 2 paid”.
- Edit: the What changes block has one line per change, in order. An extra price shows before → after
(“Extra price · Bacon: 1,00 € → 1,50 €”, summary “Bacon: +50%”), an added option has no “before” value (“Option added:
Sauce poivre · 0,80 €”), a renamed option shows “Bacon → Bacon fumé”, a removed option (“Option removed”) is marked
Removed. When there are several changes, the waiting list counts them (“4 changes”) then details them (“2 price
changes, 1 addition, 1 removal”). The The group after approval table then shows the group as it will be, option by
option. A deactivation appears on the Status line (“Active → Deactivated”).
- The notes, each preceded by an information icon, say what approval changes and does not change. The **Vendora
figures give the number of Existing groups (creation), or the Attached products and the Options before /
after** (edit).
- A creation reminds you: “This group is not offered with any product yet: attach it in “Catalog › Modifiers”.”
The confirmation box, required for a large change. When the proposal changes an extra price significantly, the line is
highlighted, with its reason written out, and Vendora requires a box to be ticked before applying:
Reason shown · When
Large change (+50%) or Large change (−40%) · an extra price goes up or down by more than 30%
Becomes paid · a free option becomes paid
Becomes free · a paid option becomes free
Removed · an option is removed from the group
The box reads, for example, “I confirm the changes to “Burgers maison”: 1 large change (+50%), 1 option removed” (other
reasons: “1 option now paid”, “1 option now free”). The button is called Apply the change, or Apply the 4 changes.
With none of these reasons there is no box, and none for a creation either. If you approve without ticking a required
box, nothing is applied (“The confirmation box is missing: nothing was applied.”). A rise or a fall of 30% or less (+25%,
for instance) is applied without a box.
The “Alcoholic drink?” flag. An extra price is sold at the VAT rate of the product it is added to: a glass of wine
added to a dish would take the dish's rate. When an option's name contains an alcoholic-drink word (wine, beer, rum,
whisky, champagne, cider… ; vin, bière… ; نبيذ, بيرة…), the line carries the Alcoholic drink? flag. This is **neither a
refusal nor a box**: the proposal can still be applied, the decision is yours. Every group proposal carries the note: “An
extra price is sold at the VAT rate of the product it is added to. An alcoholic drink (glass of wine, shot…) is sold as a
separate product, at its own rate.” The word list is imperfect: it may wrongly flag a “wine sauce” and miss a brand or a
cocktail. See also An add-on follows the product's VAT rate; your accountant's opinion
prevails.
Several currencies, and different numbers of decimals. An extra price is counted in the minor units (cents,
millimes) of your stores' currency: 1.500 DT is 1,500 millimes; 1.50 € is 150 cents. If your stores use **several
currencies, the assistant refuses to propose** a non-zero extra price (it explains why: enter it in the back office); a
proposal without an amount (renaming, removing, changing the choices, switching an extra price to free) goes through. Two
cases:
- the currencies have a different number of decimals (euro with two, dinar with three): the proposal shows no amount
(the table only has the Option column) and a note, placed among the case's notes, reads: “This business uses
currencies with different decimals: extra prices are not shown here; check them in “Catalog › Modifiers”.”;
- the currencies have the same number of decimals: amounts are shown without a symbol, with the note “This business
uses several currencies: extra prices are shown without a currency.”.
With a single currency, amounts keep their symbol (“1,50 €”, “1,500 DT”).
Who approves, and where. A manager (Manager, owner or administrator) decides it in the back office only. On the
register and the floor phone, the proposal is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge and the
sentence “Open the back office to decide.”, with no button (see
Approving a proposal on the register). A cashier cannot decide it.
The registers, the kiosk and the online menu receive the group at their next sync.
What happens to sales and orders already entered. The proposal's note says so: “Sales already recorded and table orders
already entered keep the options and extra prices chosen. A basket put on hold on the register keeps its extra prices; its
products take the catalog price again when recalled. An online order sent after approval follows the new group.” In detail:
- Sales already recorded keep their options and extra prices, and their receipt does not change (duplicate
included); so do table orders already entered.
- A basket put on hold on the register keeps its extra prices; its products take the catalog price again when it is
recalled.
- Sales made after approval are calculated with the new extra price, at the product's VAT rate.
- A removed option is no longer offered, but stays on the sales and orders already recorded (note: “A removed option is
no longer offered; it stays on sales and orders already recorded.”).
- A choice that has become mandatory is asked for on the lines added afterwards, not on those already entered.
- A deactivated group is no longer offered for sale; it can be reactivated in the back office.
- An online order sent after approval follows the new group: with a removed option, it is refused.
What the assistant refuses, explaining why (no proposal is then filed): a name that is empty, too long, with an
invisible character or quotation marks, or already taken by another group; a group that is not found or
ambiguous (two groups with the same name: it offers you the list); an option not found; an option named twice in
the same request; a group rule not respected (at least one option and at most 30, option names that differ **even by one
space**, minimum lower than or equal to the maximum, maximum at least 1 and at most the number of options); an extra price
above the cap; a VAT, tax-family or attachment field; a request with no change; more than 30 changes at once; a
non-zero extra price with several currencies; an assistant whose access is limited to some stores (a group applies
to all).
Stale. The proposal becomes stale, and nothing is applied, if since it was filed the group was deleted or
modified (“The group “Pains” was modified since the proposal.”: even elsewhere, by another manager or another tab), if a
product or category it cites has disappeared, if the name is now taken, or if your stores now use several currencies
while the proposal sets an extra price. Ask your assistant again: a more recent proposal on the same group replaces the
previous one.
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, with the “Group created” or “Group updated” banner and the **Attach to
products link (creation) or View the modifiers** (edit). The group is then identical to the one you would have saved by
hand in Catalog › Modifiers; the group's history and the audit log keep the trace of the proposal.

sections.heading: Attaching or detaching a modifier group
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “offer the cooking choice with the rib steak and the tartare” or “remove the extras from the fries”: the assistant
files an Attach or detach a modifier group proposal. It targets a single group that already exists and lists the
products and categories to attach to it or remove from it, 50 targets at most (attachments and detachments
together). It changes nothing else: not the options, not the extra prices, not the name, not the number of choices, not the
group's activation (for that, see Creating or editing a modifier group).
The group applies to all stores. Attaching a group to a product means offering it with that product on lines added
afterwards, on the register, the kiosk, in the dining room and in the online menu.
What the screen shows.
- The title and the waiting list: “Attach or detach a modifier group · Cuisson du chef”. The summary says what changes:
“Offered with 1 more product”, “Offered with the category (2 products)”, “No longer offered with this product”, or, for
several targets, “4 changes” then “3 attached, 1 detached”.
- The “What changes” block: one line per target, attachments first, then detachments. The label says the action:
Product attached, Category attached, Product detached (or category detached).
- A product shows its name and its VAT rate: “Tartare · VAT Taux réduit — 10%”. If a store applies another rate to
that product, the store's rate follows in brackets: “Pavé du midi · VAT Taux réduit — 10% (Centre: 20%)”; beyond three
stores, “(Centre: 20%, Gare: 5%, Lac: 7%, +1)”. A product that belongs to a single store says so: “Plat de la gare · VAT
Taux réduit — 10% · only at Gare”.
- A category shows its full path (“Plats › Burgers”), the number of products placed directly inside it and their
rates: “Rôtisserie · 2 products directly inside · VAT 10%”; empty: “Desserts du jour · no products yet”.
- A line can carry a highlight: “Already offered via “Burgers du chef”” when the product already offered the group
through an attached category.
- The “The group after approval” table lists everything the group will be attached to, with the Name and the Type
(“Product” or “Category”). It shows 50 lines at most: beyond that, a note says so (“Only the first 50 of 55 lines are
shown; the full list is in “Catalog › Modifiers”.”).
- The notes say what approval changes and does not change: “Products placed later in “Rôtisserie” will also offer this
group.”, “A detached product or category no longer offers this group on lines added afterwards.”, “This group is deactivated:
it will only be offered once reactivated in the back office.” and, when a product is also a choice in a combo, “Burger de
formule is also a choice in 2 combos: the group will be offered there, at this product's rate.”. Every group proposal also
carries the note on the VAT of extra prices (see above).
- Vendora figures: “Products offering the group, today”, “Products offering the group, after approval” and “Distinct VAT
rates after approval”. The products counted are those attached directly and those of the attached categories; variants
count, the parent product with variants does not.
The warnings, at the top of the proposal. They block nothing: the decision is yours.
- Different VAT rates: “Different VAT rates (10%, 20%). Each extra price will follow the rate of the product it is added
to.” It appears when the affected products do not all share the same rate, store overrides included; beyond four rates
the list ends with “…” (“3%, 5%, 7%, 10%, …”). An extra price follows the product's rate: see
An extra price follows the product's VAT.
- Alcoholic drink?: “Alcoholic drink? Option “Verre de vin”: an alcoholic drink is sold as a separate product.” It
appears when an option of the group has the name of an alcoholic drink. On its own it is neither a refusal nor a box.
- Alcoholic option at the reduced rate: “Alcoholic option sold at the rate of “Plat de la cave” (10%).” It appears when the
group has an alcoholic option and an attached product is sold below the standard rate; it comes with the box below.
The confirmation box, required in three cases. Vendora requires a box to be ticked before applying:
Case · Reason written in the box
A required group gains products · “required choice for 4 more products” (for a category: “required choice for future products in …”)
Any detachment, even of a single product · “1 detachment”
An alcoholic option and an attached product at the reduced rate · “alcoholic option sold at the rate of “Plat de la cave” (10%)”
The box says for example: “I confirm the changes to “Cuisson du chef”: required choice for 4 more products, 1 detachment”. The
button is called Apply the change or Apply the 4 changes; it stays inactive until the box is ticked. For a required
group, a note adds: “This group is required: the register, the kiosk and the online menu will ask for the choice on lines
added afterwards, not on those already entered. An online order started before approval will be refused when sent if this
choice is missing.” Without one of these three cases (attaching an optional group, for example), there is no box. If you
approve without ticking a required box, nothing is applied (“The confirmation box is missing: nothing was applied.”).
The targets the assistant refuses, explaining why (no proposal is filed). Here the assistant is **stricter than the back
office**: by hand you can tick these products (a badge warns you, see
Archived products, attachments with no effect and categories), but the assistant does not
propose them, because the group would not be offered as you expect.
Target · Why the assistant refuses
A parent with variants (size, flavour…) · the options are chosen on each variant: name the variants or their category
A product that carries a combo · the register opens the combo and would not offer this group (a product that is only a choice in a combo is accepted, with the matching note)
A product sold by weight · the register adds the weighed line without options, so this group would not be offered
An archived product · it is withdrawn from sale: put it back on sale first (a put-back-on-sale proposal), then attach the group
It also refuses: a group, product or category that is not found or ambiguous (it offers you the list), a target named
twice or both to attach and to detach, a request with no change (everything is already as requested), **more than 50
targets, a VAT or tax-family field, and an assistant whose access is limited to some stores** (a group applies to all).
A category does not cover its subcategories. Attaching a group to “Plats” offers it with the products placed directly
in “Plats”, not with those in “Plats › Burgers”. When the category has subcategories, the proposal says so: “A category does
not include its subcategories: Burgers, Desserts, Pâtes and 1 other, under “Plats”, will not offer this group. To include
them, attach them too.” Then ask the assistant to attach the subcategories too, or the products one by one. This is the rule
on the register, the kiosk, the dining room and the online menu.
The limit of 50 targets. A proposal covers 50 products or categories at most, attachments and detachments together.
For more, the assistant prepares several proposals, or you attach a whole category.
What happens to sales and orders already entered. “Sales already recorded, table orders and baskets already entered keep
their options.” A sale already recorded does not change (nor does its ticket, duplicate included). Attaching or detaching
only applies to lines added afterwards, after the next sync of the registers, the kiosk and the online menu.
Who approves, and where. A manager decides in the back office only. On the register and the dining-room phone, the
proposal is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge and the sentence “Open the back office to decide.”,
with no button (see Approving a proposal on the register). The confirmation box and its reasons are seen in the back office only.
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is applied, if since it was filed one of these happened:
Cause · What Vendora says
The group was deleted · “This group no longer exists.”
The group's products or categories changed (even elsewhere, by another manager) · “The products or categories of “Pains” changed since the proposal.”
A target disappeared · ““Baguette” no longer exists.” or “The category “Plats” no longer exists.”
A target was archived · ““Baguette” was archived since the proposal.”
A target became a parent with variants, a combo or a product sold by weight · ““Baguette” now has variants: the group is attached to each variant.”; ““Baguette” is now a combo: the register would not offer this group.”; ““Baguette” is now sold by weight: the register would not offer this group.”
A confirmation became necessary · “The group “Cuissons” became required since the proposal: it does not carry the confirmation now required.” or “The group “Vins” now has an alcoholic option sold at a reduced rate: the proposal does not carry the confirmation now required.”
A kept attachment disappeared · “A product or category attached to “Pains” no longer exists.”
Ask your assistant again: the new proposal carries the box that is now required. A more recent proposal on the same group
replaces the previous one.
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, with the banner “Changes applied” and the link View the modifiers. The
group is then identical to what you would have saved by hand in Catalog › Modifiers; the group's history and the audit log
keep the trace of the proposal.

sections.heading: Editing the sales screen
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “put the tartare on the Home page” or “file the Kir with the mains”: the assistant files an **Edit the sales
screen proposal. It targets a single screen of a single store and lists, in order**, the changes to make:
add a button (product, category or page), move it, change its size or remove it. **At most 64
operations** per proposal. It does not touch colours, page names, the screen chosen by default or the registers the screen
is assigned to.
What the screen shows.
- The title and summary: “Sales screen · Le Petit Bistrot (démo)”, then “1 addition”, “1 move”, “1 resize”, “1 removal”
or several together (“1 addition · 1 move · 1 resize · 1 removal”). The level is “Low risk”.
- The “What will change” block: one line per operation, in the order they will apply:
- addition: “a button for “Tartare de bœuf” (product)” · “Page “Accueil”, row 2, column 2” (a category or page button
reads the same way: “a button for “Plats” (category)”, “a button for “Boissons” (page)”);
- move: “the “Burger du bistrot” button” · “From page “Accueil” (row 1, column 2) to page “Boissons” (row 1, column 1)”;
- size: “the size of the “Plats” button” · “From 2 × 1 (wide) to 1 × 1 · page “Accueil”, row 1, column 3”;
- removal: “the “Kir” button” · “Page “Boissons”, row 1, column 1”.
- The “Screen concerned” block: Screen, Store, Default screen of the registers (Yes / No) and **Assigned
registers, with the Open the sales screen link. In Arabic, “العمود 1” is the right-hand** column, as on the register.
- The notes: “Changes apply in the order listed: each one takes the previous ones into account.”, “The registers at Le
Petit Bistrot (démo) receive the new screen at their next sync; a sale in progress is not affected.” and “To undo: Sales
screen › Restore previous version.” A removal adds: “Removing a button does not take the product off sale: it stays in the
register's product list.”; a category button: “The “Plats” button shows products filed directly in the category; its
subcategories (Burgers) are not included.”; a product with variants: ““Pizza margherita” has variants: the register asks
which one on tap.”; a product already on the page: ““Expresso” already has a button on page “Accueil” (row 1, column 1).”
How the assistant goes about it. It first reads the sales screen of the store (the get_sales_layout read tool: pages,
buttons and free cells of each page, hidden buttons flagged), then files all the operations at once (the
propose_sales_layout tool), in order: each operation sees the result of the previous ones, so it frees a cell before
placing a button there. Lines and columns start at 1. A product with variants is placed as is: the register asks for the
variant on tap. To read the screen, the assistant's key needs the Settings read access; to propose, the **Edit the sales
screen action, delivered switched off and switched on on request** (see “Action subject to activation” above and
“Allow the assistant to propose” below). Without either, the assistant does not see the tool and
can only describe the screen. Ask for example: “Which buttons are on the Drinks page?” (read only), then “Add the beef
tartare to the Mains page.”
Hidden buttons. A button whose product is archived or unavailable in this store stays in the screen but is
not shown on the register. The assistant never removes them on its own: the proposal flags them with the note “Buttons
left in place, hidden on the register: “Limonade artisanale” (page “Accueil”, row 3, column 1).” It may move, resize or remove
one (“the hidden “Limonade artisanale” button (archived product)”). Adding an unavailable product is possible, with the
warning ““Tartare de bœuf” is unavailable in this store: its button stays hidden until it is back on sale.”
When the screen is displayed nowhere. If the targeted screen is neither the default screen nor assigned to a register,
the warning says: “No register shows this screen yet: the change will only appear once the screen is made the default or
assigned to a register.” It blocks nothing.
The 64-operation limit. A proposal holds at most 64 operations (additions, moves, resizes and removals together).
For more, the assistant prepares several proposals, which you approve one after the other.
One store at a time. The sales screen belongs to one store: a proposal never targets another store's screen, nor several
stores. For two stores, the assistant files two proposals.
Who approves, and where. A manager decides in the back office only, with the Apply to the sales screen
button. On the register and the floor phone, the proposal is listed and readable in full with the Back office badge
and the sentence “Open the back office to decide.”, with no button (see Approve a proposal on the register).
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is applied, if the screen's pages have changed since it
was filed, even through another manager: “The sales screen has changed since the proposal.” (with the screen's name when
the store has several). Other causes: “The sales screen no longer exists.”, “… is no longer a register screen.”, “… has been
archived since the proposal.” and “The … category no longer exists.” Ask your assistant again: the new proposal starts from
the screen as it is. A newer proposal on the same screen replaces the previous one.
Going back. Once applied, the change is undone like any other change to the sales screen: **Sales screen › Restore
previous version**. Registers receive the restored screen at their next sync.
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, with the banner “Sales screen updated”, the Open the sales screen link
and the sentence “Registers receive the new screen at their next sync.” The screen is identical to the one you would have
saved by hand; the screen's history and the audit log keep a trace of the proposal.

sections.heading: Importing products
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “add these twelve products to my catalog and update the dairy prices”: the assistant files an Import products
proposal, at high risk. It gathers 1 to 100 products: new products and updates to existing ones (name,
category, barcode, selling price incl. VAT, purchase cost, stock tracking). Nothing exists and nothing changes until a
manager approves, and it is all or nothing: if a single product changes before approval, nothing is applied.
What the screen shows.
- The title and summary: “Import products · 12 products”, then “3 new products and 9 updated (Épicerie Lumière
(démo))”, and the scope (“Épicerie Lumière (démo) · EUR” or “All stores · EUR”).
- The table: one row per product (Product, Action “New” or “Updated”, Price before, Price incl. VAT, VAT, Other
changes). A row to watch carries a reason: “Unusual rate for France”, “VAT differs from the category” or “Large change
(+35%)”.
- The notes, which start with the split of the new products' rates (“New products: 2 at the rate “TVA réduite 5,5 % —
5.5%”, 1 at the rate “TVA normale 20 % — 20%”.”), then remind you: “The VAT of existing products does not change.”,
“Sales already recorded keep their prices and VAT.” and “All or nothing: if a single product changes before approval,
nothing is applied.” A store that keeps its own price for an updated product is named: “The store “Lumière Tunis”
keeps its own price for “Brie de Meaux” (12,50 €): the new price does not apply there.”
VAT: always named, never guessed.
- New products. The assistant must name the rate of every new product. If it names none, the request is refused and
the assistant explains why: you do not pick a rate at approval, and Vendora never takes a “default” rate on your
behalf. A 0% rate is refused, as is a rate missing from your business or deactivated.
- Existing products. Their VAT is never changed by an import: the assistant can restate the current rate, not
another one. To correct it, do it by hand on the product's page.
- A Tunisian store. Only the rates 7%, 13% and 19% are accepted for new products; any other rate is refused and the
assistant is reminded of these three rates.
- Another country (France, Morocco…): a rate that is unusual for that country is not refused but flagged
(“1 new product has an unusual rate for France.”), as is a rate different from the one most products in the category use.
Price changes. When the price of an updated product changes by more than 30%, a warning at the top of the proposal
says so (“1 price changes by more than 30%.”) and the row carries the reason “Large change (+35%)”. It is not a refusal:
read the table before ticking the box.
The confirmation box. A single box that names every VAT rate of the new products and says how many products each
covers: “I confirm the import of 12 products: 3 new (2 at the rate “TVA réduite 5,5 % — 5.5%”, 1 at the rate “TVA normale
20 % — 20%”) and 9 updated.” If there are flags, the sentence ends with “To check: 2 prices changed by more than 30%, 1
unusual rate for France…”. The Apply the import (12 products) button stays inactive until the box is ticked.
What the assistant refuses, explaining why (no proposal is then filed):
- a new product without a name or a price; a price of 0 or one that is too high; an invalid or already used name; a
barcode that is invalid, reserved (starting with 20 to 29) or already carried by another product;
- an update that changes nothing;
- a category that is not found or is ambiguous, or whose name contains “>”: an import only files products in
existing categories and creates none; file that product by hand;
- a product with variants (it is edited in the back office);
- with a store specified, the price of a business-wide product: it is changed by a price proposal for that store, not by
an import;
- several currencies in the same proposal (one import per currency is needed), or stores that do not share the same currency
and country when the store for the new products is not specified.
One store at a time. New products belong to the named store, or apply to all stores if the assistant names none and
your stores share the same currency and country. An assistant whose access is limited to some stores must always name the
store and only changes products that belong to that store.
Who approves, and where. A manager decides in the back office only, with the Apply the import button. On the
register and the floor phone, the proposal is listed and readable with the Back office badge, without a button (see
Approve an assistant proposal on the register). A manager who is not in charge of
the store concerned cannot decide it: it stays pending. New products count towards your plan's product limit; if it is
reached, approval is refused and the proposal stays pending.
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, with the “Import applied” banner, the View the products link and the
sentence “Registers receive the products at their next sync.” The import is the same as a file import (see
Import your catalog from a CSV file) and the audit log keeps a trace of it.
There is no button to undo it: correct a price or withdraw a product from sale, by hand or with a new proposal. A sale
already recorded keeps the product's rate at the time of the sale, even if you correct it afterwards.
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is imported, if a product it targets has changed since
it was filed (including a price, a name or a barcode), was withdrawn from sale or gained variants, if its VAT has changed (“The VAT of “Brie de Meaux” has changed (5,5 % → 20 %).”), if a
rate is no longer active (“The rate “TVA réduite 5,5 % — 5.5%” is no longer active.”), if a category has disappeared, if a
product with the same name or an identical barcode has appeared elsewhere, if a store has its own price or was archived, or
if a store's country has changed. Vendora quotes the first cause, followed by “(and 3 other lines)” when there are
several. When it cannot be precise: “The catalog has changed since the proposal.” Ask your assistant again: the new
proposal starts from the catalog as it is.

sections.heading: Correcting stock after a count, recording a loss
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “I counted 18 bottles of still water and 4 packs of milk” or “two bottles of rosé broke this morning”: the
assistant files a Correct stock proposal (at high risk) or a Stock loss proposal (at medium risk). Each one
gathers 1 to 100 products of a single store. Stock is never overwritten: each line becomes a signed movement,
written in your name and dated at your approval. Nothing moves until a manager approves, and it is all or nothing.
Correcting stock after a count.
- What the assistant provides: the counted quantity, nothing else. The difference is calculated by Vendora, never
by the assistant.
- What the screen shows: the title “Correct stock · {product}” (or “· 3 products”), then the **What will be recorded in
the stock log table, one row per product: Product, Theoretical stock, Counted, Difference and Value of
difference (“—” when the product has no average cost). The difference is signed**: “+3” when the system is short,
“−6” when it holds too much.
- The difference is recalculated at approval. It is the count minus the stock Vendora believed it had **when the
proposal was made, including sales synced since (an offline register may have sent them later). Sales made after** the
proposal do not change the difference: they lowered real and theoretical stock together. A line whose recalculated
difference is zero writes nothing (“Stock corrected: 2 adjustments recorded in the stock log, 1 with no difference.”).
- A large difference. When a line differs by at least 2 units and by more than 20% of theoretical stock (or
theoretical stock is zero or negative), a warning appears at the top (“Large difference on 2 products (over 20% of
theoretical stock): check the count before validating.”), the line shows “Large difference” and a box is required:
“I confirm the large differences on 2 products”. A large difference can hide a theft: the box proves you have read it.
Recording a loss.
- What the screen shows: the title “Stock loss · {product}”, then the table with Product, Stock at proposal time,
Quantity removed and Value at average cost.
- You choose the reason: Breakage, Expiry, Damaged, Theft or Other. The assistant can pre-fill
Breakage, Expiry, Damaged or Other (“pre-filled by the assistant, editable”). It never picks “Theft”: if the reason
is a theft, it gives none and the choice is yours. With no reason given, nothing is pre-selected and the button stays
inactive until you choose.
- What is written: a Theft movement if you choose “Theft”, a Loss movement (with the reason you chose) otherwise.
The assistant's justification is never copied into the stock log.
Who approves, and where. A manager of the store approves in the back office or on a register of the store, always
with their PIN. On the register, the reason suggested by the assistant is preselected and can be changed (never
“Theft”), and a box must be ticked before the PIN when the difference is large. On the waiter phone, the proposal can
be read without a button, with the sentence “Approve it on a register or in the back office, not on a floor phone.” (see
Approve a proposal on the register). A manager
who is not in charge of the store concerned cannot decide it: it stays pending.
Step by step to approve.
1. Open the proposal in Proposals and read the table (and the note that recalls how the difference is calculated).
2. For a loss: choose the reason. For a large difference: tick the box.
3. Click the Validate and correct stock button (or Validate and remove from stock), marked with a padlock.
4. In the Manager PIN window, enter your PIN: the reason and the box go with it. A wrong PIN leaves the window open
(“Invalid PIN: 2 attempts left before the one-minute lock.”); without a PIN, nothing is applied.
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, with “Stock corrected: … adjustments recorded in the stock log” or “Loss
recorded in the stock log (1 movement).”, and the View the stock log link. Registers receive the new stock at their next
sync. Each movement carries the mention prepared by the assistant · validated by {your name} (see
Understand the stock log). There is no button to undo: a mistake is corrected in
the stock log with a reversing movement.
What the assistant refuses, explaining why (no proposal is then filed): a store that is not named (stock is corrected
store by store); a product withdrawn from sale, not stock-tracked or with variants (the variant must be named);
a negative quantity, a zero quantity for a loss, more than 100,000 units, or a fractional quantity for a product sold by
the piece (1.5 kg is accepted, 1.5 pieces is not); a count equal to theoretical stock (“nothing to correct”); a product
with a count in progress (“stock will be corrected when it's validated”).
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is written, when stock has moved since it was filed:
- Correction after a count: a movement other than a sale or a customer return was recorded for the product (receipt
of goods, transfer, loss, theft, adjustment, opening stock, reversing movement), or a stock count covering the product
was started or validated since (“Stock for “Still water 1.5 L” has moved since the proposal (delivery, loss, adjustment,
transfer or count): the difference is no longer reliable.”). Sales and customer returns do not make it out of date.
- Loss: a manual movement was recorded for the product (loss, theft, adjustment, opening stock, reversing
movement), because the same breakage would be counted twice (“A loss, theft or adjustment has already been recorded for
“Still water 1.5 L” since the proposal: it would be counted twice.”). A receipt, a transfer or a sale does not make it out of date.
- In both cases, a product withdrawn from sale, no longer stock-tracked, given variants or whose unit changed (“Still water
1.5 L” is no longer stock-tracked, was withdrawn from sale or changed unit.”), or a count started for the product (“A stock
count has been started for “Still water 1.5 L”: validate it first.”).
Vendora quotes the first cause, followed by “(and 3 other lines)” when there are several. Ask your assistant for the
proposal again: it starts from stock as it is.

sections.heading: Receiving a sent purchase order
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “the Ferme des Collines delivery has arrived, 6 orange juices are missing”: the assistant files a
Receipt · {order number} · {supplier} proposal (high risk). It concerns a single order, already sent (or
partly received), in a single store.
- What the assistant says: what arrived and what is missing, and whether the other lines of the order are
received or not. Vendora builds the full table from that: the assistant does not have to copy the order.
- What the screen shows: the What will enter stock table, one line per product: Product, Ordered,
Already received, Received now, Difference (“short”, “over”, “damaged”), Unit cost excl. VAT, **Value excl.
VAT, then the Total excl. VAT. When something is missing, a note recalls that the remainder stays expected on the
order**.
- The costs are those of the order, shown excluding VAT and not editable: the assistant never gives any. They
update the store's average cost, exactly like a receipt made by hand.
- The box “I confirm these goods have actually been received at the store” is always required. If a line goes over the
quantity ordered by more than 20%, a warning appears at the top and the box reads “…, including the surplus on 2
products”.
- The receipt is dated when you approve it, never with a date given by the assistant. A note recalls “Proposal created
on …”; if you approve in a different month from the creation, a warning says the goods enter stock on the approval
date, which may move them to another financial year.
- A product that requires a lot or an expiry date cannot be received here: the assistant refuses, or the proposal
becomes out of date if the requirement appears afterwards. Make that receipt by hand (back office or register, which ask
for the lot and the expiry date).
Who approves, and where. A manager of the store approves in the back office only, without a PIN (like a receipt
made by hand). On the register and the waiter phone, the proposal is listed and readable with the Back-office badge,
without a button. If the same order number exists in several stores, the assistant asks you which store before filing
anything.
Step by step to approve.
1. Open the proposal in Proposals and read the table, the warnings and the costs.
2. Tick the “goods actually received” box.
3. Click Approve the receipt.
Expected result: the state becomes Applied, with “Receipt recorded: 2 lines added to stock; order PO-… partially
received.” (or “received”) and the View the purchase order link. The order's receipt and the stock journal movements
carry the mention prepared by the assistant · validated by {your name} (see
Understanding the stock journal). There is no button to undo: a validated
receipt can't be changed, a mistake is corrected by a stock adjustment or a supplier return.
What the assistant refuses (no proposal is filed then): an order still in draft, already received or
cancelled; a supplier with several orders to receive (it asks which one); any mention of cost, date, lot or note.
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is written, when the order has been received, closed
or cancelled since, when another receipt of the order has been recorded since the proposal (it would be counted twice,
even if made on an offline register), or when a product now requires a lot and an expiry date. Ask your assistant again.

sections.heading: Opening stock of a product, low-stock threshold
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
The assistant can file two more proposals, each of 1 to 100 products.
Opening stock. You say “I have 24 green teas and 12 ground coffees in reserve”: the assistant files an
Opening stock proposal for a single store.
- Only for a product that has no movement yet in that store. If it already has stock, a sale or any movement, the
assistant refuses and points you to a count (see Correcting stock after a count): opening
stock entered after sales would count the units sold twice.
- All or nothing: if a single line is refused, none is recorded. Each line becomes an “Opening stock” movement in
the stock log, in your name, dated at your approval.
- What the screen shows: the What will be recorded in the stock log table with Product, **Quantity in
stock, Average cost and Value. The average cost is the store's if there is one**, otherwise “—”: Vendora
never invents a cost, and the value of this stock stays unknown until the first delivery.
- The “I confirm these goods are in stock at …” box is always required. There is no PIN in the back office, just
like opening stock entered by hand.
Low-stock threshold. You say “alert me when 10 yoghurts are left”: the assistant files a Low-stock threshold
proposal.
- The threshold is saved per product: it applies to every store that sells the product. A proposal names a store
only if every product belongs to that store alone; otherwise it is company-wide and the stock is not shown in
the table (Product, Current threshold, New threshold, Stock).
- The assistant cannot remove a threshold: that is done in the back office.
- Approved in one click, no box and no PIN (low risk). You are then alerted when stock falls to the threshold or
below, and order suggestions take it into account (see Low-stock thresholds).
Who approves, and where. A manager decides in the back office only; the register shows these proposals with the
Back office badge, without a button.
What the assistant refuses (no proposal is then filed): a product that cannot be found, is repeated, archived, not
stock-tracked or has variants; for a threshold, one that is already set.
Stale. Opening stock becomes stale, and nothing is written, when the product has since received a movement
dated before the proposal, a delivery, a loss or a transfer, or when an inventory covers it. A sale made after the
proposal does not make it stale. A threshold becomes stale if it was changed since, or if a single store's product now
applies to the whole company. Ask your assistant again.

sections.heading: Starting a stock count, writing off an expired lot
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet
open for all accounts. Until it is on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
Both proposals require the Advanced stock module.
Starting a stock count. You say "start the dairy count": the assistant proposes to open a stock count for **one
store**, full or limited to a few categories. Vendora writes the label itself ("Inventaire : Crèmerie — 18/11/2026").
Approve it in the back office without box or PIN, like a count opened by hand. The proposal is refused if a count
is already open in that store, and stale if one opens in the meantime. Counting and closing stay manual.
Writing off an expired lot. You say "write off lot L-2610 of the fruit yogurts": the assistant proposes to remove
the whole remainder of one or more lots from stock.
- The box "I confirm these lots are removed from sale" is required. No PIN in the back office, as for a write-off
done by hand.
- The remainder is read again on approval: if a sale used part of the lot meanwhile, the new remainder goes out; if
the lot is already empty, the proposal is stale.
- The movement is a loss at average cost, with the reason "Péremption — lot …" written by Vendora (never the
assistant's text), in your name.
- A lot not yet expired shows a warning, without blocking.
- If two lots share the same number, the assistant tells them apart by their reference.
On the register, both proposals can also be decided with your PIN (see the register page).

sections.heading: Creating or editing a supplier, changing a purchase price
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
The assistant can file three proposals about suppliers. They require the Suppliers and purchasing module in your plan,
and they apply to the whole business: an assistant access limited to certain stores cannot propose them.
Creating a supplier. You say “add Ferme des Collines, payment in 30 days”: the assistant files a New supplier
proposal (low risk) with the name and, if needed, the contact, phone and payment terms. The currency is your stores',
set by Vendora and displayed. Two suppliers cannot have the same name, deactivated or not.
Editing a supplier. The Supplier · {name} proposal (medium risk) changes only the fields proposed: name,
contact, phone, payment terms, or the active state. The other fields of the record are never touched.
- Email, address, currency and notes are still entered by hand in the back office: the assistant refuses them. The
email is where purchase orders are sent, which is why it is never proposed.
- Deactivating a supplier requires a box: “it will no longer be offered on a new purchase order”. A note recalls
that open orders remain valid.
Changing a purchase price. The Purchase price · {supplier} proposal gathers **1 to 100 products of a single active
supplier. The Purchase prices that will change table shows Product, Current price excl. tax, New price excl.
tax, Change and Last price received excl. tax**.
- Only the price changes: neither the average cost, nor the price history, nor an existing purchase order.
This price will be used for the next purchase orders. The reference, pack size and preferred supplier are not touched.
- A box is required when a price changes by more than 30% (a misplaced decimal does not pass unread): it states the
number of products concerned.
- A missing product link is created with default values (not preferred).
Who approves, and where. A manager decides in the back office only, without a PIN. Once applied, the proposal
offers the See suppliers link, which opens the supplier's record (see
Managing your suppliers).
Stale. The proposal becomes stale, and nothing is written, when a supplier now has the same name, the record
or the price has changed since, the supplier was deactivated or the product was withdrawn from sale. If the module is
removed meanwhile, the proposal can only be refused. Ask your assistant again.

sections.heading: Prepare a transfer between two stores
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora opens it separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet open
for every account. As long as it is not open on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your
assistant cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “send 10 kg of flour to the Fournil”: the assistant files a Transfer · {origin} → {destination} proposal (medium
risk). The What will be ready to ship table shows, for each product, the Quantity, the Stock at origin and the
Stock at destination. The origin store is the proposal's store; the destination is named by its name or reference.
- The transfer is created as approved, never shipped. Nothing moves in stock until a manager of the origin store has
shipped it from the Transfers page; the destination then receives it as usual.
Until it is shipped, you can cancel it from that page.
- A quantity above the stock is flagged, not refused: a warning asks you to check before shipping.
- The destination must be within the assistant's access: a store outside that access answers “not found”, like a store that
does not exist. The two stores must be different and not archived.
- Products: stock-tracked, not archived, shared by all stores; a product with variants is transferred through its variant.
A product sold by the piece is transferred in whole quantities.
- Nobody is notified at approval: the destination is notified when it ships.
Who approves, and where. A manager of the origin store decides in the back office only, with no PIN and no box.
A manager of the destination alone does not see the decision. Once applied, the proposal leads to the Transfers page, where the
transfer carries the Assistant badge and the note “prepared by the assistant · validated by {name}”.
Stale. The proposal becomes stale, and nothing is written, when either store has been archived or when a product was
withdrawn from sale, is no longer stock-tracked, got variants or became store-only. Stock that drops in the meantime does not
make it stale: the warning is recalculated.

sections.heading: Edit the floor plan
sections.text:
Action subject to activation. Vendora turns it on separately from the assistant's other actions and it is not yet
open to every account. Until it is on your server, it does not appear in Settings › AI assistant and your assistant
cannot propose it: contact Vendora to find out whether it is open for you.
You say “add a table for 6 on the terrace”: the assistant proposes to edit the floor plan of one store (Tables
module). A proposal can add or rename a zone, add, rename, move or remove a table, or change its capacity and shape. The
detail lists each operation in order and the plan before and after (number of tables and covers).
- The assistant never removes or reorders a zone: those gestures stay manual, in
Floor plan.
- Removing a table requires a checkbox: its QR code stops working and no previous version of the plan is kept.
- Occupied table: a table with an open bill is flagged with a warning. At approval, if it is still occupied, the
approval is refused and the proposal stays pending: settle or move the bill, then approve again.
Who approves, and where. A store manager decides in the back office only. The register and the floor phone show
the proposal without a decision button. The published plan reaches the devices at their next sync, like a manual publish.
Out of date. The proposal becomes out of date, and nothing is written, if the plan was published in the
meantime or the store was archived.

sections.heading: States of a proposal
sections.text:
State · What it means
Pending · Up to you to decide. It expires after 72 hours without a decision.
Applied · Approved: the result exists.
Declined · Declined by you or another manager.
Expired · “Approval window has passed (72 h): nothing was applied.”
Replaced · The assistant prepared a newer proposal: “Replaced by a newer proposal · View the new proposal”.
Out of date · “The data changed since the proposal: nothing was applied.” When Vendora knows what changed, it says so. Ask for a new proposal.
If another manager has already decided, the details say “Already handled by … at …” and do nothing more. When a
proposal is not applied, nothing is created or changed. The Expired or replaced tab groups expired, out-of-date
and replaced proposals.

sections.heading: Special cases
sections.text:
- “(access removed)”: after the assistant's name, it means its access was removed since. The proposal can still be
decided.
- “The assistant can no longer propose “Catalog” actions; this proposal can still be decided.”: the family was
removed since (see Connect your AI assistant). This line is only shown
to owners and administrators, with a link to AI assistant.
- **“This version of the screen cannot show this proposal in full: refresh the page before deciding. No decision is
possible here.”**: the details then show only the title and summary, with no button. Refresh the page.
- Module removed: “The Suppliers module is no longer in your plan: approval is not possible.” You can still decline.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text:
- At most 20 pending proposals per store: beyond that, the assistant cannot file more.
- Product availability: at most 20 products per proposal, all in the same direction.
- Creating a product: a created product counts toward your plan's product limit; once it is reached, approval is refused.
- Extending a product to all stores: only an owner or an administrator can approve; the choice is final.
- Changing several prices at once: at most 100 products per proposal, a single currency; two products or more: confirmation box required; a company group is decided in the back office only.
- Creating or editing a category: a single category per proposal; approved in the back office only; no deletion, colour or icon.
- Creating or editing a modifier group: a single group per proposal, at most 30 options and 30 changes; approved in the back office only; confirmation box for a large change, a switch to paid or to free, and a removal; no attaching to products (that is another proposal), no deletion.
- Attaching or detaching a modifier group: a single, existing group per proposal; 50 products or categories at most; a parent with variants, a combo, a product sold by weight and an archived product are refused; confirmation box for a required group gaining products, any detachment and an alcoholic option at the reduced rate; a category does not cover its subcategories; approved in the back office only.
- Edit the sales screen: a single screen of a single store per proposal; at most 64 operations (add, move, resize, remove); hidden buttons (archived or unavailable product) never removed on their own; out of date if the screen's pages have changed; approval in the back office only; go back with “Restore previous version”.
- Import products: 1 to 100 products per proposal (new and updated); a single currency; a VAT rate named by the assistant for each new product (for a Tunisian store: 7, 13 or 19% only); the VAT of an existing product is never changed; existing categories only; confirmation box required; all or nothing; approval in the back office only.
- Correcting stock after a count / recording a loss: 1 to 100 products of a single store per proposal; stock is never overwritten (one signed movement per line, in your name); the assistant never picks “Theft”; confirmation box for a difference of at least 2 units and over 20%; the reason for a loss and the manager PIN are asked at approval; all or nothing; approved in the back office or on the register, not on the waiter phone.
- Receiving a sent purchase order: a single order of a single store per proposal; 1 to 100 lines; costs always those of the order (excl. VAT), never a date, lot or note given by the assistant; “goods actually received” box always required; approved in the back office only, without a PIN; a product with a lot or expiry date is received by hand.
- Opening stock / low-stock threshold: 1 to 100 products per proposal; opening stock of a single store, only for a product with no movement at all, all or nothing, “goods actually in stock” box always required, no PIN; a threshold applies to every store and the assistant cannot remove one; approved in the back office only.
- Supplier and purchase price: “Suppliers and purchasing” module required; full access only; email, address, currency and notes are never proposed (enter them by hand); two suppliers never share a name; purchase price: 1 to 100 products of a single active supplier, only the price changes (no average cost, history or existing order), confirmation box beyond a 30% change and to deactivate a supplier; approved in the back office only, without a PIN.
- Transfer between stores: 1 to 100 products, a destination within the assistant's access (otherwise “not found”); created as approved, never shipped nor received; quantity above stock flagged, not refused; approved by a manager of the origin store, in the back office only, without a PIN.
- 300 proposals per month per store; the counter restarts the following month. The Vendora team can lift the limit
for your store: contact them.
- A proposal can only be approved by a signed-in manager: never by the assistant, nor in its name.

sections.heading: Allow the assistant to propose
sections.text:
By default, an assistant reads your figures and proposes nothing. The owner or an administrator sets what it may
propose:
1. Settings › AI assistant, What the assistant can propose block: tick the families of actions allowed for your
business.
2. When connecting an assistant or creating a key, tick the families granted to that assistant: none is ticked in
advance, and a family allowed here is granted to nobody until you tick it.
3. Also tick the read access the family needs (“Purchases” for a purchase order, “Catalog” for a price, “Anti-fraud”
for an alert).
Details: Connect your AI assistant and
Connect an AI assistant in one click. Even when allowed, the assistant sends,
pays and publishes nothing. The emergency stop prevents it from filing new proposals; you can still decide on those
waiting.
The Proposals menu does not appear
No proposal has been filed yet, or your account is Cashier. Also check that a family of actions was ticked when the
assistant was connected.
The Proposal family selector does not appear
It only appears when the displayed list contains at least two families. Change the state filter (for example All).
The Suppliers module is no longer in your plan: approval is not possible.
Purchase orders need the Suppliers module. Check Settings › Subscription; you can still decline.
You do not have the role to approve this proposal.
Your account is not allowed to decide here. Ask a manager, an administrator or the owner.
No connection: nothing was approved. Try again.
The approval did not go through. Restore the connection, then click again: nothing was applied in the meantime.
The confirmation box is missing: nothing was applied.
Tick the confirmation box (or fill in the requested field), then approve again.
The approve button stays inactive
A required field is empty (the reason of an alert, or the VAT rate of a new product) or the confirmation box for a change above 30% (or an option removal) is not ticked. If the
button is missing, the details say why your account cannot decide.

pages.title: API quota and pay-as-you-go

sections.heading: API quota and pay-as-you-go
sections.text:
Each time software connected with an API key (ordering website, accounting, dashboard)
queries Vendora, that is a call. Your plan includes a number of free calls each month; beyond that, you pay
by usage, always within a limit you set.

sections.heading: How many calls are included?
sections.text:
Plan · Calls included per month
Free (Gratuit) · 1,000
Commerce · 5,000
Restaurant · 10,000
Custom (Sur mesure) · 50,000
The counter resets on the 1st of each month at midnight (Paris time).
Not counted: calls from your AI assistants (“AI Assistant” keys and assistants connected in one click, already
covered by the AI assistant option), the webhooks Vendora sends, and refused calls (unknown key, missing right,
rate limit reached). A request that ends in “not found” or invalid data does count.
This monthly quota is different from a key's rate limit (requests per minute), which only slows down software
that is in too much of a hurry.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Read the API usage card
Open Settings › API keys. The API usage card shows:
- the current month and a gauge: “3,250 / 5,000 calls · 65 %”; it turns orange at 80% and red at 100%;
- the “Resets on …” date and your plan;
- depending on your country, the spending cap (France) or the pack balance (Tunisia); beyond the quota, a line
“Included quota used up — … prepaid calls left” (Tunisia) or “Included quota used up — … calls beyond, billed by
usage” (France);
- the Last 6 months: Month, Calls, Quota, Beyond the quota (or Pack calls) and Invoice.
Only the owner and administrators see this card.
Be warned before the limit
Vendora emails the owner at 80% and then at 100% of the quota, once a month each. The card also shows a
banner: “More than 80% of this month's quota is used.”, then “Monthly quota reached.”.
France: pay-as-you-go and spending cap
Beyond the quota, calls keep working and are billed €1 excl. VAT per started block of 1,000 calls (2,500 extra
calls = €3), on an “Appels d'API au-delà du quota” line of your next invoice. The card shows the **Overage this
month (calls and amount) and the Rate beyond the quota**.
The spending cap protects you from runaway software: €50 per month by default, i.e. 50,000 calls beyond the
quota. Once it is reached, calls are refused until the reset. You are never billed beyond the cap. To change it:
1. Enter the amount in New cap (€), from 0 to €1,000. 0 = no overage: calls stop at the quota.
2. Click Change the cap, then confirm in the Change the spending cap? window.
3. The message “Spending cap saved.” confirms. The change is recorded in the audit log.
Tunisia: prepaid packs
Beyond the quota, calls are deducted from a prepaid pack balance: 10,000 calls for 15 DT, with no expiry.
Packs are sold by the Vendora team (contact it: one single-line invoice per sale). The card shows the **Pack
balance**; any unused balance carries over from month to month.
When the included quota is used up and a pack is left, the card shows “Included quota used up — … prepaid calls left”,
the gauge stays orange and the banner adds “Calls are deducted from your packs.”: nothing is blocked. With no balance
left, calls stop at the quota: “No
prepaid calls left: contact Vendora to add a pack.”
Free plan and trial: stop at the quota
The Free plan is never billed: at the quota, calls stop until the 1st of the following month. The banner “Quota
reached: switch to Commerce to continue.” offers See my subscription. During a trial, same rule: “Quota
reached during the trial: subscribe to your plan (Settings › Subscription) to continue.”
For your integrator
Every API response carries the X-Quota-Limit, X-Quota-Remaining and X-Quota-Reset headers; a refused call gets
429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED with the date calls resume. In Tunisia, X-Quota-Remaining counts what is left of the quota
plus the pack balance: it does not drop to 0 while a pack is left. Details are in the technical documentation (**OpenAPI
documentation** button on the API keys page).
Spending cap reached: calls will resume on …. Raise the cap to continue.
Your software has used up this month's cap. Raise the cap (“France” step) or wait for the reset. Variant with a cap at
0: “Overage disabled (cap at 0): calls will resume on …. Raise the cap to continue.” Also check with your provider
that no software is calling Vendora in a loop.
Spending cap between 0 and €1,000.00 (0 = no overage)
Enter an amount between 0 and €1,000.
Quota reached: switch to Commerce to continue.
Free plan: 1,000 calls per month. Wait for the 1st of the month or move to Commerce (5,000 calls, then pay-as-you-go).
The software receives, in French: “Quota mensuel de 1 000 appels de la formule Gratuit atteint : les appels
reprendront le …”.
No prepaid calls left: contact Vendora to add a pack.
(Tunisia.) The pack balance is used up: ask the Vendora team for a pack. Calls go through again as soon as it is sold.
The API usage card does not appear
It is reserved for the owner and administrators. With an unlimited quota (older contract), it shows “… calls this
month · unlimited quota”.

pages.title: Handle rejected sync events

sections.heading: Handle rejected sync events
sections.text:
Your registers send the server everything they do (sales, drawer openings, closures…): these are
events. The server checks each one. A questionable event is never deleted: either it is placed in
quarantine until you decide, or it is rejected permanently and remains viewable.
Most of the time, this page is empty: that is normal. It mainly fills up after you revoke a device
that still had offline sales to send.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Control › Sync
Choose the store. The counters (1) show the events that are pending and rejected. The
Quarantine — to resolve card (2) lists what is waiting for your decision; Permanent rejections (3), what was rejected.
Each event shows what it represents (e.g. “Cash drawer opened”, “Sale completed”), the Device,
the User, the date (Occurred) and the Reason.
Accept or decline an event in quarantine
Several reasons put an event in quarantine (shown in the Reason column):
- appareil révoqué (device revoked): the device performed this operation (often offline) before it was revoked and is
only sending it now. If the device was revoked because it was stolen or misused, be cautious;
- sealed data received from a revoked device (same “device revoked” code, DEVICE_REVOKED): a signed sale, void,
return or closure occupies a fiscal number, so the data is kept in quarantine. The label shown: “sealed data
(sale, void, return or signed closure) received from a revoked device: kept because it occupies a fiscal number.
Accepting adds it to the fiscal journal; refusing sets it aside and leaves a missing number: only refuse knowingly”.
Accept records it and flags it. Decline remains technically possible, but leaves a missing number in the
fiscal sequence: do not decline a sealed sale without having contacted Vendora support
(Fiscal compliance);
- utilisateur inconnu du magasin (user unknown to the store): the person signed in on the register does not exist (or no longer exists) in the store's team.
- kiosk order payment on hold: its sale is itself in quarantine, accept the sale first: a kiosk settled an order
citing a sale that is itself waiting for your decision. As long as that sale is not accepted, Accept on the payment
is refused: “Accept sale … first: the order's payment refers to it” (the row says “Sale … awaiting a manager's
decision”). Decide on the sale first, then come back to the payment;
- payment at the kiosk confirmed by hand whose manager code does not hold: the customer paid on the terminal and a
manager confirmed it at the kiosk, but the code check failed. The reason says which: “the manager's code was not
found”, “… has already been used for another order” or “… was granted outside the time of the payment”. Accept
marks the order “already paid at the terminal, to record at the register”: a register will record it, without
charging the customer again (An order already paid at the terminal).
Decline sets this payment aside. Before deciding, check on the terminal's statement that the payment exists and
ask the team who confirmed it (Tax compliance).
- règlement ou sortie de stock d'une vente de borne hors de la forme admise (payment or stock movement of a kiosk sale
outside the allowed form): the kiosk sale is kept, flagged and counted in turnover; only its stock movement or the
order settlement wait. The label shown: “payment or stock movement of a kiosk sale outside the allowed form: the sale is
kept and flagged, a manager decides. Accepting records the stock movement or settles the order; rejecting sets them
aside, the sale stays recorded and the order stays open”. Accept records the stock movement or settles the order;
Decline sets them aside: the sale stays recorded and the order stays open. Read the sale's anomaly sentence first
(Fiscal compliance).
For each row, enter a Reason (1), then click Accept (2) or Decline (3). The reason is optional when
accepting and required when declining.
- Accept: ““…” accepted: added to the log and sent to the registers.” The event counts as if it had arrived
normally (a sale is included in revenue, reports and tax records).
- Decline: ““…” rejected: moved to the rejections.” The event does not count, but remains visible.
Past decisions remain listed in Quarantine — decisions (who decided, when, with what note).
Suspended store (read-only account). As long as the subscription is not restored, decisions are on hold: the page
shows “Account is read-only: this decision is on hold until the subscription is restored. Only decisions on kiosk
payments remain allowed.” Accept and Decline therefore remain possible on kiosk payment reasons only; for every
other reason, the sentence above appears and the event stays in quarantine. Selling, synchronisation and Z reports are
never cut off by a suspension.
Understand permanent rejections
These events were rejected automatically (1); there is nothing to do here except understand the cause:
Reason · What it means · What to do
device revoked · Operation performed after the revocation. · Nothing: this is intended.
invalid device signature · The batch does not come from the device it claims to be. · Notify Vendora.
unreadable content · Corrupted data. · If it happens again, notify Vendora.
outside the device role's permissions · E.g. a kiosk sending something other than orders. · Check the device's role.
event version unknown to the server · The device's app is newer than the server, or too old. · Update the app; notify Vendora.
encaissement de formation sur une commande réelle (training charge on a real order; code TRAINING_SALE_ON_REAL_ORDER) · An older register in training mode sent the charge of a real order (dining room, kiosk, other channel). The server declines it: the order stays open. · Charge the order normally, outside training, and update the register app.
règlement de borne sans la vente correspondante (kiosk payment without the matching sale) · A kiosk reported the payment of an order without the sale that backs it (sale missing or unknown to the server). The server does not settle the order: it stays open. · Charge the order at the register (Charge a kiosk order). If it keeps happening, update the kiosk app and tell Vendora.
règlement ou sortie de stock d'une vente de borne hors de la forme admise (payment or stock movement of a kiosk sale outside the allowed form) · A kiosk sale falls outside the allowed form: it is kept, flagged and counted in turnover, but its stock movement or the order settlement were set aside by your decline. The sale stays recorded and the order stays open. · If the order must be settled, do it at the register; to correct the sale itself, make a return at the register (Fiscal compliance).
declined by a manager after quarantine · Your decision (or a colleague's). · —
(Owner) Change the local network key
The Local network key authenticates exchanges between the store's registers when the internet is down. Change it
if you think it has leaked (old device gone missing, former service provider). Choose the Grace period (1) — during this
period, the old key remains valid for devices not yet resynced — then Rotate key (2).
There is no confirmation.
With None (immediate), devices that have not yet received the new key are refused on the local network
until their next internet connection. We recommend 24 hours.
Accept sale … first: the order's payment refers to it
You tried to accept the payment of a kiosk order whose sale is still in quarantine. Accept or decline that sale first
(another row of the quarantine), then come back to the payment.
A payment at the kiosk confirmed by hand is waiting for your decision
The customer paid and a manager confirmed at the kiosk, but their code was not found, has already been used or was
granted outside the time of the payment. Compare with the terminal's statement: if the payment exists, Accept (the
order will be “already paid at the terminal, to record at the register”); otherwise Decline with a reason.
Account is read-only: this decision is on hold until the subscription is restored. Only decisions on kiosk payments remain allowed.
The store is suspended: Accept and Decline only go through for a kiosk payment. Restore the subscription
(Subscription), then take the decision again.
A reason is required to reject an event.
Write a reason in the row's Reason field before clicking Decline.
This event has already been resolved.
A colleague decided before you did (or you double-clicked). Reload the page: the decision appears in Quarantine — decisions.
Only the store owner rotates the LAN key.
Rotating the local network key is reserved for the owner.
Manager role required on this store.
You are not a manager of this store. Switch stores or ask the owner.
A register shows “pending” operations that are not being sent
See A register no longer syncs: the register may be offline, or
revoked (“Register revoked in the back office: its sales are no longer accepted. Pair it again or use another
register.”).

pages.title: Notify software with webhooks

sections.heading: Notify software with webhooks
sections.text:
A webhook is an address of your software that Vendora calls on its own as soon as an event happens in your stores:
Sale completed (every sale or return cashed by a register) or Low stock (a product falls below its alert
threshold). Your software no longer needs to poll Vendora every minute. Each delivery is signed with a secret
specific to the webhook: your software can check that it really comes from Vendora.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Create the webhook
Open Settings › Webhooks and click New webhook. Enter the Receiving URL (HTTPS) provided by your software
and, if you like, a Description (1). Tick the Events to receive (2), then click Create webhook (3).
The address must start with https://. The webhook receives the events of all the stores of the brand (each
delivery states the store concerned).
Copy the signing secret (only once)
The Signing secret (1), which starts with whsec_, is shown only once. Click Copy (2) and pass it to your
software or provider through a secure channel, then click I have saved the secret.
Secret lost or leaked: New secret on the webhook card generates another one (the old one stops signing at once:
update your software at the same time).
Test and track deliveries
Send a test sends a “Test” event to your address. Delivery log (2) shows the latest deliveries (3): the event,
the Status (Delivered, Pending, Failed), the number of Attempts, the Last response of your
software and the Body sent. The Active badge (1) shows that the webhook receives events.
Pause stops deliveries without deleting the webhook; Delete erases it along with its log.
Understand retries and deactivation
Your software must answer within 10 seconds with a success status (2xx). Otherwise, the delivery stays Pending and
Vendora retries automatically after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h then 6 h (2); a banner counts the consecutive failures (1).
After 15 consecutive failures, Vendora disables the webhook (1) and explains why (2); pending deliveries are
abandoned. Fix your software, use Send a test, then Reactivate (3). A Failed delivery can then be sent again
with Resend in the log.
Verify the signature (for your provider)
Each delivery is a JSON POST carrying the header X-Vendora-Signature: t=<timestamp>,v1=<signature>. The signature is a
hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 of the text <timestamp>.<body> computed with the whsec_… secret. The software rejects a
delivery whose signature does not match or whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes old, and ignores an event already
received (same X-Vendora-Event-Id). The Verify the signature card on the page and the public API technical guide
(§ Outgoing webhooks) detail the format.
Webhook URL: HTTPS required (http only to localhost in development)
Use the https://… address provided by your software. An http:// address is only accepted by a development server,
to localhost.
Webhook URL: internal address refused
The address targets an internal network (localhost, private address). Vendora only sends to an address reachable on
the Internet.
At least one event
Tick Sale completed, Low stock, or both.
Commerce plan limit reached: 3 webhook(s). Delete a webhook or contact Vendora to upgrade your plan.
Your plan sets the number of webhooks (Essentiel 1, Commerce 3, Restaurant 5, Sur mesure unlimited); the … plan card
on the page shows your usage. Delete an unneeded webhook or upgrade your plan. Variant: “Webhooks are not included in
the … plan”.
Inactive webhook: reactivate it before resending a delivery
Resend only works on an active webhook: click Reactivate first.
Deliveries stay “Pending” with “HTTP 500” or a timeout
Your software is not answering correctly. Check the address, that the software is running and that it answers within
10 seconds. The details of the last response are in the log.
Restricted to the owner and administrators.
Managers do not have access to webhooks.
