pages.title: Ticket printer and kitchen display assigned to a station

sections.heading: Ticket printer and kitchen display assigned to a station
sections.text:
A prep station receives its tickets on paper, on screen, or both. Everything is set in
Restaurant › Prep stations: the station's printer, the kitchen display that shows it, and the device that prints
the tickets sent from floor phones.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Choose the device that prints for the others
Who prints the tickets from other devices? card, Printing device list (1).
- The device that sends always prints its own tickets (a register that sends to the kitchen prints them itself).
- Floor phones, however, don't print: a single device in the store prints their tickets, the one you
choose here (usually the main register, connected to the same network as the printers).
- Local setting on each device: no printing device is designated; each device follows its own local setting.
Connect a station's printer
Select the station in the list (here Bar), then:
1. Printer (IP address, empty = none): the printer's address (e.g. 192.168.1.51); Port: 9100
for most network printers;
2. Paper width: 80 mm (the most common) or 58 mm;
3. Kitchen display: optional, a station can have a printer and a screen.
Without an IP address, the station gets no paper ticket: its tickets appear on its kitchen display.
An IP address that doesn't change
If the printer gets a new address when the router restarts, tickets stop printing. Give it a fixed address (a DHCP
reservation on the router, or a static IP in the printer's settings). Test prints and the print queue are handled on the device:
see Connect and set up the receipt printer and The print queue.
Assign a kitchen display to a station
Select the station (here Cuisine):
1. Target time (min): the preparation time you aim for; past that, the ticket shows as overdue on the screen;
2. Kitchen display: choose the paired screen; Chosen on screen lets the cook choose their stations on
the tablet;
3. Sound when target time is exceeded: the screen plays a sound when a ticket goes past the target time.
On the tablet, an assigned screen shows its stations directly with the note “Stations assigned by the
back office”; otherwise it asks “Which stations does this screen show?”. See Set up the kitchen display and choose its stations.
One screen for several stations
Several stations can share the same screen: it shows their tickets together, each labeled with its station. In
another station's Kitchen display list (here Desserts), the screen already in use is followed by “also on:
Cuisine” (1). The list of stations (2) shows “screen assigned” and each station's printer.
Publish
Click Publish.
Expected result: “Stations published (version 3) — devices apply them at the next sync.”
Run a test: send an order to the kitchen from a floor phone and check that the bar ticket prints on
the bar printer and that the dishes show up on the kitchen display.
No kitchen display paired in this store (Devices › “Kitchen display” pairing code).
The Kitchen display list is empty: no tablet is paired with the Kitchen display role in this store.
Generate a “Kitchen display” pairing code in Settings › Devices, enter it on the tablet (see
Pair a register or a phone), then come back to this page.
Publication denied. “Cuisine”: kitchen display unknown, revoked or from another store
The chosen screen was revoked or replaced in the meantime. Reload the page, choose an active screen (or **Chosen on
screen**), then publish.
Publication denied. Printing device unknown or revoked in this store: …
The
printing device no longer exists in this store (revoked, replaced). Choose another active device, or
Local setting on each device.
Publication denied. “Bar”: invalid printer port
The port must be a number
between 1 and 65535 (almost always 9100).
Tickets sent from floor phones don't print
1. Check that a Printing device is designated, that it is switched on, connected to the restaurant network and
synced.
2. Check the IP address of the station's printer.
3. On the printing device, open the print queue to retry pending tickets (see
The print queue and The printer doesn't print). Printing incidents are also reported to the back office.
The kitchen display doesn't show a station's tickets
Check that the station is assigned to this screen (or chosen on the screen), that its categories are routed
(Create prep stations) and that the tablet is synced.

sections.text:
- Create prep stations and route products
- Kitchen display: move tickets forward
- Kitchen display: target times, overdue tickets
- Follow the current service (times per station)
- The Restaurant section

pages.title: Build the sales screen (tiles, quick buttons)

sections.heading: Build the sales screen (tiles, quick buttons)
sections.text:
The sales screen is the grid of quick buttons the cashier taps to sell: a button can add a
product, open a category or another page of buttons. You build it in
Checkout and payments › Sales screen; registers apply the published version at their next sync.
Without a sales screen, the register simply shows the product list.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Checkout and payments › Sales screen and create the first screen
If no screen exists yet for this store, the page shows “No sales screen for this store: the register only shows the
product list.” Click Create from the store preset (1): Vendora creates a screen suited to your type of business
(one tile per category for a restaurant) and publishes it right away to the registers.
Find your way around the editor
1. Undo and Redo your latest changes (also Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z, ⌘ on Mac);
2. the preset picker and Start over from a preset;
3. the page grid, below the page tabs (the first one is called Home): existing tiles and empty “+”
cells;
4. the Add a product or a category palette, with its search;
5. the Pages panel: default screen, new page, page grid, kept versions.
At the top right: Restore previous version and Publish.
Add a quick button
Click an empty “+” cell (1). In New button:
2. Type: Product (adds the product to the ticket), Category (shows the category's products) or
Page (opens another page of buttons);
3. Target: the product, category or page;
4. Size: 1 × 1, 2 × 1 (wide) or 2 × 2 (big button) — ideal for your best-seller;
5. Color (optional): in #RRGGBB format; it is the color strip at the top of the button on the register;
6. Add.
To change a button, click it: Apply, Delete or Cancel.
Move a button by dragging it
Grab a button with the mouse (or your finger on a tablet) and drag it: it fades (1) and the target cell is
highlighted (2) — in green if the button fits there, in red if it would go outside the grid or overlap another
button. Release it on a green cell.
The button is in its new place (1); the badge shows “unpublished changes” (2), and Undo (3) reverts the
move.
Enlarge or shrink a button with its handle
Click the button: a handle appears in its bottom corner (1). Drag it to the right to widen the button
(2 × 1), down to make it a big button (2 × 2), to the left or up to shrink it. The preview (2) shows the
resulting size. Only three sizes exist on the register: 1 × 1, 2 × 1 and 2 × 2.
The button takes its new size (1) and the panel's Size field updates to match (2).
Do everything with the keyboard
Reach a grid button with the Tab key, then:
- arrows: move the button by one cell;
- Shift + arrows: resize it (Shift + → widens it, Shift + ↓ makes it a 2 × 2, Shift + ← and Shift + ↑ shrink
it);
- Delete: remove it; Esc: deselect it;
- Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z (⌘ on Mac): undo / redo.
The button follows (1); the key reminder is below the grid (2). Screen readers announce each action
(“Button moved to row 4, column 1.”, “Cannot move: cell taken or outside the grid.”).
Add a product or a category from the search
In Add a product or a category, type a few letters (1) — accents are optional. Drag the entry found (2)
onto an empty cell of the grid (3): it becomes a 1 × 1 button. Without a mouse, click the entry (or press Enter):
it goes into the selected empty cell, otherwise into the first free cell.
Change the grid density or start over from a preset
In the Pages panel, Grid of page “Home” changes the number of Columns and Lines of the page
shown (8 at most); then select Apply to the page. You can't shrink the grid while a button would fall outside it.
To start all over again, choose a preset in the bar (Restaurant, Grocery, Apparel, Services, General retail), then
Start over from a preset and confirm: the pages are replaced by those of the preset, **without publishing
anything. Check them, then Publish — or Undo** to go back to your version.
Organize the pages
The button appears on the grid (1). With nothing selected, the Pages panel offers:
2. Default register sales screen: the screen used by the store's registers;
3. New page: its name (e.g. “Desserts”);
4. its grid size: Columns and Lines (8 at most), then Add page;
5. Kept versions: the previous versions, which you can restore.
A new page is empty: add buttons to it, and put a Page button on Home that opens it.
Delete “Desserts” removes the page shown (possible as long as at least one page remains).
Publish
Click Publish.
Expected result: “Published (version 2) — registers apply it at their next sync.” (1), and the
new page tab (2).
After moves, the published grid (2) is exactly the one in the editor; the Undo / Redo history starts
again from scratch.
On the register, after sync, the tiles appear on the sales screen (see
Make a sale).
(If you made a mistake) Restore the previous version
Restore previous version asks for confirmation (“Sales screen “…” will take back the content of version 1 and be
published to registers. Unpublished changes will be lost.”), then republishes the old version.
This button overflows the grid or overlaps another button.
A 2 × 1 or 2 × 2 button needs free cells to its right (and below for 2 × 2). Pick a cell further
left or higher, reduce the size, or enlarge the page grid.
Cannot drop: cell taken or outside the grid.
You released the button on a red cell: it overlapped another button or went beyond the grid. It stays in its
original place; aim for a green cell, or shrink it first with its handle.
Some buttons would fall outside the grid: move or shrink them first.
The requested grid is smaller than a button's position. Drag the buttons in the last rows or columns inwards (or
shrink them), then Apply to the page.
Preset unavailable.
The server could not prepare the preset (connection lost, or insufficient rights: you must be Manager or above).
Nothing was changed; try again.
Color must be in #RRGGBB format.
The color is written with a hash sign and 6 hexadecimal characters, for example #1B7A43. Leave it empty for the
default color.
Choose a target.
The Target field is empty (for example, no page exists yet for a Page button). Create the target
first, or change the type.
A button shows “hidden on the register” and the grid shows the badge “orphan button(s), hidden on the register”
Its target was deleted (“Deleted product”, “Deleted category”, “Deleted page”): the register no longer
shows it. Click the button to give it another target, or delete it, then publish.
This sales screen was changed elsewhere: the latest version has been reloaded, reapply your changes.
Someone published the screen while you were editing it. Redo your changes on the reloaded version.
“Restore previous version” is grayed out
There is nothing to restore: “No earlier version of this sales screen”. Your first publication will keep the current version.
The register still shows the old screen
Check that you published and that Default register sales screen is checked, then wait for the register to
sync (see Sync: status, sync now, rejected events).

sections.heading: Have your assistant edit the screen
sections.text:
Your AI assistant can read this screen then propose editing it: add a button, move it, change its size or remove
it, all the operations in a single proposal (action subject to activation, delivered switched off and opened on request).
Nothing is applied without a manager's validation, in the back office: the register shows the proposal read-only. After
validation, the registers receive the new screen, stay on their open page and keep their cart; Restore previous version
undoes the change.
- How the assistant goes about it, operations and limits: Editing the sales screen
- What the register shows: Editing the sales screen on the register

sections.text:
- Create and edit a product
- Register: make a sale
- The Restaurant section

pages.title: Choose how payments are taken at the table

sections.heading: Choose how payments are taken at the table
sections.text:
When a waiter takes payment for a bill on their phone, the sale must go into a register session (the one that
produces the Z report). There are two possible setups; the store owner decides, in
Restaurant › Pay at the table.
Main register session · Phone's own session
Where floor sales go · Into the open session of the designated register · Into a session opened by each phone
Drawer and cash · A single drawer: floor cash is handed in at the register · No drawer on the phone: float 0, cash handed in at the register outside the app
Z report · A single Z, the register's (sales marked “charged on the floor”) · One Z per phone, closed without a cash count
If the register is closed · “Checkout unavailable” on the phones · No effect
Best for · Most restaurants · Large dining rooms, waiters who keep their own float

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Restaurant › Pay at the table
The Policy card shows the two options:
1. Main register session;
2. Phone's own session;
3. the Main register list (only for the first choice), with the reminder “Published main register: …”;
4. Publish.
A manager sees the box “Read-only: only the store owner changes this policy.” and grayed-out choices.
Choose the policy
- Main register session: choose the register in Main register (usually the counter
register, the one with the drawer).
- Phone's own session: nothing else to set.
The badge changes to — unpublished changes (2) and Publish becomes active (3).
Publish
Click Publish.
Expected result: “Policy published (version 2) — floor phones apply it at the next
sync.”
Then, phone by phone, you decide who is allowed to take payments: **Checkout allowed on this
phone** checkbox in Set up the floor phones. The waiter's side
is described in Charge at the table.
(Same page) Set the store's sales policy
The second card, Sales policy — returns, stock and payments, applies to all the store's registers:
1. Allow returns without the original receipt;
2. Fallback when the original method cannot refund (Cash or Card) and **Return period (days,
0 = unlimited)**, up to 365 days;
3. Allow selling beyond stock — when unchecked, the register blocks the sale of an out-of-stock item, unless overridden
with a manager PIN and a reason;
4. “Other” payment: the labels offered at the register (Check, Voucher, Works council voucher…), one per line, 8 at most;
leave it empty to disable the method; each label gets its own line in the X and Z reports;
5. Accept meal vouchers and the cap per ticket (see
Meal vouchers);
6. Publish sales policy.
Expected result: “Sales policy published (version 1) — registers apply it at their next sync.”
No register paired in this store: pair a register (REGISTER role) first.
The Main register list is empty: pair a register in Settings › Devices (see
Pair a register or a phone), or choose Phone's own session.
Choose the register whose session takes in floor sales.
You chose the main register session without choosing the register: Publish stays grayed out. Choose a
register in the list.
Publication denied. The main register must be an active register (REGISTER) in this store
The chosen register was revoked or replaced. Reload the page and choose an active register.
Only the store owner publishes the sales policy.
Only the store owner changes these two policies. Ask them, or sign in with their account.
The policy was changed elsewhere: the latest version has been reloaded.
Someone published while you were making changes. Make your choice again on the reloaded version, then publish.
(For the sales policy, the message is “The sales policy was changed elsewhere: reloaded.”)
Duplicate “Other” payment labels
Two lines of the “Other” payment are identical (or a
line is empty: “Empty “Other” payment label”).
Keep one label per line, 8 at most.
Phones show “Checkout unavailable”
With Main register session, the designated register must have an open session. Open the register
(see Open the register with its opening float). Also check that checkout is allowed in the phone's
profile.

sections.text:
- Set up the floor phones (zones, checkout)
- Review register sessions and discrepancies
- Read and download Z reports
- Floor phone: charge at the table
- The Restaurant section

pages.title: Keep your food cost under control

sections.heading: Keep your food cost under control
sections.text:
Food cost is the share of a dish's selling price excluding VAT that goes into its ingredients. Vendora calculates it in two
ways, for dishes that have a recipe sheet:
- theoretical: what the dish should cost, based on the recipe sheet that applied at the time of each sale
(sales made before the dish's first sheet, or after it was removed, are not counted);
- actual: what the ingredients really cost — the stock outflows caused by sales, plus the losses,
thefts and stock count discrepancies for those ingredients.
When the gap exceeds the store's drift threshold (10 % by default), the dish is flagged on the page, **and managers
are notified** without having to open it: an alert on the registers and a line in the daily summary.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Restaurant › Food cost and choose the period
1. the store, the period (7 days, 30 days, This month) or From / to dates;
2. the alert “1 dish(es) drift by more than 10 % from their sheet: losses, overly generous portions or a sheet to
update.”, which reminds you that managers are notified;
3. the indicators: Dish sales excl. VAT, Theoretical food cost, Actual food cost (in % and in euros), **Drifting
dishes** and the threshold;
4. Drift threshold: the link to the report settings, where you change this threshold.
Read the “Per dish” table
For each dish with a recipe sheet sold over the period: quantity, sales excl. VAT, Expected cost and percentage (1),
Actual cost and percentage (2), and the Drift (3) — in red when it exceeds the threshold.
The unknown cost badge flags a dish where an ingredient has neither a purchase price nor an average cost: complete the
ingredient's product sheet.
Find the ingredient responsible
Gaps per ingredient compares, ingredient by ingredient, the Expected quantity (sheets × dishes sold) and the
Actual quantity, in the ingredient's stock unit (“3 pieces”, “280 g”, “14 cl”), then the Discrepancy and its
value in euros (1).
In the example, 6 more steaks than expected left the stock: losses were reported (“Chambre froide mal fermée”, cold room left open). The three
usual causes:
- reported losses and breakage (see Stock and purchasing › Stock log);
- overly generous portions: the kitchen uses more than the sheet specifies;
- a sheet to update: the recipe changed, but the recipe sheet didn't.
Be notified without opening the page
Vendora checks the food cost of the current month every hour. As soon as a dish exceeds the threshold, the store's
managers receive one alert — only one per dish and per month, even if the dish drops below the threshold and goes
above it again:
- on the registers and the mobile view, Alerts tab: “Food-cost en dérive : Burger du bistrot”, status
Food cost, with the drift, the threshold and the costs (notification if a manager is signed in);
- in the daily summary email (Insights › Daily summary), two lines: “Food-cost du mois (plats à fiche technique) :
théorique 23,4 %, réel 28,83 %” and “Plats en dérive (au-delà de 10 %) : 1”, followed by each dish (the email is
written in French).
The alert is also recorded in the Audit log (“Food cost” › “Drift reported to managers”).
No dish with a recipe sheet sold over the period. Create one from the dish's product page (Catalog › Products).
None of the dishes sold over the period has a recipe sheet, or nothing was sold. Open the dish's product sheet in
Catalog › Products and add its recipe (see Recipe sheet for a dish). The calculation applies to sales
made after the sheet was created.
The actual food cost equals the theoretical one, with no gap at all
Actual only differs from theoretical if losses, thefts or stock counts are recorded for the ingredients. Report
breakage on the register and run regular stock counts (see Count stock and report breakage and Run a stock count).
Food cost doesn't appear in the menu, or shows the “Plan” badge
The page belongs to the Kitchen module of your plan (see Settings › Subscription).
No drift alert reaches the registers
The alert is sent once per dish and per calendar month: if the dish was already flagged this month, nothing new is
sent (the daily summary keeps listing it). The check runs every hour: wait for the next run. On the register, the
Alerts tab is only visible to a manager.
Report unavailable.
The server couldn't calculate the report. Check your connection, then change the period to run the calculation again.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Recipe sheet for a dish — Catalog
- Report settings (drift threshold) — Insights
- Stock and purchasing: stock log
- Stock and purchasing: stock counts
- The Restaurant section

sections.heading: Restaurant
sections.text: Restaurant-specific settings, from the back office: floor plan, prep stations (kitchen, bar), floor phones, sales screen.

pages.title: Put your menu online with QR codes

sections.heading: Put your menu online with QR codes
sections.text: Your customers scan the QR code stuck on their table with their phone and read your menu, with nothing to install. Reading the menu is open to every plan, with no option. The QR menu and online ordering option is for ordering: with it, customers can also order from their table (table ordering), and the bill is then paid at the register, as always. Takeaway ordering (click & collect) also lets the customer pick a time slot, leave their contact details and pay at the counter when they collect; it is not possible in France for now (takeaway VAT).

sections.heading: Step by step
See also
sections.text:
- Draw your floor plan
- Taking payment at the table
- Tickets and kitchen screens
- Floor phones
- Handle online orders at the register
- Track my takeaway order (the customer's page)
- Take a payment
- Kiosk orders to pay
- Catalog section

pages.title: Draw your floor plan (zones, tables)

sections.heading: Draw your floor plan (zones, tables)
sections.text:
The floor plan is what your waiters see when they open their phone: the zones (Dining room, Terrace,
Mezzanine…) and their tables, with the number of covers. You draw it once in the back office, then you
publish it: every floor phone and every register receives it at its next sync.
The whole flow: create the “Mezzanine” zone, place two tables, move one, publish.
Table status is not set here
Free, occupied, bill requested: these colors come from the bills open on the devices. The plan only describes
the layout. To follow service live, see Follow the current service.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Restaurant › Floor plan
In the left menu, open Restaurant (1) then Floor plan (2).
Shortcut: type “tables” in the Go to… search at the top of the screen.
If you have several stores and the header shows All stores, choose the store in the Store
list: a floor plan belongs to a single store.
Find your way around the page
1. the zone tabs, with the number of tables in parentheses — click a tab to show its grid;
2. the New area (Dining room, Terrace…) field and the Add zone button;
3. the zone grid: each empty cell can take a table;
4. the right-hand panel, which shows the form for the selected cell or table;
5. the Publish button, grayed out while there is nothing to publish.
Above the grid, a badge shows the published version (Version 1, or Never published) and the store total
12 table(s), 42 covers.
Create a zone
Type the zone name (for example “Terrace” or “Mezzanine”) in New area (Dining room, Terrace…), then
click Add zone. A new tab appears, with an empty grid.
Two zones cannot have the same name (regardless of capitalization).
Place a table
Click an empty cell in the grid (1): the New table panel opens.
- Name or number (2): what the waiter will read on their phone (“T9”, “Bar 2”, “Banquette”…). Two tables in the
same store cannot have the same name, even in two different zones;
- Covers (3): from 1 to 50;
- Shape (4): Square, Round or Rectangular (this is the drawing shown on the phones).
Click Add (5).
Check the draft
The table appears on the grid (1). The badge changes to Version 1 — unpublished changes (2) and Publish (3)
becomes active. Until you publish, nothing has changed on the devices: you can keep
drawing, or leave the page to discard everything.
Edit, move or remove a table
Click a table (1): the panel becomes Edit table.
- change the name, covers or shape, then Apply (2);
- Move (3): the message “Click the table's destination cell.” appears; click the new cell;
- Remove (4) takes the table off the plan;
- Cancel closes the panel without changing anything.
Switch between zones, delete a zone
Click another zone's tab (1) to draw its tables. Below the grid, Delete zone “Terrasse” (2)
removes the zone and all its tables from the draft once you confirm: the “Delete the “Terrasse” area?” dialog
reminds you how many tables go with it; click Delete area (or Cancel).
An occupied table cannot be removed
If a table you delete (alone or with its zone) has an open or partly paid bill, publishing is refused and the
message names the tables: settle or move their bill, then publish again. Your draft is kept. Renaming or moving an
occupied table is still allowed.
Nothing is lost before you publish
Deleting only affects the draft. If you made a mistake, don't publish: leave the page (or
reload it) and the published plan comes back as it was.
Publish the plan
Click Publish at the top right.
Expected result: the message “Plan published (version 2) — devices apply it at their next
sync.” appears and the badge shows the new version.
On the devices:
- floor phones show the new zones and tables (see Read the floor plan);
- so do registers in restaurant mode (Tables screen, see Restaurant on the register: tables or direct sale);
- a new zone only appears in a waiter's “My zones” if their profile includes it: see
Set up the floor phones.
Tables module inactive in this store: registers do not show the dining room (“Tables | Direct sale” switch). Turn it on in Stores › Modules to use it.
The selected store doesn't have the Tables module (profile other than restaurant, or module unticked): you can
prepare the plan, but its registers don't show the dining room. Tick Tables (floor plan) in
Stores › Modules (Stores button in the banner); registers apply it at their next sync.
Floor plan doesn't appear in the menu, or shows the “Plan” badge
The floor plan is part of the Tables module of your Vendora plan. If it isn't included, the owner sees
the entry with a Plan badge and the banner ““Floor plan” is not included in your plan: existing data remains
viewable; creating and configuring require a plan that includes it.”; other roles don't see
the entry. See View subscription in that banner (Settings › Subscription page).
Table “T3” already exists in this store.
Table names are unique across the whole store, all zones combined (the waiter must be able to say “T3”
without ambiguity). Choose another name, for example “T3 bis” or “Terrace 3”.
Zone “Terrasse” already exists.
A zone with that name already exists (even with different capitalization). Click its tab rather than creating a second one.
Give the table a name or a number.
The Name or number field is empty: type at least one character, then Add or Apply.
Capacity between 1 and 50 covers.
The number of Covers must be between 1 and 50. For a large party, place several neighboring tables.
The plan was changed elsewhere: the latest version has been reloaded, reapply your changes.
Someone else (a colleague, or you in another tab) published the plan while you were drawing. Your
unpublished changes are lost: the page shows the most recent version. Redo your changes, then
publish.
Publication denied. Table “T9”: position already taken in “Salle”
The server
checks the plan again when you publish. After “Publication denied.”, it lists each problem,
separated by “;”: “Duplicate zone: “…””, “Duplicate table in the store: “…””, “Table “…”: capacity between 1 and 50
covers”, “Table “…”: position outside the plan”… Fix the table shown, then publish again.
Waiters don't see the new plan on their phone
1. Check that you did click Publish (the badge must no longer show “unpublished changes”).
2. The phone applies the plan at its next sync: it must be connected. See
A register no longer syncs.
3. A zone missing from “My zones” is still visible in “Other zones”: set the waiter's zones in
Set up the floor phones.

sections.text:
- Set up the floor phones (zones, checkout)
- Create prep stations and route products
- Follow the current service
- Floor phone: read the plan
- Floor phone: take the order
- The Restaurant section

pages.title: Create prep stations and route products (kitchen, bar)

sections.heading: Create prep stations and route products (kitchen, bar)
sections.text:
A prep station is a team that prepares part of the order: the hot kitchen, the bar, the
pastry chef… On every send to kitchen from a floor phone or a register, Vendora splits the order and
sends each station its own ticket: only the lines from the categories (or products) routed to it.
A line with no station is sent nowhere: it simply stays on the bill (handy for a coffee served
at the counter).
Create the “Desserts” station from a template, assign it the kitchen display, route the Desserts category to it in the grid, publish.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Restaurant › Prep stations
In the menu, open Restaurant › Prep stations (shortcut: type “kitchen” or “kds” in
Go to…). The page contains:
1. Who prints the tickets from other devices? — the printing device (detailed in
Ticket printer and kitchen display);
2. Station templates — ready-to-use stations;
3. the list of stations: name, code, printer, number of routed categories and products;
4. the form for the selected station.
Further down, the Category routing card contains the grid.
Create a station from a template
Click a template: Hot kitchen (15 min), Cold kitchen (10 min), Bar (5 min), Desserts (10 min)
or Pizza (12 min). The station is created with its name, code and target time, and selected in the list (2).
A template already in use is grayed out with a check mark (1).
For a station that has no template (“Grill”, “Sushi”…), click Add a station below the list and
fill in the name and code yourself.
Set up the station
In the station form:
1. Name (shown on tickets and screens) and Code — in CAPITALS, without spaces (e.g. HOT_KITCHEN,
DESSERTS); it is a technical identifier and must be unique;
2. Printer (IP address, empty = none) and Port: leave empty if this station works from a screen only;
3. Paper width (80 or 58 mm) and Target time (min), from 1 to 240: past that, the ticket turns “overdue” on
the kitchen display;
4. Kitchen display and Sound when target time is exceeded;
5. Per-product override: sends a specific product to this station regardless of its category (see below).
The printer and the screen are detailed in Ticket printer and kitchen display assigned to a station.
Read the routing grid
Scroll down to Category routing:
1. the 2 category(ies) without a station badge (or Every category is routed) — it only counts
categories that have products to send: neither a parent category with no products, nor a combo category;
2. one column per station, plus No station;
3. one row per category; those without a station are highlighted with the Not routed badge;
4. Suggest a routing proposes a station for each category without one.
Which categories should you route?
Routing looks at the category of the product itself, not its parent categories. If your drinks are filed under
Drinks › Soft drinks, Drinks › Wines and beers…, route Soft drinks, Wines and beers and Coffees; the parent
category Drinks, which contains no products, can stay on No station (it is neither counted nor marked
Not routed). The same goes for Combos: each dish in a combo goes to the station of its own category
(the starter to the kitchen, the dessert to desserts).
(Optional) Start from a suggestion
Click Suggest a routing. Vendora proposes a station for each category without a station, based on its name
(drinks → Bar, desserts → Desserts, the rest → Hot kitchen). Nothing changes until you click **Apply the
suggestion; Cancel** closes the proposal.
Review the proposal: here, routing Boissons (drinks) and Formules (combos) changes nothing (see the tip above), so you can cancel.
Route a category
On the category's row, click the circle in the column of the station you want (1). A category goes to a single station:
clicking another column moves it. No station removes it.
Exception for one product: open Per-product override in a station's form and check the product.
It goes to that station regardless of its category (for example the “Café gourmand”, filed under Desserts, prepared at the
bar). A “→ Cuisine” badge flags a product already routed elsewhere: checking it moves it.
Publish
Click Publish (at the bottom of the station form, or below the list if no station is selected).
Expected result: “Stations published (version 2) — devices apply them at the next sync.”
(1), and the version badge (2) is updated.
What you will see on the devices, after they sync:
- on the next Send to kitchen from a floor phone or a register, each station receives its ticket (see
Send to kitchen);
- on the kitchen display, tickets arrive in the station's column, with the target time (see
Move tickets forward);
- in Restaurant › Service, the Times per prep station table measures each station
(Follow the current service).
A dish doesn't arrive on any ticket or any screen
Its category is on No station (Not routed badge) and the product has no override. Route the category
of the product (not its parent category), publish, then wait for the device to sync. Lines already
sent are not sent again: resend them from the phone if needed.
Drinks go to the kitchen instead of the bar
Check the subcategory's row in the grid (Soft drinks, Wines and beers…), and in each station's form the
Per-product override section: an override always wins over the category.
Publication denied. “Desserts”: code in CAPITALS (e.g. HOT_KITCHEN)
The code must
start with a capital letter and contain only capitals, digits and “_” (32 characters at most). Other possible
refusals, separated by “;”: “A station has no name”, “Duplicate station: “…””, “Duplicate code: …”, ““…”: invalid printer port”,
““…”: width 58 or 80 mm”, ““…”: target time between 1 and 240 min”, “Category routed to two stations: “…” and “…””. Fix the station named, then publish.
The prep stations were changed elsewhere: the latest version has been reloaded.
Another user published while you were working; your unpublished changes are lost. Redo them on
the reloaded version, then publish.
No suggestion: every category already has a station, or the Bar, Desserts and Hot kitchen stations don't exist.
The suggestion only deals with categories without a station, and only proposes stations created from the Bar,
Desserts and Hot kitchen templates. Route by hand in the grid.
Prep stations doesn't appear in the menu, or shows the “Plan” badge
The page belongs to the Kitchen module of your plan. See Settings › Subscription (the View subscription link in
the banner shown on the page).

sections.text:
- Ticket printer and kitchen display assigned to a station
- Draw your floor plan
- Kitchen display: choose its stations
- Kitchen display: move tickets forward
- Organize categories
- The Restaurant section

pages.title: Follow the current service (bills, tables)

sections.heading: Follow the current service (bills, tables)
sections.text:
Bills live on the floor phones and registers. At each sync, they are uploaded to the
back office: Restaurant › Service shows them with the state of each dish (sent, in preparation, ready, served),
what was paid, comped or voided, and the kitchen times. The page is read-only: you make changes to
a bill from the phone or the register.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Restaurant › Service
1. Current service / Closed bills: the open bills, or those paid, merged and voided;
2. All / Kiosk: all orders, or only those placed on a kiosk;
3. the indicators: number of bills (open, paid), Bill revenue and average ticket, Covers,
Complimentary (excluded from revenue), Voids (including those made after “ready”, meaning waste) and the average
Sent → ready time;
4. Times per prep station: lines, ready lines, average time, target time and Overdue lines;
5. the list of bills: table, waiter, opening time and duration, covers, status, lines by state, total,
paid and remaining;
6. Export to CSV.
The page refreshes every 30 s (checkbox in the toolbar); Refresh reloads it right
away, and “updated at …” shows when the data was last loaded.
Open a bill's details
Click a row in the list. The details (1) give the number of covers and the opening time, then each line (2)
with its Send number (1st send, 2nd send…), its kitchen note (“! Sauce à part”), its State and its
Time (3) — “ready in 12 min 00”. At the bottom, Payments received (4) lists the payments already made.
Spot voids and complimentary items
A voided line is shown as Voided: reason, with the note after ready if the dish was already ready or served (1):
this is what the indicator Voids … including N after “ready” counts. A complimentary line shows the badge
Complimentary · 2,00 € (original price) and counts as 0 € in the total.
Voiding or comping is done on the phone, with a manager's PIN (see Table actions);
each action is also recorded in the audit log.
Find a paid bill
Switch to Closed bills and click the table. The details show the complimentary items (1) and each payment (2):
time, part paid (“1× Burger du bistrot”, “Part 1/3” or “Full bill”), amount, who charged it and the
remaining amount after that payment.
Follow kiosk orders
Click Kiosk (1): only orders placed on a kiosk remain, with their number (“Kiosk K1-014”)
and their payment method (2): Pay at the counter (to be charged at the register) or Paid at the terminal.
To charge a “Pay at the counter” order, see Charge a kiosk order; to set up the
kiosks, Supervise your kiosks and set up their payment terminal.
(Optional) Export the list
Export to CSV downloads the list shown (service-additions-ouvertes-AAAA-MM-JJ.csv or
service-additions-closes-…), semicolon-separated, with these column headers (in French in the file): Table, Type
(Sur place / À emporter: dine-in / takeaway), Couverts (covers), Statut (status), Ouverte par (opened by), Ouverte le
(opened on), Close le (closed on), Lignes (lines), Total, Réglé (paid), Reste (remaining), Motif d'annulation (void reason).
No open bills — service is quiet.
No bill is open in what the server has received. If tables are occupied in the dining room, the phones
haven't synced yet (or are offline): see A register no longer syncs and
Control › Sync.
No order placed on a kiosk in this list.
The Kiosk filter is active but no kiosk order is in the chosen view. Click All, or switch
to Closed bills.
Many “Overdue” lines in the times per station
A line is overdue when the Sent → ready time exceeds the station's target time. Adjust the target time if it
is unrealistic, or add staff to the station at peak times: see
Ticket printer and kitchen display. Dishes marked “ready” late
on the kitchen display also skew the measurement.
Times are empty (no “ready in …”)
The time is measured when the kitchen display marks the dish Ready. Without a kitchen display (paper tickets only),
nobody marks dishes “Ready”: no time is calculated.
Unable to load the bills.
The back office couldn't reach the server. Check your internet connection, then click Refresh.

sections.text:
- Create prep stations and route products

- Floor phone: table actions
- Floor phone: split the bill
- Kitchen display: move tickets forward
- The Restaurant section

pages.title: Track my takeaway order

sections.heading: Track my takeaway order
sections.text: You ordered takeaway on a restaurant's site. After sending, you received a number (for example W-017), the pickup time and a Track my order link. This link opens a page that updates by itself: no need to reload it, and no account to create.

sections.heading: What this page is for
sections.text:
It tells you where your order stands. It is a summary, not a sales receipt or an invoice: the real receipt is given to you at the counter when you pay.
Keep the link to yourself: it belongs to your order, and whoever has it can see it.

sections.heading: What each status means
sections.text:
What you read · What it means
Received · The restaurant could not be reached just now. Your order is saved and will be confirmed as soon as possible.
Waiting for confirmation · The restaurant still has to say yes. This usually takes a few minutes.
Accepted · The restaurant said yes. Your order is about to go to the kitchen.
Being prepared · Your order is being prepared.
Ready · It is ready: come to the counter with your number.
Collected · You have picked up your order.
Declined · The restaurant cannot prepare it. The reason is shown.
Cancelled · The order will not happen, for example because the restaurant could not confirm it in time.

sections.heading: Pay at the counter
sections.text: You pay nothing online. You pay at the counter, when you collect, by giving your number (for example W-017). The restaurant then gives you its receipt. Come at the pickup time you chose.

sections.heading: If the restaurant declines or cancels
If the page does not open
sections.text:
- “This order cannot be found. Check the link you received.”: the link is incomplete or is not the right one; open it again from the confirmation page.
- “Connection lost. The page will update as soon as the network is back.”: wait for the network to return, the page refreshes by itself.
Your name and phone number are only used to hand over your order: the restaurant erases them after a few weeks.

pages.title: Set up the floor phones (zones, checkout)

sections.heading: Set up the floor phones (zones, checkout)
sections.text:
Each waiter's phone has its own profile: the plan zones it shows first, whether it can take payment for a
bill, and the printer where the receipt comes out. The profile follows the phone, whichever waiter signs in to it
with their PIN. The phone applies its profile at its next sync.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Restaurant › Floor phones
The page shows one card per floor phone paired in the store. Each card has three settings:
1. Server's zones;
2. Checkout;
3. Receipt printer;
and its Cancel / Publish buttons (4). Each card is published separately: publishing Inès's phone doesn't
affect Lucas's.
No card? The message “No floor phone” appears with a Devices button: first pair a
phone with the Floor phone role.
Choose the waiter's zones
By default, All zones is checked (1): the phone shows the whole plan. Uncheck it, then check this
waiter's zones (2), here Terrasse.
On the phone, these zones form the My zones tab; the others remain available in Other zones, to
help a colleague or transfer a table. This setting doesn't block anything: it just saves the waiter from hunting for their table.
Faster: set it during pairing
When you add a floor phone in Settings › Devices, you can already check its Zones served:
the profile is created with these zones as soon as the phone redeems the code.
Allow checkout or not
Checkout allowed on this phone checkbox (1).
- Checked: the waiter can take payment for the bill at the table, within the limits of the store policy, shown
just below (2) — for example “Store policy: floor sales join the main register's session (Caisse comptoir (démo));
register closed → checkout unavailable.”
- Unchecked: “Without checkout, the server requests the bill and the table is settled at the register.” (3)
The policy itself (main register session or phone's own session) is chosen in
Choose how payments are taken at the table.
(Optional) Set the receipt printer
Under Receipt printer, enter the IP address of the printer where the phone prints the receipt after a
payment, its Port (usually 9100) and the Paper width. If left empty, the phone keeps its
local setting.
Publish the profile
Click Publish in the phone's card (Cancel goes back to the published profile).
Expected result: “Profile published (version 2) — the phone applies it at the next sync.” (1)
On the phone: the My zones tab now shows only Terrasse, and the checkout button disappears
(the bill is settled at the register). See Start service on the phone.
No zone in the floor plan: the phone shows the whole plan.
The floor plan has no zone yet. Draw and publish the plan
(Draw your floor plan), then come back to choose the zones.
Store policy: table checkout not set up (no main register designated) — no phone can take payments until the owner chooses the policy.
Even with the box checked, no phone will take payments: the owner must first choose the table
checkout policy. See Choose how payments are taken at the table.
Port between 1 and 65535
The printer port isn't valid; Publish stays grayed out until it is fixed. Enter 9100.
The profiles were changed elsewhere: the latest version was reloaded.
Another profile was published at the same time (by you in another tab, or by a colleague). Redo your
changes on the reloaded version and publish.
The waiter has the Checkout box checked but sees “Checkout unavailable”
With the “Main register session” policy, the phone only takes payments if **the main register has an open
session**. Open the register (see Open the register with its opening float) or change the policy.
A phone doesn't appear on the page
Only devices with the Floor phone role in the selected store have a card. Check the store shown and the
device's role in Settings › Devices (see Manage your devices).

sections.text:
- Choose how payments are taken at the table
- Draw your floor plan
- Floor phone: start service
- Floor phone: charge at the table
- The Restaurant section

pages.title: Place a purchase order and receive it

sections.heading: Place a purchase order and receive it
sections.text:
A purchase order goes through Draft → Sent → Partially received → Received (or Canceled). When
goods are received, stock goes up and the weighted average cost is recalculated with the order's price.
Receiving an incomplete delivery: 30 bottles received out of 36, “Missing” discrepancy, confirmation.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Stock and purchasing › Purchase orders
Choose the store in the header, then Stock and purchasing (1) › Purchase orders (2). At the top, the
Low stock card lists the products below their threshold (see Low stock thresholds).
Create the draft
Click New order, choose the supplier (1), a product (2), the quantity (3), then
Create draft (4).
The draft opens on the right: adjust the quantities (price and reference come from the supplier record), then
Save. PDF preview shows the document; Cancel purchase order abandons it.
Send it to the supplier
Click Send (email + PDF) — or Send (PDF) if the supplier has no email. The order gets its
number (PO-…) and moves to Sent.
- “Order PO-… emailed to … (PDF attached).”: it's on its way.
- “Order PO-… sent — no email: hand the PDF to the supplier.”: download the PDF and pass it on.
- “Order PO-… sent — …” followed by an error: the order is marked as sent in Vendora, but the email failed: pass on the PDF.
Receive the delivery
When the goods arrive, open the Sent order: the Received just now column is prefilled with the
outstanding quantity (1).
1. Correct Received just now if the delivery is different: the cell turns orange (missing) or red (surplus);
2. choose the reason under Discrepancy: Missing, Surplus, Damaged on delivery, Substitution;
3. for a product tracked for expiry, fill in Lot no. and the Use-by date (expiry);
4. a surplus of more than 20% requires you to check Confirm a surplus of more than 20%;
5. click Confirm receipt of goods (2).
Expected result: “Receipt recorded: 3 line(s), 1 variance(s). Stock and average cost updated.” (1).
If some quantity is still outstanding, the order moves to Partially received (2); otherwise to Received.
The details of the Last receipt (quantities, lot, use-by date, discrepancy) appear below the lines:
You can also receive goods on the register: Stock › Supplier receipts (it appears as “on the register”
in the Goods receipts list).
Your AI assistant can also propose the receipt of a sent order (“the delivery has arrived, 6 juices are missing”): you
approve it in the back office, with the “goods actually received” box, and it carries the mention “prepared by the
assistant · validated by {name}” (action subject to activation, see
Receiving a sent purchase order).
Receive the rest, or close the remainder
A Partially received order shows its progress (1), the lines with their Outstanding quantity (2) and the history of
Goods receipts (4). Is the rest arriving? Receive again. Will it never arrive? Enter a reason and
click Close the remainder (3): “Backorder closed: the purchase order moves to “Received”.”
Surplus of more than 20%: … — confirm
You are receiving much more than you ordered: check Confirm a surplus of more than 20%, then confirm again.
Lot number and use-by date are required for “…” (product tracked for expiry).
Fill in Lot no. and Use-by date on that product's line.
Nothing to receive
All the Received just now quantities are 0.
Supplier deactivated: no longer available for a new order
Reactivate the supplier in its record (Suppliers).
Supplier currency (…) differs from the store's (…): multi-currency not supported
The supplier and the store don't use the same currency: create a supplier record in the store's currency.
Quantity must be greater than zero
A line has a zero or empty quantity: correct it.
Outdated version (… ≠ …)
The draft was changed elsewhere (another tab, a colleague): reopen the order to get the latest version,
then make your change again.
This order has already been received: close the remainder instead of canceling it.
An order that has already been received (even partly) can no longer be canceled: close the remainder instead.
Only a partly received order can be closed.
The order is not Partially received (it was sent with nothing received yet, or it's already received).

sections.text:
- Low stock thresholds and order suggestions

- Manage your suppliers and their prices

pages.title: Track supplier invoices and payables

sections.heading: Track supplier invoices and payables
sections.text:
Each invoice you record increases what you owe the supplier; each payment or credit note reduces it.
The due date is calculated from the payment terms in the supplier record (you can change it for each invoice).
Invoices that are overdue or due within 7 days also show up on the Dashboard (Supplier due dates).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Stock and purchasing › Supplier debts
1. Due dates: invoices that are Overdue and those Due soon (7 days), with the amount left to pay.
2. Balances: what you owe each supplier, the number of overdue invoices and the next due date.
Open a supplier: invoices and payments
Select a supplier (1) (or choose one under Open a supplier). For each invoice, the **Invoices and
payments table (2) shows the due date, the Total (with the amount already Paid** below it) and
the Remaining amount (with the status below it: Unpaid, Partially paid, Paid). Below each unsettled invoice, a Pay …: line holds the payment fields.
With “All stores” in the header, first choose the Store for invoices and returns.
Record an invoice
In the line below the table (3): Invoice no., Date (today if empty), Due date (date +
the supplier's payment terms if empty), Amount including VAT, then Save invoice.
Expected result: “Invoice … recorded, due on YYYY-MM-DD.”; the balance goes up.
Enter a payment
On the invoice's Pay …: line: Amount (can be partial), method (Bank transfer, Check,
Cash, Other), Ref. (check or transfer number), then Pay.
Expected result: “Payment recorded: invoice … partially paid.” (or “… paid.”).
Return goods and read the statement
Returns (1): choose the product, the quantity and the category (Defective, Expired, **Wrong
product, Overstock), enter the reason (required) and the expected credit note, then select Confirm return**: “Return confirmed:
stock removed, credit note deducted from the balance.” Stock goes down (Supplier return movement).
The Statement (2) sums up every transaction (invoices as debits, payments and credit notes as credits) with the balance
after each one — handy for checking against the supplier's own statement.
Invoice … already recorded for this supplier
This number already exists for this supplier: check that the invoice wasn't entered twice.
Due date before the invoice date
Correct the due date or the invoice date.
Amount must be greater than zero
Enter the invoice amount (greater than 0). A credit note is entered through a return.
The payment exceeds the invoice's remaining balance (…).
The payment is more than the amount left to pay on the invoice, shown in parentheses (e.g. “125,50 €”). Enter at most
that amount.
Reason required
A return must have a reason (e.g. “Damaged batch”).
Unable to load the suppliers: check your connection, then reload the page.
The server didn't respond: reload the page.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Manage your suppliers and their prices
- Place a purchase order and receive it

pages.title: Manage your suppliers and their prices

sections.heading: Manage your suppliers and their prices
sections.text:
Supplier records are shared by all your stores. They are used for
purchase orders (prices, references, email address the orders are sent to), order
suggestions and supplier debts (payment terms).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Stock and purchasing › Suppliers
The list shows each supplier with its payment terms (30 d or cash), the date of the last purchase,
its contact and the amount Due (overdue invoices are flagged). Click a row (1) to open its record:
contact details, Payment terms (days) (2) and Supplied products (3).
Create a supplier
Click New supplier and fill in at least the Name (1); add a contact, phone, Email
(purchase orders will be sent there), address, Payment terms (days) (2; 0 = cash) and notes,
then Create (3).
Expected result: “Supplier … created.” Later changes are saved with Save (“Record saved.”).
Link the supplied products
In the record, under Supplied products:
1. choose the product;
2. its Supplier ref. (optional, shown on the purchase order);
3. the Purchase price excluding VAT;
4. the Pack size (packs of 6, 12…);
5. check Preferred if this is your main supplier for this product, then Link the product.
The preferred supplier is the one Vendora offers in
order suggestions. Select Edit on a line to change the price.
The Last received column shows the last cost actually invoiced when goods were received.
Deactivate a supplier
A supplier is never deleted: click Deactivate at the bottom of its record. “Supplier deactivated:
its history remains viewable.” It's no longer offered on new orders; Reactivate puts it back in use.
Supplier name required
The Name field is empty.
Negative payment term
Enter a positive number of days, or 0 for payment in cash.
Negative purchase price
The purchase price must be zero or positive.
Pack size of at least 1
The pack size is the number of units per pack: at least 1.
Supplier deactivated: no longer available for a new order
Reactivate the supplier in its record before ordering from it.
Unable to load the suppliers: check your connection, then reload the page.
The server didn't respond: reload the page.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Your AI assistant can also propose creating or editing a supplier and changing a purchase price: Creating or editing a supplier, changing a purchase price (action subject to activation).
- Place a purchase order and receive it
- Track supplier invoices and payables

pages.title: Stock and purchasing

sections.heading: Stock and purchasing
sections.text: Track your stock, run a stock count, manage expiry dates, order from suppliers and receive deliveries, transfer between stores.

pages.title: Start a stock count and validate it

sections.heading: Start a stock count and validate it
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Stock counts are part of advanced stock, included in the Commerce plan and higher plans. On the Free plan, the page is hidden and shows Included in Commerce; past counts are kept and reappear when you subscribe. Basic stock and low-stock alerts stay available.
A stock count happens in three stages: you start it in the back office, the team counts on the registers
(scan or search, even offline), then you validate. Vendora compares each count with the expected stock
at the moment of the count, so you can count while the store keeps selling.
Settling a conflict between two counters, typing your PIN and validating the stock count.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Stock and purchasing › Stock counts
Choose the store in the header, then Stock and purchasing (1) › Stock counts (2).
Start the stock count
In Start a stock count:
1. enter a label (e.g. “Crèmerie du samedi”);
2. check one or more categories for a partial count — nothing checked = full stock count;
3. click Start.
Expected result: “Stock count “Crèmerie du samedi” started: the store's registers can count.” (1) and
the stock count at the top of the list with the status Counting (2).
Count on the register
On each register in the store, the team opens the Stock › Stock count menu, chooses the ongoing count,
then for each product: Scan or search for a product, enters the quantity and taps Count. The register
confirms (“Apples: 12 counted — as expected” or “— variance …”) and keeps the running total “My counts: … product(s)”.
Several people can count at the same time, each in their own session. Offline, counts are sent as soon as
the network is back.
In the back office, click Refresh to see the counts come in.
Read the discrepancies
Open the stock count from the list:
1. Counters: who counted and how many products;
2. one row per counted product: Expected, Counted, Discrepancy, Value (WAC) of the discrepancy. When two
people counted the same product differently, the row is highlighted “conflict between counters”;
3. the Total discrepancy value;
4. the validation bar: PIN and Confirm stock count (grayed out while a conflict remains to be settled).
Settle the conflicts
On a row in conflict, each count is listed with its time. The one marked (provisional) is the one
Vendora would keep by default. Click Keep next to the right count: the row changes to “conflict resolved”.
If in doubt, have the product counted again: the new count is added.
Validate
Type your PIN in the bottom bar, then click Confirm stock count.
Expected result: “Stock count approved: … stock adjustment(s) created.” (1) and the status Approved (2).
Each row with a discrepancy becomes a Stock count adjustment in the stock log
(a delta, never an overwritten quantity); products that were not counted don't change.
You'll find the gains and losses of each stock count in the Inventory discrepancies tab of the
stock reports.
(If needed) Abandon
Started a stock count by mistake? Enter an Abandonment reason, then click Abandon: “Stock count
abandoned: no stock movement.”
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
… row(s) in conflict between counters: choose a count
A conflict hasn't been settled: click Keep on the right count in each highlighted row.
Invalid PIN
That PIN isn't yours. Set it again in Settings › PIN & approvals.
Manager PIN required: enter the PIN of a store manager to confirm.
The PIN is empty or was never set: set it in Settings › PIN & approvals.
… count(s) arrived after closing: not taken into account, to be handled manually.
A register that was offline sent counts after validation. They change nothing: if the difference matters,
record an adjustment from the Stock page. On the register, the message
“Stock count closed: count refused” appears.
Label required
Give the stock count a name before clicking Start.
“Stock counts and losses” is not included in the … plan. Contact Vendora to add it.
Your plan doesn't include stock counts. See Settings › Subscription or contact Vendora.
The register shows “No stock count in progress: the manager starts it from the back office.”
The stock count was started for another store, or the register hasn't synced yet: check the
store, then wait a few seconds (or run the sync again on the register).
On the register: “… is not part of this stock count”
The product doesn't belong to any category of this partial count. It doesn't need to be counted.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Track your stock and stockouts
- Understand the stock log
- Stock reports
- The Free plan

pages.title: Understand the stock log

sections.heading: Understand the stock log
sections.text:
Every time stock moves, a line is added to the stock log: sale, customer return, receipt of goods,
stock count, loss, theft, transfer, supplier return, opening stock. Nothing is ever erased: a mistake
is corrected with a reversing movement, which is also visible. Open this page whenever a quantity looks
wrong.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Stock and purchasing › Stock log
The page lists the movements of the store chosen in the header, from newest to oldest.
1. Filters: period (From / to), Category, User, Device; Clear filters resets everything.
2. Movement types: click one or more types to keep only those.
3. Export to CSV downloads the filtered log (journal-stock.csv).
4. Each line: date, product and category, type, quantity (red = outflow), reason and details, Who · where
(person and device).
The screen shows the 200 most recent movements; beyond that, the note “the 200 most recent; the CSV
export contains everything” appears: narrow the period or export.
A movement written after a proposal from your assistant carries the mention prepared by the assistant · validated by {name}: the assistant prepared it, but a manager validated it with their PIN, and the movement is in their name (see Approve the assistant's proposals). In the CSV export, the Validé par column then reads “Lina (préparé par l'assistant)” (the mention is written in French in the file).
Filter by type
Example: to review manual corrections, click Stock count adjustment, Loss and Theft (1).
Manual movements and opening stock have a Correct button (2).
Correct a mistake with a reversing movement
A loss entered twice, a wrong quantity? Click Correct on the faulty line:
1. Vendora shows the reversing movement (here “Perte +0,800”, which cancels “Perte −0,800”);
2. enter the reason (required);
3. type your Manager PIN;
4. click Confirm correction.
Expected result: “Movement corrected: a reversing movement was added to the log.” (1). The new
line carries the correction badge (2), the old one the corrected badge (3); the stock returns to its previous level.
Only manual movements (loss, theft, adjustment) and opening stock can be corrected here, once
each. A sale is corrected with a return on the register, a receipt of goods with a
supplier return.

sections.heading: The exported file
sections.text:
Stock log (extract)
Extract (30 lines) of the demo grocery store's log. Opens directly in Excel or LibreOffice.
Column · Content
Date · Date and time of the movement, in the store's time zone (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
Produit, Catégorie · The product and its category.
Type · Movement type, as written in the file: Vente (sale), Retour client (customer return), Réception (receipt of goods), Ajustement d'inventaire (stock count adjustment), Perte (loss), Vol (theft), Transfert sortant (outgoing transfer), Transfert entrant (incoming transfer), Écart de transfert (transfer discrepancy), Retour fournisseur (supplier return), Stock initial (opening stock).
Quantité · Signed, decimal comma: -0,8 = outflow of 0.8.
Motif, Détail · Reason chosen (Casse, Péremption, Inventaire…) and details entered (or the name of the stock count).
Utilisateur, Validé par · Who made the movement, who validated it with their PIN.
Appareil · Register it came from, or “Back-office (serveur)” (back office, server).
Vente · Sale ID for a sale or return movement.
Correction de · For a reversing movement: ID of the corrected movement.
Correction denied. This movement has already been corrected
A movement can only be corrected once. If you still need to adjust, record a new adjustment from the
Stock page.
Correction denied. A reversal movement cannot be corrected: record a new adjustment
You clicked a correction line. To go back, record an adjustment.
Correction denied. Only manual movements and initial stock are corrected here (a sale goes through a return, a receipt of goods through a supplier return)
The movement comes from a sale, a receipt of goods or a transfer: use the intended process (customer return on the
register, supplier return, transfer).
Correction denied. Invalid PIN
That PIN isn't yours. Set it again if needed in Settings › PIN & approvals.
Correction denied. Reason required
Enter the reason for the correction: it stays in the log.
No movements for these filters.
Widen the period or click Clear filters. Also check the store in the header.
Log unavailable.
The server didn't respond: reload the page. Do the same for “Export failed.”

sections.text:

- Stock reports: turnover, losses, dormant products

pages.title: Track lots and expiry dates

sections.heading: Track lots and expiry dates
sections.text:
Included in Commerce
Batch and expiry-date tracking is part of advanced stock, included in the Commerce plan and higher plans. On the Free plan, the page is hidden and shows Included in Commerce, and batches are no longer entered at receiving; batches already recorded are kept and reappear when you subscribe.
For a fresh product (yogurt, butter, meat…), turn on Expiry tracking in its product record and
set the number of alert days (e.g. 5). From then on, every receipt of goods asks for a lot number and
a use-by date, and the Expiry page lists the lots to keep an eye on.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Receive goods with lot and use-by date
When you confirm receipt of a purchase order containing a tracked
product, a Lot / use-by column appears: fill in Lot no. and the date for each line received (reminder on
screen: “Expiry-tracked products: lot number and use-by date are required on every received line.”). The
same goes for a receipt on the register
(Stock › Supplier receipts), where one line can be split across several lots.
Open Stock and purchasing › Expiry
1. Three counters: Expired lots, Expiring soon (use-by date within the product's alert period),
Quantity concerned.
2. Filters All, Expiring soon, Expired.
3. One lot per row: product and date received, lot number, use-by date and days left (D-3), quantity
left, status (Expired, Expiring soon, OK).
Sales use up lots in order of their use-by date (oldest first): a lot's quantity goes down
on its own. At the register, the cashier sees the product's lots and can choose another one:
that lot then goes out first and the choice is written to the audit log. A return puts the item back on the lot sold.
Write off a lot
On an expired lot (or one you need to throw away), click Write off, optionally enter a reason (1), then
Confirm write-off (2). Cancel closes without doing anything.
Expected result: “Lot YA-2610 of “Yaourt nature x4” written off (6).” The lot's quantity drops to 0
and a Loss with the reason Expiry is recorded in the stock log;
it counts in the Losses and theft tab of the stock reports.
The page is missing from the menu, or shows “Included in Commerce”
Your plan (for example Free) does not include this module: the page shows “This feature is not included in your current plan. Your data stays intact: it reappears as soon as you subscribe.” Nothing is deleted. The owner subscribes from Settings › Subscription (View subscription link). See The Free plan.
No tracked lots
No product has expiry tracking, or no goods have been received since it was turned on.
Turn on “Expiry tracking” on a product: every receipt will create a lot with its use-by date.
Lot number and use-by date are required for “…” (product tracked for expiry).
When receiving goods, a line for a tracked product has no lot or no use-by date. Fill in both fields in the
Lot / use-by column, then confirm again.
Use-by date expected in YYYY-MM-DD format
The date entered can't be read. Use the field's date picker.
Lot already empty
The lot was entirely sold or already written off in the meantime. Refresh the page.
Reserved for the store's managers.
The page is reserved for the store's Manager, Administrator and Owner roles.
The write-off could not be recorded.
The server didn't respond: reload the page and try again. Do the same for “Unable to load lots.”

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Place a purchase order and receive it
- Stock reports: losses and theft
- The Free plan

pages.title: Low stock thresholds and order suggestions

sections.heading: Low stock thresholds and order suggestions
sections.text:
The low stock threshold is the quantity below which a product needs to be reordered. Vendora
flags it everywhere (Stock page, dashboard, registers) and can automatically prepare draft purchase
orders with the preferred supplier.
Your AI assistant can also prepare a threshold for you, which you approve in the back office: see Opening stock of a product, low-stock threshold (action subject to activation).

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Set a product's threshold
In Stock and purchasing › Stock, click the product. At the top of the panel:
1. enter the Low stock threshold (e.g. 15; empty = no threshold);
2. click Save: “Threshold saved: the product will be suggested for ordering below this stock level.”;
3. to help you, the table shows the last price received from each supplier and its Trend
(↗ rising, ↘ falling, → stable).
The threshold is shared by all stores. Empty the field and save to remove it (“Threshold removed.”).
See the products below their threshold
On the Purchase orders page, the Low stock card (1) lists each product below its threshold: current stock /
threshold, quantity already on order (orders sent but not received) and preferred supplier. On the Stock page,
the Below threshold alert filters the same products.
Generate the suggestions
Click Generate suggestions (2). Vendora creates one draft per preferred supplier, with
quantities calculated from the threshold, the stock and what is already on order — check them before sending.
Expected result: “1 suggested draft(s) — check before sending.” (1); the drafts carry the
suggested badge (2). If there's nothing to order: “No suggestions: nothing to order.”
Check and send
Open the draft: correct the quantities (1), Save (2), then Send (3). The next steps (sending,
receiving) are described in Place a purchase order.
A product below its threshold isn't in the suggestions
It has no preferred supplier: the card says so in “To assign (no preferred supplier): …”.
Open the right supplier's record and check Preferred for this product (Suppliers).
It's also skipped if the quantity already on order is enough.
No product below its threshold.
No threshold has been reached (or no threshold is set): nothing to order.
Unable to save the threshold.
The threshold must be a positive number (decimal comma allowed). If the message persists, reload the page.
On the server side, a negative threshold is rejected: “Negative threshold”.

sections.heading: See also
sections.text:
- Track your stock and stockouts
- Place a purchase order and receive it

pages.title: Track your stock and stockouts

sections.heading: Track your stock and stockouts
sections.text:
In Vendora, stock is never entered by hand: it's the sum of all movements (register
sales, receipts of goods, transfers, losses, stock counts…). The Stock page shows the result, store by
store, and flags what needs your attention.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.text:
Open Stock and purchasing › Stock
In the left menu, open Stock and purchasing (1), then Stock (2). Shortcut: type “stock” in
Go to… at the top of the screen.
Read the list
1. The store: the page covers a single store, the one chosen in the header. With “All stores”,
a Store selector appears on the page (first store by default).
2. Search for a product… filters the list by name.
3. Alerts: one button per alert type, with their count — Negative stock, Out of stock (stock at zero),
Below threshold (low stock threshold reached). They only appear if there are alerts.
4. Click the Quantity header to sort: ascending, then descending, then back to alphabetical order.
Quantities sold by weight are shown with three decimals (30,200 = 30.2 kg). A negative or zero quantity
has a red background; the negative and below threshold (15) badges repeat the alert next to the name.
Show only the alerts
Click an alert, for example Below threshold (3) (1): the list keeps only those products (2). Click
again or click Show all to go back to the full list.
Negative stock: don't panic
A register can sell a product the system thinks is sold out (receipt not yet entered, counting error).
The stock then goes negative. Receive the goods (purchase orders)
or run a stock count to set it right.
Open a product's stock record
Click a row: the Movements — … panel opens on the right with three parts.
1. Low stock threshold and purchase prices: weighted average cost and last price received from each supplier
(see Low stock thresholds).
2. Record a movement: loss, theft or adjustment.
3. The product's latest movements: type, quantity (+ inflow, − outflow), date, device and person. A movement
that comes from an assistant proposal carries the mention “prepared by the assistant · validated by {name}”.
Close the panel with the X button, the Esc key or by clicking outside it.
Record a loss, a theft or an adjustment
In Record a movement:
1. choose the type: Loss, Theft or Adjustment (±);
2. enter the quantity: for a loss or a theft, the quantity removed (positive, e.g. 0,8); for an
adjustment, the difference with its sign (e.g. -2 or 3);
3. choose the reason (Breakage, Expiry, Damaged, Theft, Counting error, Other) and
add details if needed;
4. type your PIN;
5. click Save.
Expected result: the message “Movement saved and signed: stock updated.” (1) and the movement at the top
of the history (2), with the name of the person who validated it.
You can't overwrite a quantity (“there are 12 left”): you always record a difference. To recount
a whole aisle, use a stock count instead. Correct an entry mistake from the stock log.
Invalid PIN
The PIN you typed isn't yours (it's your PIN that validates, not a colleague's). Check it or
reset it in Settings › PIN & approvals.
Manager PIN required: enter the PIN of a store manager to confirm.
The PIN field was empty when you submitted, or you have never set a PIN: do it in
Settings › PIN & approvals, then try again.
Product not tracked in stock
The product doesn't have the Stock tracking box checked in its record (Catalog › Products). Check it if you
want to track its quantities.
A loss or theft is an outflow (negative quantity)
The type is Loss or Theft but the quantity was sent as an inflow. Enter the quantity removed
(positive): the sign is added automatically. To add stock, use Adjustment (±).
Zero quantity
Enter a quantity other than zero.
Manager role required for this store
Your role doesn't allow you to change this store's stock. Ask the owner to give you the Manager
role for this store (Settings › Team).
Unable to load the stock: check your connection, then reload the page.
The server didn't respond (connection lost, session expired). Reload the page; if the message stays,
see the error message index.
A product doesn't appear in the list
The list only shows products tracked in stock that have already had at least one movement in this store.
Receive goods, enter an opening stock or check the store
chosen in the header.

sections.text:
